αθεσφατοσ.def: ἀθέσφατος beyond even a god's power to express: ineffable, aweful, ὄμβρος, θάλασσα, νύξ Hom.; also marvellous in quantity, ἀθ. οἶνος, σῖτος, βόες Od.

αθετεω.def: ἀθετέω (From ἄθετος) to set aside: ἀθ. τινα to deny one, refuse his request, NTest.

αθετοσ.def: ἄθετος (τίθημι) set aside:— adv. -τως, ἀθέσμως, lawlessly, despotically, Aesch.

αθηναι.def: Ἀθῆναι the city of Athens, used in pl., because it consisted of several parts (cf. Θῆβαι, Μυκῆναι, Hom., etc.; the sg. (like Θήβη) Od.

αθηναιον.def: Ἀθήναιον (Ἀθηνᾶ) the temple of Athena, Hdt.

αθηναιοσ.def: Ἀθηναῖος Athenian, of or from Athens, Il., etc

αθηνη.def: Ἀθήνη Athena, goddess of wisdom, warlike prowess, and skill in the arts, often called Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη.

αθηνηθεν.def: Ἀθήνηθεν from Athens, Lys., etc.; poet. Ἀθήνοθεν Anth.

αθηνιαω.gloss: to long to be at Athens
αθηνιαω.def: Ἀθηνιάω (Ἀθῆναι) to long to be at Athens, Luc.

αθηρ.def: ἀθήρ I. an ear of corn, Hes. 2. husks, chaff, Luc. II. the point of a weapon, Aesch., etc.

αθηρηλοιγοσ.def: ἀθηρηλοιγός (ἀθήρ) consumer of ears of corn, of a winnowing fan, Od.

αθηροσ.def: ἄθηρος (θήρ) without wild beasts or game, Hdt.: τὸ ἄθηρον absence of game, Plut.

αθιγησ.def: ἀθιγής (θιγγάνω) untouched, of a virgin, Anth.

αθικτοσ.def: ἄθικτος (θιγγάνω) 1. untouched: c. gen. untouched by a thing, Soph.; κερδῶν ἄθικτον βουλευτήριον untouched by gain, i. e. incorruptible, Aesch.; also c. dat., νόσοις ἄθ. id. 2. not to be touched, holy, sacred, of Delphi, Soph.; ἄθικτα holy things, Aesch.

αθλευω.gloss: to contend for a prize, combat, wrestle
αθλευω.def: ἀθλεύω (ἆθλον) to contend for a prize, combat, wrestle, Il.; ἀθλεύων πρὸ ἄνακτος struggling or suffering for him, id.

αθλεω.def: ἀθλέω (ἆθλος, commoner form of ἀθλεύω.) Λαομέδοντι ἀθλήσαντες having contended with him, Il.; πολλά περ ἀθλήσαντα having gone through many struggles, id.: to contend in battle, πρός τινα Hdt.

αθλημα.def: ἄθλημα (ἀθλέω) I. a contest, Plat., etc. II. an implement of labour, Theocr.

αθλητησ.def: ἀθλητής (ἀθλέω) I. a prizefighter, Lat. athleta: as adj., ἀθλ. ἵππος a race-horse, Lys. II. c. gen. rei, practised in a thing, Plat.

αθλιοσ.def: ἄθλιος (attic contr. of epic ἀέθλιος, see also ἄεθλον, ἆθλον) I. gaining the prize, or running for it (this sense only in epic form) ἵππος ἀεθλίη a race-horse, Theogn.; μῆλον ἀέθλ. the apple of discord, Anth. II. metaph. struggling, wretched, miserable (this sense only in attic form), of persons Aesch., etc.: comp. -ιώτερος Soph.: Sup. -ιώτατος Eur.:—also of states of life, γάμοι, βίος, τύχη Trag.: —adv. -ίως, miserably, Soph. 2. in moral sense, pitiful, wretched, Dem. 3. without any moral sense, wretched, sorry, θηρσὶν ἀθλία βορά Eur.:—adv., ἀθλίως καὶ κακῶς with wretched success, Dem.

αθλιοτησ.def: ἀθλιότης (from ἄθλιος) suffering, wretchedness, Plat., etc.

αθλοθετησ.gloss: one who awards the prize, the judge
αθλοθετησ.def: ἀθλοθέτης (τίθημι) one who awards the prize, the judge in the games, Plat., etc.

αθλον.def: ἆθλον (contr. from epic and ionic ἄεθλον) I. the prize of contest, Hom., etc.; ἄεθλα κεῖται or πρόκειται prizes are proposed, Hdt.; ἆθλα προφαίνειν, προτιθέναι, τιθέναι to propose prizes, Xen.; ἆθλα λαμβάνειν or φέρεσθαι to win prizes, Plat.; ἆθλα πολέμου, τῆς ἀρετῆς Dem. II. = ἆθλος, a contest, Od.:—metaph. a conflict, struggle, Aesch., Soph.

αθλοσ.def: ἆθλος (contr. from epic and ionic ἄεθλος) a contest for a prize, Hom., etc.; ἄεθλος πρόκειται a task is set one, Hdt.; ἄεθλον προτιθέναι to set it, id.;—metaph. a conflict, struggle, Aesch.

αθλοφοροσ.def: ἀθλοφόρος (φέρω) bearing away the prize, victorious, ἵππος Il.; in ionic form ἀεθλ-, id., Hdt.

αθορυβητοσ.def: ἀθορύβητος (θορυβέω) undisturbed: τὸ ἀθ. tranquillity, Xen.

αθρεω.gloss: to look at, gaze at, observe, perceive
αθρεω.def: ἀθρέω I. to look at, gaze at, observe, perceive, Hom., etc. 2. absol., or with a prep., to look, gaze, Il.; δεῦρ’ ἄθρησον Eur.; οὐ γὰρ ἴδοις ἂν ἀθρῶν by observing, Soph. II. of the mind, to look into a thing, consider, id., Eur., etc.:—foll. by an interrog. or rel. clause, ταῦτ’ ἄθρησον, εἰ.. consider this also, whether.., Soph.; ἄθρει Plat.

αθρητεον.def: ἀθρητέον (verb. adj. of ἀθρέω) one must consider, Eur., Xen.

αθροιζω.def: ἀθροίζω (ἀθρόος) 1. to gather together, to muster forces, Soph., Xen.; Τροίαν ἀθρ. to gather the Trojans together, Eur.; πνεῦμα ἄθροισον collect breath, id.:—Mid. to gather for oneself, collect round one, id., Xen.:—Pass. to be gathered together, ἐς τὴν ἀγορήν Hdt.; ἀθροισθέντες having rallied, Thuc.; τὸ ξύμπαν ἠθροίσθη δισχίλιοι the whole amounted collectively to 2000, id. 2. in Pass. also of the mind, ἀθροίζεσθαι εἰς ἑαυτόν to collect oneself, Plat.; φόβος ἤθροισται fear has gathered strength, arisen, Xen.

αθροισισ.def: ἄθροισις (from ἀθροίζω) a gathering, mustering, στρατοῦ Eur.; χρημάτων Thuc.

αθροισμα.def: ἄθροισμα (from ἀθροίζω) a gathering, λαοῦ Eur.

αθροιστεον.def: ἀθροιστέον (verb. adj. of ἀθροίζω,) one must collect, Xen.

αθροοσ.def: ἀθρόος (α copul.. θρόος) I. in crowds or masses, crowded together, mostly in pl.; πάντες ἁθρόοι Od., etc.; ἀθρόοι, of soldiers, in close order, Lat. conferto agmine, Hdt., Xen., etc.; also, πολλαὶ κῶμαι ἀθρόαι close together, id. II. taken together, ἁθρόα πάντ’ ἀπέτισεν he paid for all at once, Od.; ἁθρόα πόλις the citizens as a whole, Thuc.; τὸ ἀθρόον their assembled force, Xen.; ἀθρόωι στόματι with one voice, Eur.; ἁθρόους κρίνειν to condemn all by a single vote, Plat.; κατήριπεν ἀθρόος he fell all at once, Theocr. III. multitudinous, δάκρυ Eur., Plat. IV. comp. ἁθροώτερος Thuc., etc.; later ἀθρούστερος Plut.

αθρυπτοσ.def: ἄθρυπτος (θρύπτω) not broken, not enervated, Plut.; ἄθρυπτος εἰς γέλωτα never breaking into laughter, id. adv. -τως, id.

αθυμεω.def: ἀθυμέω (ἄθυμος) to be disheartened, lose heart, Aesch., etc.; τινι at or for a thing, Soph.; ἐπί τινι, εἴς τι, πρός τι, attic Prose:—foll. by a relat. word, to be sore afraid, ἀθυμῶ δ’ εἰ φανήσομαι Soph.; δεινῶς ἀθυμῶ μὴ βλέπων ὁ μάντις ἦι id.

αθυμητεον.def: ἀθυμητέον (verb. adj. of ἀθυμέω) one must lose heart, Xen.

αθυμια.def: ἀθυμία (from ἀθυμέω) want of heart, faintheartedness, Hdt., Soph., etc.; εἰς ἀθυμίαν καθιστάναι τινά Plat.; ἀθυμίαν παρέχειν τινί Xen.; ἐν ἀθυμίαι εἶναι id.; ἀθυμία ἐμπίπτει τινί id.

αθυμοσ.def: ἄθυμος 1. without heart, fainthearted, Od., Hdt., etc.; ἄθ. εἶναι πρός τι to have no heart for a thing, Xen.; so adv., ἀθύμως ἔχειν πρός τι id. 2. without passion, Plat.

αθυρμα.gloss: a plaything, toy: a delight, joy
αθυρμα.def: ἄθυρμα (ἀθύρω) a plaything, toy: a delight, joy, Hom., etc.

αθυρογλωττοσ.gloss: one that cannot keep his mouth shut, a ceaseless babbler
αθυρογλωττοσ.def: ἀθυρόγλωττος (θύρα, γλῶττα) one that cannot keep his mouth shut, a ceaseless babbler, Eur.

αθυρω.def: ἀθύρω I. to play, sport, of children, Il., Eur.; c. acc. cogn., μοῦσαν ἀθύρων singing sportive songs, Hhymn.:—Mid., simply, to sing, id. II. c. acc., ἔργα φωτῶν ἀθ. to play the deeds of men, of an actor, Anth.

αθυτοσ.def: ἄθυτος (θύω) I. not offered, i. e. neglected, ἱερὰ ἄθ., Lat. sacra inauspicata, Aeschin. II. act. without sacrificing, ἄθυτος ἀπελθεῖν Xen.

αθωοσ.def: ἀθῷος (θωή) I. unpunished, scot-free, Eur., etc.; ἀθώιους καθιστάναι τινάς to secure their immunity, Dem.; ἀθῶιον ἀφιέναι id.; ἀθῶιος ἀπαλλάττειν to get off scot-free, Plat. 2. free from a thing, c. gen., Ar. 3. unharmed by a thing, c. gen., Dem. II. not deserving punishment, without fault, id.

αθωπευτοσ.def: ἀθώπευτος (θωπεύω) I. not flattered, without flattery, τῆς ἐμῆς γλώσσης from my tongue, Eur. II. act. not flattering, discourteous, Anth.

αι.def: αἴ Exclam. of astonishment, ha! αἲ τάλας Ar.

αἰ I. if:— αἴ κε or κεν if only, so that, Lat. dummodo, with subj., Hom.; so doric αἴκᾱ, Theocr. II. αἲ γάρ (with accent), epic for εἰ γάρ, to express a wish, O that! would that! Lat. utinam! with opt., Hom.; cf. αἴθε.

αια.def: αἶα epic form used for γαῖα metri grat., Hom., Trag.; never in pl.

αιαζω.def: αἰάζω to cry αἰαῖ, to wail, Trag.; c. acc. to bewail, Aesch., Eur.

αιαι.def: αἰαῖ exclam. of grief, ah! Lat. vae! c. gen., αἰαῖ τόλμας Eur.; and repeated, αἰαῖ αἰαῖ μελέων ἔργων Aesch.:—later c. acc., αἰαῖ τὰν Κυθέρειαν Bion.

αιακτοσ.def: αἰακτός (verb. adj. of αἰάζω) I. bewailed, lamentable, Aesch., Ar. II. wailing, miserable, Aesch.

αιανησ.def: αἰανής I. dreary, dismal, direful, horrid, νυκτὸς αἰανῆ τέκνα, νυκτὸς αἰανὴς κύκλος, αἰανὴς νόσος Aesch., Soph., etc. II. of Time, εἰς τὸν αἰανῆ χρόνον Aesch.; and so in adv. αἰανῶς for ever, id. (The prob. deriv. is from αἰεί, everlasting, whence may come the notion of neverending, wearisome, dreary.)

αιασ.def: Αἴας Ajax, pr. n., borne by two heroes, the Greater son of Telamon, the Less son of Oileus, Hom.

αιβοι.def: αἰβοῖ bah! exclam. of disgust or astonishment; but αἰβοῖ, βοῖ, of laughter, Ar.

αιγαγροσ.def: αἴγαγρος (αἴξ, ἄγρος) the wild goat, Babr.

αιγαιοσ.def: Αἰγαῖος I. Aegaean, πέλαγος Aesch.; ὄρος Αἰγ. mount Ida, Hes. II. Αἰγαῖος (sc. πόντος), the Aegaean, Plat., etc.

αιγαιων.def: Αἰγαίων I. Aegaeon, the name given by men to the hundred-armed son of Uranus and Gaia, called by gods Βριάρεως, Il. II. the Aegaean sea, Eur.

αιγανεη.def: αἰγανέη a hunting-spear, javelin, Hom., Anth. (Perh. from αἴξ, a goatspear.)

αιγειοσ.def: αἴγειος (αἴξ, αἴγειος) of a goat or goats, Lat. caprinus, αἴγειος τυρός goats-milk cheese, Il.; ἀσκῶι ἐν αἰγείωι in a goat's skin, id.; αἰγείη κυνέη a helmet of goatskin.

αιγεοσ.def: αἴγεος I. = αἴγειος, Od. II. as Subst. αἰγέη (sc. δορά), a goat's skin, Hdt.

αιγιαλιτησ.def: αἰγιαλίτης (from αἰγιαλός) one who haunts the shore, Anth.

αιγιαλοσ.def: αἰγιαλός (αἴξ 11) the sea-shore, beach, strand, Hom., Hdt.; αἰγιαλὸν ἔνδον τρέφει, i. e. he has a whole sea-beach (i. e. quantities of voting-pebbles, ψῆφοι) in his house, Ar.

αιγιβοτοσ.def: αἰγίβοτος (αἴξ, βόσκω) browsed by goats, Od.

αιγιθαλλοσ.def: αἰγίθαλλος the titmouse, Lat. parus, Ar.

αιγικορεισ.def: αἰγικορεῖς goatherds; name of one of the four old Attic Tribes, Hdt., Eur. (If from αἴξ, κορέννυμι, the literal sense would be goatfeeders.)

αιγιλιψ.def: αἰγίλιψ (αἴξ, λείπω) destitute even of goats, hence steep, sheer, πέτρη Il.

αιγιλοσ.gloss: a herb of which goats are fond
αιγιλοσ.def: αἴγιλος (αἴξ) a herb of which goats are fond, Theocr.

αιγιναιοσ.def: Αἰγιναῖος (from Αἴγινα) of Aegina, Thuc., etc.

αιγινητησ.def: Αἰγινήτης (from Αἴγινα) an Aeginetan, Hdt., etc.

αιγινομοσ.def: αἰγίνομος (αἴξ, νέμω) (cf. αἰγινόμος) pass. browsed by goats, βοτάνη id.
αἰγινόμος (αἴξ, νέμω) (cf. αἰγίνομος) feeding goats: as Subst. a goatherd, Anth.

αιγιπυροσ.def: αἰγίπυρος a plant of which goats were fond, perh. buckwheat, Theocr.

αιγισ.def: αἰγίς (αἴξ) I. the aegis or shield of Zeus, described in Il. 5. 738 sqq. the aegis on statues of Athena is a short cloak of goat-skin, covered with scales, set with the Gorgon's head, and fringed with snakes, v. Hdt. 4. 189. 2. a goatskin coat, Eur. II. （αἴξ II) a rushing storm, hurricane, Aesch.

αιγλη.gloss: the light of the sun, radiance
αιγλη.def: αἴγλη 1. the light of the sun, radiance, Od.:—then simply daylight, λευκὴ αἴγλη id.; εἰς αἴγλαν μολεῖν, i. e. to be born, Pind 2. any dazzling light, lustre, gleam, χαλκοῦ Il.

αιγληεισ.def: αἰγλήεις (from αἴγλη) dazzling, radiant, lustrous, Hom.

αιγοκερωσ.def: αἰγόκερως (αἴξ, κέρας) I. goat-horned, Anth., Plut. II. as Subst. Capricorn in the Zodiac, Luc.

αιγυπιοσ.def: αἰγυπιός a vulture, Hom., etc.:— αἰγυπιός is the vulture which preys on live animals, γύψ the carrion vulture.

αιγυπτιακοσ.def: Αἰγυπτιακός of or for the Egyptians, Plut., etc.

αιγυπτιοσ.def: Αἰγύπτιος Egyptian, Hom., etc. (Αἰγυπτίη, Αἰγυπτίων, etc., are trisyll. in Hom.)

αιγυπτιστι.def: Αἰγυπτιστί (as if from Αἰγυπτίζω) I. in the Egyptian tongue, Hdt. II. in Egyptian fashion, craftily, Theocr.

αιγυπτοσ.def: Αἴγυπτος I. the river Nile, Od.; called Νεῖλος first in Hes. II. Egypt, Od.

αιδεομαι.def: αἰδέομαι I. to be ashamed to do a thing, c. inf., Hom., etc.; rarely c. part., αἴδεσαι μὲν πατέρα προλείπων feel ashamed of deserting him, Soph.:—absol., αἰδεσθείς from a sense of shame, Il. 2. c. acc. pers. to stand in awe of, fear, respect, αἰδεῖο θεούς id., Hom., etc.; and of things, αἴδεσσαι μέλαθρον respect the house, Il.; ὅρκον αἰδεσθείς Soph. II. to feel regard for a person, μήδε τί μ’ αἰδόμενος μήδ’ ἐλεαίρων Od.

αιδεσιμοσ.def: αἰδέσιμος (from αἰδέομαι) exciting shame, venerable, Luc.

αιδηλοσ.def: ἀίδηλος (⁎εἴδω) I. making unseen, annihilating, destroying, Il.:—adv. -λως, ὀλεθρίως, id. II. pass. unseen, obscure, Hes.

αιδημων.def: αἰδήμων (αἰδέομαι) bashful, modest, Xen.: Sup. αἰδημονέστατος, id.: adv. -μόνως, id.

αιδιοσ.def: ἀίδιος (ἀεί) everlasting, eternal, Hes. and attic:— ἐς ἀΐδιον for ever, Thuc.

αιδοιον.def: αἰδοῖον (αἴδομαι) mostly in pl. αἰδοῖα, τά, the genitals, pudenda, Il., etc.

αιδοιοσ.def: αἰδοῖος (αἰδέομαι) I. of persons, regarded with reverence, august, venerable, and of women, deserving respect, tender, Hom. II. act. shamefaced, reverent, Od.:—adv. -ως, reverently, id. III. comp. αἰδοιότερος, Od.; Sup. αἰδοιέστατος, Pind.

αιδοφρων.def: αἰδόφρων (αἴδομαι, φρήν) respectful in mind, compassionate, Soph.; πρός τινα Eur.

αιδρειη.def: ἀιδρείη (from ἄιδρις) want of knowledge, ignorance, Od., Hdt.

αιδρισ.def: ἄιδρις poet. adj. unknowing, ignorant, Il.; c. gen., Od., etc.

αιδρυτοσ.def: ἀίδρυτος (ἱδρύω) unsettled, vagabond, Ar.; δρόμοις ἀν. in vagabond courses, Eur.

αιδωνευσ.def: Ἀιδωνεύς (= Ἄαιδης) (poets used the obl. cases Ἀϊδονῆος, ῆϊ, ῆα, with ᾱ, metri grat.)

αιδωσ.gloss: a sense of shame, shame, modesty, self-respect
αιδωσ.def: αἰδώς (αἰδέομαι) I. a sense of shame, shame, modesty, self-respect, Hom., etc.:—personif., Ζηνὶ σύνθακος θρόνων Αἰδώς Shame that shares his throne with Zeus, Soph. 2. regard for others, respect, reverence, Theogn.; τὴν ἐμὴν αἰδῶ respect for me, Aesch. II. that which causes shame, and so, 1. a shame, Il.; as an exclam., shame! αἰδώς, Ἀργεῖοι, κακ’ ἐλέγχεα! id.; αἰδώς, ὦ Λύκιοι· ποῖ φεύγετε; id. 2. = τὰ αἰδοῖα, id.

αιενυπνοσ.def: αἰένυπνος lulling in eternal sleep, of Death, Soph.

αιζηιοσ.def: αἰζήιος strong, lusty, vigorous, Hom. (Deriv. uncertain.)

αιζηοσ.def: αἰζηός strong, lusty, vigorous, Hom. (Deriv. uncertain.)

αιητοσ.def: αἴητος in Il. Vulcan is πέλωρ αἴητον, ἄητον, terrible, mighty monster.

αιθαλιων.def: αἰθαλίων (αἴθαλος) epith. of the τέττιξ, swarthy, dusky, Theocr.

αιθαλοεισ.def: αἰθαλόεις (αἴθαλος) I. smoky, sooty, Il., Theocr.; κόνις αἰθ. black ashes that are burnt out, Hom. II. burning, Hes., Aesch.

αιθαλοω.def: αἰθαλόω to soil with soot or smoke, Eur.

αιθε.def: αἴθε Epic for εἴθε, αἴθ’ ὄφελες would that Hom.; cf. αἰ.

αιθερεμβατεω.def: αἰθερεμβατέω (ἐμβαίνω) to walk in ether, Anth.

αιθεριοσ.def: αἰθέριος (αἰθήρ) of or in the upper air, high in air, on high, Aesch., Soph., etc.; αἰθερία ἀνέπτα flew up into the air, Eur.

αιθηρ.gloss: ether, the brighter purer air, the sky
αιθηρ.def: αἰθήρ (αἴθω) (in Hom. fem; in Hes., Aesch., and attic Prose masc; in Soph. and Eur. masc or fem.) I. ether, the brighter purer air, the sky, above the ἀήρ (q. v.); Ζεὺς αἰθέρι ναίων Il. II. a clime, region, Eur.

αιθιοπικοσ.def: Αἰθιοπικός 1. Ethiopian, Hdt., etc. 2. in literal sense, sun-burnt, Anth.

αιθιοψ.def: Αἰθίοψ (αἴθω, ὄψ) I. properly burnt-face, i. e. an Ethiop, African, Hom., etc. II. adj. Ethiopian, Hdt., etc.

αιθοσ.def: αἶθος (αἴθω) a burning heat, fire, Eur.

αιθουσα.def: αἴθουσα (sc. στοά, αἴθουσα being partic. of αἴθω) in the Homeric house, the corridor, open in front like a verandah, looking E. or S. to catch the sun, whence the name; the sleeping place of travellers, Od.

αιθοψ.def: αἶθοψ (αἴθω, ὄψ) I. fiery-looking, of metal, flashing, Il., etc.; of wine, sparkling, id.; of smoke, mixed with flame, Od. 2. swart, dark, Anth. II. metaph. fiery, keen, eager, Lat. ardens, Hes., Soph.

αιθρη.def: αἴθρη (αἰθήρ) not αἴθρα even in attic; clear sky, fair weather, Lat. sudum, Hom.

αιθρηγενησ.gloss: born in ether, sprung from ether
αιθρηγενησ.def: αἰθρηγενής (γίγνομαι) epith. of Boreas, born in ether, sprung from ether, Il.

αιθρια.def: αἰθρία (later form of αἴθρη, Solon, etc.) 1. αἰθρίης, attic -ίας, in clear weather, Hdt., Ar.; ὑπὸ τῆς αἰθρίας in the open air, Lat. sub dio, Xen. 2. the clear cold air of night, Hdt. (ῑ in dactylics and anapaestics.)

αιθριαω.def: αἰθριάω to be clear, of the sky, ὡς δ’ ᾐθρίᾱσε Babr.

αιθριοκοιτεω.def: αἰθριοκοιτέω (κοίτη) to sleep in open air, Theocr.

αιθριοσ.def: αἴθριος (αἴθρη) clear, bright, fair, of weather, Hhymn., Hdt.; epith. of Ζεύς, Theocr.

αιθροσ.def: αἶθρος the clear chill air of morn, Od.; cf. αἰθρία.

αιθυια.def: αἴθυια a sea-bird, a gull or diver, Od. (Deriv. unknown.)

αιθυκτηρ.def: αἰθυκτήρ (from αἰθύσσω) one that darts swiftly, Anth.

αιθυσσω.gloss: to put in rapid motion, stir up, kindle
αιθυσσω.def: αἰθύσσω (αἴθω) to put in rapid motion, stir up, kindle, Soph.:—Pass. to quiver, of leaves, Sapph.

αιθω.def: αἴθω 1. to light up, kindle, Hdt., Trag. 2. intr. to burn or blaze, Soph.:—in this sense the Pass. αἴθομαι is used by Hom. in part., πυρὸς μένος αἰθομένοιο Il., Od., etc.; so metaph., ἔρωτι αἴθεσθαι Xen.

αιθων.def: αἴθων (αἴθω) I. fiery, burning, blazing: of metal, flashing, glittering, Hom., etc. II. in Hom. of the horse, lion, bull, eagle, —where it is either fiery, fierce, or tawny. 2. metaph. ablaze, fiery, Aesch., Soph. (The penult. of the obl. cases may be shortd. in Poets, metri grat., αἴθονος Soph.; αἴθονα Hes.)

αικαλλω.def: αἰκάλλω (αἰκάλος) 1. to flatter, wheedle, fondle, c. acc., Soph., Eur. 2. absol., of a dog, to wag the tail fawningly, Babr.: (this is prob. the orig. sense).

αικη.def: ἀική (ἀΐσσω) rapid flight, rush, impetus, Il.

αικησ.def: ἀικής (poetic for ἀεικής) adv. ἀϊκῶς, Il.:—in Trag., αἰκής, αἰκῶς.

αικια.def: αἰκία (attic for the ionic ἀεικείη) 1. injurious treatment, an affront, outrage, Aesch., etc. 2. in Prose mostly as law-phrase, αἰκίας δίκη an action for assault, less serious than that for ὕβρις, Plat., etc.

αικιζω.gloss: to treat injuriously, to plague, torment
αικιζω.def: αἰκίζω (attic for epic αεἰκίζω) I. Act. only in pres., to treat injuriously, to plague, torment, τινά Soph.; of a storm, αἰκίζων φόβην ὕλης id.:—Pass. to be tormented, Aesch. II. Dep. in same sense as Act., c. acc., Soph., etc.; c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, αἰκίζεσθαί τινα τὰ ἔσχατα Xen.

αικισμα.def: αἴκισμα (from αἰκίζω) an outrage, torture, Aesch.:—in pl. mutilated corpses, Eur.

αιλινοσ.def: αἴλινος 1. a plaintive dirge, Trag.; (said to be from αἶ Λίνον, ah me for Linus! v. Λίνος II.) 2. adj. αἴλινος, ον, mournful, plaintive, Eur.:— neut. pl. αἴλινα as adv., Mosch.

αιλουροσ.def: αἴλουρος a cat, Hdt., attic (Deriv. uncertain.)

αιμα.def: αἷμα I. blood, Hom., etc.; in pl. streams of blood, Trag. II. bloodshed, murder, Aesch., etc.: —ἐφ’ αἵματι φεύγειν to avoid trial for murder by going into exile, Dem.; so, αἷμα φεύγειν Eur. III. like Lat. sanguis, blood-relationship, kin, Soph., Hom., etc.; ὁ πρὸς αἵματος one of the blood or race, Soph.; μητρὸς τῆς ἐμῆς ἐν αἵματι akin to her by blood, Aesch. (Deriv. uncertain.)

αιμακτοσ.def: αἱμακτός (verb. adj. of αἱμάσσω) mingled with blood, of blood, Eur.

αιμασ.def: αἱμάς (αἷμα) a gush or stream of blood, Soph.

αιμασια.def: αἱμασιά a wall of dry stones, Lat. maceria, Od., etc. (Deriv. uncertain.)

αιμασσω.gloss: to make bloody stain with blood
αιμασσω.def: αἱμάσσω (αἷμα) to make bloody stain with blood, Aesch.:—hence to smite so as to make bloody, Soph., Eur.; so in Mid., Anth.:—Pass. to welter in blood, be slain, Soph.

αιματηροσ.def: αἱματηρός (αἷμα) I. bloody, bloodstained, murderous, Trag. II. of blood, consisting thereof, Aesch., Eur.

αιματοεισ.def: αἱματόεις 1. contr. αἱματοῦς, οῦσσα, οῦν, αἱματηρός Il. 2. blood-red or of blood, id. 3. bloody, murderous, id.

αιματολοιχοσ.def: αἱματολοιχός (λείχω) licking blood, ἔρως αἱμ. thirst for blood, Aesch.

αιματορρυτοσ.def: αἱματόρρυτος (ῥέω) blood-streaming, αἱμ. ῥανίδες a shower of blood, Eur.

αιματοω.gloss: to make bloody, stain with blood
αιματοω.def: αἱματόω (αἷμα) to make bloody, stain with blood, Aesch., Eur.

αιμοβοροσ.def: αἱμοβόρος (βορά) blood-sucking, greedy of blood, Theocr.

αιμορροεω.def: αἱμορροέω (ῥέω) to have a αἱμόρροια, discharge of blood.

αιμοφορυκτοσ.def: αἱμοφόρυκτος (φορύσσω) defiled with blood, κρέα Od.

αιμυλοσ.def: αἱμύλος flattering, wheedling, wily, Hes., Aesch.; τὸν αἱμυλώτατον Soph. (Deriv. unknown.)

αιμων.def: αἵμων (= δαήμων,) I. skilful in a thing, c. gen., αἵμονα θήρης Il. II. （αἷμα) bloody, Aesch., Eur.

αινετοσ.def: αἰνετός (verb. adj. of αἰνέω) praiseworthy, Arist., Anth.

αινεω.def: αἰνέω This is a Poet. and ionic Verb, while ἐπαινέω is used in attic Prose I. properly, to tell or speak of (cf. αἶνος), Aesch. II. commonly, to speak in praise of, praise, Lat. laudo, c. acc., Hom., Hdt. 2. to allow, recommend, Od.: c. inf. to recommend to do a thing, Aesch.; also c. part., αἰνεῖν ἰόντα to commend one's going, id. 3. like ἀγαπάω, to be content, acquiesce, Eur.:—c. acc. rei, to be content with, acquiesce in, γάμον Pind., etc.; θῆσσαν τράπεζαν Eur. 4. to decline courteously, Hes. III. to promise or vow, τί τινι or τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Soph., Eur.

αινη.def: αἴνη (= αἶνος) praise, fame, ἐν αἴνηι ἐών Hdt.

αινιγμα.def: αἴνιγμα (αἰνίσσομαι) a dark saying, riddle, Aesch., etc.; ἐξ αἰνιγμάτων in riddles, id.; δι’ αἰνιγμάτων Aeschin.; αἴνιγμα προβάλλειν, ξυντιθέναι to propose a riddle, Plat.; opp. to αἴνιγμα λύειν, εὑρίσκειν to solve it, Soph., etc.

αινιγμοσ.def: αἰνιγμός (= αἴνιγμα) a riddle, δι’ αἰνιγμῶν ἐρεῖν Ar.; ἐν αἰνιγμοῖσι σημαίνειν Eur.

αινιζω.def: αἰνίζω (usually dep., = αἰνέω, Hom.:—act. αἰνίζω, Anth.)

αινικτηριοσ.def: αἰνικτήριος (from αἰνίσσομαι) known from the adv. -ίως, in riddles, Aesch.

αινικτοσ.def: αἰνικτός (from αἰνίσσομαι) expressed in riddles, riddling, Soph.

αινισσομαι.def: αἰνίσσομαι (αἶνος) I. to speak in riddles, Soph., Eur.; γνωρίμως αἰνίξομαι I will speak in riddles but so as to be understood, Soph.; αἰνίσσεσθαι ἔπεα to speak riddling verses, Hdt.:—c. acc. rei, to hint a thing, intimate, shadow forth, Plat. II. as Pass. to be wrapt up in riddles, only in aor1 ἠινίχθην, perf. ᾔνιγμαι, Theogn., Plat., etc.

αινοθεν.gloss: from horror to horror, right horribly
αινοθεν.def: αἰνόθεν (αἰνός) adv. only in phrase αἰνόθεν αἰνῶς, from horror to horror, right horribly, Il.

αινολινοσ.def: αἰνόλινος (λίνον) unfortunate in life's thread, in allusion to the Parcae, Anth.

αινομοροσ.def: αἰνόμορος doomed to a sad end, Hom.

αινοπαθησ.def: αἰνοπαθής (πάσχω) suffering dire ills, Od., Anth.

αινοπαρισ.def: Αἰνόπαρις like Δύσπαρις, unlucky Paris, Eur.

αινοσ.def: αἰνός (= δεινός,) I. dread, dire, grim, terrible, Hom.; αἰνότατε Κρονίδη most dread son of Cronus, Il. II. adv. -νῶς, terribly, i. e. strangely, exceedingly, Hom., Hdt.; also αἰνά as adv., Il.; Sup. -ότατον, id.
αἶνος (cf. αἰνέω) I. = μῦθος, a tale, story, Od.; αἰνεῖν αἶνον to tell a tale, Aesch., Soph.: generally, a saying, proverb, Theocr. II. = attic ἔπαινος, praise, Hom., Trag.

αινοτοκεια.def: αἰνοτόκεια (τίκτω) unhappy in being a mother, Mosch.

αινυμαι.gloss: to take, take off, take hold of
αινυμαι.def: αἴνυμαι to take, take off, take hold of, Hom.; c. gen. partit., τυρῶν αἰνυμένους taking of the cheeses, Od.

αιξ.def: αἴξ I. a goat, Lat. caper, capra, Hom. 2. αἲξ ἄγριος the wild goat, the ibex, id. II. αἶγες, old name for waves. (Prob. not from ἀΐσσω, of which the root is ΑΙΚ.)

αιολευσ.def: Αἰολεύς an Aeolian; pl. Αἰολέες, attic Αἰολεῖς or -ῆς Hdt., Thuc.

αιολικοσ.def: Αἰολικός of or like the Aeolians, Theocr.

αιολλω.gloss: to shift rapidly to and fro
αιολλω.def: αἰόλλω (αἰόλος) to shift rapidly to and fro, Od.:—Pass. to shift colour, of grapes, Hes.

αιολοβροντησ.def: αἰολοβρόντης (βροντή) wielder of lightning, Ζεύς Pind.

αιολομητισ.def: αἰολόμητις full of various wiles, Hes., Aesch.

αιολομιτρησ.def: αἰολομίτρης (μίτρα) I. with glancing or glittering girdle (for it was plated with metal), Il. II. with variegated turban, Theocr.

αιολοπωλοσ.def: αἰολόπωλος with quick-moving steeds, Il., Theocr.

αιολοσ.def: αἰόλος (Deriv. uncertain.) (The penult. is lengthd. in the gen. Αἰόλου μεγαλήτορος, metri grat., Od.) I. quick-moving, Il.; αἰόλαι εὐλαί wriggling worms, id.; so of wasps and serpents, id. II. changeful of hue, gleaming, glancing, of arms and armour, id.; (but here also it may be explained moving with the body, manageable, Lat. habilis);— also, αἰόλα νύξ star-spangled night, Soph.; Aesch. calls smoke flushed by fire-light αἰόλη πυρὸς κάσις; αἰόλα σάρξ discoloured from disease, Soph. III. metaph., 1. changeful, shifting, varied, κάκα Aesch.; of sounds, ἰαχή Eur. 2. shifty, wily, slippery, ψεῦδος Pind. B. as prop. n., proparox. Αἴολος, ου, ὁ, lord of the winds, properly the rapid or the changeable, Od.

αιολοστομοσ.def: αἰολόστομος (στόμα) shifting in speech, of an oracle, Aesch.

αιπεινοσ.def: αἰπεινός (αἰπύς) I. high, lofty, Hom. II. metaph., 1. precipitate, hasty, Pind. 2. hard to win, difficult, Pind., Eur.

αιπολεω.def: αἰπολέω to tend goats, Theocr.: —Pass., of the flock, Aesch.

αιπολικοσ.def: αἰπολικός (αἰπόλος) of or for goatherds, Anth.

αιπολιον.def: αἰπόλιον (from αἰπόλος) I. a herd of goats, Il., etc. II. a goat-pasture, Anth.

αιπολοσ.def: αἰπόλος (αἰπόλος is for αἰγοπόλος from αἴξ, πολέω.) a goatherd, Od., etc.

αιποσ.def: αἶπος (αἰπύς) a height, a steep, Aesch.:— πρὸς αἶπος ἔρχεσθαι, metaph. of a difficult task, Eur.
αἰπός (epic for αἰπύς,) high, lofty, of cities, Il.; αἰπὰ ῥέεθρα streams falling sheer down, Il.

αιπυμητησ.def: αἰπυμήτης (μῆτις) with high thoughts, Θέμιδος αἰπυμῆτα παῖ Aesch.

αιπυνωτοσ.def: αἰπύνωτος high-backed, on a high mountain-ridge, of Dodona, Aesch.

αιπυσ.def: αἰπύς I. high and steep, lofty, of cities on heights, as Troy, Od.; of hills, Il.; βρόχος αἰπ. a noose hanging straight down, Od. II. metaph. sheer, utter, αἰπὺς ὄλεθρος Hom. (death being regarded as the plunge over a precipice); so, φόνος αἰπύς Od.; also αἰπὺς χόλος towering wrath, Il. 2. arduous, difficult, id.

αιρεσιμοσ.def: αἱρέσιμος (αἱρέω) that can be taken, Xen.

αιρεσισ.def: αἵρεσις (αἱρέω) I. a taking especially, esp. of a town, Hdt., etc.; ἡ βασιλῆος αἵρ. the taking by the king, Hdt. 2. means for taking a place, Thuc. II. （αἱρέομαι) a taking for oneself, a choosing, choice, νέμειν, προτιθέναι, προβάλλειν to give or offer choice, Hdt., attic; αἵρ. γίγνεταί τινι a choice is allowed one, Thuc.; αἵρεσιν λαμβάνειν to have choice given, Dem. 2. choice or election of magistrates, Thuc., etc. 3. a choice, deliberate plan, purpose, Plat., etc. 4. a sect, school, etc.: esp. a religious sect, such as the Sadducees and Pharisees, NTest. 5. a heresy, Eccl.

αιρετεοσ.def: αἱρετέος (verb. adj. of αἱρέω,) I. to be taken, desirable, Xen. II. αἱρετέον, one must choose, Plat.

αιρετιζω.def: αἱρετίζω (αἱρέομαι) to choose, select, Babr., NTest.

αιρετικοσ.def: αἱρετικός (αἱρέομαι) 1. able to choose, Plat. 2. heretical, NTest.

αιρετοσ.def: αἱρετός (verb. adj. of αἱρέω) I. that may be taken or conquered, Hdt.; that may be understood, Plat. II. （αἱρέομαι) to be chosen, eligible, id., Hdt., etc.; ζοῆς πονηρᾶς θάνατος αἱρετώτερος Menand. 2. chosen, elected, Plat., etc.

αιρεω.gloss: to take with the hand, grasp
αιρεω.def: αἱρέω (The forms εἷλον etc. come from the stem ἑλ-.) A. Act. to take with the hand, grasp, αἱρ. τι ἐν χερσίν, μετὰ χερσίν to take a thing in hand, Od.; αἱρ. χερσὶ δόρυ Il.; αἱρ, τινὰ χειρός to take one by the hand, id.:—part. ἑλών is sometimes used as adv., by force, Soph. 2. to take away, Hom. II. to take by force, to take a city, Il., etc.; to overpower, kill, Hom., etc.:—often of passions, etc., to seize, id., etc.:—to conquer (in a race), Il. 2. to take, catch, as in hunting, in good sense, to win over, Xen., etc.:—c. part. to catch or detect one doing a thing, Soph. 3. to win, gain, κῦδος Il.; of the public games, Simon., etc. 4. as attic law-term, to convict a person of a thing, τινά τινος Ar., etc.: also c. part., αἱρεῖν τινὰ κλέπτοντα to convict of theft, id.; ἡιρῆσθαι κλοπεύς (sc. ὤν) Soph.; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ὃ ἐμὲ αἱρήσει Plat. 5. ὁ λόγος αἱρέει, Lat. ratio evincit, reason proves, Hdt. B. Mid. to take for oneself, Hom., etc.; αἱρ. δόρπον, δεῖπνον to take one's supper, id.:—so in most senses of Act. II. to choose, id.: to take in preference, prefer one thing to another, τι πρό τινος Hdt.; τι ἀντί τινος Xen.; also, τί τινος Soph.; τι μᾶλλον ἢ.., or μᾶλλόν τινος attic:—c. inf. to prefer to do, Hdt., etc. 2. αἱρεῖσθαι τά τινος or τινά to take another's part, join his party, id., etc. 3. to choose by vote, elect to an office, Plat., etc. C. Pass. to be taken, Hdt.; but ἁλίσκομαι is used in attic for Pass. II. as Pass. to the mid. sense, to be chosen, in perf. ᾕρημαι (which is also mid.), Hdt., attic

αιροσ.def: ἄιρος Od. 18. 73 Ἶρος ἄϊρος, Irus unhappy Irus, — a play upon his name, like δῶρα ἄδωρα.

αιρω.gloss: to take up, raise, lift up
αιρω.def: αἴρω (epic and poet. ἀείρω q.v.) (distinguish ἀρῶ from ᾱ̓ρῶ, contr. of ἀερῶ.) A. Act. I. to take up, raise, lift up, Il., etc.; αἴρειν βῆμα to step, walk, Eur.; αἴρ. σημεῖον to hoist a signal, Xen.:—Pass. to mount up, ascend, id. 2. often of armies and ships, αἴρ. τὰς ναῦς to get the fleet under sail, Thuc.:—also intr. to get under way, start, set out, ἆραι τῶι στρατῶι id.;—so in Mid. and Pass., Hdt., etc. II. to bear, sustain, μόρον Aesch.; ἆθλον Soph. III. to raise up, exalt, Aesch.:—of passion, to exalt, excite, ὑψοῦ αἴρειν θυμόν to grow excited, Soph.; αἴρειν θάρσος to pluck up courage, Eur., etc.: Pass., οὐκ ἤρθη νοῦν ἐς ἀτασθαλίην Simon. 2. to raise by words, to extol, exaggerate, Eur., Dem. IV. to lift and take away, to remove, Aesch., etc.:—to take off, kill, NTest. B. Mid., with perf. pass. ἦρμαι, to take up for oneself: to carry off, win, gain, κλέος Il.; ἀέθλια (of horses) id.; κῦδος Hom.:—hence simply to receive, get, ἕλκος ἀρέσθαι Il.; also, δειλίαν ἀρεῖ wilt incur a charge of cowardice, Soph. II. to take upon oneself, undergo, carry, bear, Il., etc. 2. to undertake, begin, πόλεμον Thuc., etc.; φυγὴν ἀρέσθαι, Lat. fugam capere, Aesch. III. to raise up, σωτῆρά τινι Soph.: of sound, αἴρεσθαι φωνήν to raise, lift up one's voice, Ar.

αισα.def: Αἶσα I. like Μοῖρα, the goddess of destiny, Lat. Parca, Il. II. as appellat. 1. the decree, dispensation of a god, Διὸς αἴσηι, ὑπὲρ Διὸς αἶσαν id.; θεοῦ αἶσα Eur.:— κατ’ αἶσαν fitly, duly, Il., etc.; κατ’ αἶσαν, οὐδ’ ὑπὲρ αἶσαν id. 2. one's appointed lot, destiny, Hom., etc. 3. one's share in a thing, Od.; ληΐδος αἶσα id., etc.

αισθανομαι.gloss: to perceive, apprehend by the senses, to see, hear, feel
αισθανομαι.def: αἰσθάνομαι (ἀΐω) 1. to perceive, apprehend by the senses, to see, hear, feel, Hdt., attic 2. to perceive by the mind, understand, hear, learn, often in attic: absol., αἰσθάνει, Lat. tenes, you are right, Eur.:—Construct., c. gen. to have perception of, τῶν κακῶν id., etc.; also c. acc., Soph., etc.:—dependent clauses are mostly added in part. agreeing with subject, αἰσθάνομαι κάμνων Thuc.; or agreeing with object, τυράννους ἐκπεσόντας ἠισθόμην Aesch.

αισθημα.def: αἴσθημα (from αἰσθάνομαι) perception of a thing, κακῶν Eur.

αισθησισ.def: αἴσθησις (αἰσθάνομαι) I. perception by the senses, αἴσθ. πημάτων perception, sense of calamities, Eur.— The phrase αἴσθησιν ἔχειν is used 1. of persons, αἴσθ. ἔχειν τινός, αἰσθάνεσθαί τινος or τι, to have a perception of a thing, perceive it, Plat. 2. of things, to give a perception, i. e. to become perceptible, serving as a Pass. to αἰσθάνομαι, Thuc.; more freq. αἴσθησιν παρέχειν id., Xen. II. one of the senses, Plat.: and in pl. the senses, id. III. a perception, αἰσθήσεις θεῶν visions of the gods, id. 2. in hunting, the scent, Xen.

αισθητηριον.def: αἰσθητήριον (αἰσθάνομαι) an organ of sense, Arist., etc.; τὰ αἰσθ. the senses, faculties, NTest.

αισθητικοσ.def: αἰσθητικός (αἰσθάνομαι) I. of or for perception by the senses, perceptive, Plat., etc.:—adv. αἰσθητικῶς ἔχειν to be quick of perception, Arist. II. of things, perceptible, Plut.

αισθητοσ.def: αἰσθητός (verb. adj. of αἰσθάνομαι,) perceptible by the senses, Plat.

αισθω.def: ἀίσθω (ἄημι) to breathe out, like ἀποπνέω, θυμὸν ἄϊσθε he was giving up the ghost, Il.

αισιμια.def: αἰσιμία (from αἴσιμος) happiness, αἰσιμίαις πλούτου Aesch.

αισιμοσ.def: αἴσιμος (αἶσα) I. Lat. fatalis, appointed by the will of the gods, destined, αἴσιμον ἦμαρ the fatal day, day of death, Il., etc.; αἴσιμόν ἐστι it is fated, id. II. agreeable to fate, meet, right, αἴσιμα εἰπεῖν, αἴσιμα εἰδώς Od.

αισιοσ.def: αἴσιος (αἶσα) boding well, auspicious, Il., etc.:—adv. -ίως, Eur.

αισσω.gloss: to move with a quick shooting motion, to shoot, dart, glance
αισσω.def: ἀίσσω (Root ΑΙΚ) I. to move with a quick shooting motion, to shoot, dart, glance, Lat. impetu ferri, Il., etc.; so in aor. mid., ἀΐξασθαι, and aor. pass. ἀϊχθῆναι id.; κόμη δι’ αὔρας ἀίσσεται floats on the breeze, Soph. 2. to turn eagerly, be eager, εἴς τι Eur. II. trans. to put in motion, Eur.

αιστοσ.def: ἄιστος (α privat.., ⁎εἴδω) I. not to be seen, unseen. II. act. unconscious of, c. gen., Eur.

αιστοω.def: ἀιστόω (from ἄιστος) to make unseen, to annihilate, Hom., etc.

αιστωρ.def: ἀίστωρ (α privat.., εἰδέναι) unknowing, unconscious, Plat.; τινός of a thing, Eur.

αισυμναω.def: αἰσυμνάω to rule over, c. gen., Eur. (Deriv. uncertain.)

αισυμνητησ.def: αἰσυμνήτης (αἰσυμνάω) I. a regulator of games, a judge or umpire, Od.: a president, manager, Theocr. II. an elective prince, Arist.

αισχοσ.def: αἶσχος I. shame, disgrace, Hom., etc.:—in pl. shameful deeds, Od. II. ugliness or deformity, of mind or body, Plat., Xen.

αισχροκερδησ.def: αἰσχροκερδής (κέρδος) sordidly greedy of gain, Hdt., Eur.—adv. -δῶς, NTest.

αισχρολογια.def: αἰσχρολογία (from αἰσχρολογέω) foul language, abuse, Xen.

αισχροσ.def: αἰσχρός (αἶσχος) I. causing shame, abusive, ἔπεα Il.; so in adv., αἰσχρῶς ἐνένισπε id. II. opp. to καλός: 1. of outward appearance, ugly, ill-favoured, of Thersites, id. 2. in moral sense, shameful, disgraceful, base, infamous, Hdt., etc.; αἰσχρόν [ἐστι], c. inf., Il.: —τὸ αἰσχρόν, as Subst., dishonour, disgrace, Soph., etc.; τὸ καλὸν καὶ τὸ αἰσχρόν, Lat. honestum et turpe, virtue and vice, Arist.:—adv. shamefully, Sup. αἴσχιστα, Trag. 3. awkward, Xen. III. instead of the regul. comp. and Sup. αἰσχρότερος, -ότατος, the forms αἰσχίων [ῑ], αἴσχιστος (formed from αἶσχος) are used.

αισχυνη.def: αἰσχύνη (αἶσχος) I. shame done one, disgrace, dishonour, Hdt., attic 2. a disgrace, of a person, Aesch. II. shame for an ill deed, personified in Aesch. 2. generally, like αἰδώς, shame, the sense of shame, Soph., etc.

αισχυντεοσ.def: αἰσχυντέος (verb. adj. of αἰσχύνομαι) one must be ashamed, Xen.

αισχυνω.def: αἰσχύνω I. to make ugly, disfigure, mar, πρόσωπον, κόμην Il. 2. in moral sense, to dishonour, tarnish, γένος πατέρων id., etc. 3. to dishonour a woman, Aesch., etc. B. Pass. to be dishonoured, νέκυς ᾐσχυμμένος, of Patroclus, Il. II. to be ashamed, feel shame, absol., Od., Hdt., etc. 2. to be ashamed at a thing, c. acc. rei, Od., etc.; also c. dat. rei, Ar., etc.; and with Preps., αἰσχ. ἐπί τινι Xen.; ἔν τινι Thuc.; ὑπέρ τινος Dem.:—c. part to be ashamed at doing a thing, Aesch., Soph., etc.:—but c. inf. to be ashamed to do a thing, Hdt., etc. 3. c. acc. pers. to feel shame before one, Eur., etc.

αιτασ.def: ἀίτας (ἀΐω) doric word for a beloved youth, favourite, Theocr.: generally a lover, Anth.

αιτεω.def: αἰτέω I. to ask, beg, Od., etc. 2. c. acc. rei, to ask for, crave, demand, Hom., etc.; ὁδὸν αἰτ. to beg one's departure, i. e. ask leave to depart, Od.:—c. acc. pers. et rei, to ask a person for a thing, Hom., etc.; δίκας αἰτ. τινὰ φόνου to demand satisfaction from one for murder, Hdt. 3. c. acc. pers. et inf. to ask one to do, Od., etc. II. Mid. to ask for oneself, to claim, Aesch., etc.:—but often used just like Act. III. Pass.: 1. of persons, to have a thing begged of one, Hdt., Thuc. 2. of things, to be asked, τὸ αἰτεόμενον Hdt., etc.

αιτημα.def: αἴτημα (from αἰτέω) a request, demand, Plat., NTest.

αιτητεον.def: αἰτητέον (verb. adj. of αἰτέω) one must ask, Xen.

αιτητικοσ.def: αἰτητικός (αἰτέω) fond of asking, c. gen., Arist.

αιτητοσ.def: αἰτητός (verb. adj. of αἰτέω) asked for, Soph.

αιτια.def: αἰτία (αἰτέω) I. a charge, accusation, Lat. crimen, and then the guilt or fault implied in such accusation, Pind., Hdt.:—Phrases: αἰτίαν ἔχειν to be accused, τινός of a thing, id., etc.;—reversely, αἰτία ἔχει με id.; ἐν αἰτίαι εἶναι or γίγνεσθαι Xen., etc.; αἰτίαν ὑπέχειν to lie under a charge, Plat.; αἰτίαν φέρεσθαι Thuc.; αἰτίαις ἐνέχεσθαι Plat.:—opp. to these are ἐν αἰτίαι ἔχειν or δι’ αἰτίας to hold one guilty, accuse, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἐν αἰτίαι βάλλειν Soph.; αἰτίαν νέμειν τινί id., etc. 2. in good sense, εἰ εὖ πράξαιμεν, αἰτία θεοῦ the credit is his, Aesch.; οἳ ἔχουσι ταύτην τὴν αἰτίαν who have this as their characteristic, Plat. 3. expostulation, μὴ ἐπ’ ἔχθραι τὸ πλέον ἢ αἰτίαι Thuc. II. a cause, Lat. causa, Plat., etc.; dat. αἰτίαι, like Lat. causa, for the sake of, κοινοῦ ἀγαθοῦ Thuc. III. an occasion, opportunity, αἰτίαν παρέχειν Luc. IV. the head under which a thing comes, Dem.

αιτιαμα.def: αἰτίαμα (from αἰτιάομαι) a charge, guilt imputed, λαβεῖν ἐπ’ αἰτιάματί τινα Aesch.; τοιοῖσδε ἐπ’ αἰτιάμασιν on such charges, id.

αιτιαομαι.def: αἰτιάομαι (αἰτία) I. to charge, accuse, censure, blame, c. acc. pers., τάχα κεν καὶ ἀναίτιον αἰτιόωιτο Il.; αἰτ. τινά τινος to accuse of a thing, Hdt., etc.;—c. inf., αἰτ. τινα ποιεῖν τι to accuse one of doing, id.:—in this signf., certain tenses are used in pass. sense, to be accused, aor1 ἠιτιάθην Thuc., Xen.; perf. ἠιτίαμαι Thuc. 2. c. acc. rei, to lay to one's charge, impute, τοῦτο αἰτ. Xen.; ταῦτα Dem.; c. dupl. acc., τί ταῦτα τοὺς Λάκωνας αἰτιώμεθα; Ar. II. to allege as the cause, αἰτ. τινα αἴτιον Plat.; φωνάς τε καὶ ἄλλα μυρία αἰτ. id.; τῆς ἱερᾶς χώρας ἠιτιᾶτο εἶναι he alleged that it was part of the sacred territory, Dem.

αιτιατεον.def: αἰτιατέον (verb. adj. of αἰτιάομαι) I. one must accuse, Xen. II. one must allege as the cause, Plat.

αιτιζω.def: αἰτίζω (epic form of αἰτέω) 1. to ask, beg, c. acc. rei, σῖτον Od. 2. c. acc. pers. to beg of, μνηστῆρας id. 3. absol., αἰτίζων βόσκειν ἣν γαστέρα to fill one's belly by begging, id.

αιτιολογικοσ.def: αἰτιολογικός inquiring into causes: τὸ αἰτιολογικόν, investigation of causes, Strab.

αιτιοσ.def: αἴτιος (αἰτέω) I. to blame, blameworthy, culpable, Il., etc.: comp., αἰτιώτερος more culpable, Thuc.; Sup., τοὺς αἰτιωτάτους the most guilty, Hdt.; τινος for a thing, id. 2. as Subst., αἴτιος, ὁ, the accused, culprit, Lat. reus, Aesch., etc.; οἱ αἴτιοι τοῦ πατρός they who have sinned against my father, id.:—c. gen. rei, οἱ αἴτ. τοῦ φόνου those guilty of murder, id. II. being the cause, responsible for, c. gen. rei, Hdt., etc.; c. inf., Soph.: Sup., αἰτιώτατος ναυμαχῆσαι mainly instrumental in causing the seafight, Thuc. 2. αἴτιον, τό, a cause, Plat., etc.

αιτναιοσ.def: Αἰτναῖος 1. of or belonging to Etna (Αἴτνη), Pind., Aesch., etc. 2. metaph. like Etna, enormous, Eur.; some explain it so when used of horses, but better Etnean, i. e. Sicilian (for the Sicilian horses were famous), Soph.

αιφνιδιοσ.def: αἰφνίδιος (ἄφνω) unforeseen, sudden, Aesch., Thuc.:—adv. -ίως, Iδ͂Thuc.; also -ιον Plut.

αιχμαζω.def: αἰχμάζω (αἰχμή) I. to throw the spear, Il.; ἔνδον αἰχμάζειν to play the warrior at home, Aesch. II. to arm with the spear, ἤιχμασας χέρα Soph.

αιχμαλωσια.def: αἰχμαλωσία (αἰχμάλωτος) captivity: a body of captives, Diod., NTest.

αιχμαλωτευω.def: αἰχμαλωτεύω (from αἰχμάλωτος) to take prisoner, NTest.

αιχμαλωτικοσ.def: αἰχμαλωτικός (from αἰχμάλωτος) of or for a prisoner, Eur.

αιχμαλωτοσ.gloss: taken by the spear, captive to one's spear, taken prisoner
αιχμαλωτοσ.def: αἰχμάλωτος I. taken by the spear, captive to one's spear, taken prisoner, Hdt., etc.; αἰχμάλωτον λαμβάνειν, ἄγειν to take prisoner, Xen.; αἰχμ. γίγνεσθαι to be taken, id.; τὰ αἰχμάλωτα booty, id. II. = αἰχμαλωτικός, δουλοσύνη αἰχμ. such as awaits a captive, Hdt., Aesch.

αιχμη.def: αἰχμή (ἀκή I, or ἀΐσσω) I. the point of a spear, Lat. cuspis, Il., etc. II. a spear, id., etc.; τοξουλκὸς αἰχμή, of an arrow, Aesch. 2. a body of spearmen, Pind., Eur.; cf. ἀσπίς. 3. war, battle, κακῶς ἡ αἰχμὴ ἐστήκεε the war went ill, Hdt. III. warlike spirit, mettle, Pind.; so, in Aesch., γυναικὸς or γυναικεία αἰχμά seems to be a woman's spirit. IV. a sceptre, id.

αιχμηεισ.def: αἰχμήεις (from αἰχμή) armed with the spear, Aesch.

αιχμητησ.def: αἰχμητής (αἰχμή) I. a spearman, Hom. II. In Pind. as adj., 1. pointed, κεραυνός. 2. warlike, θυμός.

αιχμοφοροσ.gloss: one who trails a pike, a spearman
αιχμοφοροσ.def: αἰχμοφόρος (φέρω) one who trails a pike, a spearman, Hdt.:—esp. like δορυφόρος, of body-guards, id.

αιψα.gloss: quick, with speed, on a sudden
αιψα.def: αἶψα quick, with speed, on a sudden, Hom.

αιψηροσ.def: αἰψηρός (αἶψα) quick, speedy, in haste, Hom.

αιω.def: ἀίω 1. to perceive by the ear, to hear, c. acc. rei, Il.; c. gen., Trag.:—also to perceive by the eye, to see, Od. 2. to listen to, give ear to, δίκης Hes.: to obey, Aesch.; cf. ἐπαΐω. (Hom. has αιω; but ᾱιεις, ᾱιων Soph.)
ἀίω (= ἄημι) to breathe, only in imperf., ἐπεὶ φίλον ἄϊον ἦτορ when I was breathing out my life, Il.

αιων.def: αἰών (poet.: apocop. acc. αἰῶ) (properly αἰϝών, aevum, v. αἰεί）) a period of existence: 1. one's life-time, life, Hom. and attic Poets. 2. an age, generation, Aesch.; ὁ μέλλων αἰών posterity, Dem. 3. a long space of time, an age, ἀπ’ αἰῶνος of old, for ages, Hes., NTest.; τὸν δι’ αἰῶνος χρόνον for ever, Aesch.; ἅπαντα τὸν αἰ. Lycurg. 4. a definite space of time, an era, epoch, age, period, ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος this present world, opp. to ὁ μέλλων, NTest.:—hence its usage in pl., εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας for ever, id.

αιωνιοσ.def: αἰώνιος lasting for an age (αἰών 3), Plat.: ever-lasting, eternal, id.

αιωρα.def: αἰώρα (ἀείρω) I. a machine for suspending bodies: a noose for hanging, a halter, Soph. in the form ἐώρα). II. suspension in the air, oscillation, plat.

αιωρεω.def: αἰωρέω (ἀείρω) I. to lift up, raise, ὑγρὸν νῶτον αἰωρεῖ, of the eagle raising his feathers, Pind.; τοὺς ὄφεις ὑπὲρ τῆς κεφαλῆς αἰωρῶν Dem.:—cf. ἐωρέω. 2. to hang, Plut., Luc. II. Pass. to be hung, hang, Hdt.; αἰωρουμένων τῶν ὀστῶν being raised, lifted, Plat.; αἷμα ἠιωρεῖτο spouted up, Bion. 2. to hang suspended, float in air, hover, oscillate, Soph., Plat. 3. metaph. to be in suspense, Thuc.; αἰωρεῖσθαι ἐν ἄλλοις to depend upon others, Plat.; αἰωρηθεὶς ὑπὲρ μεγάλων playing for a high stake, Hdt.

αιωρημα.gloss: that which is hung up: a hanging cord, a halter
αιωρημα.def: αἰώρημα (from αἰωρέω) that which is hung up: a hanging cord, a halter, Eur.

αιωρητοσ.def: αἰωρητός (verb. adj. of αἰωρέω) a hovering, Anth.

ακαδημεια.def: Ἀκαδήμεια the Academy, a gymnasium near Athens, where Plato taught: hence Platonic philosophers were called Ἀκαδημικοί, Academics.

ακαθαρτοσ.def: ἀκάθαρτος (καθαίρω) I. uncleansed, unclean, impure, Plat.:—adv., ἀκαθάρτως ἔχειν id. II. of things, not purged away, Soph.

ακαιρια.def: ἀκαιρία (ἄκαιρος) 1. unfitness of times: unseasonableness, Plat. 2. want of opportunity, τὴν ἀκαιρίαν τὴν ἐκείνου καιρὸν ὑμέτερον νομίσαντες Dem.

ακαιροσ.def: ἄκαιρος I. ill-timed, unseasonable, inopportune, ἐς ἄκαιρα πονεῖν, Lat. operam perdere, Theogn.; οὐκ ἄκαιρα λέγειν Aesch.; ἄκ. προθυμία Thuc.:—adv. -ρως, Aesch., etc.; neut. pl. as adv., Eur. II. of persons, importunate, Lat. molestus, Theophr.

ακακητα.def: ἀκάκητα (epic form of ἄκακος,) guileless, gracious, epith. of Hermes, Hom., Hes.

ακακοσ.def: ἄκακος 1. unknowing of ill, guileless, Aesch., Plat. 2. innocent, simple, Dem.:—adv. -κως, id.

ακαλαρρειτησ.def: ἀκαλαρρείτης (ἀκαλός, ῥέω) soft-flowing, of Ocean, Hom.

ακαληφη.def: ἀκαλήφη (Deriv. unknown.) a nettle, Lat. urtica, Ar.

ακαμαντολογχησ.def: ἀκαμαντολόγχης (λόγχη) unwearied at the spear, Pind.

ακαμαντοπουσ.def: ἀκαμαντόπους untiring of foot, unwearied, Pind.

ακαματοσ.def: ἀκάματος without sense of toil: hence — untiring, unresting, Hom.; ἀκ. γῆ earth that never rests from tillage, Soph.:—neut. ἀκάματα, as adv., id. (ἀκάματος, Soph.; but ᾱ̓κάματος in dactylics.)

ακαμπτοσ.gloss: unbent, that will not bend, rigid
ακαμπτοσ.def: ἄκαμπτος (κάμπτω) unbent, that will not bend, rigid, Plat.:—metaph. unbending, unflinching, inexorable, Pind.; ψυχὰν ἄκαμπτος id.; ἀκάμπτωι μένει Aesch.; ἄκαμπτον Plut.

ακανθα.def: ἄκανθα (ἀκή I) 1. a thorn, prickle, Theocr., etc. 2. a prickly plant, thistle; in pl. thistledown, Od.:—also a kind of acacia, Hdt. 3. the backbone or spine of animals, id., etc. 4. metaph., ἄκανθαι, thorny questions, Luc.

ακανθινοσ.def: ἀκάνθινος (ἄκανθα) I. of thorns, NTest. II. of acacia wood, Hdt.

ακανθισ.def: ἀκανθίς I. a bird, the goldfinch, or the linnet, Arist., Theocr. II. as fem. adj. prickly, Anth.

ακανθοβατησ.def: ἀκανθοβάτης (βαίνω) walking among thorns, nickname of grammarians, Anth.:—fem. ἀκανθοβάτις, ιδος, Anth.

ακανθολογοσ.def: ἀκανθολόγος (λέγω) gathering thorns, nickname of quibblers, Anth.

ακανθοσ.def: ἄκανθος (ἀκή) Lat. acanthus, brank-ursine, a plant imitated in Corinthian capitals, Theocr.

ακανθωδησ.def: ἀκανθώδης (εἶδος) 1. full of thorns, thorny, Hdt. 2. metaph., λόγοι ἀκ. thorny arguments, Luc.

ακαπνοσ.def: ἄκαπνος without smoke, θυσία ἄκαπνος an offering but no burnt offering, Luc.; a poem is called Καλλιόπης ἄκαπνον θύος Anth.

ακαρησ.gloss: too short to be cut, very short
ακαρησ.def: ἀκαρής (κείρω) of hair, too short to be cut, very short: mostly in neut. ἀκαρές, 1. of Time, a moment, ἐν ἀκαρεῖ χρόνου Ar.; ἀκαρῆ διαλιπὼν (sc. χρόνον) having waited a moment, id.; ἀκαρὲς ὥρας a moment, Plut. 2. the acc. ἀκαρῆ is used adverbially without reference to Time, οὐκ ἀκαρῆ or οὐδ’ ἀκαρῆ not a bit, Ar.

ακαρπιστοσ.gloss: where nothing is to be reaped, unfruitful
ακαρπιστοσ.def: ἀκάρπιστος (καρπίζω) where nothing is to be reaped, unfruitful, of the sea, like ἀτρύγετος, Eur.

ακαρποσ.def: ἄκαρπος I. without fruit, barren, Eur. 2. metaph. fruitless, unprofitable, id.:—adv. -πως, Soph. II. act. making barren, blasting, Aesch.

ακαρπωτοσ.def: ἀκάρπωτος (καρπόω) not made fruitful, without fruit: of an oracle, fruitless, unfulfilled, Aesch.; νίκας ἀκάρπωτον χάριν because of victory which yielded no fruit, Soph.

ακαταβλητοσ.def: ἀκατάβλητος (καταβάλλω) not to be overthrown, irrefragable, Ar.

ακαταγνωστοσ.def: ἀκατάγνωστος (καταγιγνώσκω) not to be condemned, NTest.

ακαταλλακτοσ.def: ἀκατάλλακτος (καταλλάσσω) irreconcileable:— adv. -τως, ἀκ. πολεμεῖν Dem.

ακαταπαυστοσ.def: ἀκατάπαυστος (καταπαύομαι) that cannot cease from τινός NTest.

ακατασχετοσ.def: ἀκατάσχετος (κατέχω) not to be checked:— adv. -τως, Plut.

ακαταφρονητοσ.def: ἀκαταφρόνητος (καταφρονέω) not to be despised, important, Lat. haud spernendus, Xen., Plut., etc.

ακατιον.def: ἀκάτιον (Dim. of ἄκατος) I. a light boat, Thuc., etc. II. a small sail, perh. a top-sail, Xen., Luc.

ακατοσ.def: ἄκατος 1. a light vessel, Lat. actuaria, Hdt., etc.; cf. ἀκάτιον. 2. generally, a ship, Eur.

ακαχιζω.def: ἀκαχίζω (ἀχέω) to trouble, grieve, τινά Od.:—Pass., μὴ λίην ἀκαχίζεο θυμῶι be not troubled in mind, Il.; μήτι θανὼν ἀκαχίζευ be not grieved at death, Od.

ακαχμενοσ.def: ἀκαχμένος a part. (as if from a Verb ⁎ἄκω, v. ἀκή Ι), sharpened, of axes and swords, Hom.

ακεντητοσ.def: ἀκέντητος (κεντέω) needing no goad or spur, Pind.

ακεομαι.def: ἀκέομαι (ἄκος) (The form ἀκέο is for ἀκέεο.) I. trans. to heal, cure, ἕλκος ἄκεσσαι heal the sore, Il.; or of part healed, βλέφαρον ἀκέσαιο Eur.; also to heal a person, Il. 2. to stanch, quench, δίψαν id. 3. generally, to mend, repair, νῆας Od.; applied to a tailor or cobbler, like Lat. resarcire, Luc. 4. metaph. to repair, make amends for, ἁμαρτάδα Hdt.; κακόν Soph.:—absol. to make amends, ἀλλ’ ἀκεώμεθα, ἀλλ’ ἀκέσασθε Hom.

ακεραιοσ.def: ἀκέραιος (= the poetic ἀκήρατος) I. unmixed, pure in blood, Eur. II. entire, unharmed, unravaged, of cities or countries, Hdt., Thuc.; ἀκ. δύναμις an army in full force, id.; ἀκ. λέχος inviolate, Eur.; of persons, uncontaminated, guileless, id.: c. gen., ἀκέραιος κακῶν ἠθῶν uncontaminated by bad habits, Plat.

ακερδεια.def: ἀκέρδεια (from ἀκερδής) want of gain, loss, Pind.

ακερδησ.def: ἀκερδής (κέρδος) I. without gain, bringing loss, Soph., Plat. II. not greedy of gain, Plut.

ακερσεκομησ.def: ἀκερσεκόμης (cf. ἀκειρεκόμης) (κείρω, κόμη) with unshorn hair (the Greek youths wore their hair long till they reached manhood), epith. of Phoebus, Il., etc.

ακεσμα.def: ἄκεσμα (ἀκέομαι) a remedy, cure, Pind., Aesch.

ακεστηρ.def: ἀκεστήρ (ἀκέομαι) a healer: metaph. as adj., ἀκ. χαλινός the rein that tames the steed, Soph.

ακεστησ.def: ἀκεστής (= ἀκεστήρ) ἀκεσταὶ ἱματίων ῥαγέντων menders of torn clothes, Xen.

ακεστοσ.def: ἀκεστός (verb. adj. of ἀκέομαι) curable:— metaph., easily revived, Il.

ακεσφοροσ.def: ἀκεσφόρος (ἄκος, φέρω) bringing a cure, healing, Eur.

ακεφαλοσ.def: ἀκέφαλος (κεφαλή) 1. without head, Hdt. 2. without beginning, λόγος Plat.

ακεων.def: ἀκέων (v. ἀκή II) a participial form, used as adv. like ἀκήν, softly, silently, Hom.; also dual ἀκέοντε Od. —Though ἀκέουσα occurs in Hom., yet ἀκέων stands with fem., Ἀθηναίη ἀκέων ἦν Il.; and though he has dual ἀκέοντε, yet ἀκέων occurs with pl. Verbs.

ακη.def: ἀκή a Subst. cited in two senses, I. a point, (whence ἀκίς, ἄκων, ἀκόνη, ἀκαχμένος, ἀκωκή, αἰχμή; cf. Lat. acus, acuo, acies). II. silence, calm, (whence ἀκήν, ἀκέων, ἀκασκαῖος, ἦκα): a lulling, healing (whence ἀκέομαι).

ακηδεστοσ.def: ἀκήδεστος (κηδέω) uncared for, unburied, Il.: adv., -τως, without due rites of burial, or (perh.) without care for others, recklessly, remorselessly, id.

ακηδεω.gloss: to take no care for, no heed of
ακηδεω.def: ἀκηδέω (ἀκηδής) to take no care for, no heed of, c. gen., Il., Aesch.

ακηδησ.def: ἀκηδής (κῆδος) I. pass. uncared for, unburied, Hom. II. act. without care or sorrow, careless, heedless, id.

ακηλητοσ.gloss: to be won by no charms, proof against enchantment, inexorable
ακηλητοσ.def: ἀκήλητος (κηλέω) to be won by no charms, proof against enchantment, inexorable, Od., Soph.

ακημα.def: ἄκημα (= ἄκεσμα) a cure, relief, ὀδυνάων for pains, Il.

ακηρασιοσ.def: ἀκηράσιος (epic form of ἀκήρατος) I. unmixed, οἶνος Od. II. untouched, Lat. integer, ἀκ. λειμῶνες meadows not yet grazed or mown, Hhymn.; ἄνθος ἀκ. fresh, Anth.

ακηρατοσ.def: ἀκήρατος (κεράννυμι) I. unmixed, uncontaminated, undefiled, ὕδωρ Il.; ποτόν Aesch.; ὄμβρος Soph.; ἀκ. χρυσός pure gold, Hdt. II. metaph., 1. of things, untouched, unhurt, undamaged, Lat. integer, Hom.; ἀκ. κόμη unshorn hair, Eur.; ἀκ. λειμών an unmown meadow, id., etc. 2. of persons, undefiled, id.; c. dat., ἀκήρατος ἄλγεσι untouched by woes, id.; c. gen., ἀκ. κακῶν without taint of ill, id.

ακηριοσ.def: ἀκήριος A. unharmed by the Κῆρες, unharmed, Od. II. act. unharming, harmless, Hhymn., Hes. B. （κῆρ) without heart, i. e., I. lifeless, Il. II. heartless, spiritless, id.

ακηρυκτει.gloss: without needing a flag of truce
ακηρυκτει.def: ἀκηρυκτεί (from ἀκήρυκτος) without needing a flag of truce, Thuc.

ακηρυκτοσ.def: ἀκήρυκτος (κηρύσσω) I. unannounced, unproclaimed, ἀκ. πόλεμος a sudden war, Hdt.; but also a war in which no herald was admitted, implacable, Xen., Dem.:—adv. -τως, without needing a flag of truce, Thuc. II. not proclaimed by heralds, inglorious, Eur. III. with no tidings, not heard of, Soph.

ακιβδηλοσ.def: ἀκίβδηλος 1. unadulterated, genuine, Plat., Luc. 2. metaph. of men, guileless, honest, Hdt.

ακιδνοσ.def: ἀκιδνός (Deriv. unknown.) weak, feeble, faint, Hom. always in the comp., ἀκιδνότερος Od.

ακινακησ.def: ἀκινάκης Persian word, a short straight sword, Hdt., who declines it -εος, -εϊ, -εα; but Xen. has ἀκινάκην, ἀκινάκας as acc. sg. and pl.

ακινδυνοσ.def: ἀκίνδυνος I. without danger, free from danger, Eur., Thuc., etc. II. adv. -νως, Eur., etc.: comp., ἀκινδυνότερον with less danger, Plat.; Sup., ἀκινδυνότατα most free from danger, Xen.

ακινητοσ.def: ἀκίνητος (κινέω) I. unmoved, motionless, of Delos, Orac. ap. Hdt.; ἐξ ἀκινήτου ποδός without stirring a step, Soph. 2. idle, sluggish, Ar. 3. unmoved, unaltered, of laws, Thuc., etc. II. immovable, hard to move, Plat., Luc.:—adv., ἀκινήτως ἔχειν to be immovable, Plat., etc. 2. not to be stirred or touched, inviolate, Lat. non movendus, τάφος Hdt.: proverb. of sacred things, κινεῖν τὰ ἀκίνητα id.; also τἀκίνητα φράσαι Soph. 3. of persons, not to be shaken, steadfast, stubborn, id.

ακιοσ.def: ἄκιος (κίς) not worm-eaten: Sup. ἀκιώτατος Hes.

ακισ.def: ἀκίς (ἀκή I) 1. a point, the barb of an arrow or hook, Plut., Anth.:—an arrow, dart, Ar. 2. metaph., πόθων ἀκίδες the stings of desire, Anth.

ακιχητοσ.def: ἀκίχητος (κιχάνω) I. not to be reached, unattainable, Il. II. of persons, not to be reached by prayer, inexorable, Aesch.

ακκιζομαι.def: ἀκκίζομαι (ἀκκώ) to affect indifference or coyness, dissemble, Plat.

ακκω.def: ἀκκώ (Deriv. unknown.) a bugbear or a silly woman.

ακλαυστοσ.def: ἄκλαυστος unlamented, Hom.: (κλαίω): I. pass. unwept, φίλων by friends, Soph.; ἄκλαυτα τέκνα, i. e. children not liable to death, Eur. II. act. not weeping, tearless, Od. 2. Soph. = χαίρων, with impunity.

ακλεησ.def: ἀκλεής (κλέος) without fame, inglorious, unsung, Hom., etc. adv. ἀκλεῶς, Hdt., epic ἀκλειῶς, Il., etc.: also neut. ἀκλεές as adv., id.

ακλειστοσ.def: ἄκλειστος (κλείω) not closed or fastened, Eur., Thuc.

ακληροσ.def: ἄκληρος I. without lot or portion, poor, needy, Od., Xen., etc.: c. gen. without lot or share in a thing, Aesch., etc. II. unallotted, without an owner, Eur.

ακληρωτοσ.def: ἀκλήρωτος (κληρόω) without lot or portion in a thing, c. gen., Pind.

ακλινησ.def: ἀκλινής (κλίνω) bending to neither side, unswerving, Plat.: steadfast, regular, Anth., etc.:— adv. -νῶς, ionic -νέως, id.

ακλυστοσ.def: ἄκλυστος (κλύζω) unwashed by waves, Plut., etc.; as fem., Αὖλιν ἀκλύσταν Eur.

ακμαζω.gloss: to be in full bloom, be at one's prime
ακμαζω.def: ἀκμάζω (ἀκμή) to be in full bloom, be at one's prime or perfection, I. of persons, cities and states, Hdt., etc. 2. c. dat. to flourish or abound in a thing, πλούτωι id.; παρασκευῆι Thuc. 3. c. inf. to be strong enough to do, Xen. II. of things, ἀκμάζει ὁ πόλεμος, ἡ νόσος the war, the plague is at its height, Thuc.; ἀκμάζον θέρος mid-summer, id.; of corn, to be just ripe, id. 2. impers. ἀκμάζει, c. inf., it is high time to do, Aesch.

ακμαιοσ.gloss: in full bloom, at the prime, blooming, vigorous
ακμαιοσ.def: ἀκμαῖος (ἀκμή) I. in full bloom, at the prime, blooming, vigorous, Aesch.; ἀκμαῖος φύσιν in the prime of strength, id. II. in time, in season, Lat. opportunus, Soph.

ακμη.def: ἀκμή (ἀκή I) I. a point, edge: proverb., ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge (v. ξυρόν); ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, Soph.; ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, id. II. the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime, of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης id.; ἀκμὴ βίου Xen.; ἐν ἀκμῆι εἶναι ἀκμάζειν, Plat.; ἀκμὴν ἔχειν, of corn, to be ripe, Thuc.; also of time, ἀ. ἦρος the spring-prime, Pind.; ἀ. θέρους mid-summer, Xen.; ἀ. τῆς δόξης Thuc.; periphr. like βία, ἀκμὴ Θησειδᾶν Soph. III. like καιρός, the best, most fitting time, Trag.; ἔργων, λόγων ἀκμή the time for doing, speaking, Soph.; ἀκμή ἐστι, c. inf., 'tis high time to do, Aesch.; ἐπ’ ἀκμῆς εἶναι, c. inf., to be on the point of doing, Eur.; ἐπ’ αὐτὴν ἥκει τὴν ἀκμήν ’tis come to the critical time, Dem. IV. ἀκμήν, acc. of ἀκμή, used as adv., just, Xen. 2. yet, still, Theocr., NTest.

ακμηνοσ.def: ἄκμηνος (Deriv. uncertain.) fasting, Il.; c. gen., ἄκμηνος σίτοιο fasting from food, id.

ακμησ.def: ἀκμής (κάμνω, ἀκάμας) untiring, unwearied, Il., Soph.

ακμοθετον.def: ἀκμόθετον (ἄκμων, τίθημι) the anvil-block, smithy Hom.

ακμων.def: ἄκμων I. orig. prob. a thunderbolt, ἄκμων οὐρανόθεν κατιών Hes. II. an anvil, Hom., etc.: metaph., λόγχης ἄκμονες very anvils to bear blows, Aesch.

ακνηστισ.def: ἄκνηστις the spine or backbone, Od.

ακνισοσ.def: ἄκνισος (κνῖσα) without the fat of sacrifices, Anth.

ακοη.def: ἀκοή I. a hearing, the sound heard, Il. 2. the thing heard, hearsay, report, news, tidings, μετὰ πατρὸς ἀκουήν in quest of tidings of his father, Od.; ἀκοῆι ἱστορεῖν, παραλαβεῖν τι to know by hearsay, Hdt.; so, ἐξ ἀκοῆς λέγειν Plat. II. the sense of hearing, Hdt., etc. 2. the act of hearing, hearing, ἀκοῆι κλύειν, ἀκοαῖς δέχεσθαι, εἰς ἀκοὰς ἔρχεταί τι Soph., Eur.; δι’ ἀκοῆς αἰσθάνεσθαι Plat. III. the ear, Sapph., Aesch.

ακοιμητοσ.def: ἀκοίμητος (κοιμάω) sleepless, of the sea, Aesch.

ακοινωνητοσ.def: ἀκοινώνητος (κοινωνέω) I. not shared with another, c. dat., Eur. II. act. having no share of or in, c. gen., Plat.: absol. unsocial, inhuman, id.

ακοιτησ.def: ἀκοίτης (α copul., κοίτη, cf. ἄλοχος) a bedfellow, spouse, husband.

ακοιτισ.def: ἄκοιτις a spouse, wife, Hom., etc.

ακολασταινω.def: ἀκολασταίνω (ἀκόλαστος) to be licentious, intemperate, Ar., Plat., etc.

ακολαστημα.def: ἀκολάστημα an act of ἀκολασία, Plut.

ακολαστοσ.def: ἀκόλαστος (κολάζω) 1. Lat. non castigatus, unchastised, undisciplined, unbridled, Hdt., attic, etc. 2. licentious, intemperate, opp. to σώφρων, Soph., etc.:— so in adv., ἀκολάστως ἔχειν Plat.; comp., ἀκολαστοτέρως ἔχειν πρός τι to be too intemperate in a thing, Xen.

ακολοσ.def: ἄκολος (Deriv. uncertain.) a bit, morsel, Od.

ακολουθεω.def: ἀκολουθέω (ἀκόλουθος) I. to follow one, go after or with him, c. dat. pers., Ar., etc.; also, ἀκ. μετά τινος Plat.; σύν τινι Xen.; κατόπιν τινός Ar.:— absol., Plat., etc. II. metaph. to follow, obey, τινι Thuc., etc.; ἀκ. τοῖς πράγμασιν to follow circumstances, Dem. 2. to follow the thread of a discourse, Plat. 3. of things, to follow upon, be consequent upon, τοῖς εἰρημένοις id.

ακολουθητεον.def: ἀκολουθητέον (verb. adj. of ἀκολουθέω,) one must follow, Xen., etc.

ακολουθια.def: ἀκολουθία (ἀκολουθέω) I. a following, train, Soph., Plat. II. a following upon, conformity with, τοῖς πράγμασι id.

ακολουθοσ.def: ἀκόλουθος (α copul., κέλευθος) 1. following, attending on; as Subst. a follower, attendant, Lat. pedisequus, Ar., Thuc., etc.; οἱ ἀκόλουθοι the camp-followers, Xen. 2. following after, c. gen., Νηρήιδων ἀκ. Soph. 3. following or consequent upon, in conformity with, c. gen., Ar.; also c. dat., Plat.:—absol. agreeing with one another, Xen., etc.:— adv. -θως, in accordance with, τοῖς νόμοις Dem.

ακολυμβοσ.def: ἀκόλυμβος unable to swim, Batr., Plut.

ακομιστια.def: ἀκομιστία (from ἀκόμιστος) want of tending or care, Od.

ακομψοσ.def: ἄκομψος unadorned, boorish, ἐγὼ δ’ ἄκομψος "rude I am in speech," Eur.

ακοναω.def: ἀκονάω (ἀκόνη) to sharpen, whet, μαχαίρας Ar.; λόγχην Xen.:—Mid., ἀκονᾶσθαι μαχαίρας to sharpen their swords, id.

ακονη.def: ἀκόνη (ἀκή I) a whetstone, hone, Pind., etc.

ακονιτι.gloss: without the dust of the arena
ακονιτι.def: ἀκονιτί (adverb of ἀκόνιτος) without the dust of the arena, i. e. without a struggle, without effort, Lat. sine pulvere, Thuc., Xen.

ακονιτικοσ.def: ἀκονιτικός (from ἀκόνιτον) made of aconite, Xen.

ακονιτον.def: ἀκόνιτον (Deriv. uncertain.) aconite, a poisonous plant, Theophr.

ακοντι.def: ἀκοντί (adverb of ἄκων, contr. for ἀεκοντί, Plut.)

ακοντιζω.def: ἀκοντίζω (ἄκων) I. to hurl a javelin, τινός at one, Il.; ἐπί τινι id.:—the weapon is put in dat., ἀκόντισε δουρί darted with his spear, id.; also in acc., ἀκόντισαν ὀξέα δοῦρα darted their spears, Od. 2. c. acc. pers. to hit with a javelin, Hdt., etc.; Pass. to be so hit or wounded, Eur., Xen. 3. to shoot forth rays, of the moon, Eur. II. intr. to pierce, εἴσω γῆς id.

ακοντιον.def: ἀκόντιον (Dim. of ἄκων, Hhymn., Hdt., etc.)

ακοντισμα.def: ἀκόντισμα (ἀκοντίζω) I. a javelin's throw, Xen. II. the thing thrown, a dart, javelin, Plut. III. in pl. = ἀκοντισταί, id.

ακοντιστησ.def: ἀκοντιστής (ἀκοντίζω) a darter, javelin-man, Hom., Hdt., etc.

ακοντιστικοσ.def: ἀκοντιστικός (ἀκοντίζω) skilled in throwing the javelin, Xen.

ακοντιστυσ.gloss: the game of throwing the javelin
ακοντιστυσ.def: ἀκοντιστύς (ionic for ἀκόντισις) the game of throwing the javelin, Il.

ακοποσ.def: ἄκοπος without weariness, and so, I. pass. untired, Plat. II. act. not wearying, of a horse, easy, Xen. 2. removing weariness, refreshing, Plat.

ακορεστοσ.def: ἀκόρεστος (κορέννυμι) (attic for ἀκόρητος) I. insatiate, Trag.; c. gen. insatiate in a thing, Aesch.:—in Soph. (πάντων ἀκορέστατος, most insatiate, most shameless), the word is either sync. for ἀκορεστότατος, or Sup. of ἀκορής, ἀκόρεστος. 2. of things, I. insatiate, unceasing, Lat. improbus, Trag. II. act. not satiating, Aesch. 2. not liable to surfeit, φιλία Xen.

ακορητοσ.def: ἀκόρητος (κορέννυμι) I. insatiate, unsated in or with a thing, c. gen., Il. II. （κορέω) unswept, ungrimmed, ungarnished, Ar.

ακοροσ.def: ἄκορος (= ἀκόρεστος) untiring, ceaseless, Lat. improbus, εἰρεσία Pind.

ακοσ.def: ἄκος 1. a cure, relief, remedy for a thing, c. gen., Od., etc.:—absol., ἄκος εὑρεῖν Il., Soph.; ἐξευρεῖν, λαβεῖν, ποιεῖσθαι, Hdt., etc.:—by a medical metaph., ἄκος ἐντέμνειν, τέμνειν, cf. ἐντέμνω II. 2. a means of obtaining a thing, c. gen., Eur.

ακοσμεω.def: ἀκοσμέω (ἄκοσμος) to be disorderly, to offend, Soph., Dem., etc.

ακοσμητοσ.def: ἀκόσμητος (κοσμέω) 1. unarranged, unorganised, Plat.:—adv. -τως, id. 2. unfurnished with, c. dat., Xen.

ακοσμια.def: ἀκοσμία (from ἄκοσμος) disorder, Plat.: extravagance, Eur.:—in moral sense, disorderliness, disorderly conduct, Soph.

ακοσμοσ.def: ἄκοσμος I. without order, disorderly, Aesch.:—in Hom. of Thersites' words, disorderly:— adv. -μως, Hdt., etc. II. κόσμος ἄκοσμος, a world that is no world, Anth.; also of an inappropriate ornament, id.

ακοσταω.def: ἀκοστάω only in aor1 part. ἵππος ἀκοστήσας ἐπὶ φάτνηι a horse corn-fed at manger, a stalled horse, Il.

ακουαζομαι.def: ἀκουάζομαι (ἀκούω) (Dep., only in pres.) to hearken or listen to, c. gen., Od.; δαιτὸς ἀκουάζεσθον ye are bidden to the feast, Il.

ακουροσ.def: ἄκουρος (κοῦρος ionic for κόρος) I. without male heir, Od. II. （κουρά) unshaven, unshorn, Ar.

ακουσμα.def: ἄκουσμα (ἀκούω) 1. a thing heard, such as music, Xen. 2. a rumour, tale, Soph.

ακουστεον.def: ἀκουστέον (verb. adj. of ἀκούω) 1. one must hear or hearken to, c. gen. pers., Hdt., etc.; c. acc. rei, Plat. 2. ἀκουστέος, α, ον, to be hearkened to, Soph.

ακουστοσ.def: ἀκουστός (verb. adj. of ἀκούω) I. heard, audible, Hhymn., Plat., etc. II. that should be heard, Soph., Eur.

ακουω.def: ἀκούω (Root ΑΚΟϜ) I. to hear, Hom., etc. —Construct., properly, c. acc. of thing heard, gen. of pers. from whom it is heard, ταῦτα Καλυψοῦς ἤκουσα Od.; the gen. pers. may be omitted, ἀκήκοας λόγον Soph., or the acc. rei, ἄκουε τοῦ θανόντος id.:—often however c. gen. rei, to have hearing of a thing. 2. c. gen. objecti, to hear of, hear tell of, ἀκ. πατρός Od.; so c. acc., Od.:—so, ἀκ. περί τινος. 3. the pers. from whom the thing is heard takes a prep., ἀκούειν τι ἀπό, ἔκ, παρά, πρός τινος, Il., attic II. to know by hearsay, εἴ που ἀκούεις Od.; so Plat., etc. III. absol. to hearken, give ear, to begin a proclamation, ἀκούετε λεώι hear, O people. IV. to listen to, give ear to, Il. 2. to obey, c. gen., or more rarely c. dat., id. 3. to hear and understand, κλύοντες οὐκ ἤκουον Aesch. V. in pass. sense, with an adv., to hear oneself called, be called so and so, like Lat. audire, κακῶς ἀκ. πρός τινος to be ill spoken of by one, Hdt.; εὖ, κακῶς, ἄριστα ἀκ., Lat. bene, male audire, id., attic 2. with a Noun, ἀκούειν κακός, καλός Soph., Plat.; κόλακες ἀκούουσι Dem. 3. c. acc. rei, ἀκ. κακά to have evil spoken of one, Ar.; φήμας κακὰς ἤκουσεν Eur.

ακρα.def: ἄκρα (ἄκρος) 1. a headland, foreland, cape, Hom., etc. 2. a mountain-top, summit: used by Hom. only in the phrase κατ’ ἄκρης from top to bottom, i. e. utterly, πόλιν αἱρέειν κατ’ ἄκρης Hdt.; so in attic, κατ’ ἄκρας utterly, Trag., Plat. 3. the citadel of a city, Lat. arx, Xen.

ακρααντοσ.def: ἀκράαντος (epic form of ἄκραντος) unfulfilled, fruitless, Lat. irritus, Hom.

ακραησ.def: ἀκραής (ἄκρος, ἄημι) blowing strongly, fresh-blowing, of the north and west wind, Od.; si ἀκραὲς erit, if it shall be clear weather, Cic.

ακραιοσ.def: ἀκραῖος (ἄκρα) dwelling on the heights, Eur.

ακραιφνησ.def: ἀκραιφνής (syncop. form of ἀκεραιοφανής (ἀκέραιος, φαίνομαι）) I. unmixed, pure, Eur., Ar.: metaph., πενία ἀκρ. utter poverty, Anth. II. unharmed, entire, Lat. integer, Eur., Thuc. 2. c. gen. untouched by a thing, Soph.

ακραντοσ.def: ἄκραντος (κραίνω, like epic ἀκράαντος) unfulfilled, fruitless, Pind., Aesch.:—neut. pl. as adv., in vain, id., Eur.

ακρασια.def: ἀκρασία (ἄκρατος) bad mixture, ill temperature, Theophr.

ακρατεια.def: ἀκράτεια (ἀκρατής) incontinence, want of self-control, Plat.:—the later form is ἀκρασία.

ακρατησ.def: ἀκρατής (a_priv, κράτος) I. powerless, impotent, Soph. II. c. gen. rei, not having power or command over a thing, Lat. impotens, γλώσσης Aesch.; ὀργῆς Thuc.:—also, intemperate in the use of a thing, οἴνου Xen., Arist.; περὶ τὰ πόματα id. 2. absol. without command over oneself, incontinent, Lat. impotens sui, id. 3. of things, immoderate, δαπάνη Anth.

ακρατιζομαι.gloss: to drink wine unmixed with water
ακρατιζομαι.def: ἀκρατίζομαι (ἄκρατος) to drink wine unmixed with water: hence, to breakfast, because this meal consisted of bread dipped in wine, Ar.

ακρατοποσια.def: ἀκρατοποσία (from ἀκρατοπότης) a drinking of sheer wine, Hdt.

ακρατοποτησ.def: ἀκρατοπότης (ἄκρατος, πίνω) a drinker of sheer wine, Hdt.

ακρατοσ.def: ἄκρατος (κεράννυμι) 1. of liquids, unmixed, sheer, of wine, Od.:—esp., οἶνος ἄκρητος wine without water, Lat. merum, Hdt.; and ἄκρατος without (οἶνος), Ar., etc. 2. metaph., ἄκρ. μέλαν pure black, Theophr.; ἄκρατος νύξ sheer night, Aesch.; ἄκρ. νοῦς pure intellect, Xen. 3. of conditions or states, pure, untempered, absolute, ἐλευθερία, ἡδονή Plat.; ἄκρ. ψεῦδος a sheer lie, id.:—adv. -τως absolutely, Luc. 4. of persons, intemperate, excessive, violent, ἄκρατος ὀργήν Aesch.: so of things we feel, ἄκρ. ὀργή, ἄκρ. καῦμα, etc. II. comp. ἀκρατέστερος, Sup. -έστατος (as if from ἀκρατής).

ακρατωρ.def: ἀκράτωρ II. = ἀκρατής I, Soph. II. = ἀκρατής II, Plat.

ακραχολοσ.def: ἀκράχολος (ἄκρος, χόλος) I. quick to anger, passionate, Ar. II. in passionate distress, Theocr.

ακρεμων.def: ἀκρέμων (ἄκρος) a branch, twig, spray, Eur., Theocr.

ακρεσπεροσ.def: ἀκρέσπερος (ἄκρος II, ἑσπέρα) at eventide, Anth.: neut. ἀκρέσπερον as adv., Theocr.

ακρηβησ.def: ἀκρήβης (ἄκρος, ἥβη) a youth in his prime, Anth.

ακρηβοσ.def: ἄκρηβος (ἄκρος, ἥβη) in earliest youth, Theocr.

ακριβεια.def: ἀκρίβεια (ἀκριβής) 1. exactness, minute accuracy, precision, Thuc., etc.; with Preps. in adv. sense, δι’ ἀκριβείας, ἀκριβῶς, with minuteness or precision, Plat.; so, εἰς τὴν ἀκρ., πρὸς τὴν ἀκρ. id.:— ἡ ἀκρ. τοῦ ναυτικοῦ its perfect condition, Thuc. 2. parsimony, frugality, Plut.

ακριβησ.def: ἀκριβής (Deriv. uncertain.) I. exact, accurate, precise, made or done to a nicety, Eur., etc. II. of persons, exact, precise, strict, consummate, Thuc., etc.:—esp. painfully exact, over-nice, precise, curious, Plat.:— τὸ ἀκριβές ἀκρίβεια, Thuc.:—adv. -βῶς, to a nicety, precisely, Hdt., etc. 2. parsimonious, frugal, Menand.

ακριβολογεομαι.def: ἀκριβολογέομαι (from ἀκριβολόγος) to be exact or precise in language or thought, Plat.; c. acc. rei, to weigh accurately, id.

ακριβοω.def: ἀκριβόω (ἀκριβής) 1. to make exact or accurate, Eur.; ἀκρ. τάδε to be perfect in bearing these hardships, Xen.:—Pass. to be or become perfect, Ar. 2. to investigate accurately, to understand thoroughly, οἱ τάδ’ ἠκριβωκότες Eur.; τοὔνομά μου σὺ ἀκριβοῖς; are you sure of my name? Plat.

ακριτοδακρυσ.def: ἀκριτόδακρυς shedding floods of tears, Anth.

ακριτομυθοσ.def: ἀκριτόμυθος I. recklessly or confusedly babbling, Il. II. hard of interpretation, Od.

ακριτοσ.def: ἄκριτος I. undistinguishable, unarranged, disorderly, Hom.; τύμβος ἄκριτος one common undistinguished grave, Il. 2. continual, unceasing, ἄχεα id.; neut. as adv., πενθήμεναι ἄκριτον αἰεί Od.:— ὄρος ἄκρ. a continuous mountain-range, Anth., Babr. II. undecided, doubtful, νείκεα, ἄεθλος Il.; ἀκρίτων ὄντων while the issue was doubtful, Thuc.:—adv. ἀκρίτως, without decisive issue, id. 2. unjudged, untried, of persons and things, ἄκριτόν τινα κτείνειν to put to death without trial, Lat. indicta causa, Hdt., etc. III. act. not giving a judgment, id.: without judgment, ill-judged, rash, Eur.

ακριτοφυλλοσ.def: ἀκριτόφυλλος (φύλλον) of undistinguishable, i. e. closely blending, leafage, Il.

ακροαμα.def: ἀκρόαμα (ἀκροάομαι) anything heard with pleasure, as a play or musical piece, Xen.

ακροαματικοσ.def: ἀκροαματικός (ἀκροάομαι) designed for hearing only, Plut.

ακροαομαι.def: ἀκροάομαι (Deriv. uncertain.) I. to hearken to, listen to, c. gen. pers., acc. rei, Thuc., etc.; c. gen. rei, id. 2. absol. to listen, ὁ ἀκροώμενος a hearer, disciple, Plat., Xen. II. to attend to, obey, τινός Thuc., etc.

ακροασισ.def: ἀκρόασις (ἀκροάομαι) 1. a hearing or listening, Thuc., etc. 2. obedience to another, c. gen., id.

ακροατεοσ.def: ἀκροατέος (verb. adj. of ἀκροάομαι) one must listen to, τινός Ar.

ακροατηριον.def: ἀκροατήριον (ἀκροάομαι) I. a place of audience, NTest. II. an audience, Plut.

ακροατησ.def: ἀκροατής (ἀκροάομαι) I. a hearer, Lat. auditor, Thuc., etc.: a disciple, Arist. II. a lecturer, Plut.

ακροατικοσ.def: ἀκροατικός (ἀκροάομαι) of or for hearing, μισθὸς ἀκρ. a lecturer's fee, Luc.

ακροβαφησ.def: ἀκροβαφής (βαφή) tinged at the point, Anth.

ακροβελησ.gloss: with a point at the end
ακροβελησ.def: ἀκροβελής (βέλος) with a point at the end, Anth.

ακροβολιζομαι.gloss: to throw from afar, to fight with missiles, to skirmish
ακροβολιζομαι.def: ἀκροβολίζομαι (ἀκροβόλος) to throw from afar, to fight with missiles, to skirmish, πρός τινα or absol., Thuc., Xen.:—metaph., ἀκρ. ἔπεσι Hdt.—The Act. in Anth.

ακροβολισισ.def: ἀκροβόλισις (From ἀκροβολίζομαι) a skirmishing, Xen., etc.

ακροβολοσ.def: ἀκρόβολος (βάλλω) pass., struck from afar, Aesch.

ακροβυστια.def: ἀκροβυστία ((Deriv. uncertain.)) I. the foreskin, NTest. II. circumcision, id.;—and as collect. the uncircumcision, i. e. the uncircumcised, id.

ακρογωνιαιοσ.def: ἀκρογωνιαῖος (γωνία) at the extreme angle, ἀκρ. λίθος the corner foundation-stone, NTest.

ακροδετοσ.def: ἀκρόδετος bound at the end or top, Anth.

ακροδρυα.def: ἀκρόδρυα (δρῦς) (The sg. occurs in Anth.) I. fruit-trees, Xen. II. fruits, Arist.

ακροθιγησ.gloss: touching on the surface, touching the lips
ακροθιγησ.def: ἀκροθιγής (θιγγάνω) touching on the surface, touching the lips, Anth.

ακροθινιαζομαι.gloss: to take of the best, pick out for oneself
ακροθινιαζομαι.def: ἀκροθινιάζομαι (ἀκροθίνια) to take of the best, pick out for oneself, Eur.

ακροθινιον.gloss: the topmost part of a heap, the choice part, first-fruits
ακροθινιον.def: ἀκροθίνιον (ἄκρος, θίς) (mostly in pl. ἀκροθίνια) the topmost part of a heap, the choice part, first-fruits, taken as an offering to the gods, Hdt., etc.

ακροκελαινιαω.def: ἀκροκελαινιάω (κελαινός) only in epic part.; growing black on the surface, of a swollen stream, Il.

ακροκνεφαιοσ.gloss: at the beginning of night, in twilight
ακροκνεφαιοσ.def: ἀκροκνέφαιος (κνέφας) at the beginning of night, in twilight, Hes.

ακροκομοσ.def: ἀκρόκομος (κόμη) I. with hair on the crown, of the Thracians, who seem to have shaved all the head except the crown, Il. II. with leaves at the top, Eur., Theocr.

ακροκορινθοσ.def: Ἀκροκόρινθος the citadel of Corinth, Eur., Xen.

ακρολιθοσ.gloss: with the ends made of stone
ακρολιθοσ.def: ἀκρόλιθος with the ends made of stone; ξόανον ἀκρ. a statue with the head, arms, and legs marble, the rest wood, Anth.

ακρολογεω.def: ἀκρολογέω (λέγω) to gather at top, στάχυας Anth.

ακρολοφοσ.def: ἀκρόλοφος I. high-crested, peaked, Anth. II. as Subst. a mountain crest, Plut.

ακρολυτεω.def: ἀκρολυτέω (λύω) to untie at the ends, Anth.

ακρομανησ.def: ἀκρομανής (μαίνομαι) on the verge of madness, Hdt.

ακρομολιβδοσ.def: ἀκρομόλιβδος leaded at the edge, of a net, Anth.

ακρον.def: ἄκρον (neut. of ἄκρος) I. the highest or furthest point: 1. a mountain-top, peak, Hom., etc. 2. a headland, foreland, cape, Od. 3. an end, extremity, Plat.; ἄκρα χειρῶν the hands, Luc. II. metaph. the highest pitch, height, Pind.; εἰς ἄκρον exceedingly, Theocr.; τὰ ἄκρα τοῖς ἄκροις ἀποδιδόναι the highest place to the highest men, Plat.; ἄκρα φέρεσθαι to win the prize, Theocr. 2. of persons, Ἄργεος ἄκρα the oldest rulers of Argos, id.

ακρονυχι.gloss: with the tip of the nail
ακρονυχι.def: ἀκρονυχί (from ἀκρόνυχος) with the tip of the nail, Anth.

ακρονυχοσ.def: ἀκρόνυχος (νύξ) at night-fall, at even, Theocr., etc.

ακροπολισ.def: ἀκρόπολις I. the upper city, i. e. the citadel, Lat. arx, Od., Hdt.:—esp. the Acropolis of Athens, which served as the treasury, Thuc. II. metaph. of men, a tower of defence, Theogn.

ακροποροσ.def: ἀκροπόρος (πείρω) piercing with the point, Od.

ακροπρωρον.gloss: the end of a ship's prow
ακροπρωρον.def: ἀκρόπρῳρον (πρῷρα) the end of a ship's prow, Strab.

ακροπτερον.def: ἀκρόπτερον the tip of the wing, Anth.

ακροσ.def: ἄκρος (ἀκή I) I. at the furthest point, and so either topmost = Lat. summus, or outermost = Lat. extremus: 1. highest, topmost, ἐν ἄκρηι πόλει ἐν ἀκροπόλει, Il.; μέλαν ὕδωρ ἄκρον at its surface, id., etc. 2. outermost, ἄκρη χείρ, ἄκροι πόδες, ἄκρος ὦμος the end of the hand, ends of the feet, tip of the shoulder, id., Thuc.; ἐπ’ ἄκρων [δακτύλων] on tiptoe, Soph.; ἄκροισι λαίφους κρασπέδοις with the outermost edges of the sail, i. e. under close-reefed sails, Eur. II. of Time, it denotes completeness, ἄκραι σὺν ἑσπέραι when eve was fully come, Pind.; ἄκρας νυκτός at dead of night, Soph. III. of Degree, the highest in its kind, exceeding good, consummate, excellent: of persons, Hdt., etc.; ἄκρος μάντις Soph.:—often with an acc. modi added, ψυχὴν οὐκ ἄκρος not strong in mind, Hdt.; ἄκροι τὰ πολέμια, skilful in war, id., etc.; also c. gen. modi, οἱ ἄκροι τῆς ποιήσεως Plat.; also, ἄκρος εἰς or περί τι id. IV. as Subst., v. ἄκρα, ἄκρον. V. neut. as adv. on the top or surface, just, ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος on the very edge of the surf, il. 2. exceedingly, Theocr. 3. utterly, completely, Plat.

ακροσιδηροσ.def: ἀκροσίδηρος pointed or shod with iron, Anth.

ακροστολιον.def: ἀκροστόλιον (στολή) the gunwale of a ship, Plut.

ακροσφαλησ.def: ἀκροσφαλής (σφάλλω) apt to trip, unsteady, precarious, Plat.

ακροτελευτιον.def: ἀκροτελεύτιον the fag-end of a verse, Thuc.

ακροτομεω.gloss: to lop off, shave the surface
ακροτομεω.def: ἀκροτομέω (from ἀκρότομος) to lop off, shave the surface, Xen.

ακροτομοσ.def: ἀκρότομος (τέμνω) cut off sharp, abrupt, Polyb.

ακροφυσιον.def: ἀκροφύσιον (φῦσα) the snout or pipe of a pair of bellows, Thuc.

ακροχειριζομαι.def: ἀκροχειρίζομαι to struggle at arm's length, of a kind of wrestling, in which they grasped one another's hands, without clasping the body, Plat., etc.

ακροχορδων.gloss: a wart with a thin neck
ακροχορδων.def: ἀκροχορδών (χορδή) a wart with a thin neck, Plut.

ακρυσταλλοσ.def: ἀκρύσταλλος free from ice, ἡ χώρη Hdt.

ακρωμια.def: ἀκρωμία (ὦμος) the point of the shoulder; in a horse, the withers, Xen.

ακρωνια.def: ἀκρωνία a dub. word in Aesch., perh. = ἀκρωτηριασμός, mutilation.

ακρωνυχια.def: ἀκρωνυχία (from ἀκρώνυχος) the tip of the nail: metaph. the ridge of a mountain, Xen.

ακρωνυχοσ.def: ἀκρώνυχος (ἄκρος, ὄνυξ) with nails at the extremities, χερὸς ἀκρώνυχα the tips of the fingers, Anth.

ακρωτηριαζω.gloss: to cut off the extremities, mutilate
ακρωτηριαζω.def: ἀκρωτηριάζω (from ἀκρωτήριον) to cut off the extremities, mutilate, τὰς πρῴρας ἠκρωτηρίασαν cut the beaks off the prows, Hdt.:—so in Mid., τὰς τριήρεις ἀκρωτηριασάμενοι Xen.; perf. pass. in mid. sense, ἠκρωτηριασμένοι τὰς πατρίδας having mutilated their countries, Dem.

ακρωτηριον.def: ἀκρωτήριον (ἄκρος) I. any prominent part, ἀκρ. τοῦ οὔρεος a mountain-peak, Hdt. 2. a cape, promontory, id., Thuc. II. the extremity of anything, ἀκρ. νηός a ship's beak, Hdt. 2. in pl. the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes, Thuc., etc.; τὰ ἀκρ. τῆς Νίκης her wings, Dem.

ακταινω.def: ἀκταίνω (Deriv. uncertain.) (only in pres.) to lift up, raise, ἀκταίνειν στάσιν to raise oneself so as to stand, to stand upright, Aesch.; so in the form ἀκταινόω, Plat.

ακταιοσ.def: ἀκταῖος (ἀκτή) 1. on the coast, of Ionian cities, Thuc.: so, Ἀκταία (sc. γῆ), coast-land, an old name of Attica, id. 2. haunting the coast, βάτραχοι Babr.

ακτεανοσ.def: ἀκτέανος (κτέανον) without property, poor, τίνος in a thing, Anth.

ακτεοσ.def: ἀκτέος (verb. adj. of ἄγω) I. one must lead, Plat., etc.; εἰρήνην ἀκτέον one must keep peace, Dem. II. one must go or march, Xen.

ακτεριστοσ.def: ἀκτέριστος (κτερίζω) unhallowed by funeral rites, Soph.

ακτη.def: ἀκτή A. a headland, foreland, promontory, shore, Od., etc.: of the banks of rivers, ἀκταὶ Σιμόεντος Aesch.; Ἀχέροντος Soph. 2. generally, coast-land, ἀκταὶ διφάσιαι of the N. and S. coasts of Asia Minor, Hdt.; of Attica (cf. ἀκταῖος), Soph. II. generally, any edge or strand, like the sea-coast, Lat. ora, χώματος ἀκτή of a sepulchral mound, Aesch.; βώμιος ἀ. of an altar, Soph. (Perh. from ἄγνυμι, cf. ῥηγμίν.） B. corn or meal, Δημήτερος ἀκτή Il.; ἀλφίτου ἀκτή Od. (Deriv. uncertain.)

ακτημων.def: ἀκτήμων (κτῆμα) without property, poor, χρυσοῖο in gold, Il.: absol., ἀκτ. πενία Theocr.

ακτιοσ.def: ἄκτιος (ἀκτή) haunting the shore, of Pan, Theocr.

ακτισ.def: ἀκτίς ((Deriv. uncertain.)) I. a ray, beam, of the sun, Hom.; ἀνὰ μέσσαν ἀκτῖνα, i. e. from the south, Soph.; ἀκτῖνες τελευτῶσαι sunset, Eur. 2. metaph. brightness, splendour, glory, Pind. II. like Lat. radius, the spoke of a wheel, Anth.

ακτιτησ.def: ἀκτίτης (ἀκτή) a dweller on the coast, Anth.

ακυλοσ.def: ἄκυλος an acorn, the fruit of the ilex, Od.

ακυμαντοσ.def: ἀκύμαντος (κυμαίνω) I. not washed by the waves, ψαμάθοις ἐπ’ ἀκυμάντοις on sands washed by no waves, i. e. on the sands of the stadium, Eur. II. waveless, calm, πέλαγος Luc.

ακυμοσ.def: ἄκυμος (κῦμα) (= ἀκύμαντος, Arist., Plut., etc.) tranquil, ἀκ. βίοτος Eur.

ακυμων.def: ἀκύμων (κύεω) without fruit, barren, of women, Eur.

ακυροσ.def: ἄκυρος (κῦρος) without authority: I. of laws and contracts, invalid, ἄκυρον ποιεῖν, Lat. irritum facere, to set aside, and ἄκυρον γίγνεσθαι, to become of no force, to be set aside, Plat.; νόμοις ἀκύροις χρωμένη, i. e. having laws, but not enforcing them, Thuc. II. of persons, having no right or power, ἄκ. ποιεῖν τινά Xen.; c. gen., ἄκυροι πάντων γενήσεσθε Dem.

ακυρωτοσ.def: ἀκύρωτος (verb. adj. of κυρόω) unconfirmed, Eur.

ακωκη.def: ἀκωκή (ἀκή I) a point, Hom., etc.

ακωμωδητοσ.def: ἀκωμῴδητος (α privat., κωμῳδέω) not ridiculed: adv. -τως, Luc.

ακων.def: ἄκων (ἀκή 1) a javelin, dart, Hom., etc.

αλαβαρχια.def: Ἀλαβαρχία the office of Ἀλαβάρχης, in Egypt, ἐξ Ἀλαβαρχίης, Anth.

αλαβαστοθηκη.def: ἀλαβαστοθήκη (ἀλάβαστος, θήκη) a case for alabaster ornaments, Dem.

αλαβαστοσ.def: ἀλάβαστος (Prob. a foreign word.) a box or casket of alabaster, Hdt., Ar., etc.: ἀλάβαστρος is a later form in Lxx., NTest., Plut.

αλαβαστρον.def: ἀλάβαστρον (ἀλάβαστος) (Prob. a foreign word.) a box or casket of alabaster, in NTest., pl. ἀλάβαστρα ορ -τα in Theocr. and Anth.

αλαδε.def: ἅλαδε adverb of ἅλς, to or into the sea, Il., etc.; also, εἰς ἅλαδε Od.

αλαδρομοσ.def: ἁλάδρομος (in Ar. Av. 1359,) either from ἅλλομαι, the bounding race; or from ἅλς, a race over the sea.

αλαζονεια.def: ἀλαζονεία (ἀλαζών) false pretension, imposture, quackery, Ar., Plat., etc.

αλαζονευμα.def: ἀλαζόνευμα (from ἀλαζονεύομαι) an imposture, piece of quackery, Ar., etc.

αλαζονευομαι.def: ἀλαζονεύομαι (ἀλαζών) to make false pretensions, of the Sophists, Xen.

αλαζονικοσ.def: ἀλαζονικός (ἀλαζών) boastful, braggart, Xen. adv. -κῶς, Plut.

αλαζων.def: ἀλαζών (ἄλη) I. properly a vagabond: then, a false pretender, impostor, quack, of Sophists, Ar., Plat., etc. II. as adj. swaggering, boastful, braggart, Lat. gloriosus, Hdt., Plat.

αλαινω.def: ἀλαίνω (= ἀλάομαι) to wander about, Aesch., Eur.; ἀλ. πόδα to wander on foot, id.

αλαλαγη.def: ἀλαλαγή (from ἀλαλάζω) a shouting, Soph., Hdt.
