III. Mid. to attach to oneself, make dependent upon one, τινά Xen.

αναρτεομαι.def: ἀναρτέομαι (ionic Verb, only used in perf. pass.) to be ready, prepared to do, c. inf., Hdt.: cf. ἀρτέομαι.

αναρτιοσ.def: ἀνάρτιος uneven, odd, opp. to ἄρτιος (even), Plat.

αναρχαιζω.def: ἀναρχαΐζω (ἀρχαῖος) to make old again, Anth.

αναρχια.def: ἀναρχία (ἄναρχος) I. lack of a leader, Hdt. II. the state of a people without government, anarchy, Aesch., Thuc., etc.:—at Athens this name was given to the year of the thirty tyrants (B. C. 404), when there was no archon, Xen.

αναρχοσ.def: ἄναρχος (ἀρχή) without head or chief, Il., Eur.: τὸ ἄναρχον ἀναρχία, Aesch.

ανασαλευω.def: ἀνασαλεύω to shake up, stir up, Luc.

ανασειραζω.gloss: to draw back with a rein, to hold in check
ανασειραζω.def: ἀνασειράζω (σειρά) I. to draw back with a rein, to hold in check, Anth. II. to draw aside from the road, Eur.

ανασειω.gloss: to shake back, swing to and fro, move up and down
ανασειω.def: ἀνασείω I. to shake back, swing to and fro, move up and down, Hes.: esp. as a signal, Thuc. II. to stir up, NTest.

ανασευομαι.def: ἀνασεύομαι Pass., only in syncop. aor2, αἷμα ἀνέσσυτο the blood sprang forth, spouted up, Il.

ανασκαπτω.gloss: to dig up, to dig up ground
ανασκαπτω.def: ἀνασκάπτω to dig up, to dig up ground, Plut.

ανασκευαζω.def: ἀνασκευάζω 1. to pack up the baggage (τὰ σκεύη), Lat. vasa colligere: to carry away, Xen.:—Mid. to break up one's camp, march away, Thuc., Xen. 2. to disfurnish, dismantle a place, Thuc.: Mid. to dismantle one's house or city, id. 3. to waste, ravage, destroy, Xen. 4. Pass. to be bankrupt, break, of bankers, Dem.; metaph., ἀνεσκευάσμεθα we are ruined, Eur.

ανασκολοπιζω.def: ἀνασκολοπίζω (The middle future form ἀνασκολοπιοῦμαι has a passive meaning.) to fix on a pole or stake, impale, Hdt.

ανασκοπεω.gloss: to look at narrowly, examine well
ανασκοπεω.def: ἀνασκοπέω to look at narrowly, examine well, Ar., Thuc.

ανασοβεω.gloss: to scare and make to start up, to rouse
ανασοβεω.def: ἀνασοβέω to scare and make to start up, to rouse, Plat.:—Pass., ἀνασεσοβημένος τὴν κόμην with hair on end through fright, Luc.

ανασπαστοσ.def: ἀνασπαστός (From ἀνασπάω) I. drawn up, Ar. II. dragged up the country, of tribes compelled to emigrate into Central Asia, Hdt. 2. of a door or gate, drawn back, opened, Soph.

ανασπαω.def: ἀνασπάω I. to draw up, pull up, Solon, Hdt.:—Mid., ἐκ χροὸς ἔγχος ἀνεσπάσατο he drew his spear forth again, Il. 2. to draw a ship up on land, Hdt., Thuc. 3. to draw or suck up greedily, αἷμα Aesch.: but, ὕδωρ ἀν. to draw water, Thuc. 4. to tear up, Hdt., attic 5. metaph., ἀνασπᾶν λόγους to draw forth words, to utter violent, offensive words, Soph. 6. τὰς ὀφρῦς ἀνασπᾶν to draw up the eyebrows, and so put on a grave important air, Ar.; so, τὰ μέτωπα ἀν. id. II. to draw back, τὴν χεῖρα id. III. to carry away from home, Luc.

ανασσα.def: ἄνασσα (fem. of ἄναξ,) I. a queen, lady, mistress, addressed to goddesses, Od., Aesch.; also to a mortal, Od., Trag. II. generally, like ἄναξ IV, ἄνασσα ὀργίων Ar.

ανασσω.gloss: to be lord, master, owner, to rule, in
ανασσω.def: ἀνάσσω I. to be lord, master, owner, to rule, in a place, c. dat., Ἄργεϊ, νήσοισι ἀν.; or c. gen. to be lord of, rule over, Τενέδοιο, Ἀργείων Hom.: also, μετ’ ἀθανάτοισι ἀν. to be first among the immortals, Il.:—Mid., τρὶς ἀνάξασθαι γένεα ἀνδρῶν to have been king for three generations, Od.:—Pass. to be ruled, id. II. in Trag. metaph. of things, κώπης ἀνάσσειν, etc., Eur., cf. ἄναξ IV:—Pass., παρ’ ὅτῳ σκῆπτρον ἀνάσσεται by whom the sceptre is held as lord, Soph.

αναστασισ.def: ἀνάστασις (ἀνίστημι) I. act. a raising up of the dead, Aesch. 2. a making men rise and leave their place, removal, as of suppliants, Thuc.; ἀν. τῆς Ἰωνίας the removal of all the Greeks from Ionia, Hdt.:— an overthrow, destruction, ruin, Aesch., Eur. 3. a setting up, restoration, τειχῶν Dem. II. （ἀνίσταμαι) a standing or rising up, in token of respect, Plat. 2. a rising and moving off, removal, Thuc. 3. a rising up, ἐξ ὕπνου Soph. 4. a rising again, the Resurrection, NTest.

αναστατοσ.gloss: made to rise up and depart, driven from one's home
αναστατοσ.def: ἀνάστατος (ἀνίσταμαι) 1. made to rise up and depart, driven from one's home, Hdt. 2. of cities and countries, ruined, laid waste, id., Soph., etc.

ανασταυροω.def: ἀνασταυρόω I. to impale, Hdt.: — Pass., Thuc. II. in the Rom. times, to affix to a cross, crucify, Plut. 2. to crucify afresh, NTest.

αναστελλω.def: ἀναστέλλω I. to raise up:— Mid. to gird up one's clothes, Eur., Ar. II. to keep back, repulse an attack, Eur., Thuc.:—Pass. to retire, Thuc.

αναστεναζω.def: ἀναστενάζω (= ἀναστένω) I. Hdt.; τοιάδ’ ἀνεστέναζες ἐχθοδοπά such hateful words didst thou groan forth, Soph. II. c. acc. pers. to groan for, lament, Aesch., Eur.

αναστεναχω.def: ἀναστενάχω c. acc. pers. to groan aloud over, bemoan, c. acc., Il.; so in Mid., id.

αναστενω.def: ἀναστένω (only in pres.) I. to groan aloud, Aesch. II. like ἀναστενάχω, c. acc., Eur.

αναστεφω.def: ἀναστέφω to crown, wreath, κρᾶτα Eur.:—Pass., ἀνέστεμμαι κάρα I have my head wreathed, id.

αναστηριζω.def: ἀναστηρίζω to set up firmly, Anth.

αναστολη.def: ἀναστολή (ἀναστέλλω) a putting back, τῆς κόμης Plut.

αναστομοω.def: ἀναστομόω to furnish with a mouth, ἀν. τάφρον to clear out a trench, Xen.:—Mid., φάρυγος ἀναστόμου τὸ χεῖλος open the lips of your gullet wide, Eur.

αναστρεφω.def: ἀναστρέφω I. to turn upside down, upset, Il., Eur., etc.; ἀν. καρδίαν to upset the stomach, i. e. cause sickness, Thuc.:—Pass., ὄρος ἀνεστραμμένον ἐν τῆι ζητήσει turned up by digging, Hdt. II. to turn back, bring back, τινὰ ἐξ Ἅδιου Soph.; ὄμμ’ ἀν. κύκλωι to roll one's eye about, Eur.: to rally soldiers, Xen. 2. intr. to turn back, return, retire, Hdt., attic III. Pass. to be or dwell in a place, Lat. versari, ἄλλην γαῖαν ἀν. to go to a place and dwell there, Od.; ἀν. ἐν Ἄργει Eur.:— to conduct oneself, ὡς δεσπότης Xen. 2. to revolve, of the sun, id. 3. of soldiers, to face about, rally, id.

αναστροφη.def: ἀναστροφή (ἀναστρέφω) I. a turning upside down, upsetting, Eur.; εἰς ἀναστροφὴν διδόναι ἀναστρέφειν, id. 2. a turning back, return, Soph.: a wheeling about, of soldiers, whether to flee or rally, Xen.; of a ship, Thuc. II. (from Pass.) a dwelling in a place, Plut.: a mode of life, conversation, NTest. 2. the place where one tarries, an abode, haunt, Aesch.

αναστρωφαω.def: ἀνα-στρωφάω (Frequentat. of ἀναστρέφω) (only in pres.) intr., to keep turning about, Od.

ανασυρομαι.def: ἀνασύρομαι to pull up one's clothes, Hdt.; perf. part. ἀνασεσυρμένος obscene, Theophr.

ανασφαλλω.def: ἀνασφάλλω intr., to rise from a fall or illness, to recover, Babr.

ανασχεσισ.def: ἀνάσχεσις (ἀνέχομαι) a taking on oneself, endurance, τῶν δεινῶν Plut.

ανασχιζω.def: ἀνασχίζω to rip up, τὴν γαστέρα Hdt.: to rend, Theocr.

ανασωζω.gloss: to recover what is lost, rescue
ανασωζω.def: ἀνασώζω 1. to recover what is lost, rescue, Soph.: Mid., ἀνασώζεσθαί τινα φόβου to recover one from fear, id.:—Mid. in proper sense, ἀν. τὴν ἀρχήν to recover the government for oneself, Hdt.:—Pass. to return safe, of exiles, Xen. 2. in Mid. also to preserve in mind, remember, Hdt.

αναταρασσω.gloss: to disturb greatly, rouse to frenzy, confound
αναταρασσω.def: ἀναταράσσω to disturb greatly, rouse to frenzy, confound, Soph., Plat.:—Pass., ἀνατεταραγμένος in disorder, Xen.

ανατεινω.def: ἀνατείνω I. to stretch up, hold up, χεῖρα ἀν. to lift up the hand in adjuration or in prayer, Pind.; or as token of ascent in voting, Xen. 2. to stretch forth, τὴν μάχαιραν ἀνατεταμένος with his sword stretched out, id.; οὐδὲν ἀνατείνασθαι φοβερόν to hold out no alarming threat, Dem. 3. to hold up as a prize, Pind. 4. to lift up, exalt, id. II. to stretch out, extend, e. g. a line of battle, Xen.; ἀετὸς ἀνατεταμένος a spread eagle, id. III. intr. to reach up, πέδιλα ἐς γόνυ ἀνατείνοντα Hdt.: to extend out, οὖρος ἀν. ἐς τὴν Οἴτην id.

ανατειχισμοσ.def: ἀνατειχισμός (from ἀνατειχίζω.) a rebuilding of the walls, Xen.

ανατελλω.def: ἀνατέλλω I. to make to rise up or to grow up, Il.:—Pass., φλὸξ ἀνατελλομένη a flame mounting up, Pind. 2. to give birth to, bring to light, id.: of events, Soph. II. intr. to rise, of the sun and moon, Hdt., Soph., etc. 2. of a river, to take its rise, Hdt. 3. to grow, of hair, Aesch.

ανατεμνω.def: ἀνατέμνω to cut open, Hdt., Luc.

ανατι.def: ἀνατί (adverb of ἄνατος,) without harm, with impunity, Trag.

ανατιθημι.def: ἀνατίθημι I. to lay upon (as a burden), Il., Ar. 2. to refer, attribute, ascribe a thing to a person, Hdt., etc.; οὐ γὰρ ἂν οἱ πυραμίδα ἀνέθεσαν ποιήσασθαι would not have attributed to him the erection of the pyramid, id.; ἐμοὶ ἀναθήσετε will give me the credit of it, Thuc.:—also, ἀν. τινὶ πράγματα to lay them upon him, entrust them to him, Ar., Thuc. II. to set up as a votive gift, dedicate, τί τινι Hes., Hdt., etc.; hence the votive gift itself was ἀνάθημα:— Pass., aor1 inf. ἀνατεθῆναι Ar.; but ἀνάκειμαι is more freq. as the Pass. 2. metaph., ἀν. τι λύραι to commit a song to the lyre, Pind. 3. to set up and leave in a place, Ar. III. to put back, remove, προσθεῖσα κἀναθεῖσα τοῦ γε κατθανεῖν by adding or putting off somewhat of the necessity of death, Soph. B. Mid. to put upon for oneself, τὰ σκεύη ἐπὶ τὰ ὑποζύγια Xen. 2. to impart something of one's own, τί τινι NTest. II. to place differently, change about, Orac. ap. Hdt., Plat. 2. metaph. to retract one's opinion, Xen.

ανατιμαω.def: ἀνατιμάω to raise in price, Hdt.

ανατινασσω.gloss: to shake up and down, brandish
ανατινασσω.def: ἀνατινάσσω to shake up and down, brandish, Eur.; of the wind shaking about a sail, id.

ανατληναι.def: ἀνατλῆναι to bear up against, endure, Od., attic; φάρμακ’ ἀνέτλη resisted the strength of the magic drink, Od.

ανατολη.def: ἀνατολή (ἀνατέλλω) 1. a rising, rise, of the sun, often in pl., Od.; of the stars, Aesch. 2. the quarter of sunrise, East, Lat. Oriens, Hdt.

ανατοσ.def: ἄνατος (ἄτη) unharmed, Aesch.; c. gen., κακῶν ἄνατος harmed by no ills, Soph.

ανατρεπτεοσ.def: ἀνατρεπτέος (verb. adj. of ἀνατρέπω) one must overthrow, Luc.

ανατρεπτικοσ.def: ἀνατρεπτικός (From ἀνατρέπω) likely to upset a thing, c. gen., Plat.

ανατρεπω.def: ἀνατρέπω (Note that aor2 middle is used in a passive sense.) I. to turn up or over, overturn, upset, Archil., etc.:—Pass., ἀνετράπετο ὕπτιος ἔπεσεν, Il.; of ships, Plat., etc. 2. to overthrow, Lat. evertere, Hdt., attic 3. to upset in argument, refute, Ar.:—Pass. to be upset, disheartened, ἀνετράπετο φρένα λύπαι Theocr. II. to stir up, awaken, Soph.

ανατρεφω.gloss: to feed up, nurse up, educate
ανατρεφω.def: ἀνατρέφω to feed up, nurse up, educate, Aesch., Ar., Xen.

ανατρεχω.def: ἀνατρέχω I. to run back, Il. 2. c. acc. to retrace, Lat. repetere, Pind. II. to jump up and run, start up, of men, Hdt., Thuc. 2. of things, ἐγκέφαλος ἀνέδραμε ἐξ ὠτειλῆς the brains spurted up from the wound, Il.; σμώδιγγες ἀνέδραμον weals started up under the blow, id. 3. to run up, shoot up, of plants, id.; then of cities and peoples, to shoot up, rise quickly, Hdt. 4. ἀναδέδρομε πέτρη the rock ran sheer up, Od.

ανατριβω.def: ἀνατρίβω 1. to rub well, rub clean, κύνας Xen. 2. Pass. to be worn away, Hdt.

ανατροπη.def: ἀνατροπή (ἀνατρέπω) an upsetting, overthrow, Aesch., Plat.

ανατυρβαζω.def: ἀνατυρβάζω to stir up, confound, Ar.

αναυδητοσ.gloss: not to be spoken, unutterable, ineffable
αναυδητοσ.def: ἀναύδητος (αὐδάω) I. not to be spoken, unutterable, ineffable, Lat. infandus, Aesch., Eur. 2. unspoken, impossible, Soph. II. speechless, id.

αναυδοσ.def: ἄναυδος (αὐδή) I. speechless, silent, Od., Aesch., etc. 2. preventing speech, silencing, Aesch. II. like ἀναύδητος, unutterable, Soph.

αναυλοσ.def: ἄναυλος I. without the flute, i. e. joyless, melancholy, Eur.: neut. pl. ἄναυλα as adv., Babr. II. unskilled in flute-playing, Luc.

αναυροσ.def: Ἄναυρος I. a river in Thessaly, Hes. II. as appellat. ἄναυρος, ὁ, a torrent, Mosch.

αναυσ.def: ἄναυς without ships, νᾶες ἄναες ships that are ships no more, Aesch.

αναφαινω.gloss: to make to give light, make to blaze up
αναφαινω.def: ἀναφαίνω I. to make to give light, make to blaze up, ξύλα Od. 2. to bring to light, shew forth, display, Hom., attic; ἀν. μελέων νόμους Ar. 3. to proclaim, declare, βασιλέα ἀν. τινά Pind.; ἀν. πόλιν to proclaim it victor in the games, id.:—c. inf., ἀναφανῶ σε τόδε ὀνομάζειν I proclaim that they call thee by this name, i. e. order that thou be so named, Eur. 4. of things, to appoint, νόμους Ar. 5. ἀναφάναντες τὴν Κύπρον having opened, come in sight of, Cyprus, NTest. II. Pass., with fut. mid. ἀναφανήσομαι or -φανοῦμαι: perf. ἀναπέφαμμαι, or in mid. form -πέφηνα:— to be shewn forth, come to light or into sight, appear plainly, Hom., etc. 2. to reappear, Hdt. 3. ἀναφανῆναι μούναρχος to be declared king, id.; ἀναφαίνεσθαι σεσωσμένος to be plainly in safety, Xen.

αναφερω.def: ἀναφέρω I. to bring or carry up, Od., etc.; ἀν. τινὰ εἰς Ὄλυμπον Xen.:— to carry up the country, esp. into Central Asia, Hdt.:—Mid. to carry up to a place of safety, take with one, id. 2. to bring up, pour forth, tears, Aesch.:—Mid., ἀνενείκασθαι, absol. to fetch up a deep-drawn breath, heave a deep sigh, Il., Hdt.:—c. acc. rei, to utter, ἀνενείκατο φωνάν, μῦθον Theocr. 3. to uphold, take upon one, ἄχθος Aesch.; κινδύνους Thuc. 4. to offer, contribute, εἰς τὸ κοινόν Dem.:— to offer in sacrifice, NTest. 5. intr. to lead up, of a road, Xen. II. to bring or carry back, Eur., etc.; ἀν. τὰς κώπας to recover the oars, at the end of the stroke, Thuc. 2. to bring back tidings, report, Hdt., etc. 3. to bring back from exile, Thuc. 4. to carry back, trace up one's family to an ancestor, Plat. 5. to refer a matter to another, Hdt., etc.: to ascribe, Eur., etc.:—without acc., ἀν. εἴς τινα to appeal to another, make reference to him, Hdt., Plat.:—of things, ἀν. εἴς τι to have reference to a thing, Plat. 6. to bring back, restore, recover, Thuc.:—Pass. to recover oneself, come to oneself, Hdt.:—so also intr. in Act. to come to oneself, recover, id., etc. 7. to return, yield, as revenue, Xen. 8. to recall a likeness, Plut.

αναφευγω.def: ἀναφεύγω 1. to flee up, Xen. 2. to escape, id. 3. of a report, to disappear gradually, Plut.

αναφησ.def: ἀναφής (ἁφή) not to be touched, impalpable, Plat.

αναφθεγγομαι.def: ἀναφθέγγομαι Dep. to call out aloud, Plut.

αναφθειρομαι.def: ἀναφθείρομαι Pass. to be undone, κατὰ τί δεῦρ’ ἀνεφθάρης; by what ill luck came you hither? Ar.

αναφλεγμαινω.def: ἀναφλεγμαίνω to inflame and swell up, Plut.

αναφλεγω.def: ἀναφλέγω to light up, rekindle, Eur.: metaph., ἀν. ἔρωτα Plut.:—Pass. to be inflamed, excited, Anth.

αναφλεξισ.def: ἀνάφλεξις (from ἀναφλέγω) a lighting up, Plut.

αναφλυω.def: ἀναφλύω (only in imperf.) to bubble or boil up, Il.

αναφορα.def: ἀνα-φορά (ἀναφέρω) 1. a carrying back, reference, Theophr., Plut. 2. recourse to another [in difficulty], Dem. 3. a means of repairing a fault or loss, a means of recovery, Eur., Plut.

αναφορεω.def: ἀναφορέω (Frequent. of ἀναφέρω Ι, Hdt., Thuc.)

αναφορον.def: ἀνάφορον a pole or yoke for carrying things, Ar.

αναφραζομαι.def: ἀναφράζομαι Mid. to be ware of a thing, perceive, Od.

αναφροδιτοσ.def: ἀναφρόδιτος (Ἀφροδίτη) 1. without the favour of Venus, Plut., Luc. 2. Lat. invenustus, without charms, Plut.

αναφρονεω.gloss: to come back to one's senses
αναφρονεω.def: ἀναφρονέω to come back to one's senses, Xen.

αναφροντιζω.def: ἀναφροντίζω c. inf., to meditate how to do a thing, Pind.

αναφυγη.def: ἀναφυγή (ἀναφεύγω) I. escape from a thing, c. gen., Aesch. II. a retreat, Plut.

αναφυρω.def: ἀναφύρω 1. to mix up, confound:— Pass., ἦν πάντα ἀναπεφυρμένα Hdt. 2. to defile, αἵματι ἀναπεφυρμένος id.

αναφυσαω.def: ἀναφυσάω I. to blow up or forth, eject, of volcanoes, Plat. II. metaph. in Pass. to be puffed up, Xen.

αναφυσιαω.def: ἀναφυσιάω to blow upwards, of a dolphin, Hes.

αναφυω.gloss: to produce again, to let grow
αναφυω.def: ἀναφύω I. to produce again, to let grow, πώγωνα Theocr. II. Pass., with aor2 act. ἀν-έφυν, pf. ἀμ-πέφῡκα, to grow up, Hdt., etc. 2. to grow again, of the hair, id.

αναφωνεω.def: ἀναφωνέω 1. to call aloud, declaim, Plut. 2. to proclaim id.

αναφωνησισ.def: ἀναφώνησις (from ἀναφωνέω) an outcry, ejaculation, Plut.

αναχαζω.gloss: to make to recoil, force back
αναχαζω.def: ἀναχάζω I. to make to recoil, force back, only 3rd pl. poet. aor1 ἀνέχασσαν, Pind. II. Mid: to draw back, retire, Hom.; ἐπὶ πόδα ἀναχάζεσθαι to retire slowly, of soldiers, Xen. (who also uses Act. in same sense).

αναχαιτιζω.gloss: to throw back the mane, rear up
αναχαιτιζω.def: ἀναχαιτίζω (χαίτη) 1. of a horse, to throw back the mane, rear up, Eur.: metaph. of men, to become restive, Plut. 2. c. acc. to rear up and throw the rider, Eur.:—metaph. to upset, id., Dem. 3. c. gen., ἀν. τῶν πραγμάτων to shake off the yoke of business, Plut.

αναχασκω.gloss: to open the mouth, gape wide
αναχασκω.def: ἀναχάσκω (only in pres. and imperf., the other tenses being formed from ⁎ἀναχαίνω) to open the mouth, gape wide, Ar., Luc.

αναχνοαινομαι.def: ἀναχνοαίνομαι (χνόος) Pass. to get the first down (χνόος), Ar.

αναχορευω.def: ἀναχορεύω I. to begin a choral dance, ἀν. θίασον Eur. 2. to celebrate in the chorus, Βάκχιον id. 3. οὐκ ἄν με ἀνεχόρευ’ Ἐρινύσι would not scare me away by a band of Furies, id. II. intr. to dance for joy, id.

αναχωννυμι.gloss: to heap up into a mound
αναχωννυμι.def: ἀναχώννυμι to heap up into a mound, Anth.

αναχωρεω.def: ἀναχωρέω I. to go back, Hom.: esp. to retire or withdraw from battle, Hom., Hdt., attic 2. to retire from a place, c. gen., Od. II. to come back or revert to the rightful owner, ἐς τὸν παῖδα Hdt. III.. to withdraw from the world, Ar., Plat.

αναχωρησισ.def: ἀναχώρησις (ἀναχωρέω) I. a drawing back, retiring, retreating, Hdt., Thuc. II. a means or place of retreat, refuge, Thuc.

αναχωρητεοσ.def: ἀναχωρητέος one must withdraw, retreat, Plat.

αναχωριζω.def: ἀναχωρίζω to make to go back or retire, Xen.

αναψαω.def: ἀναψάω to wipe up:— Mid. to wipe up for oneself, Plut.

αναψηφιζω.gloss: to put to the vote again
αναψηφιζω.def: ἀναψηφίζω to put to the vote again, Thuc.

αναψυχη.gloss: a cooling, refreshing: relief, recovery, respite
αναψυχη.def: ἀναψυχή (from ἀναψύχω) a cooling, refreshing: relief, recovery, respite, Plat.: from a thing, c. gen., Eur.

αναψυχω.gloss: to cool, to revive by fresh air, to refresh
αναψυχω.def: ἀναψύχω I. to cool, to revive by fresh air, to refresh, Hom., Eur.:—Pass. to be revived, refreshed, Il. 2. ναῦς ἀν. to let the ships rest and get dry, relieve them, Hdt., Xen.; so, ἀν. τὸν ἱδρῶτα to let it dry off, Plut. 3. metaph. c. gen., ἀν. πόνων τινα to give him relief from toil, Eur. II. intr. in Act. to recover oneself, revive, Anth., Babr.

ανδανω.def: ἁνδάνω I. to please, delight, gratify, c. dat. pers., Hom., etc.:—absol., ἑᾱδότα μῦθον a pleasing speech, id. II. ἁνδάνει, Lat. placet, expressing opinion, οὔ σφι ἥνδανε ταῦτα Hdt.; c. inf., τοῖσι μὲν ἕαδε βοηθέειν it was their pleasure to assist, id.:—impers., ἐπεί νύ τοι εὔαδεν οὕτως (sc. ποιεῖν) Hom.

ανδηρον.def: ἄνδηρον (Perh. akin to ἄνθος.) a raised border, flower-bed, Theocr., Anth.:— any raised bank, a dyke, Mosch.

ανδιχα.def: ἄνδιχα (ἀνά, δίχα) asunder, in twain, Il.

ανδραγαθεω.def: ἀνδραγαθέω (ἀνδραγαθίζομαι) = ἀνδραγαθίζομαι:— Pass., ἠνδραγαθημένα = brave deeds, Plut.

ανδραγαθημα.def: ἀνδραγάθημα (ἀνήρ, ἀγαθός) a brave deed, Plut.

ανδραγαθια.gloss: bravery, manly virtue, the character of a brave honest man
ανδραγαθια.def: ἀνδραγαθία (ἀνήρ, ἀγαθός) bravery, manly virtue, the character of a brave honest man, Hdt., Ar.

ανδραγαθιζομαι.gloss: to act bravely, honestly, play the honest man
ανδραγαθιζομαι.def: ἀνδραγαθίζομαι (ἀνήρ, ἀγαθός) Dep. to act bravely, honestly, play the honest man, Thuc.

ανδραγρια.gloss: the spoils of a slain enemy
ανδραγρια.def: ἀνδράγρια (ἀνήρ, ἄγρα) the spoils of a slain enemy, Il.

ανδρακασ.def: ἀνδρακάς (ἀνήρ) man by man, = κατ’ ἄνδρα, Od.

ανδραποδιζω.def: ἀνδραποδίζω (ἀνδράποδον) (the middle future form ἀνδραποδιεῦμαι is used in a passive sense.) to reduce to slavery, enslave, esp. to sell the free men of a conquered place into slavery, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be sold into slavery, Hdt., Xen., etc.:—the Mid. was also used in act. sense, Hdt.

ανδραποδισμοσ.gloss: a selling free men into slavery, enslaving
ανδραποδισμοσ.def: ἀνδραποδισμός (from ἀνδραποδίζω) a selling free men into slavery, enslaving, Thuc., etc.

ανδραποδιστησ.def: ἀνδραποδιστής (from ἀνδραποδίζω) a slave-dealer, kidnapper, Ar., Plat.; ἀνδρ. ἑαυτοῦ one who sells his own independence, Xen.

ανδραποδον.gloss: one taken in war and sold as a slave, a captive
ανδραποδον.def: ἀνδράποδον (Deriv. uncertain.) (epic dat. pl. ἀνδραπόδεσσι) I. one taken in war and sold as a slave, a captive, Il., Hdt., attic II. generally, a slave, a slavish low fellow, Plat., Xen.

ανδραποδωδησ.def: ἀνδραποδώδης (εἶδος) slavish, servile, abject, Plat., Xen. adv. -δῶς, Plat.

ανδραριον.def: ἀνδράριον (Dim. of ἀνήρ) a manikin, Ar.

ανδραχθησ.gloss: loading a man, as much as a man can carry
ανδραχθησ.def: ἀνδραχθής (ἀνήρ, ἄχθος) loading a man, as much as a man can carry, Od.

ανδρεια.def: ἀνδρεῖα the public meals of the Cretans, also the older name for the Spartan φειδίτια, Alcman, Plut.
ἀνδρεία (ἀνδρία is a doubtful form.) manliness, manhood, manly spirit, Lat. virtus, Trag., etc.

ανδρεικελον.def: ἀνδρείκελον (ἀνήρ, εἴκελος) I. an image of a man, Plat. II. a flesh-coloured pigment, id.

ανδρεικελοσ.def: ἀνδρείκελος (ἀνήρ, εἴκελος) like a man, Plut.

ανδρειοσ.def: ἀνδρεῖος (ἀνήρ) (Comp. and Superl. ἀνδρειότερος, -οτατος.) I. of or for a man, Aesch., etc.; for αὐλοὶ ἀνδρεῖοι, v. αὐλός. II. manly, masculine, Hdt., attic; in bad sense, stubborn, Luc.:—neut. τὸ ἀνδρεῖον, by crasis τἀνδρεῖον, ἀνδρεία, Eur., Thuc. 2. of things, strong, vigorous, Ar.

ανδρηλατεω.gloss: to banish from house and home
ανδρηλατεω.def: ἀνδρηλατέω (from ἀδρηλάτης) to banish from house and home, Aesch., Soph.

ανδρηλατησ.gloss: he that drives one from home, the avenger of blood
ανδρηλατησ.def: ἀνδρηλάτης (ἀνήρ, ἐλαύνω) he that drives one from home, the avenger of blood, Aesch.

ανδριαντισκοσ.def: ἀνδριαντίσκος (Dim. of ἀνδριάς) a puppet, Plut.

ανδριαντοποιεω.def: ἀνδριαντοποιέω (from ἀνδριαντοποιός) to make statues, Xen.

ανδριαντοποιια.def: ἀνδριαντοποιΐα (from ἀνδριαντοποιός) the sculptor's art, statuary, Plat., Xen.

ανδριαντοποιοσ.def: ἀνδριαντοποιός (ἀνδριάς, ποιέω) a statue-maker, statuary, sculptor, Pind., Plat.

ανδριασ.gloss: the image of a man, a statue
ανδριασ.def: ἀνδριάς (ἀνήρ) the image of a man, a statue, Hdt., attic

ανδριζω.def: ἀνδρίζω (ἀνήρ) to make a man of: Pass. or Mid. to come to manhood, behave like a man, play the man, Plat.

ανδρικοσ.def: ἀνδρικός (ἀνήρ) I. of or for a man, masculine, manly, Lat. virilis, Plat.; ἀνδρ. ἱδρώς the sweat of manly toil, Ar.:—adv. -κῶς, like a man, comp. -ώτερον, Sup. -ώτατα, id. II. composed of men, χορός Xen.

ανδριον.def: ἀνδρίον (Dim. of ἀνήρ) a manikin, Ar., Theocr.

ανδριστεοσ.def: ἀνδριστέος (ἀνδρίζομαι.) one must play the man, Plat.

ανδριστι.def: ἀνδριστί (ἀνήρ) like a man, like men, Ar., Theocr.

ανδροβουλοσ.def: ἀνδρόβουλος (ἀνήρ, βουλή) of manly counsel, man-minded, Aesch.

ανδρογυνοσ.def: ἀνδρόγυνος (ἀνήρ, γυνή) I. a man-woman, hermaphrodite, Plat. 2. a womanish man, effeminate person, Hdt. II. as adj. common to men and women, Anth.

ανδροθεα.def: ἀνδροθέα the man-goddess, i. e. Athena, Anth.

ανδροθεν.def: ἀνδρόθεν (ἀνήρ) from a man or men, Anth.

ανδροκμησ.def: ἀνδροκμής (ἀνήρ, κάμνω) man-wearying, Aesch.: man-slaying, id.

ανδροκμητοσ.def: ἀνδρόκμητος (κάμνω) wrought by men's hands, Il.

ανδροκτασια.def: ἀνδροκτασία (ἀνήρ, κτείνω) slaughter of men in battle, Il., Aesch.

ανδροκτονεω.def: ἀνδροκτονέω (from ἀνδροκτόνος) to slay men, Aesch.

ανδροκτονοσ.def: ἀνδροκτόνος (ἀνήρ, κτείνω) man-slaying, murdering, Hdt., Eur.

ανδροληψια.def: ἀνδροληψία (ἀνήρ, λαμβάνω) seizure of men guilty of murdering a citizen abroad, Lex. ap. Dem.

ανδρομαχοσ.def: ἀνδρομάχος (ἀνήρ, μάχομαι) fighting with men, Anth.; fem. ἀνδρομάχη id.

ανδρομεοσ.def: ἀνδρόμεος (ἀνήρ) of man or men, human, κρέα Hom.; ψωμοὶ ἀνδρ. goblets of man's flesh, Od.

ανδρομηκησ.def: ἀνδρομήκης (ἀνήρ, μῆκος) of a man's height, Xen.

ανδροπαισ.def: ἀνδρόπαις (ἀνήρ) a man-boy, i. e. a youth near manhood, Aesch.

ανδροπληθεια.def: ἀνδροπλήθεια (ἀνήρ, πλῆθος) a multitude of men, Aesch.

ανδροσινισ.def: ἀνδρόσινις (ἀνήρ, σίνομαι) hurtful to men, Anth.

ανδροσφαγειον.def: ἀνδροσφαγεῖον (ἀνήρ, σφάζω) a slaughter-house of men, Aesch.

ανδροσφιγξ.gloss: a man-sphinx, sphinx with the bust of a man
ανδροσφιγξ.def: ἀνδρόσφιγξ (ἀνήρ) a man-sphinx, sphinx with the bust of a man, not (as usually) of a woman, Hdt.

ανδροτησ.def: ἀνδρότης manliness, manhood, courage, = ἀνδρεία: cf. ἁδροτής.

ανδροτυχησ.def: ἀνδροτυχής (ἀνήρ, τυγχάνω) getting a husband, ἀνδρ. βίοτος wedded life, Aesch.

ανδροφαγεω.def: ἀνδροφαγέω (from ἀνδροφάγος) to eat men, Hdt.

ανδροφθοροσ.def: ἀνδρόφθορος (φθείρω) (cf. ἀνδροφθόρος) ἀνδρόφθορον αἷμα the blood of a slain man, id.
ἀνδροφθόρος (φθείρω) (cf. ἀνδρόφθορος) I. man-destroying, murderous, Soph.

ανδροφονια.def: ἀνδροφονία (ἀνδροφόνος) slaughter of men, Arist., Plut.

ανδροφονοσ.def: ἀνδροφόνος (ἀνήρ, Φένω) I. man-slaying, Il. 2. of women, murdering husbands, Pind. II. as law-term, one convicted of manslaughter, a homicide, Plat., Dem.

ανδροω.def: ἀνδρόω (ἀνήρ) I. to rear up into manhood, Anth.: —Pass. to become a man, reach manhood, Hdt., Eur. II. in Pass. also of a woman, to be of marriageable age, Eur.

ανδρωδησ.def: ἀνδρώδης (ἀνήρ, εἶδος) like a man, manly, Isocr. adv., -δῶς, Sup. -δέστατα, Xen.

ανδρων.def: ἀνδρών (ἀνήρ) the men's apartment in a house, the banqueting hall, etc., Hdt., Aesch., etc.; ionic ἀνδρεών, Hdt.; epic -ειών, Anth.:—also ἀνδρωνῖτις, ιδος, ἡ Xen.

ανεβραχε.def: ἀνέβραχε (⁎βράχω) (no pres. in use) clashed or rung loudly, of armour, Il.; creaked or grated loudly, of a door, Od.

ανεγγυοσ.def: ἀνέγγυος (ἐγγύη) not accredited, Plat.; of a woman, unwedded, Plut.

ανεγειρω.def: ἀνεγείρω I. to wake up, rouse, ἐξ ὕπνου, ἐκ λεχέων Hom.:—Pass., Eur., Xen. 2. metaph. to wake up, raise, Pind. 3. metaph. also to rouse, encourage, Od. II. of buildings, to raise, Anth.

ανεγκλητοσ.gloss: not accused, without reproach, void of offence
ανεγκλητοσ.def: ἀνέγκλητος (ἐγκαλέω) not accused, without reproach, void of offence, Xen., etc.:—adv. -τως, Dem.

ανεδην.def: ἀνέδην (ἀνίημι) I. let loose, freely, without restraint, Plat., Dem.:— remissly, carelessly, Soph. II. without more ado, absolutely, Plat.

ανειλειθυια.def: ἀνειλείθυια without the aid of Eileithuia, Eur.

ανειλεω.def: ἀνειλέω 1. to roll up together:— Pass. to crowd or throng together, Thuc. 2. ἀνείλω, Pass. to shrink up or back, Plat.

ανειμενοσοσ.gloss: let go free, released from labour
ανειμενοσοσ.def: ἀνειμένοσος (part. perf. pass. of ἀνίημι, used as adj.) I. let go free, released from labour, of animals dedicated to the gods, Soph.: metaph., ἀν. ἔς τι devoted to a thing, Hdt. II. remiss, slack, unconstrained, Thuc.; ἐν τῶι ἀνειμένωι τῆς γνώμης when their minds are unstrung, id.:—adv. ἀνειμένως, at ease, carelessly, without restraint, Thuc., Xen.

ανειμι.def: ἄνειμι (εῖμι, ibo, in attic serving as fut. to ἀνέρχομαι.) I. to go up, Hom., etc.; ἅμ’ ἠελίωι ἀνιόντι at sun- rise, Il. 2. to sail up, i. e. out to sea, Od. 3. to go up inland, esp. into Central Asia, Plat. II. to approach, esp. as a suppliant, Il. III. to go back, go home, return, Od., Hdt., etc.

ανειπειν.def: ἀνειπεῖν (aor2 with no pres. in use, ἀναγορεύω being used instead.) I. to say aloud, announce, proclaim, Pind., Xen.: —c. acc. et inf. to make proclamation that.., Ar., Thuc.:—in the Athen. assemblies, ἀνεῖπεν ὁ κῆρυξ Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be proclaimed, ἀναρρηθέντος τοῦ στεφάνου when the crown was proclaimed, Dem. II. to call upon, invoke, Plut.

ανειργω.def: ἀνείργω to keep back, restrain, Hom., Xen.

ανειρω.def: ἀνείρω to fasten on or to, to string, Hdt.; ἀν. στεφάνους to twine or wreathe them, Ar.

ανεισοδοσ.def: ἀνείσοδος without entrance or access, Plut.

ανεισφορια.def: ἀνεισφορία (from ἀνείσφορος) exemption from the εἰσφορά, Plut.

ανεισφοροσ.def: ἀνείσφορος exempt from the εἰσφορά, Plut.

ανεκαθεν.def: ἀνέκαθεν (ἀνεκάς) I. adv. of Place, from above, Hdt., Aesch. II. of Time, from the first, by origin, Hdt.; so with Art., τὸ ἀνέκαθεν id.

ανεκασ.def: ἀνεκάς upwards, Lat. sursum, Pind., attic

ανεκδοτοσ.def: ἀνέκδοτος not given in marriage, Dem., etc.

ανεκπιμπλημι.def: ἀνεκπίμπλημι to fill up or again, Xen.

ανεκπληκτοσ.def: ἀνέκπληκτος (ἐκπλήσσω) undaunted, intrepid, Plat.:— τὸ ἀνέκπληκτον intrepidity, Xen.

ανεκτεοσ.def: ἀνεκτέος (verb. adj. of ἀνέχομαι.) to be borne, Soph.

ανεκτοσ.def: ἀνεκτός (verb. adj. of ἀνέχομαι.) I. bearable, sufferable, tolerable, mostly with a negat., Il., attic 2. without a negat. that can be endured, Od., Thuc. II. adv. -τως, Hom.; οὐκ ἀνεκτῶς ἔχει it is not to be borne, Xen.

ανελεγκτοσ.gloss: not cross-questioned, safe from being questioned
ανελεγκτοσ.def: ἀνέλεγκτος (ἐλέγχω) 1. not cross-questioned, safe from being questioned, Thuc.: unconvicted, id. 2. not refuted, irrefutable, Plat.:—adv. -τως, without refutation, Plut.

ανελεγχω.def: ἀνελέγχω to convince or convict utterly, Eur.

ανελευθεροσ.gloss: not fit for a free man
ανελευθεροσ.def: ἀνελεύθερος I. not fit for a free man, Aesch., Arist. 2. illiberal, servile, Plat., etc. 3. in money matters, niggardly, stingy, Ar. II. adv. -ρως, meanly, Xen.

ανελιγμα.def: ἀνέλιγμα (from ἀνελίσσω) anything rolled up, a ringlet, Anth.

ανελισσω.def: ἀνελίσσω I. to unroll a book written on a roll, i. e. to unfold, read, interpret, Xen.; ἀν. βίον to pass one's whole life, Plut. 2. to cause to move backward, πόδα Eur. II. to cause to revolve:— Pass. to revolve, move glibly, Ar.

ανελκω.def: ἀνέλκω I. to draw up, τάλαντα ἀνέλκει holds them up (in weighing), Il.; ἀνελκύσαι ναῦς to haul them up high and dry, Hdt., Thuc. 2. to drag up, drag into open court or into the witness-box, Ar.:— Mid., ἀνέλκεσθαι τρίχας to tear one's own hair, Il. II. to draw a bow, in act to shoot, Hom.:—Mid., ἔγχος ἀνελκόμενος drawing back his spear [out of the corpse], Od.

ανελπιστοσ.def: ἀνέλπιστος (ἐλπίζω) I. unhoped for, unlooked for, Trag., etc.; τὸ ἀνέλπιστον τοῦ βεβαίου the hopelessness of security, Thuc. II. act., 1. of persons, having no hope, hopeless, Theocr.; c. inf. having no hope or not expecting that.., Thuc. 2. of things or conditions, leaving no hope, hopeless, desperate, Soph., Thuc.; τὸ ἀνέλπιστον despair, Thuc.:—comp. -ότερος more desperate, id.

ανεμβατοσ.def: ἀνέμβατος (ἐμβαίνω) 1. inaccessible, Babr., Plut. 2. act. not going to or visiting, Anth.

ανεμεσητοσ.def: ἀνεμέσητος free from blame, without offence, Plat.

ανεμητοσ.def: ἀνέμητος (νέμω) 1. not distributed, Dem. 2. act. having no share, Plut.

ανεμιζομαι.gloss: to be driven with the wind
ανεμιζομαι.def: ἀνεμίζομαι (ἄνεμος) Pass. to be driven with the wind, NTest.

ανεμοδρομοσ.def: ἀνεμόδρομος running with the wind, Luc.

ανεμολον.def: ἀνέμολον to go through, c. acc., Eur.

ανεμοσ.def: ἄνεμος (Root ΑΝ, cf. ἄημι) wind, Hom., etc.; ἀνέμου κατιόντος a squall having come on, Thuc.; ἄν. κατὰ βορέαν ἑστηκώς the wind being settled in the north, id.; ἀνέμοις φέρεσθαι παραδοῦναί τι to cast a thing to the winds, Lat. ventis tradere, Eur.:—Hom. and Hes. mention only four winds, Boreas, Eurus, Notus (or Argestes), Zephyrus; Arist. gives twelve, which served as points of the compass.

ανεμοσκεπησ.def: ἀνεμοσκεπής (σκέπη) sheltering from the wind, Il.

ανεμοσφαραγοσ.def: ἀνεμοσφάραγος echoing to the wind, Pind.

ανεμοτρεφησ.def: ἀνεμοτρεφής (τρέφω) fed by the wind, of a wave, Il.; ἔγχος ἀνεμ. a spear from a tree reared by the wind, i. e. made tough by battling with the wind, id.

ανεμοω.def: ἀνεμόω (ἄνεμος) to expose to the wind:— Pass., of the sea, to be raised by the wind, Anth.

ανεμωκησ.def: ἀνεμώκης (ὠκύς) swift as the wind, Eur., Ar.

ανεμωλιοσ.def: ἀνεμώλιος (ἄνεμος) windy: metaph., ἀνεμώλια βάζειν to talk words of wind, Hom.; οἱ δ’ αὖτ’ ἀνεμώλιοι are like the winds, i. e. good for naught, Il.; τί νυ τόξον ἔχεις ἀνεμώλιον; why bear thy bow in vain? id.; ἀνεμώλιος empty fool! Anth.

ανενδεησ.def: ἀνενδεής in want of naught, Anth.

ανεξελεγκτοσ.def: ἀνεξέλεγκτος (ἐξελέγχω) 1. unquestioned, impossible to be questioned or refuted, of statements or arguments, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔχει τὸ ἀνδρεῖον leaves their courage without proof, id. 2. of persons, not to be convicted, irreproachable, Xen., etc.

ανεξεταστοσ.def: ἀνεξέταστος (ἐξετάζω) I. not inquired into or examined, Dem. II. uninquiring, Plat.

ανεξευρετοσ.def: ἀνεξεύρετος (ἐξευρίσκω) not to be found out, Thuc.

ανεξικακοσ.def: ἀνεξίκακος (ἀνέχομαι, κακόν) enduring evil, forbearing, long-suffering, NTest., Luc.

ανεξιχνιαστοσ.gloss: not to be traced, unsearchable, inscrutable
ανεξιχνιαστοσ.def: ἀνεξιχνίαστος (ἐκ, ἴχνιον) not to be traced, unsearchable, inscrutable, NTest.

ανεξοδοσ.gloss: with no outlet, allowing no return
ανεξοδοσ.def: ἀνέξοδος with no outlet, allowing no return, Lat. irremeabilis, Theocr.

ανεορτοσ.def: ἀνέορτος (ἑορτή) without festival, c. gen., ἀν. ἱερῶν without share in festal rites, Eur.

ανεπαισχυντοσ.def: ἀνεπαίσχυντος (ἐπαισχύνομαι) having no cause for shame, NTest.

ανεπαφοσ.def: ἀνέπαφος (ἐπαφή) untouched, ἀν. παρέχειν τι rem integram praestare, Dem.

ανεπαχθησ.def: ἀνεπαχθής not burdensome, without offence, Plut., Luc.:—adv. -θῶς, Thuc.

ανεπιβουλευτοσ.def: ἀνεπιβούλευτος (ἐπιβουλεύω) without plots, τὸ ἀνεπιβούλευτον the absence of intrigue, Thuc.

ανεπιγραφοσ.def: ἀνεπίγραφος (ἐπιγράφω) without title or inscription: metaph. without noticeable features, Luc.

ανεπιδικοσ.gloss: not disputed by legal process, undisputed
ανεπιδικοσ.def: ἀνεπίδικος (ἐπί, δίκη) not disputed by legal process, undisputed, Dem.

ανεπικλητοσ.def: ἀνεπίκλητος (ἐπικαλέω) I. unaccused, unblamed, Xen. II. without preferring any charge:— adv. -τως, Thuc.

ανεπιληπτοσ.gloss: not open to attack, not censured, blameless
ανεπιληπτοσ.def: ἀνεπίληπτος not open to attack, not censured, blameless, Eur., Thuc.: adv. -τως, Xen.

ανεπιμικτοσ.def: ἀνεπίμικτος (ἐπιμίγνυμι) not mixing with others, unsocial, Plut.

ανεπιξεστοσ.def: ἀνεπίξεστος (ἐπί, ξέω) not polished or finished, Hes.

ανεπιπλεκτοσ.def: ἀνεπίπλεκτος (ἐπί, πλέκω) without connexion with others, isolated, Strab.

ανεπισκεπτοσ.def: ἀνεπίσκεπτος (ἐπισκέπτομαι) I. inattentive, inconsiderate: adv. -τως, Hdt. II. pass. not examined, unregarded, Xen.

ανεπιστημοσυνη.def: ἀνεπιστημοσύνη (From ἀνεπιστήμων) want of knowledge, ignorance, unskilfulness, Thuc.

ανεπιστημων.def: ἀνεπιστήμων I. not knowing, ignorant, unskilful, Hdt., Thuc.; ναῦς ἀνεπιστήμονες ships with unskilful crews, Thuc.;—c. gen. rei, unskilled in a thing, Plat.; c. inf. not knowing how to do a thing, Xen. II. without knowledge, unintelligent: comp. ἀνεπιστημονέστερος less intelligent, Hdt.

ανεπιτακτοσ.def: ἀνεπίτακτος subject to no control, Thuc.

ανεπιτηδειοσ.def: ἀνεπιτήδειος 1. unserviceable, unfit, Xen., Plat., etc.:— mischievous, prejudicial, hurtful, Hdt., Thuc. 2. unkind, unfriendly, Thuc., Xen.

ανεπιτηδευτοσ.def: ἀνεπιτήδευτος (ἐπιτηδεύω) I. made without care or design, simple, artless, Luc. II. unpractised, untried, Plut.

ανεπιτιμητοσ.def: ἀνεπιτίμητος (ἐπιτιμάω) not to be censured, τινος for a thing, Dem.

ανεπιφθονοσ.def: ἀνεπίφθονος without reproach, Soph.; ἀν. ἐστι πᾶσιν ’tis no reproach to any one, Thuc.; ἀνεπιφθονώτατον least invidious, Dem. adv. -νως so as not to create odium, Thuc.

ανεραμαι.def: ἀνέραμαι (ἐράω) to love again, love anew, c. gen., Andoc., Xen.

ανεραστοσ.def: ἀνέραστος I. not loved, Luc. II. act. not loving, Anth.

ανερεθιζω.def: ἀνερεθίζω to stir up, excite, Plut.:—Pass. to be in a state of excitement, Thuc., Xen.

ανερειπομαι.gloss: to snatch up and carry off
ανερειπομαι.def: ἀνερείπομαι Dep., only used in aor1, to snatch up and carry off, ἀνηρείψαντο Hom.; ἀνερειψαμένη Hes.

ανερευναω.def: ἀνερευνάω to examine closely, investigate, Plat.

ανερευνητοσ.def: ἀνερεύνητος (ἐρευνάω) 1. not investigated, Plat. 2. that cannot be found out, inscrutable, Eur.

ανερομαι.def: ἀνέρομαι 1. c. acc. pers. to enquire of, question, Od., Soph. 2. c. acc. rei, to ask about, Od., Plat. 3. c. dupl. acc. to ask a person about a thing, Il., Soph.

ανερπω.def: ἀνέρπω to creep up or upwards, Ar., Luc.

ανερρω.def: ἀνέρρω to go quite away: ἄνερρε away with you, Lat. abi in malam rem, Eur.

ανερυθριαω.gloss: to begin to blush, blush up
ανερυθριαω.def: ἀνερυθριάω to begin to blush, blush up, Xen.

ανερυω.def: ἀνερύω to draw up, haul up sails, Od.: to haul ships up on land, Hdt.: —Mid. to deliver, Anth.

ανερχομαι.def: ἀνέρχομαι (ἄνειμι) I. to go up, Od., attic: absol. to mount the tribune, Plut.:— to go up from the coast inland, Od.:— to come up from the nether world, Theogn., Soph. 2. of trees, to grow up, shoot up, Od.: of the sun, to rise, Aesch.:—metaph., ὄλβος ἀν. Eur. II. to go or come back, go or come home again, return, Hom. 2. to come back to a point, recur, Eur., Plat. 3. νόμος εἴς ς’ ἀνελθών a law brought home or having relation to you, Eur.

ανερωταω.def: ἀνερωτάω 1. c. acc. pers. to ask or inquire of, question, Od., Plat. 2. c. acc. rei, to ask about, inquire into, Plat.; so, ἀν. περί τινος Hdt. 3. c. dupl. acc. to question a person about a thing, ask it of him, Eur., Ar.

ανεσισ.def: ἄνεσις (ἀνίημι) I. a loosening, relaxing of strings, Plat., etc. 2. metaph. remission, abatement, κακῶν Hdt.; ἄν. φόρων, τελῶν remission of tribute, taxes, Plut. 3. relaxation, recreation, Plat., Arist. II. a letting loose, indulgence, license, Plat., Arist.

ανεστιοσ.def: ἀνέστιος (ἑστία) without hearth and home, homeless, Il., Ar.

ανετεοσ.def: ἀνετέος (verb. adj. of ἀνίημι) one must dismiss, Plat.

ανευ.def: ἄνευ (ἀνά) I. prep. c. gen. without, οὐκ ἄνευ θεῶν, Lat. non sine Diis, not without divine aid, Od.; ἄνευ ἐμέθεν without my knowledge, Il.; ἄνευ πολιτῶν without their consent, Aesch. II. away from, far from, ἄνευ δηΐων Il. III. in Prose, except, besides, like χωρίς, Xen.

ανευθε.def: ἄνευθε (ἄνευ) (ἄνευθεν before a vowel) 1. prep. c. gen., without, Hom. 2. away from, Il. II. adv. far away, distant, Hom.

ανευθυνοσ.gloss: not having to render an account, irresponsible
ανευθυνοσ.def: ἀνεύθυνος (εὔθυναι) 1. not having to render an account, irresponsible, Hdt., Thuc. 2. guiltless, because such a one is not liable to trial, Luc.; c. gen. guiltless of.., id.

ανευκτοσ.def: ἄνευκτος not wishing, not praying, Anth.

ανευρεσισ.def: ἀνεύρεσις (From ἀνευρίσκω) a discovery, Eur., Plut.

ανευρισκω.gloss: to find out, make out, discover
ανευρισκω.def: ἀνευρίσκω to find out, make out, discover, Hdt., attic: —Pass. to be found out or discovered, Thuc.; c. part. to be discovered to be.., Hdt.

ανευφημεω.def: ἀνευφημέω to shout εὐφήμει or εὐφημεῖτε: as this was mainly done on sorrowful occasions, to cry aloud, shriek, Eur., etc.; ἀνευφήμησεν οἰμωγῆι Soph.

ανεφελοσ.def: ἀνέφελος (νεφέλη) unclouded, cloudless, Od.: metaph. not to be veiled or concealed, Soph.

ανεχεγγυοσ.def: ἀνεχέγγυος not giving surety or confidence, Thuc.

ανεχω.def: ἀνέχω A. trans. to hold up one's hands in fight, Od.; also in token of defeat, Theocr.:— to lift up the hands in prayer, Il., etc. 2. ἀν. φλόγα to hold up a torch at weddings, Eur.; hence ἄνεχε, πάρεχε (sc. τὸ φῶς), i. e. make ready, go on, id.; also, ἀν. φῶς σωτήριον to hold up a signal fire, Thuc. 3. to lift up, exalt, τινά Pind. 4. metaph. to uphold, maintain, Od., Thuc.; ἀνέχων λέκτρα remaining constant to the bed, Eur.; so, ἀν. κισσόν Soph. 5. to put forth, πτόρθους Eur. II. to hold back, Il.; ἀν. Σικελίαν μὴ ὑπό τινα εἶναι to keep it from being subject, Thuc. B. intr. to rise up, rise, emerge from water, Od., Hdt.:—esp. in form ἀνίσχω, of the sun, Hdt., Xen. 2. of events, to arise, happen, Hdt. 3. to appear, shew oneself, Soph. 4. to project, Il.; of a headland, to jut out, Hdt., Thuc. 5. to hold on, keep doing, c. part., Thuc.; στέρξας ἀνέχει is constant in his love, Soph.; c. acc. et inf. to aver constantly that.., id. 6. to hold up, cease, Theogn.:—generally, to wait, delay, Thuc. 7. c. gen. to cease from suffering, get rest from pain, Soph. C. Mid. to hold up what is one's own, ἔγχος, χεῖρας Il.; hence ἀνασχόμενος absol. (sub. ἔγχος etc.), id. II. to hold oneself up, bear up, hold out, Il.; aor2 imperat. ἀνάσχεο, epic ἄνσχεο, be of good courage, id.:—in part., ἀνεχόμενοι with patience, Hdt. 2. c. acc. to bear up against, Il., Hdt., attic:— so, c. gen., Od., Plat. 3. the dependent clause is added in part., οὔ σε ἀνέξομαι ἄλγε’ ἔχοντα I will not suffer thee to have.., Il., etc.; οὐ σῖγ’ ἀνέχει (sc. ὤν); Soph. 4. c. inf. to suffer, Aesch.

ανεψιαδουσ.def: ἀνεψιαδοῦς a first-cousin's son, or second cousin, Dem.

ανεψιοσ.def: ἀνεψιός (From α euphon. or α copul., and ΝΕΠ, whence also Lat. nepos, neptis.) 1. a first-cousin, cousin, Il., Hdt., attic 2. a nephew, Hdt. (When the ult. is long, Hom. lengthens also the penult., ἀνεψῑοῦ κταμένοιο.)

ανεω.def: ἄνεω (α privat., αὔω to cry) without a sound, in silence, in Od. certainly an Adv.; in other places it may be nom. pl. ἄνεωι, from ἄν-εως ἄν-αυος

ανηβαω.def: ἀνηβάω to grow young again, Theogn., Eur., etc.

ανηβητηριοσ.def: ἀνηβητήριος (ἀνά, ἡβάω) returning as in youth, Eur.

ανηβοσ.gloss: not yet come to man's estate, beardless
ανηβοσ.def: ἄνηβος (ἥβη) not yet come to man's estate, beardless, Plat., Theocr.

ανηγεομαι.gloss: to tell as in a narrative, relate, recount
ανηγεομαι.def: ἀνηγέομαι 1. Dep. to tell as in a narrative, relate, recount, Pind., Hdt. 2. intr. to advance, Pind.

ανηδυντοσ.def: ἀνήδυντος not sweetened or seasoned, Arist.: unpleasant, Plut.

ανηθινοσ.def: ἀνήθινος (ἄνηθον) made of anise or dill, Theocr.

ανηθον.def: ἄνηθον (Deriv. unknown.) anise, dill, Ar., Theocr.; ionic ἄννησον or ἄνησον Hdt.; aeolic ἄννητον, or ἄνητον, Sapph..

ανηκεστοσ.gloss: not to be healed, incurable, irreparable, fatal
ανηκεστοσ.def: ἀνήκεστος (ἀκέομαι) I. not to be healed, incurable, irreparable, fatal, Il., Hdt., attic; ἀνήκεστα ποιεῖν τινα to do one irreparable injuries, Xen.; ἀνήκεστα πάσχειν Thuc. 2. of persons, implacable, Xen. II. act. damaging beyond remedy, deadly, Soph.:—adv., ἀνηκέστως διατιθέναι to treat with barbarous cruelty, Hdt.

ανηκοοσ.def: ἀνήκοος (ἀκοή) 1. without hearing, of the dead, Mosch. 2. c. gen. not hearing a thing, never having heard it, ignorant of it, Xen., etc.:—absol., σκαιὸς καὶ ἀν. ignorant, Dem.

ανηκουστεω.gloss: to be unwilling to hear, to disobey
ανηκουστεω.def: ἀνηκουστέω (from ἀνήκουστος) to be unwilling to hear, to disobey, c. gen., Il., Aesch., Thuc.; c. dat., Hdt.; absol., id.

ανηκουστοσ.def: ἀνήκουστος (ἀκούω) I. unheard of, Lat. inauditus, ἤκους’ ἀνήκουστα Soph. II. act. not willing to hear: τὸ ἀνήκουστον disobedience, Xen.

ανηκω.def: ἀνήκω I. to have come up to a point, reach up to, of persons, αἱμασιὴν ἀνήκουσαν ἀνδρὶ ἐς τὸν ὀμφαλόν a wall reaching up to a man's middle, Hdt.; ἀν. ἐς τὰ μέγιστα to reach up to the highest point, id. 2. of things, τοῦτο ἐς οὐδὲν ἀν. amounts to nothing, id.; αἱ πολλαὶ [ζημίαι] ἐς τὸν θάνατον ἀν. have gone as far as death, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔς σε ἔχειν it has come to you to have, has become yours to have, Hdt. II. to appertain, be fit or proper, NTest.; τὸ ἀνῆκον what is fit and proper, id.

ανηλεησ.def: ἀνηλεής (ἔλεος) without pity, unmerciful:— adv. -εῶς, Andoc.

ανηλιποσ.def: ἀνήλιπος (ἦλιψ a kind of shoe) unshod, barefoot, Theocr.

ανημεροσ.def: ἀνήμερος not tame, wild, savage, of persons and countries, Aesch.

ανηνεμοσ.def: ἀνήνεμος (ἄνεμος) without wind, ἀνήνεμος χειμώνων without the blast of storms, Soph.

ανηνοθε.def: ἀνήνοθε (Formed as if from ⁎ἀνέθω (ἀνά) to rise up; cf. ἐνήνοθε.) (epic perf. with aor. signf.) αἷμα ἀνήνοθεν ἐξ ὠτειλῆς blood gushed forth from the wound, Il.; κνίση ἀνήνοθεν the savour mounted up, Od.

ανηνυτοσ.def: ἀνήνυτος 1. = ἀνήνυστος, Soph., Plat. 2. endless, Plat.

ανηπυω.def: ἀνηπύω (v. ἠπύω) to cry aloud, roar, Mosch.

ανηρ.def: ἀνήρ (Root ΑΝΕΡ) a man, Lat. vir (not homo): I. a man, opp. to a woman, Hom., etc. II. a man, opp. to a god, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε id. III. a man, opp. to a youth, a man in the prime of life, id., etc.; εἰς ἄνδρας ἐγγράφεσθαι to be enrolled among the men, Dem. IV. a man emphatically, a man indeed, ἀνέρες ἔστε, φίλοι Il.; πολλοὶ μὲν ἄνθρωποι, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἄνδρες many human beings, but few men, Hdt. V. a man, opp. to his wife, a husband, Hom., etc.; αἰγῶν ἄνερ, Virgil's vir gregis, Theocr.

ανηφαιστοσ.def: ἀνήφαιστος without real fire, πῦρ ἀνήφαιστον, i. e. the fire of discord, Eur.

ανθαιρεομαι.def: ἀνθαιρέομαι I. Dep.:— to choose one person or thing instead of another, τινά (or τί) τινος Eur.; to prefer, choose rather, id. II. to dispute, lay claim to, τι id.

ανθαλισκομαι.def: ἀνθαλίσκομαι Pass. to be captured in turn, ἁλόντες αὖθις ἀνθαλοῖεν ἄν Aesch.

ανθαμιλλαομαι.gloss: to vie one with another, to race one another
ανθαμιλλαομαι.def: ἀνθαμιλλάομαι Dep. to vie one with another, to race one another, Xen.

ανθαπτομαι.gloss: to lay hold of in turn
ανθαπτομαι.def: ἀνθάπτομαι I. Dep. to lay hold of in turn, c. gen., Hdt., Eur. II. simply to lay hold of, grapple with, engage in, c. gen., Hdt., Thuc.: generally, to reach, attain, τερμόνων Eur. 2. to lay hold of, attack, πλευμόνων, φρενῶν, Soph., Eur.

ανθεκτεοσ.def: ἀνθεκτέος (verb. adj. of ἀντέχω) one must cleave to, c. gen., Plat.; so in pl. ἀνθεκτέα, Thuc.

ανθελκω.def: ἀνθέλκω to draw or pull against, Thuc.; ἀνθ. ἀλλήλαις to pull against one another, Plat.

ανθεμιον.def: ἀνθέμιον (= ἄνθος.) ἀνθέμιον ἐστιγμένος tattooed with flowers, Xen.

ανθεμοεισ.def: ἀνθεμόεις (from ἄνθεμον) I. flowery, of meadows, Il. II. of works in metal, bright, burnished, or wrought with flowers, Hom.; of tapestry, flowered, Anth.

ανθεμον.def: ἄνθεμον (ἀνθέω, ἄνθος, Sapph., Ar.) ἄνθεμα χρυσοῦ, i. e. the costliest gold, Pind.

ανθεμορρυτοσ.def: ἀνθεμόρρυτος (ῥέω) flowing from flowers, of honey, Eur.

ανθεμουργοσ.def: ἀνθεμουργός (⁎ἔργω) working in flowers, of bees, Aesch.

ανθερεων.def: ἀνθερεών (ἀνθέω) the chin or part on which the beard grew, Lat. mentum, Il.

ανθεριξ.def: ἀνθέριξ (ἄνθος, ἀθήρ) I. the beard of an ear of corn, the ear itself, Lat. spica, Il. II. = the stalk of asphodel, Hdt., Theocr.

ανθεστηρια.def: Ἀνθεστήρια (ἄνθος) the feast of flowers, i.e. the three days' festival of Dionysus at Athens, in the month Anthesterion.

ανθεστηριων.def: Ἀνθεστηριών the month Anthesterion, eighth of the Attic year, answering to the end of February and the beginning of March.

ανθεστιαω.def: ἀνθεστιάω (ἀντί, ἑστιάω) to entertain in return or mutually, Plut.

ανθεσφοροσ.def: ἀνθεσφόρος (ἄνθος, φέρω) bearing flowers, flowering, Eur.

ανθεω.def: ἀνθέω (ἄνθος) I. to blossom, bloom, of the youthful beard, Od.; of flowers and plants, Hes., etc. II. metaph., 1. to be bright with colour, ἀνθεῖν φοινικίσι Xen. 2. to be in bloom, Pind.; ἐν ὥραι, ἐφ’ ὥραι ἀνθεῖν to be in the bloom of youth, Plat. 3. to flourish in wealth and prosperity, Hes., Hdt., attic; c. dat., ἀνθ. ἀνδράσι to abound in men, Hdt. 4. to be at the height or pitch, Aesch., Soph.

ανθηροσ.def: ἀνθηρός (ἀνθέω) I. flowering, blooming, Ar. II. metaph. blooming, fresh, Eur., Xen. 2. ἀνθηρὸν μένος rage bursting into flower, i. e. at its height, Soph. 3. bright-coloured, bright, Eur.; τὸ ἀνθ. brightness, Luc.

ανθησσαομαι.def: ἀνθησσάομαι Pass. to give way in turn, τινί Thuc.

ανθιζω.def: ἀνθίζω (ἄνθος) 1. to strew or deck with flowers, Eur. 2. to dye with bright colour: Pass., Hdt.; metaph., ἠνθισμένος dyed, disguised, Soph.

ανθινοσ.def: ἀνθινός (ἄνθος) I. like flowers, blooming, fresh, ἄνθινον εἶδαρ, of the lotus, Od. II. bright-coloured, Lat. floridus, of women's dress, Plut.

ανθιππασια.def: ἀνθιππασία a sham-fight of horse, Xen.

ανθιππευω.def: ἀνθιππεύω to ride against, ἀλλήλοις Xen.

ανθιστημι.def: ἀνθίστημι I. to set against, Ar., Thuc.: to set up in opposition, Thuc. 2. to match with, compare, Plut. II. Pass., with intr. aor2 act. ἀντέστην, perf. ἀνθέστηκα, attic contr. part. ἀνθεστώς: fut. mid. ἀντιστήσομαι, aor1 ἀντεστησάμην and pass. ἀντεστάθην [α]:— to stand against, esp. in battle, to withstand, oppose, τινι Il., Hdt., attic; also, πρός τινα Thuc., etc.: rarely c. gen., φρενῶν ἀνθίσταται (al. ἀνθάπτεται) Aesch. 2. absol. to make a stand, Il., Hdt.

ανθοβολεω.def: ἀνθοβολέω (from ἀνθόβολος) to bestrew with flowers, Anth.:— Pass. to have flowers showered upon one, Plut.

ανθοκομεω.def: ἀνθοκομέω (from ἀνθοκόμος) to produce flowers, Anth.

ανθοκομοσ.def: ἀνθοκόμος (κόμη) decked with flowers, flowery, Anth.

ανθοκροκοσ.def: ἀνθόκροκος (κρέκω) worked with flowers or brightcoloured, Eur.

ανθολκη.gloss: a pulling in the contrary direction, resistance
ανθολκη.def: ἀνθολκή (ἀνθέλκω) a pulling in the contrary direction, resistance, Plut.

ανθολογια.def: ἀνθολογία a flower-gathering, Luc.: Ἀνθολογίαι were collections of small Greek poems and epigrams by several authors, which the editor made up into a posy or nosegay.

ανθολογοσ.def: ἀνθολόγος (λέγω) flower-gathering, Anth.; c. gen. culling the flower of.., id.

ανθομολογεομαι.def: ἀνθομολογέομαι I. Mid. to make a mutual agreement, πρός τινα Dem. II. to confess freely and openly, Plut. III. to return thanks, NTest.

ανθοπλιζω.def: ἀνθοπλίζω to arm against: Pass. to be arrayed against, τινί Eur.:—Mid. to arm oneself, Xen.

ανθορμεω.gloss: to lie at anchor opposite to
ανθορμεω.def: ἀνθορμέω to lie at anchor opposite to, τινί Thuc.; πρός τινα id.

ανθοσ.def: ἄνθος (note that ἀνθέων shows up even in Attic.) I. a blossom, flower, Hom., etc. 2. generally, anything thrown out upon the surface, froth, scum. II. metaph. the bloom or flower of life, ἥβης ἄνθος Il.; ὥρας ἄνθος Xen.; χροιᾶς ἄνθος the bloom of complexion, Aesch.:—also, the flower of an army and the like, Aesch., Thuc.; τὸ σὸν ἄνθος thy pride or honour, Aesch. 2. the height or highest pitch of anything, bad as well as good, ἔρωτος id.; μανίας Soph. III. brightness, brilliancy, Theogn.; in pl. bright colours, Plat.; ἁλὸς ἄνθεα, i.e. purple, Anth.

ανθοσμιασ.def: ἀνθοσμίας (ἄνθος, ὀσμή) redolent of flowers, of wine, οἶνος ἀνθ. with a fine "bouquet", Ar.; so ἀνθοσμίας alone, Xen., Luc.

ανθοφορεω.def: ἀνθοφορέω (from ἀνθοφόρος) to bear flowers, Anth.

ανθοφοροσ.def: ἀνθοφόρος (φέρω) bearing flowers, flowery, Ar., Anth.

ανθρακια.gloss: a heap of charcoal, hot embers
ανθρακια.def: ἀνθρακιά (ἄνθραξ) 1. a heap of charcoal, hot embers, Il.; ἀνθρακιᾶς ἄπο hot from the embers, Eur. 2. black sooty ashes, Anth.

ανθρακιασ.gloss: a man black as a collier
ανθρακιασ.def: ἀνθρακίας (ἄνθραξ) a man black as a collier, Luc.

ανθρακιζω.gloss: to make charcoal of, to roast
ανθρακιζω.def: ἀνθρακίζω (ἄνθραξ) to make charcoal of, to roast or toast, Ar.

ανθρακοω.def: ἀνθρακόω (ἄνθραξ) Pass. ἀνθρακόομαι, to be burnt to cinders, Aesch.

ανθρηνη.def: ἀνθρήνη (Deriv. unknown.) a hornet, wasp, Ar.

ανθρωπαριον.def: ἀνθρωπάριον Dim. of ἄνθρωπος, a manikin, Ar.

ανθρωπεη.def: ἀνθρωπέη (cf. δορά) a man's skin, Hdt.

ανθρωπειοσ.def: ἀνθρώπειος I. of or belonging to man, human, Hdt., etc.; ἀνθρώπεια πήματα such as man is subject to, Aesch.; ἀνθρωπήϊα πρήγματα human affairs, man's estate, Hdt.; τὸ ἀνθρώπειον either mankind or human nature, Thuc. 2. human, of which man is capable, Hdt., Plat. 3. human, as opp. to mythical, Hdt. II. adv. -ως, humanly, in all human probability, Thuc.; ἀνθρ. φράζειν to speak as befits a man, Ar.

ανθρωπευομαι.def: ἀνθρωπεύομαι Dep. to be or act as a human being, Arist.

ανθρωπιζω.def: ἀνθρωπίζω to be or act like a man, Luc.

ανθρωπικοσ.def: ἀνθρωπικός (ἄνθρωπος) of or for a man, human, Plat. adv. -κῶς, Luc.

ανθρωπινοσ.def: ἀνθρώπινος (ἄνθρωπος) I. of, from or belonging to man, human, Hdt., etc.; ἅπαν τὸ ἀνθρώπινον all mankind, id.; τὸ ἀνθρ. γένος Plat.; τὰ ἀνθρ. πράγματα or τἀνθρώπινα human affairs, man's estate, id. 2. human, suited to man, id., Arist. II. adv., ἀνθρωπίνως ἁμαρτάνειν to commit human, i. e. venial, errors, Thuc. 2. humanely, gently, Dem.

ανθρωπιον.def: ἀνθρώπιον Dim. of ἄνθρωπος, a manikin, Lat. homuncio, Eur., Xen.: a paltry fellow, Xen.

ανθρωποδαιμων.def: ἀνθρωποδαίμων a man-god, i. e. a deified man, Eur.

ανθρωποειδησ.gloss: like a man, in human form
ανθρωποειδησ.def: ἀνθρωποειδής (εἶδος) like a man, in human form, Hdt.

ανθρωποκτονοσ.def: ἀνθρωποκτόνος (κτείνω) murdering men, a homicide, Eur.
ἀνθρωπόκτονος (κτείνω) furnished by slaughtered men, Eur.

ανθρωποποιια.def: ἀνθρωποποιΐα (from ἀνθρωποποιός) a making of man or men, Luc.

ανθρωποσ.def: ἄνθρωπος (prob. from ἀνήρ, ὤψ, manfaced) I. man, Lat. homo (not vir), opp. to gods, ἀθανάτων τε θεῶν, χαμαὶ ἐρχομένων τ’ ἀνθρώπων Il. 2. with or without the Art. to denote man generally, Plat., etc. 3. in pl. mankind, ἀνθρώπων, ἀνδρῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν Il.; ὁ ἄριστος ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὄρτυξ the best quail in the world, Plat.; μάλιστα, ἥκιστα ἀνθρώπων most, least of all, Hdt., etc. 4. with another Subst., to give it a contemptuous sense, ἄνθρ. ὑπογραμματεύς, συκοφάντης, Oratt.; so homo histrio Cic.:—so, ἄνθρωπος or ὁ ἄνθρωπος was used alone, the man, the fellow, Plat.:— also in vocat. it was addressed contemptuously to slaves, ἄνθρωπε or ὦ ’νθρωπε, sirrah! you sir! Hdt., Plat. II. fem. (as homo also is fem.), a woman, Hdt., etc.; with a sense of pity, Dem.

ανθρωποφαγεω.def: ἀνθρωποφαγέω to eat men or man's flesh, Hdt.

ανθρωποφαγια.def: ἀνθρωποφαγία (from ἀνθρωποφάγος) an eating of men, Arist.

ανθυβριζω.gloss: to abuse one another, abuse in turn
ανθυβριζω.def: ἀνθυβρίζω to abuse one another, abuse in turn, Eur., Plut.

ανθυπαγω.gloss: to bring to trial in turn
ανθυπαγω.def: ἀνθυπάγω to bring to trial in turn, Thuc.

ανθυπατευω.def: ἀνθυπατεύω (from ἀνθύπατος) to be proconsul, Plut.

ανθυπατοσ.def: ἀνθύπατος a proconsul, Lat. pro consule, Polyb., etc.

ανθυπεικω.def: ἀνθυπείκω to yield in turn, τινί Plut.

ανθυπειξισ.def: ἀνθύπειξις (from ἀνθυπείκω) a mutual yielding, Plut.

ανθυπηρετεω.def: ἀνθυπηρετέω to serve in turn, τινί Arist.

ανθυποκρινομαι.def: ἀνθυποκρίνομαι Mid. I. to answer in return, Hdt. II. to put on in turn, ὀργήν Luc.

ανθυπομνυμαι.def: ἀνθυπόμνυμαι Mid. to make a counter-affidavit, Dem.

ανθυποπτευω.def: ἀνθυποπτεύω to suspect mutually:— Pass., ἀνθυποπτεύεται he is met by the suspicion that.., Thuc.

ανθυπουργεω.def: ἀνθυπουργέω to return a kindness, τινί τι Hdt., Eur.

ανθυφισταμαι.def: ἀνθυφίσταμαι (sc. χορηγὸς γενέσθαι) to undertake to serve as choragus instead of another, Dem.

ανια.def: ἀνία (Deriv. uncertain.) (In Hom. and Soph. ῑ: in other Poets ι or ῑ.) 1. grief, sorrow, distress, trouble, Od., Hes., etc. 2. actively, δαιτὸς ἀνίη the bane of our feast, Od.

ανιαζω.def: ἀνιάζω I. to grieve, distress, c. acc. pers., Hom. II. intr. to be grieved or distressed, feel grief, id.; c. dat. at or for a thing, Il.

ανιαομαι.def: ἀνιάομαι Dep. to cure again, repair, Hdt.

ανιαροσ.def: ἀνιαρός (ἀνιάω) (In Hom and Soph. always ανῑ-, in other Poets ανι-.) I. grievous, troublesome, annoying, of persons, Od.; ἐχθροῖς ἀνιαροί Ar., of animals, Hdt.:—adv. ἀνιαρῶς Soph. 2. of things, I. painful, grievous, distressing, Theogn., etc.; irreg. comp. ἀνιηρέστερος Od. II. pass. grieved, distressed, Xen.:—adv. -ρῶς wretchedly, id.

ανιατοσ.def: ἀνίατος (α privat.., ἰατός) 1. incurable, Plat., etc. 2. of persons, incorrigible, id.; ἀνιάτως ἔχειν to be incurable, id.

ανιαχω.def: ἀνιάχω to cry aloud: c. acc. to praise loudly, Anth.

ανιαω.def: ἀνιάω (ἀνία) (ῑ in Hom. and Soph., ι or ῑ in other Poets.) Like ἀνιάζω, to grieve, distress, c. acc., Od., etc.; c. dupl. acc., ὁ δρῶν ς’ ἀνιᾶι τὰς φρένας Soph.:—Pass. to be grieved, distressed, Od., etc.; with neut. adj., τοῦτ’ ἀνιῶμαι I am vexed at this, Soph.; aor1 part. as adj., a sorrowful man, Hom.

ανιδρωτι.def: ἀνιδρωτί (ἱδρόω) without sweat: metaph. without toil, Il.: lazily, slowly, Xen.

ανιδρωτοσ.def: ἀνίδρωτος (ἱδρόω) without having sweated or exercised oneself, Xen.

ανιεροσ.def: ἀνίερος I. unholy, unhallowed, Aesch.; ἀνίερος ἀθύτων πελάνων unhallowed because of unoffered sacrifices, Eur. II. unconsecrated, Plat.

ανιεροω.def: ἀνιερόω to dedicate, devote, τί τινι Plut.

ανιημι.def: ἀνίημι (For quantities, ἀνι epic, ἀνῑ- attic; but Hom. has ἀνῑει, ἀνῑέμενος.) (The forms ἀνιεῖς, -εῖ are formed as if they were from ἀνιέω.) (The Homeric forms in ἀνες- are created as if from ἀν-έζω.) (The Ionic form ἀνέωνται is formed as if from ἀν-εόω.) I. to send up or forth, Hom., etc.; of the earth, to make spring up, Hhymn.; of females, to produce, Soph.:— Pass. to be sent up, produced, Aesch., etc.; to send up from the grave or nether world, id., etc. II. to send back, put back, open, Hom., Eur. III. to let go, leave, Hom., etc.; c. gen. rei, δεσμῶν ἀνίει loosed them from bonds, Od.: to let go unpunished, Xen. 2. ἀν. τινί to let loose at one, ἀν. κύνας, Lat. canes immittere, Xen.; hence, ἄφρονα τοῦτον ἀνέντες Il.: c. inf. to set on or urge to do a thing, Hom. 3. ἀν. τινὰ πρός τι to let go for any purpose, Hdt.; ἀν. τινὰ μανίας to set free from madness, Eur. 4. to let, allow one to do a thing, c. acc. et inf., Hdt., etc.: —so, ἀν. κόμην to let it hang, loosen, Eur. 5. Mid., c. acc., κόλπον ἀνιεμένη baring her breast, Il.; αἶγας ἀνιέμενοι flaying goats, Od. 6. to let go free, leave untilled, of ground dedicated to a god, Thuc.:—Pass. to devote oneself, give oneself up, Hdt.; of animals dedicated to a god, which are let range at large, id.; esp. in perf. pass. part. ἀνειμένος, Soph., etc. 7. to slacken, relax, let down, unstring, Hdt., Plat.:—then, to remit, neglect, give up, Soph., Thuc., etc.:—Pass. to be treated remissly, Thuc. 8. so intr. in Act. to slacken, abate, of the wind, Soph., etc.; οὐδὲν ἀνιέναι not to give way at all, Xen.:—c. part. to give up or cease doing, ὕων οὐκ ἀνίει [ὁ θεός] Hdt.:—c. gen. to cease from a thing, Eur., Thuc.

ανικετευτοσ.def: ἀνικέτευτος (ἱκετεύω) without prayer, not entreating, Eur.

ανιμαω.def: ἀνιμάω (only in pres. and imperf.) I. to draw up water, by means of leather straps: generally, to draw out or up, Xen.: also Mid. ἀνιμῶμαι, Luc., etc. II. intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν), to mount up, Xen.

ανιπποσ.gloss: without horse, not serving on horseback
ανιπποσ.def: ἄνιππος 1. without horse, not serving on horseback, Hdt., Soph.: without a horse to ride on, Ar. 2. of countries, unsuited for horses, Hdt.

ανιπτοσ.def: ἄνιπτος (νίζω) 1. unwashen, Il. 2. not to be washed out, Aesch.

ανισοσ.def: ἄνισος (ἴσος) unequal, uneven, Plat., etc.:—adv., ἀνίσως, unfairly, Dem.

ανισοω.def: ἀνισόω (ἀνά, ἰσόω) to make equal, equalise, Xen.:—Pass. to be made equal, Hdt.

ανιστημι.gloss: to make to stand up, raise up
ανιστημι.def: ἀνίστημι A. Causal in pres., imperf. to make to stand up, raise up, χειρός by his hand. Il.:— to raise from sleep, wake up, Il.: metaph., ἀν. νόσον Soph.:— to raise from the dead, Il., Aesch.; from misery, Soph. 2. of things, to set up, build, Hdt., etc.; so, ἀν. τινὰ χαλκοῦν to set up a bronze statue of him, Plut.;—aor1 mid., ἀναστήσασθαι πόλιν to build oneself a city, Hdt. 3. to build up again, restore, Eur., Dem. 4. to put up for sale, Hdt. II. to rouse to action, stir up, Il.:— to rouse to arms, raise troops, Thuc.; ἀν. πόλεμον ἐπί τινα Plut. III. to make people rise, break up an assembly, Il., Xen. 2. to make people rise from their home, make them emigrate, transplant, Od., Hdt., etc. 3. to make suppliants rise and leave sanctuary, Hdt., Thuc. 4. of sportsmen, to put up game, spring it, Xen. B. Intr. in pres. and imperf. ἀνίσταμαι, -μην, in fut. ἀναστήσομαι, in aor2 ἀνέστην, perf. ἀνέστηκα, attic plup. ἀνεστήκη; also in aor1 pass. ἀνεστάθην [α]:— to stand up, rise, to speak, Hom., etc.:— to rise from one's seat as a mark of respect, Lat. assurgere, Il.:— to rise from bed, id., etc.:— to rise from the dead, id.:— to rise from an illness, recover, Hdt. 2. to rise as a champion, Il., Soph.: c. dat. to stand up to fight against, τινι Il.; πᾶσιν ὃς ἀνέστη θεοῖς Aesch. 3. of buiildings and statues, to be set up, to rise up, rear itself, Eur., Plut., etc. 4. of a river, to rise, Plut. II. to rise to go, set out, go away, Eur., Thuc., etc. 2. to be compelled to migrate, Thuc.; of a country, to be depopulated, Hdt., Eur.; οὐκέτι ἀνισταμένη no longer subject to migration, Thuc. 3. of a law-court, to rise, Dem. 4. of game, to be put up, Xen.

ανιστορεω.gloss: to make inquiry into, ask about
ανιστορεω.def: ἀνιστορέω to make inquiry into, ask about, Soph.: c. acc. pers. et rei, to ask a person about a thing, Aesch., Soph.; so, ἀν. τινὰ περί τινος Eur.

ανιστορητοσ.def: ἀνιστόρητος (α privat.., ἱστορέω) ignorant of history:— adv., ἀνιστορήτως ἔχειν τινός to be uninformed about a thing, Plut.

ανιχνευω.def: ἀνιχνεύω (ἀνά, ἰχνεύω) to trace back, as a hound, Il.: generally, to trace out, Plut.

αννιβιζω.def: ἀννιβίζω (Ἀννίβας) to side with Hannibal, Plut.

ανοδοσ.def: ἄνοδος (α privat.., ὁδός) having no road, impassable, Eur., Xen.
ἄνοδος (ἀνά, ὁδός) a way up, as to the Acropolis, Hdt.:— a journey inland, esp. into Central Asia, id., Xen.

ανοδυρομαι.def: ἀνοδύρομαι Dep. to set up a wailing, Xen.

ανοητοσ.def: ἀνόητος I. not thought on, unheard of, Hhymn. 2. not within the province of thought, unintelligent, Plat. II. act. not understanding, unintelligent, Lat. ineptus, Hdt., attic; ὠνόητε oh you fool, Ar.; ἀνόητα follies, id.:—adv. -τως, Plat., etc.

ανοια.def: ἄνοια (ἄνοος) want of understanding, folly, Hdt., etc.; ὑπ’ ἀνοίας Aesch.; πολλὴ ἄνοιά [ἐστι] πολεμῆσαι Thuc.

ανοιγνυμι.def: ἀνοίγνυμι I. to open doors, etc., ἀναοίγεσκον κληῖδα they tried to put back the bolt so as to open the door, Il.; πύλας, θύραν ἀν., Aesch., Ar. 2. to undo, open, πῶμ’ ἀνέωιγε took off the cover and opened it, Il.; metaph., ἀνοίξαντι κληῖδα φρενῶν Eur.; ἀν. οἶνον to tap it, Theocr. 3. to lay open, unfold, disclose, Soph. 4. as nautical term, absol. to get into the open sea, get clear of land, Xen. II. Pass. to be open, stand open, of doors, Hdt., Plat.; κόλποι δ’ ἀλλήλων ἀνοιγόμενοι opening one into another, Plut.

ανοιδεω.def: ἀνοιδέω 1. to swell up, of a wave, Eur. 2. metaph. of passion, Hdt.

ανοικιζω.def: ἀνοικίζω I. to remove up the country:— Pass. and Mid. to shift one's dwelling up the country, to migrate inland, Ar.; and of cities, to be built up the country, away from the coast, Thuc.:—generally, to migrate, δεῦρ’ ἀνοικισθείς Ar., Thuc. II. to resettle:— Pass. to be re-peopled, Plut.

ανοικοδομεω.def: ἀνοικοδομέω I. to build up, Hdt. 2. to wall up, Ar. II. to build again, rebuild, Thuc., Xen.

ανοικτεοσ.def: ἀνοικτέος (verb. adj. of ἀνοίγω) one must open, Eur.

ανοικτοσ.def: ἄνοικτος pitiless, ruthless, Eur.:—adv. -τως, without pity, without being pitied, Soph., Eur.

ανοιμωζω.def: ἀνοιμώζω to wail aloud, Aesch., Thuc.

ανοιμωκτι.gloss: without need to wail, with impunity
ανοιμωκτι.def: ἀνοιμωκτί without need to wail, with impunity, Soph.

ανοιστεοσ.def: ἀνοιστέος (verb. adj. of ἀναφέρω,) one must report, Soph., Eur.:— one must refer, τι πρός τι Plut.

ανοιστοσ.def: ἄνοιστος (ἀναφέρω, fut. ἀνοίσω) referred, ἔς τινα to some one for decision, Hdt.

ανοιστρεω.def: ἀνοιστρέω to goad to madness, Eur.

ανοκωχευω.def: ἀνοκωχεύω (from ἀνοκωχή) I. to hold back, ἀν. τὰς νέας to keep them at anchor, Hdt.: of a chariot, to hold it in, keep it back, Soph. 2. ἀν. τὸν τόνον τῶν ὅπλων to keep up the tension of the ropes, keep them taut, Hdt. II. intr. to keep back, keep still, id.

ανοκωχη.def: ἀνοκωχή (formed by redupl. from ἀνοχή (cf. ὄκωχα perf. of ἔχω). The forms ἀνακωχή, ἀνακωχεύω are late and corrupt.) 1. a stay, cessation, κακῶν Thuc.: absol. a cessation of arms, truce, δι’ ἀνοκωχῆς γίγνεσθαί τινι to be at truce with one, id. 2. a hindrance, id.

ανολβοσ.def: ἄνολβος unblest, wretched, luckless, Theogn., Trag.

ανολκη.def: ἀνολκή (ἀνέλκω) a hauling up, λίθων Thuc.

ανολολυζω.def: ἀνολολύζω I. to cry aloud, shout (with joy), Trag. 2. c. acc. to bewail loudly, Soph. II. in a causal sense, to excite by Bacchic cries, Eur.

ανολοφυρομαι.def: ἀνολοφύρομαι Dep. to break into loud wailing, Thuc., Xen.

ανομαλιζω.def: ἀνομαλίζω to restore to equality, equalise, 1 perf. pass. inf. ἀνωμαλίσθαι Arist.

ανομβροσ.def: ἄνομβρος without rain, of countries, Hdt.; ἄν. ῥοαί streams not fed by showers, Eur.

ανομεω.def: ἀνομέω (ἄνομος) to act lawlessly, περί τι Hdt.

ανομιλητοσ.gloss: having no communion with others, unsociable
ανομιλητοσ.def: ἀνομίλητος 1. having no communion with others, unsociable, Plat. 2. c. gen., ἀνομ. παιδείας unacquainted with education, Luc.

ανομοιοειδησ.def: ἀνομοιοειδής (εἶδος) of unlike kind, heterogeneous, Arist.

ανομοιοσ.def: ἀνόμοιος and α, ον, unlike, dissimilar, Pind., Plat.; ἀν. τινι unlike it, Plat.:—adv. -ως, Thuc.; ἀν. ἔχειν to be unlike, Xen.

ανομοιοω.def: ἀνομοιόω (from ἀνόμοιος) to make unlike or dissimilar, Plat.: —Pass. to be or become so, id.

ανομολογεομαι.def: ἀνομολογέομαι I. Dep. to agree upon a thing, come to an understanding, περί τινος Plat.; πρός τινα with one, id. 2. to sum up one's conclusions, τὰ εἰρημένα id. II. perf. in pass. sense, ἀνωμολόγημαι πράττειν I am allowed to be doing, Dem.

ανομολογητεοσ.def: ἀνομολογητέος (verb. adj. of ἀνομολογέομαι) one must admit, Plat.

ανομοσ.def: ἄνομος I. without law, lawless, Hdt., Trag., etc.:— adv. -μως, Eur., etc.; comp. -ώτερον, Plat. II. （νόμος II) musical, Aesch.

ανονητοσ.def: ἀνόνητος (ὀνίνημι) I. unprofitable, useless, Soph., Eur., etc.; neut. pl. ἀνόνητα as adv. in vain, Eur. II. c. gen. making no profit from a thing, Dem.

ανοοσ.def: ἄνοος without understanding, foolish, silly, Il., Soph., etc.:—comp. ἀνούστερος, Aesch.

ανοπαια.def: ἀνοπαῖα either from ἀν-priv., ⁎ ὄπτομαι she flew away unseen; or = ἄνω, up into the air; or ἀν’ ὀπαῖα (= ἀνὰ ὀπήν) up by the smoke-vent, Od.:—others write ἀνόπαια, ἡ, a kind of eagle.

ανοπλοσ.def: ἄνοπλος without the ὅπλον or large shield, Hdt., Plat.

ανορθοω.gloss: to set up again, restore, rebuild
ανορθοω.def: ἀνορθόω 1. to set up again, restore, rebuild, Hdt., Thuc. 2. to restore to health or well-being, πόλιν Soph. 3. to set straight again, set right, correct, τινα Eur.

ανορμοσ.def: ἄνορμος without harbour: metaph., ὑμέναιον ἄν. εἰσπλεῖν to sail into a marriage that was no haven for thee, Soph.

ανορνυμι.def: ἀνόρνυμι to rouse, stir up, Pind.:—Pass., epic aor2 ἀνῶρτο, to start up, Hom.

ανορουω.def: ἀνορούω to start up, leap up, Hom.; of the sun, ἀνόρουσεν οὐρανὸν ἐς went swiftly up the sky, Od.; ἀνορούσαις (doric part. aor1) Pind.

ανορταλιζω.gloss: to clap the wings and crow
ανορταλιζω.def: ἀνορταλίζω (ὀρταλίς) to clap the wings and crow, like a cockrel, Ar.

ανορυσσω.def: ἀνορύσσω 1. to dig up what has been buried, Hdt., Ar. 2. ἀν. τάφον to dig it up, break open, Hdt.

ανορχεομαι.def: ἀνορχέομαι Dep. to leap up and dance, Eur.

ανοσιοσ.def: ἀνόσιος unholy, profane, Lat. profanus, of persons and things, Hdt., attic; ἀνόσιος νέκυς a corpse with all the rites unpaid, Soph.:—adv. -ίως, in unholy wise, id.: without funeral rites, Eur.

ανοσοσ.def: ἄνοσος I. without sickness, healthy, sound, Od., Hdt., attic 2. c. gen., ἄνοσος κακῶν untouched by ill, Eur. 3. of a season, free from sickness, Thuc. II. of things, not causing disease, harmless, Eur.

ανοστεοσ.def: ἀνόστεος (ὄστεον) boneless, of the polypus, Hes.

ανοστιμοσ.def: ἀνόστιμος 1. not returning, κεῖνον ἀν. ἔθηκεν cut off his return, Od. 2. not to be retraced, Eur.

ανοστοσ.def: ἄνοστος unreturning, without return, Od.; Sup., ἥβη ἀνοστοτάτη never, never to return, Anth.

ανοτοτυζω.def: ἀνοτοτύζω to break out into wailing, Aesch., Eur.

ανουατοσ.def: ἀνούατος (οὖς) without ear: without handle, Theocr.

ανοχη.def: ἀνοχή (ἀνέχω) I. a holding back, stopping, esp. of hostilities: pl., like Lat. induciae, an armistice, truce, Xen. II. （ἀνέχομαι) forbearance, NTest.

ανοχμαζω.def: ἀνοχμάζω to hoist, lift up, Anth.

ανσχετοσ.def: ἀνσχετός (ἀνέχομαι) to be borne, sufferable, endurable, Theogn., Soph.; mostly with negat., οὐκ ἀνσχετά insufferable, Od.; πτώματ’ οὐκ ἀνασχετά Aesch.: —οὐκ ἀνασχετόν [ἐστι], c. inf., Hdt., Soph.

αντα.def: ἄντα (ἀντί) I. over against, face to face, ἄντα μάχεσθαι to fight man to man; ἄντα ἰδεῖν to look before one; θεοῖς ἄντα ἐώικει was like the gods to look at, Hom.; ἄντα τιτύσκεσθαι to aim straight at them, Od. II. as prep. with gen., over against, Hom.; ἄντα παρειάων before her cheeks; ἄντ’ ὀφθαλμοῖϊν Od.; ἄντα σέθεν before thee, id. 2. in hostile sense, against, Διὸς ἄντα Il.

ανταγοραζω.gloss: to buy with money received in payment
ανταγοραζω.def: ἀνταγοράζω to buy with money received in payment for something else, Xen.:—Pass., aor1 part. ἀνταγορασθείς Dem.

ανταγορευω.def: ἀνταγορεύω to speak against, reply, Pind.:— to gainsay, contradict, τινί Ar.

ανταγωνιζομαι.gloss: to struggle against, prove a match for
ανταγωνιζομαι.def: ἀνταγωνίζομαι as Dep. to struggle against, prove a match for, τινί Hdt., Thuc.:—generally, to struggle or dispute with, τινί Thuc.:— οἱ ἀνταγωνιζόμενοί τι the parties in a lawsuit, Xen.

ανταγωνιστεω.def: ἀνταγωνιστέω (from ἀνταγωνιστής) to oppose, be a rival, Arist.

ανταγωνιστησ.def: ἀνταγωνιστής (ἀνταγωνίζομαι) an opponent, competitor, rival, Xen., etc.; ἀντ. ἔρωτος a rival in love, Eur.

ανταειρω.def: ἀνταείρω (= ἀνταίρω:) Mid., ἀνταείρεσθαι χεῖράς τινι to raise one's hands against one, Hdt.

ανταθλοσ.def: ἄνταθλος contending against, rivalling, τινος Anth.

ανταιδεομαι.def: ἀνταιδέομαι Dep. to respect in return, Xen.

ανταιοσ.def: ἀνταῖος (ἄντα) 1. set over against, right opposite, ἀνταία πληγή a wound in front, Soph., Eur. 2. opposed to, hostile, hateful, Eur.; τινι to one, Aesch.; τἀνταῖα θεῶν their hostile purposes, id.

ανταιρω.def: ἀνταίρω I. to raise against, χεῖράς τινι Anth.; so in Mid., Thuc. II. intr. to rise up against, τινί Plat., Dem.; πρός τι or τινα, Dem., etc. 2. of a cliff, to rise opposite to, πρὸς τὴν Λιβύην Plut.

ανταιτεω.def: ἀνταιτέω to demand in return, Thuc.

αντακαιοσ.def: ἀντακαῖος (Deriv. unknown.) a sort of sturgeon, Hdt.

αντακουω.def: ἀντακούω to hear in turn, τι ἀντί τινος Soph.: absol. to hear in return, Aesch., Xen.

ανταλαλαζω.def: ἀνταλαλάζω to return a shout, Aesch.

ανταλλαγμα.def: ἀντάλλαγμα (ἀνταλλάσσω) that which is given or taken in exchange, φίλου for a friend, Eur.; τῆς ψυχῆς for one's soul, NTest.

ανταλλακτεοσ.def: ἀνταλλακτέος (verb. adj. from ἀνταλλάσσω) one must give in exchange, τινός for a thing, Dem.

ανταλλασσω.def: ἀνταλλάσσω I. to exchange one thing with another, τί τινι Eur.; τὴν ἀξίωσιν τῶν ὀνομάτων ἀντ. to change the signification of the names, Thuc. II. Mid. to take in exchange, τί τινος one thing for another, Eur., Dem.; τι ἀντί τινος Dem.; θάνατον ἀνταλλάξεται shall receive death in exchange, i. e. as a punishment, Eur.:—Pass., ἀντηλλαγμένος τοῦ ἑκατέρων τρόπου having made an interchange of each other's custom, i. e. having each adopted the other's way, Thuc.

ανταμειβομαι.def: ἀνταμείβομαι I. Mid. to exchange one thing with another, τί τινι Archil. II. c. acc. pers. to repay, requite, punish, id., Aesch., etc. III. to answer again, Hdt.; ἀντ. τι πρός τινα Soph.

ανταμυνομαι.def: ἀνταμύνομαι I. Mid. to defend oneself against, resist, Thuc. II. to requite, τινὰ κακοῖς Soph.

ανταναβιβαζω.gloss: to make go up in turn
ανταναβιβαζω.def: ἀνταναβιβάζω to make go up in turn, Xen.

ανταναγω.def: ἀντανάγω I. to lead up against, ἀντ. νέας to put ships to sea against, Hdt.; but also, ἀντ. ναυσί with ships, Thuc.;—so, ἀντανάγειν or ἀντανάγεσθαι alone, id., Xen. II. to bring up or out instead, Anth.

ανταναιρεω.gloss: to take away from the opposite sides of an account, to cancel
ανταναιρεω.def: ἀνταναιρέω to take away from the opposite sides of an account, to cancel, Dem.

ανταναλισκω.def: ἀνταναλίσκω to destroy in return, Eur.

ανταναμενω.def: ἀνταναμένω to wait instead of taking active measures, Thuc.

ανταναπιμπλημι.def: ἀνταναπίμπλημι to fill up in return, Xen.

ανταναπλεκω.def: ἀνταναπλέκω to plait in rivalry with, τινί Anth.

ανταναπληροω.def: ἀνταναπληρόω to supply as a substitute or balance, τινὰ πρός τινα Dem.

αντανδροσ.gloss: instead of a man, as a substitute
αντανδροσ.def: ἄντανδρος (ἀνήρ) instead of a man, as a substitute, Luc.

αντανειμι.gloss: to rise so as to balance
αντανειμι.def: ἀντάνειμι (ἀντί,ἀνά εἶμι ibo) to rise so as to balance, τινί Thuc.

αντανιστημι.def: ἀντανίστημι I. to set up against, τί τινι Plut. II. Pass., with aor2 act., to rise up against, τινι Soph.

ανταξιοσ.def: ἀντάξιος 1. worth just as much as, c. gen., Il., Hdt., attic 2. absol. worth as much, worth no less, Il.

ανταξιοω.def: ἀνταξιόω (from ἀντάξιος) to demand as equivalent, or in turn, Thuc.

ανταπαιτεω.def: ἀνταπαιτέω to demand in return, Thuc.:— Pass. to be called on for a thing in turn, τι Plut.

ανταπαμειβομαι.def: ἀνταπαμείβομαι Mid. to obey in turn, τινι Tyrtae.

ανταπερυκω.def: ἀνταπερύκω to keep off in turn, Anth.

ανταποδεικνυμι.def: ἀνταποδείκνυμι to prove in return or answer, Xen.

ανταποδιδωμι.gloss: to give back, repay, tender in repayment
ανταποδιδωμι.def: ἀνταποδίδωμι I. to give back, repay, tender in repayment or requital, Batr., Hdt., attic:—absol. to make a return, Thuc. II. to make correspondent, Plat. 2. intr. to answer to, correspond with, τοῖς ἑτέροις id. 3. to give back words, answer, τινί id. III. to deliver in turn, τὸ σύνθημα Xen. IV. to give back a sound, Plut.

ανταποδοσισ.def: ἀνταπόδοσις (ἀνταποδίδωμι) a giving back in turn, Thuc.: a rendering, requiting, repayment, reward, NTest.

ανταποκρινομαι.def: ἀνταποκρίνομαι Mid. to answer again, NTest.: to argue against, τινι id.

ανταποκτεινω.def: ἀνταποκτείνω to kill in return, Hdt., attic

ανταπολαμβανω.def: ἀνταπολαμβάνω to receive or accept in return, Plat., Dem.

ανταπολλυμι.def: ἀνταπόλλυμι I. to destroy in return, Eur., Plat. II. Pass. and Mid., with perf. 2 act. -απόλωλα, to perish in turn, Eur.; ὑπὲρ ἀνδρὸς ἑκάστου δέκα ἀνταπόλλυσθαι that ten be put to death in revenge for each man, Hdt.

ανταποφαινω.gloss: to shew on the other hand
ανταποφαινω.def: ἀνταποφαίνω to shew on the other hand, Thuc.

ανταρκεω.def: ἀνταρκέω I. to hold out against, τινι Thuc.; πρός τι Plut. II. absol. to hold out, persist, Ar.

αντασπαζομαι.def: ἀντασπάζομαι Dep. to welcome or greet in turn, Xen.; to receive kindly, id.

ανταυγεια.def: ἀνταυγεία (from ἀνταυγέω) reflexion of light, Xen.

ανταυγεω.def: ἀνταυγέω (αὐγή) to reflect light, φάσγανον ἀνταυγεῖ φόνον flashes back murder, Eur.

ανταυδαω.def: ἀνταυδάω to speak against, answer, τινα Soph.

ανταυω.def: ἀνταύω to sound in turn, answer, τινί Pind.

ανταφιημι.def: ἀνταφίημι (ἀντί,ἀπό ἵημι) to let go or let fall in turn, Eur.

ανταω.gloss: to come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with
ανταω.def: ἀντάω (ἄντα) I. c. dat. pers. to come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with, Il., Trag. II. c. gen., either 1. gen. pers. to meet in battle, Hom.; or 2. gen. rei, to take part in, partake in or of, id.; ὅπως ἤντησας ὀπωπῆς how thou hast sped in getting sight of him, Od.; so, ἀντ. ξεινίων Hdt.; κακῶν Soph.; so, ἄντασεἘρεχθειδᾶν partook of their blood, id.

αντεγγραφω.def: ἀντεγγράφω to insert one name instead of another, Dem.

αντεγκαλεω.def: ἀντεγκαλέω to accuse in turn, Dem.

αντεικαζω.def: ἀντεικάζω to compare in return, τινά τινι Ar.; absol., Plat.

αντειπον.def: ἀντεῖπον (aor2 with no pres, ἀνταγορεύω being used instead, cf. ἀντερῶ) 1. to speak against or in answer, gainsay, c. dat., οὐδὲν ἀντ. τινι Aesch., etc.:—absol. to speak in answer, Thuc., etc.; ἀντ. ἔπος to utter a word of contradiction, Eur. 2. ἀντ. τινί τι to set one thing against another, Plat. 3. κακῶς ἀντ. τινά to speak ill of him in turn, Soph.

αντεισαγω.def: ἀντεισάγω I. to introduce instead, substitute, Dem. II. to bring into office in turn, Plut.

αντεκκλεπτω.def: ἀντεκκλέπτω to steal away in return, Ar.

αντεκκοπτω.def: ἀντεκκόπτω to knock out in return, Dem.

αντεκπεμπω.def: ἀντεκπέμπω to send out in return, Xen.

αντεκπλεω.def: ἀντεκπλέω to sail out against, τινί Thuc.

αντεκτεινω.def: ἀντεκτείνω to stretch out in opposition, ἀν. αὑτόν τινι to match oneself with another, Ar.

αντεκτιθημι.def: ἀντεκτίθημι to set forth or state instead, Plut.

αντεκτρεχω.def: ἀντεκτρέχω to sally out against, Xen.

αντελπιζω.def: ἀντελπίζω to hope instead or in turn, Thuc.

αντεμβαλλω.gloss: to make an inroad in turn
αντεμβαλλω.def: ἀντεμβάλλω to make an inroad in turn, Xen.: to attack in turn, Plut.

αντεμβιβαζω.def: ἀντεμβιβάζω to put on board instead, Thuc.

αντεμπηγνυμαι.def: ἀντεμπήγνυμαι Pass. to stick right in, τινί Ar.

αντεμπιπλημι.def: ἀντεμπίπλημι to fill in turn, Xen.: to fill in return, by way of compensation, τί τινος id.

αντεμπιπρημι.gloss: to set on fire in return
αντεμπιπρημι.def: ἀντεμπίπρημι to set on fire in return, Hdt.

αντενδιδωμι.def: ἀντενδίδωμι to give way in turn, of sawyers, Ar.

αντεξαγω.def: ἀντεξάγω to export in turn or instead, Xen.

αντεξαιτεω.def: ἀντεξαιτέω to demand in return, Plut.

αντεξελαυνω.gloss: to drive, ride, sail out against
αντεξελαυνω.def: ἀντεξελαύνω to drive, ride, sail out against, Plut.

αντεξερχομαι.def: ἀντεξέρχομαι (εἶμι ibo, = ἀντέξειμι) Xen. to go out against, Xen.

αντεξεταζω.def: ἀντεξετάζω to try one by the standard of another, Aeschin.; τι πρός τι Plut.:—Mid. to measure oneself against another, τινί Luc.:— to dispute with him at law, id.

αντεξιππευω.def: ἀντεξιππεύω to ride out against, Plut.

αντεξορμησισ.def: ἀντεξόρμησις (ἐξορμάω) a sailing against, Thuc.: a mode of attack, Plut.

αντεπαγω.def: ἀντεπάγω to lead against: intr. to advance against, Thuc.

αντεπαινεω.def: ἀντεπαινέω I. to praise in return, Xen. II. Pass., ἀντ. τινί to be extolled in comparison with, Luc.

αντεπαναγομαι.def: ἀντεπανάγομαι Pass. to put to sea against, πρός τινα Thuc.

αντεπαφιημι.def: ἀντεπαφίημι to let slip against, τινί Luc.

αντεπειμι.gloss: to rush upon, meet an advancing enemy
αντεπειμι.def: ἀντέπειμι (εἶμι ibo) to rush upon, meet an advancing enemy, c. dat. or absol., Thuc.

αντεπεξαγω.def: ἀντεπεξάγω intr., to go out against, Thuc.

αντεπεξειμι.def: ἀντεπέξειμι (εἶμι ibo) to march out to meet an enemy, πρός τινα Thuc.; absol., Xen.

αντεπεξελαυνω.def: ἀντεπεξελαύνω to march out to meet an enemy, Thuc.

αντεπηχεω.def: ἀντεπηχέω to clamour against one, Luc.

αντεπιγραφω.def: ἀντεπιγράφω to write something instead, Dem.

αντεπιδεικνυμι.def: ἀντεπιδείκνυμι to exhibit in turn, Xen.; so Mid., Plut.

αντεπιθυμεω.def: ἀντεπιθυμέω to desire a thing in rivalry with another, c. gen. rei, Andoc.:—Pass., ἀντεπιθυμεῖσθαι τῆς ξυνουσίας to have one's company desired in turn, Xen.

αντεπικουρεω.def: ἀντεπικουρέω to help in return, τινι Xen.

αντεπιμελεομαι.def: ἀντεπιμελέομαι Dep. to attend or give heed in turn, τινός to one, Xen.

αντεπιστελλω.def: ἀντεπιστέλλω to write an answer, Luc.

αντεπιστρατευω.def: ἀντεπιστρατεύω to take the field against, Xen.

αντεπιτασσω.def: ἀντεπιτάσσω to order in turn, τινὶ ποιεῖν τι Thuc.

αντεπιτειχιζομαι.gloss: to build a fort in retaliation
αντεπιτειχιζομαι.def: ἀντεπιτειχίζομαι Dep. with pf pass to build a fort in retaliation, Thuc.

αντεπιτιθημι.def: ἀντεπιτίθημι to entrust a letter in answer, πρός τινα Thuc.

αντεπιχειρεω.def: ἀντεπιχειρέω to attack in turn, τινι Plut.

αντεραμαι.def: ἀντέραμαι to rival another in love for a person, τινί τινος Luc.

αντερανιζω.def: ἀντερανίζω to contribute in turn; Pass. to be repaid, Anth.

αντεραστησ.def: ἀντεραστής a rival in love, τινός for another, Ar.: a rival, Plat.

αντεραω.def: ἀντεράω I. to love in return, Aesch.; ἀντερᾶν τινός Luc. II. ἀντ. τινί τινος to rival one in love for another, Eur.: absol., τὸ ἀντερᾶν jealous love, Plut.

αντερειδω.def: ἀντερείδω (from ἀντέρεισις) I. to set firmly against, τί τινι Eur.; ἀντ. ξύλα [τῶι πύργωι] to set wooden props against it, Xen.; ἀντ. βάσιν to plant it firm, Soph. II. intr. to stand firm, resist pressure, Xen.

αντερομαι.def: ἀντέρομαι Dep. to ask in turn, Hdt., Xen.

αντερυομαι.gloss: to make equal in weight with, to value equally with
αντερυομαι.def: ἀντερύομαι to make equal in weight with, to value equally with, c. gen., Theogn.
