αντερω.def: ἀντερῶ (ἀντεῖπον) (fut. with no pres. in use.) to speak against, gainsay, Soph.; τι πρός τινα Ar.; c. inf. to refuse, Aesch.:—Pass., οὐδὲν ἀντειρήσεται no denial shall be given, Soph.

αντερωταω.def: ἀντερωτάω to question in turn, ἐρωτώμενος ἀντερωτᾶν Plat.

αντευεργετεω.def: ἀντευεργετέω to return a kindness, Xen.

αντευνοεω.def: ἀντευνοέω to wish well in return, τινί Xen.

αντεχω.def: ἀντέχω I. to hold against, c. acc. et gen., χεῖρα ἀντ. κρατός to hold one's hand against one's head, so as to shade the eyes, Soph.; c. dat., ὄμμασι δ’ ἀντίσχοις τάνδ’ αἴγλαν may'st thou keep this sunlight upon his eyes (al. off his eyes), id. II. to hold out against, withstand, c. dat., Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Thuc.; c. acc. to endure, Anth. 2. absol. to hold out, stand one's ground, Hdt., attic: to hold out, endure, last, Hdt., etc.; of the rivers drunk by the Persian army, to hold out, suffice, id. III. Mid. to hold before one against something, c. acc. et gen., Od. 2. c. gen. to hold on by, cling to, Hdt., attic:—metaph., ἀντ. τῶν ὄχθων to cling to the banks, keep close to them, Hdt.; ἀντ. ἀρετῆς, τοῦ πολέμου id.; τῆς θαλάσσης Thuc. 3. absol. to hold out, Soph. 4. c. dupl. gen. pers. et rei, ἀνθέξεταί σου τῶν χρημάτων will lay claim to the property from you, dispute it with you, Ar.

αντηλιοσ.def: ἀντήλιος (Note that it is not not ἀνθ-ήλιος) I. opposite the sun, i. e. facing east, Soph.; δαίμονες ἀντήλιοι statues of gods which stood in the sun before the door, Aesch. II. like the sun, formed like ἀντίθεος, Eur.

αντην.def: ἄντην (ἀντί) against, over against, ἄντην στήσομαι I will confront him, Il.; ὁμοιωθήμεναι ἄντην to match himself against me, Hom.; ἄντην ἔρχεσθαι to go straight forwards, Il.; ἄντην βάλλεσθαι to be struck in front, id.; ἄντην εἰσιδέειν to look him in the face, id.; ἄντην λόεσθαι to bathe before all, Od.; θεῶι ἐναλίγκιος ἄντην like a god in presence, id.

αντηνωρ.def: ἀντήνωρ (ἀνήρ) instead of a man, σποδὸς ἀντ. dust for men, Aesch.

αντηρετησ.def: ἀντηρέτης (ἐρέτης) properly, one who rows against another: generally an adversary, Aesch.

αντηρησ.gloss: set over against, opposite, face to face
αντηρησ.def: ἀντήρης (ἀντί, v. -ήρης) set over against, opposite, face to face, Eur.:—c. gen. over against, facing, id.; ἀντήρεις στέρνων πληγάς aimed straight at the breast, Soph.:—c. dat., ἀντ. τινί opposite to a thing, Eur.

αντηρισ.def: ἀντηρίς (ἀντί, ἐρείδω) a prop, stay, support, Eur., Xen.; in Thuc., ἀντηρίδες are stay-beams, fixed so as to strengthen the timbers of the bow.

αντηχεω.def: ἀντηχέω I. to sound or sing in answer, Eur. II. of a musical string, to sound responsively, Plut., Luc.

αντι.def: ἀντί over against, opposite. c. gen. c. gen. orig.:— sense over against, opposite. A. Usage, 1. of Place, instead, in the place of, Hom., etc. 2. as good as, equal to, ἀντὶ πολλῶν λαῶν ἐστίν he is as good as many men, Il.; ἀντὶ κασιγνήτου Od. 3. at the price of, for, ἀντὶ χρημάτων for money paid, Hdt., etc. 4. for the sake of, Soph. 5. to mark comparison, ἓν ἀνθ’ ἑνός one set against the other, compared with it, Plat.: so, after Comparatives, πλέον ἀντὶ σοῦ Soph.; also (esp. after a negative), ἄλλος ἀντ’ ἐμοῦ Aesch. B. Position: ἀντί rarely follows its case, and then does not suffer anastrophe. C. IN COMPOS., 1. over against, opposite, as ἀντίπορος. 2. against, in opposition to, as ἀντιλέγω. 3. in return, as ἀντιβοηθέω. 4. instead, as ἀντήνωρ. 5. equal to, like, as ἀντίθεος. 6. counter, as ἀντίτυπος.

αντιαζω.def: ἀντιάζω (ἀντίος) to meet face to face, I. c. acc. pers. to encounter, whether as friend or foe, Hdt., Aesch.: absol. to meet, answer, Pind. 2. to approach as suppliants, to entreat, supplicate, Hdt., Soph. II. c. dat. pers. to meet in fight, Pind.

αντιανειρα.def: ἀντιάνειρα (ἀντί, ἀνήρ) I. fem. adj. a match for men, of the Amazons, Il. II. στάσις ἀντιάνειρα faction wherein man is set against man, Pind.

αντιαω.gloss: to go for the purpose of meeting
αντιαω.def: ἀντιάω (ἀντίος) I. to go for the purpose of meeting: 1. c. gen. rei, to go in quest of, Hom.; of an arrow, to hit, Il.; of the gods, to come (as it were) to meet an offering, to accept it, or to partake of it, Hom.; then, generally, to partake of, enjoy, obtain, Od., Soph.; so in Mid., Il. 2. c. gen. pers. to match or measure oneself with, id., Theogn. II. c. dat. pers. to meet with, encounter, Hom. III. c. acc. rei, to come to, visit, share, ἐμὸν λέχος ἀντιόωσα Il.

αντιβαινω.def: ἀντιβαίνω to go against, withstand, resist, c. dat., Hdt., Aesch.; πλευραῖσιν ἀντιβᾶσα having set her foot against, Eur.; also absol., Hdt., etc.; ἀντιβάς reluctant, Soph.; but, ἀντιβὰς ἐλᾶν to pull stoutly against the oar, going well back, Ar.

αντιβαλλω.def: ἀντιβάλλω I. to throw against or in turn, return the shots, Thuc. II. to put one against the other, λόγους ἀντ. πρὸς ἀλλήλους to exchange words in conversation, NTest.

αντιβιαζομαι.def: ἀντιβιάζομαι Dep. to use force against, Anth.

αντιβιην.def: ἀντιβίην (βία) against, face to face, Il.

αντιβιοσ.def: ἀντίβιος (βία) opposing force to force, ἀντιβίοις ἐπέεσσι with wrangling words, Hom.:—neut. as adv. = ἀντιβίην, Il.

αντιβλεπτεοσ.gloss: one must look in the face
αντιβλεπτεοσ.def: ἀντιβλεπτέος (from ἀντιβλέπω) (verb. adj. of ἀντιβλέπω) one must look in the face, Luc.

αντιβλεπω.gloss: to look straight at, look in the face
αντιβλεπω.def: ἀντιβλέπω to look straight at, look in the face, c. dat. pers., Xen.

αντιβλεψισ.gloss: a looking in the face, a look
αντιβλεψισ.def: ἀντίβλεψις a looking in the face, a look, Xen.

αντιβοαω.def: ἀντιβοάω to return a cry, Bion.

αντιβοηθεω.def: ἀντιβοηθέω to help in turn, τινι Thuc., Xen.

αντιβολεω.def: ἀντιβολέω (ἀντιβάλλω) 1. to meet by chance, esp. in battle, c. dat. pers. or absol., Hom. 2. c. dat. rei, to be present at, φόνωι ἀνδρῶν, τάφωι ἀνδρῶν Od. 3. c. gen. rei, to partake of, have one's share of, μάχης Il.; τάφου Od. 4. to fall to one's lot, c. gen. pers., γάμος ἀντιβολήσει ἐμέθεν id. 5. c. acc. pers. to meet as a suppliant, entreat, supplicate, Ar.; c. acc. et inf., id.:—absol. to supplicate, entreat, id.

αντιβρονταω.def: ἀντιβροντάω to rival in thundering, τινί Luc.

αντιγεγωνα.def: ἀντιγέγωνα (perf. in pres. sense,) to return a cry, Anth.

αντιγενεηλογεω.def: ἀντιγενεηλογέω ionic form, to rival in pedigree, Hdt.

αντιγνωμονεω.gloss: to be of a different opinion
αντιγνωμονεω.def: ἀντιγνωμονέω (γνώμων) to be of a different opinion: ἀντ. τι μὴ οὐκ εἶναι to think that a thing is otherwise, Xen.

αντιγραφευσ.def: ἀντιγραφεύς a check-clerk, controller, Aeschin.; ἀντ. τῶν εἰσενεγκόντων one who keeps a check upon their accounts, Dem.

αντιγραφη.def: ἀντιγραφή I. a reply in writing, such as Caesar's Anticato in reply to Cicero's Cato, Plut. II. as law-term, a plea, indictment, Plat., Dem.

αντιγραφοσ.def: ἀντίγραφος (from ἀντιγράφω) copied, Dem.:—as Subst., ἀντίγραφον, τό, a transcript, copy, counterpart, id.

αντιγραφω.def: ἀντιγράφω I. to write against or in answer, write back, Thuc., Plut. II. Mid., with perf. pass., as law-term, to put in as a plea, to plead against, Dem.

αντιδακνω.def: ἀντιδάκνω to bite in turn, Hdt.

αντιδειπνοσ.def: ἀντίδειπνος (δεῖπνον) taking another's place at dinner, Luc.

αντιδεξιοομαι.def: ἀντιδεξιόομαι Dep. to salute in return, τινα Xen.

αντιδεομαι.def: ἀντιδέομαι Dep. to entreat in return, Plat.

αντιδερκομαι.def: ἀντιδέρκομαι Dep. = ἀντιβλέπω, c. acc., Eur.

αντιδεχομαι.def: ἀντιδέχομαι Dep. to receive or accept in return, Aesch., Eur.

αντιδημαγωγεω.def: ἀντιδημαγωγέω to rival as a demagogue, Plut.

αντιδιαβαινω.def: ἀντιδιαβαίνω to cross over in turn, Xen.

αντιδιαβαλλω.def: ἀντιδιαβάλλω to attack in return, Arist.

αντιδιατιθεμαι.def: ἀντιδιατίθεμαι to offer resistance, τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους opponents, NTest.

αντιδιδασκω.def: ἀντιδιδάσκω to teach in turn or on the other side, Anth.:—of poets, to contend for the prize, Ar.

αντιδιδωμι.def: ἀντιδίδωμι I. to give in return, repay, τί τινι Hdt., attic 2. to give for or instead of, τί τινος Eur.; τι ἀντί τινος Ar. II. at Athens, ἀντ. [τὴν οὐσίαν] to offer to change fortunes with one (cf. ἀντίδοσις), Dem., etc.

αντιδιεξειμι.def: ἀντιδιέξειμι (εἶμι ibo) to go through in turn, Aeschin.

αντιδικεω.def: ἀντιδικέω (from ἀντίδικος) to dispute, go to law, περί τινος Xen.; οἱ ἀντιδικοῦντες the parties to a suit, Plat.; absol. of the defendant, Ar.; ἀντ. πρός τι or πρός τινα, to urge one's suit against.., Dem.

αντιδικοσ.gloss: an opponent in a suit, defendant
αντιδικοσ.def: ἀντίδικος (δίκη) an opponent in a suit, defendant or plaintiff, Plat., etc.: generally an opponent, Aesch.

αντιδοξοσ.def: ἀντίδοξος (δόξα) of a different opinion or sect, Luc.

αντιδοροσ.def: ἀντίδορος (δορά) clothed with something instead of a skin, Anth.

αντιδοσισ.def: ἀντίδοσις (ἀντιδίδωμι) I. a giving in return, exchange, Arist., Luc. II. at Athens, a form by which a citizen charged with a λειτουργία or public charge might call upon any other citizen whom he thought richer than himself either to exchange properties, or to take the charge upon himself, Xen., Dem., etc.

αντιδοτοσ.def: ἀντίδοτος (ἀντιδίδωμι) I. given in lieu of, πυρός Anth. II. given as a remedy for, κακῶν id.:—as Subst., ἀντίδοτος, ἡ, an antidote, id.

αντιδουλευω.def: ἀντιδουλεύω to serve in place of, τινός Eur.

αντιδουλοσ.def: ἀντίδουλος treated as a slave, Aesch.

αντιδουποσ.def: ἀντίδουπος re-echoing, Aesch.; ἀντίδουπά τινι id.

αντιδραω.def: ἀντιδράω I. to act against, retaliate, Soph., Eur. II. c. acc. pers. to repay, requite, Soph., Eur.

αντιδωρεομαι.def: ἀντιδωρέομαι Dep. to present in return, τινά τινι one with a thing, Hdt., Plat., etc.; also, ἀντ. τινί τι to present a thing in turn to one, Eur.

αντιζητεω.gloss: to seek one who is seeking us
αντιζητεω.def: ἀντιζητέω to seek one who is seeking us, Xen.

αντιζωγρεω.def: ἀντιζωγρέω to save alive in turn, Babr.

αντιθαπτω.def: ἀντιθάπτω to bury opposite: Pass., aor2 ἀντετάφην [ᾶ], Anth.

αντιθεοσ.def: ἀντίθεος equal to the gods, godlike, Hom.

αντιθεραπευω.gloss: to take care of in return
αντιθεραπευω.def: ἀντιθεραπεύω to take care of in return, Xen.

αντιθεσισ.def: ἀντίθεσις (ἀντιτίθημι) 1. opposition, resistance, Plat., Anth. 2. antithesis, Isocr.

αντιθεω.def: ἀντιθέω I. to run against another, compete in a race, Hdt. II. to run contrary ways, Anth.

αντιθηγω.def: ἀντιθήγω to whet against another, ὀδόντας ἐπί τινα Luc.

αντιθυροσ.def: ἀντίθυρος (θύρα) 1. opposite the door: as neut. Subst., ἀντίθυρον, ου, τό, the part facing the door, the vestibule, Od., Soph. 2. the side of a room facing the door, Luc.

αντικαθευδω.def: ἀντικαθεύδω to sleep again or instead. Anth.

αντικαθημαι.def: ἀντικάθημαι (perf. of ἀντικαθίζομαι, but used as pres.) to be set over against; of armies or fleets, to lie over against, so as to watch each other, Hdt., Thuc.

αντικαθιζομαι.def: ἀντικαθίζομαι (here you need to generate ἀντικατίζομαι) Mid. to sit or lie over against, or armies or fleets watching one another, Hdt., Thuc.

αντικαθιστημι.def: ἀντικαθίστημι I. to lay down or establish instead, substitute, replace, Hdt., Thuc. 2. to set against, oppose, τινὰ πρός τινα Thuc.; τινά τινι Plat. 3. to bring back again, restore, Thuc. II. Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., and aor1 pass. κατεστάθην [ᾰ], to be put in another's place, reign in his stead, Hdt., Xen. 2. to stand against, resist, τινί Xen.; absol., Thuc.

αντικακουργεω.def: ἀντικακουργέω to damage in turn, τινά Plat.

αντικαλεω.def: ἀντικαλέω to invite in turn, Xen.

αντικαταθνησκω.def: ἀντικαταθνήσκω to die or be slain in turn, Aesch.

αντικαταλειπω.def: ἀντικαταλείπω to leave in one's stead, Plat.

αντικαταλλασσομαι.def: ἀντικαταλλάσσομαι Mid., to exchange one thing for another: 1. to give one thing for another, τί τινος Dem.; τι ἀντί or ὑπέρ τινος Oratt. 2. to receive one thing in exchange for another, τι ἀντί τινος Isocr.

αντικατατεινω.def: ἀντικατατείνω to stretch out or set directly in contrast, τι παρά τι Plat.

αντικατηγορεω.gloss: to accuse in turn, recriminate upon
αντικατηγορεω.def: ἀντικατηγορέω to accuse in turn, recriminate upon, τινός Aeschin.

αντικατων.def: ἀντικάτων Anticato, name of a book written by Caesar in reply to the Cato of Cicero, Plut.

αντικειμαι.gloss: to be set over against, lie opposite
αντικειμαι.def: ἀντίκειμαι (used as pass. of ἀντιτίθημι) to be set over against, lie opposite, Plat.: adv. part. ἀντικειμένως, by way of opposition, Arist.

αντικελευω.def: ἀντικελεύω to command in turn, Thuc.:— Pass. to be bidden to do a thing in turn, id.

αντικεντρον.def: ἀντίκεντρον something acting as a goad, Aesch.

αντικηδευω.def: ἀντικηδεύω to tend instead of another, τινός Eur.

αντικηρυσσω.def: ἀντικηρύσσω to proclaim in answer, Eur.

αντικλαζω.gloss: to sound against, to be echoed by
αντικλαζω.def: ἀντικλάζω to sound against, to be echoed by a thing, Eur.:— ἀντ. ἀλλήλαις μέλος to sing against one another, id.

αντικλαιω.def: ἀντικλαίω to weep in return, Hdt.

αντικνημιον.gloss: the part of the leg opposite the
αντικνημιον.def: ἀντικνήμιον the part of the leg opposite the κνήμη, the shin, Ar.

αντικολαζομαι.def: ἀντικολάζομαι Pass. to be punished in return, Luc.

αντικολακευω.def: ἀντικολακεύω to flatter in turn, Plut.

αντικομιζω.gloss: to bring back as an answer
αντικομιζω.def: ἀντικομίζω to bring back as an answer, Plut.

αντικομπαζω.def: ἀντικομπάζω to boast in opposition, τινί Plut.

αντικοπτω.def: ἀντικόπτω 1. to beat back, resist, oppose, Xen. 2. impers., ἤν τι ἀντικόψηι if there be any hindrance, id.

αντικορυσσομαι.def: ἀντικορύσσομαι Mid. to take arms against, τινί Anth.

αντικρατεω.def: ἀντικρατέω to hold instead of another, Anth.

αντικρουσισ.gloss: a striking against, hindrance: a repartee
αντικρουσισ.def: ἀντίκρουσις (from ἀντικρούω) a striking against, hindrance: a repartee, Aeschin.

αντικρουω.gloss: to strike against, to be a hindrance, counteract
αντικρουω.def: ἀντικρούω to strike against, to be a hindrance, counteract, τινί Thuc.; πρός τι Plut.; absol., Dem.

αντικρυ.def: ἀντικρύ I. = ἄντην, over against, right opposite, c. dat., θεοῖς ἀντικρὺ μάχεσθαι Il.; c. gen., Ἕκτορος ἀντικρύ id. II. = ἄντικρυς, straight on, right on, Hom.; followed by a prep., ἀντικρὺ ἀν’ ὀδόντας, ἀντικρὺ δι’ ὤμου id.; ἀντικρὺ κατὰ μέσσον right in the middle, Il. 2. outright, utterly, ἀντικρὺ δ’ ἀπόφημι id.

αντικρυσ.def: ἄντικρυς I. straight on, right on, Thuc., etc. 2. outright, openly, without disguise, Aesch., Thuc., etc.; ἀντ. δουλεία downright slavery, Thuc.; οὐκ ἄντικρυς not at all, Ar. II. later, = ἀντῑκρύ, opposite, Arist., Plut.

αντικτονοσ.def: ἀντικτόνος (κτείνω) in requital for murder, Aesch.

αντικτυπεω.def: ἀντικτυπέω to ring, clash against, τινί Anth.

αντικυρω.def: ἀντικύρω to hit upon, meet, τινί Pind., Soph.

αντικωμωδεω.def: ἀντικωμῳδέω to ridicule in turn, Plut.

αντιλαβη.gloss: a thing to hold by, a handle
αντιλαβη.def: ἀντιλαβή (ἀντιλαμβάνω) a thing to hold by, a handle, Lat. ansa, Thuc.:—metaph., πολλὰς.. ἔχει ἀντιλαβάς gives many handles against one, points of attack, Plat.

αντιλαγχανω.def: ἀντιλαγχάνω as a law-term, ἀντ. δίαιταν to have a new arbitration granted, i. e. to get the old one set aside, Dem.; ἀντ. ἔρημον (sc. τὴν δίκην) to get it set aside by default, id.

αντιλαζομαι.gloss: to take hold of, hold by
αντιλαζομαι.def: ἀντιλάζομαι 1. to take hold of, hold by, c. gen., Eur.; to partake in, πόνων id. 2. c. acc. to receive in turn, id.

αντιλακτιζω.def: ἀντιλακτίζω to kick against, τινί Ar.

αντιλαμβανω.def: ἀντιλαμβάνω I. to receive instead of, τί τινος Eur.: to receive in turn or as a return, τι id., etc. II. Mid., with perf. pass. -είλημμαι, like ἀντέχομαι, c. gen. to lay hold of, Theogn., etc.; χώρας ἀντ. to gain or reach it, Thuc. 2. to help, take part with, assist, Eur.; c. gen. rei, to help towards a thing, Thuc.; c. gen. pers., NTest. 3. to lay claim to, τοῦ θρόνου Ar. 4. to take part, or share in a thing, take in hand, Lat. capessere, τῶν πραγμάτων Xen., etc. 5. to take hold of for the purpose of finding fault, to reprehend, ἡμῶν Plat. 6. to take fast hold of, to captivate, ὁ λόγος ἀντιλαμβάνεταί μου id. III. in Mid. also, to hold against, hold back, ἵππου Xen.

αντιλαμπω.gloss: to kindle a light in turn
αντιλαμπω.def: ἀντιλάμπω I. to kindle a light in turn, Aesch. II. intr. to reflect light, shine, Xen. 2. to shine opposite to or in the face of, ὁ ἥλιος ἀντ. τινί Plut.

αντιλεγω.def: ἀντιλέγω (the common fut. is ἀντερῶ; the aor. commonly used is ἀντεῖπον) 1. to speak against, gainsay, contradict, τινί Thuc., etc.; τινὶ περί τινος Xen.; ὑπέρ τινος id.; πρός τι Ar.:— ἀντ. ὡς.. to declare in opposition or answer that.., Hdt., etc.; c. inf. to reply that.., Thuc.; ἀντ. μὴ ποιεῖν to speak against doing, id. 2. c. acc. rei, to allege in answer, Soph., Thuc.:—Pass. to be disputed, Xen.; of a place, to be counter-claimed, id. 3. absol. to speak one against the other, speak in opposition, Hdt., etc.; οἱ ἀντιλέγοντες Thuc.

αντιλεκτεοσ.def: ἀντιλεκτέος (verb. adj. from ἀντιλέγω) one must gainsay, Eur.

αντιλεων.def: ἀντιλέων lion-like, formed like ἀντίθεος, Ar.

αντιληξισ.gloss: a motion for a new arbitration
αντιληξισ.def: ἀντίληξις (ἀντιλαγχάνω) a motion for a new arbitration, Dem.

αντιληπτεοσ.def: ἀντιληπτέος one must take part in a matter, Ar.; τῶν πραγμάτων αὐτοῖς ἀντ. Dem.

αντιληψισ.def: ἀντίληψις (ἀντιλαμβάνω) I. a receiving in turn or exchange, Thuc.: a counter-claim, Xen. II. (from Mid.), a hold, support, defence, succour, id. 2. a claim to a thing, id. 3. an objection, Plat. III. (from Pass.) a being seized, a seizure, attack of sickness, Thuc.

αντιλογεω.def: ἀντιλογέω 1. =ἀντιλέγω to deny, Soph. 2. = ἀντ. λέγω 3, Ar.

αντιλογια.def: ἀντιλογία (ἀντιλογέω) contradiction, controversy, disputation, Hdt., Thuc.; in pl. opposing arguments, answering speeches, Ar., Thuc.

αντιλογιζομαι.def: ἀντιλογίζομαι Dep. to count up or calculate on the other hand, Xen.

αντιλογικοσ.def: ἀντιλογικός (ἀντιλέγω) given to contradiction, contradictory, disputatious, Ar., etc.:— ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) the art of contradiction or of arguing from contradictories, Plat.

αντιλοιδορεω.def: ἀντιλοιδορέω to rail at or abuse in turn, NTest.; Mid., c. acc. rei, Luc.

αντιλυπεω.def: ἀντιλυπέω to vex in return, Plut.

αντιλυροσ.def: ἀντίλυρος (λύρα) responsive to the lyre, Soph.

αντιμαινομαι.def: ἀντιμαίνομαι Pass. to rage or bluster against, τινί Anth.

αντιμαρτυρεω.gloss: to appear as witness against, to contradict solemnly
αντιμαρτυρεω.def: ἀντιμαρτυρέω to appear as witness against, to contradict solemnly, τινί Plut.

αντιμαρτυρομαι.gloss: to protest on the other hand
αντιμαρτυρομαι.def: ἀντιμαρτύρομαι Dep. to protest on the other hand, Luc.

αντιμαχομαι.def: ἀντιμάχομαι Dep. to fight against one, Thuc.

αντιμεθελκω.def: ἀντιμεθέλκω to drag different ways, Anth.

αντιμεθιστημι.gloss: to move from one side to the other, to revolutionise
αντιμεθιστημι.def: ἀντιμεθίστημι I. to move from one side to the other, to revolutionise, Ar. II. Pass., with aor. 2 and perf. act., to pass over to the other side, Luc.

αντιμειρακιευομαι.def: ἀντιμειρακιεύομαι Dep. to behave petulantly in return, πρός τινα Plut.

αντιμελλω.def: ἀντιμέλλω to wait and watch against one, aor1 inf. ἀντιμελλῆσαι, Thuc.

αντιμεμφομαι.def: ἀντιμέμφομαι Dep. to blame in turn, Hdt.

αντιμεριζομαι.def: ἀντιμερίζομαι Dep. to impart in turn, Anth.

αντιμετειμι.def: ἀντιμέτειμι (εἶμι ibo) to compete: οἱ ἀντιμετιόντες competitors, Plut.

αντιμετρεω.gloss: to measure out in turn, to give in compensation
αντιμετρεω.def: ἀντιμετρέω to measure out in turn, to give in compensation, Luc.: Pass. to be measured in turn, NTest.

αντιμηχαναομαι.def: ἀντιμηχανάομαι to contrive against or in opposition, Hdt., Thuc.

αντιμιμησισ.def: ἀντιμίμησις close imitation of a person in a thing, c. dupl. gen., Thuc.

αντιμισθια.def: ἀντιμισθία (from ἀντίμισθος) a requital, recompense, NTest.

αντιμοιρει.def: ἀντιμοιρεί (μοῖρα) by way of compensation, Dem.

αντιμολποσ.gloss: sounding instead of, differing in sound from
αντιμολποσ.def: ἀντίμολπος (μέλπω) sounding instead of, differing in sound from, c. gen., Eur.; ὕπνου ἀντίμολπον ἄκος song, sleep's substitute, Aesch.

αντιναυπηγεω.def: ἀντιναυπηγέω to build ships against, Thuc.

αντινικαω.def: ἀντινικάω to conquer in turn, Aesch.

αντινομια.def: ἀντινομία (νόμος) ambiguity in the law, ἐν ἀντινομίαι γίγνεσθαι to be in a strait between two laws, Plut.

αντιξοεω.def: ἀντιξοέω (from ἀντίξοος) to set oneself against, Pind.

αντιξοοσ.def: ἀντίξοος (ξέω?) opposed, adverse, Hdt.:— τὸ ἀντίξοον opposition, id.

αντιοομαι.def: ἀντιόομαι (ἀντίος) Dep. to resist, oppose, τινί Hdt., Aesch.:— οἱ ἀντιούμενοι οἱ ἐναντίοι, Hdt.:—c. acc., once in Hdt.

αντιοσ.def: ἀντίος (ἀντί) set against, and so I. in local sense, face to face, opposite, esp. in battle, Hom., etc.; ἀντίος ἦλθε went to meet him, Il.; c. gen., Ἀγαμέμνονος ἀντίος id.; usually c. dat., Od., Hdt., attic 2. opposite, contrary, Aesch., Eur.: οἱ ἀντίοι οἱ ἐναντίοι, Pind., Hdt.: ἐκ τῆς ἀντίης contrariwise, Hdt. II. as adv. in neut. ἀντία and ἀντίον, against, straight at, right against, ἀντίον ἷζεν Od., etc.; c. gen., ἀντί’ ἐμεῖο Il.; so, ἀντία σευ in thy presence, Hdt.; ἀντία τῆς ἵππου opposite it, id. 2. against, ἀντίον τινος εἰπεῖν Od.; c. dat., ἀντία τοῖς Πέρσηισι Hdt. 3. τὸν δ’ ἀντίον ηὔδα ἠμείβετο, answered, Od., attic

αντιοστατεω.def: ἀντιοστατέω =ἀνθίσταμαι,to be contrary, of a wind, Soph.

αντιοχευομαι.def: ἀντιοχεύομαι Pass. to drive against, Anth.

αντιπαθησ.def: ἀντιπαθής (πάθος) I. in return for suffering, Aesch.: felt mutually, Luc. II. as Subst., ἀντιπαθές, a remedy for suffering, Plut.

αντιπαιζω.def: ἀντιπαίζω to play one with another, Xen.

αντιπαισ.def: ἀντίπαις like a boy or child, Aesch., Eur.

αντιπαλοσ.def: ἀντίπαλος (πάλη) 1. properly wrestling against: then, generally, struggling against, antagonistic, rival, Aesch.; c. dat. rivalling, a match for another, Eur.; c. gen., ὑμεναίων γόος ἀντίπαλος id.:—as Subst., ἀντίπαλος, ὁ, an antagonist, rival, adversary, mostly in pl., Hdt., attic; τὸ ἀντίπαλον the rival party, Thuc. 2. of things, like ἰσόπαλος, nearly balanced, id.; ἀντ. τριήρης equally large, id.; ἀντ. δέος fear equal on both sides, mutual fear, id.; ἤθεα ἀντίπαλα [τῆι πόλει] habits corresponding to the constitution, id.:— τὸ ἀντίπαλον τῆς ναυμαχίας the equal balance, undecided state of the action, id.:—adv. -λως, and in neut. pl. ἀντίπαλα, id. [II.] τὸν ἀμὸν ἀντ. him who fights for me, my champion, Aesch.

αντιπαραβαλλω.gloss: to hold side by side, to compare
αντιπαραβαλλω.def: ἀντιπαραβάλλω to hold side by side, to compare or contrast, τι πρός τι or παρά τι Plat., etc.

αντιπαραβολη.def: ἀντιπαραβολή (from ἀντιπαραβάλλω) close comparison or contrast, Arist.

αντιπαραγγελια.def: ἀντιπαραγγελία competition for a public office, Plut.

αντιπαραγγελλω.def: ἀντιπαραγγέλλω I. to command in turn or also, Xen. II. to compete for a public office, τινί with one, Plut.

αντιπαραγω.gloss: to lead the army against, advance to meet the enemy
αντιπαραγω.def: ἀντιπαράγω (sub. στρατόν) to lead the army against, advance to meet the enemy, Xen.

αντιπαρακαλεω.def: ἀντιπαρακαλέω to summon in turn or contrariwise, Thuc., etc.

αντιπαρακελευομαι.def: ἀντιπαρακελεύομαι Dep. to exhort in turn or contrariwise, Thuc., etc.

αντιπαραλυπεω.def: ἀντιπαραλυπέω to annoy in turn, Thuc.

αντιπαραπλεω.gloss: to sail along on the other side
αντιπαραπλεω.def: ἀντιπαραπλέω to sail along on the other side, Thuc.

αντιπαρασκευαζομαι.gloss: to prepare oneself in turn, arm on both sides
αντιπαρασκευαζομαι.def: ἀντιπαρασκευάζομαι Mid. to prepare oneself in turn, arm on both sides, Thuc.; ἀντ. ἀλλήλοις ὡς ἐς μάχην id.

αντιπαρατασσομαι.def: ἀντιπαρατάσσομαι Mid. and Pass. to stand in array against, τινι Thuc.; πρός τι Aeschin.:—absol. to stand in hostile array, Thuc.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιπαραταχθέντος in hostile array, id.

αντιπαρατεινω.def: ἀντιπαρατείνω to stretch side by side, so as to compare, τι πρός τι Plat.

αντιπαρατιθημι.def: ἀντιπαρατίθημι to contrast and compare, τινί τι Plat.

αντιπαρειμι.gloss: to march so as to meet
αντιπαρειμι.def: ἀντιπάρειμι (εἶμι ibo) to march so as to meet, of armies on opposite sides of a river or the like, Xen.

αντιπαρεξαγω.def: ἀντιπαρεξάγω I. to lead on against, Plut. II. (sub. στρατόν) to march against, Philipp. ap. Dem. 2. to march parallel with, τινί Plut.

αντιπαρερχομαι.gloss: to pass by on the opposite side
αντιπαρερχομαι.def: ἀντιπαρέρχομαι Dep. to pass by on the opposite side, NTest.

αντιπαρεχω.def: ἀντιπαρέχω to supply in turn, Thuc.:—Mid., Xen.; ἀντ. πράγματα to cause trouble in return, Dem.

αντιπασχω.def: ἀντιπάσχω 1. to suffer in turn, ἀντιπάσχω χρηστά I receive good for good done, Soph.; ἀντ. ἀντί τινος Thuc.: absol. to suffer for one's acts, Xen. 2. absol., τὸ ἀντιπεπονθός reciprocity, Arist.

αντιπαταγεω.gloss: to clatter so as to drown
αντιπαταγεω.def: ἀντιπαταγέω to clatter so as to drown other sounds, Thuc.

αντιπεμπω.def: ἀντιπέμπω I. to send back an answer, Hdt. 2. to send in repayment, Soph. II. to send against, στρατιάν τινι Thuc. III. to send in the place of another, στρατηγούς id.

αντιπενθησ.def: ἀντιπενθής (πένθος) causing grief in turn, Aesch.

αντιπεραιοσ.def: ἀντιπέραιος lying over against: ἀντιπέραια the lands just opposite, Il.

αντιπερασ.gloss: over against, on the other side
αντιπερασ.def: ἀντιπέρας over against, on the other side, c. gen., Thuc.; absol., ἡ ἀντ. Θράικη id.

αντιπερηθεν.def: ἀντιπέρηθεν from the opposite side, c. gen., Anth.

αντιπεριλαμβανω.def: ἀντιπεριλαμβάνω to embrace in turn, Xen.

αντιπεριπλεω.gloss: to sail round on the other side
αντιπεριπλεω.def: ἀντιπεριπλέω to sail round on the other side, Strab.

αντιπεριχωρεω.def: ἀντιπεριχωρέω to move round in turn or in opposition, Plut.

αντιπηξ.def: ἀντίπηξ (πήγνυμι) a kind of cradle for infants, on wheels, Eur.

αντιπιπτω.def: ἀντιπίπτω to fall against, resist, τινί NTest.

αντιπλεω.def: ἀντιπλέω to sail against an enemy, Thuc.

αντιπληξ.def: ἀντιπλήξ beaten by the opposing waves, Soph.

αντιπληροω.def: ἀντιπληρόω I. to man ships against the enemy, Thuc. II. to fill up by new members, Xen.

αντιπλησσω.def: ἀντιπλήσσω to strike in turn, Arist.

αντιπνεω.def: ἀντιπνέω of winds to be contrary, Plut., Luc.

αντιπνοοσ.def: ἀντίπνοος (from ἀντιπνέω) caused by adverse winds, Aesch.: adverse, hostile, id.

αντιποθεω.def: ἀντιποθέω to long for in turn, τι Xen.

αντιποιεω.def: ἀντιποιέω I. to do in return, τι Plat.: absol. to retaliate, Xen. II. Mid. to exert oneself about a thing, seek after, lay claim to, c. gen., Thuc., Plat., etc.; c. inf., ἀντ. ἐπίστασθαί τι to lay claim to knowing, Plat. 2. to contend with one for a thing, ἀντ. τινὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς Xen.; τινι περί τινος id.

αντιποινα.def: ἀντίποινα (ποινή) requital, retribution, ἀντίποινα τίνειν ἀντιτίνειν, to atone for, c. acc., Aesch.; ἀντίποινά τινος πράσσειν to exact retribution for a thing, id.; ἀντίποιν’ ἐμοῦ παθεῖν to suffer retribution forthe wrong done me, Soph.

αντιπολεμεω.def: ἀντιπολεμέω to urge war against others, Thuc., etc.; c. dat., Xen.

αντιπολεμιοσ.def: ἀντιπολέμιος warring against, οἱ ἀντιπολέμιοι enemies, Thuc.

αντιπολιορκεω.def: ἀντιπολιορκέω to besiege in turn, Thuc.

αντιπολισ.def: ἀντίπολις a rival city, τινι Strab.

αντιπολιτευομαι.def: ἀντιπολιτεύομαι Dep. to be a political opponent, Arist.; ἀντ. τινι to oppose his policy, Plut.

αντιπορειν.def: ἀντιπορεῖν (aor2 with no pres. in use) to give instead, Anth.

αντιπορευομαι.def: ἀντιπορεύομαι Pass. to march to meet another, Xen.

αντιπορθεω.def: ἀντιπορθέω to ravage in return, Eur.

αντιπορθμοσ.gloss: over the straits, on the opposite side of the straits
αντιπορθμοσ.def: ἀντίπορθμος over the straits, on the opposite side of the straits, Aesch., Eur.

αντιποροσ.def: ἀντίπορος on the opposite coast, Aesch.; Ἄρτεμιν Χαλκίδος ἀντίπορον, i. e. her temple at Aulis over against Chalcis, id.:—simply, over against, opposite to, τινι Xen.

αντιπρασσω.gloss: to act against, seek to counteract
αντιπρασσω.def: ἀντιπράσσω to act against, seek to counteract, τινί Xen.:— absol. to act in opposition, Hdt., etc.; so in Mid., Xen.

αντιπρεσβευομαι.def: ἀντιπρεσβεύομαι Mid. to send counter-ambassadors, Thuc.

αντιπροειμι.def: ἀντιπρόειμι (εἶμι ibo) to come forward against or to meet, τινί Thuc.

αντιπροικα.def: ἀντίπροικα for next to nothing, cheap, Xen.

αντιπροκαλεομαι.def: ἀντιπροκαλέομαι Mid. to retort a legal challenge (πρόκλησις), Dem.

αντιπροσαγορευω.def: ἀντιπροσαγορεύω to salute in turn, Plut.

αντιπροσειμι.def: ἀντιπρόσειμι (εἶμι ibo) to go against, Xen.

αντιπροσειπον.def: ἀντιπροσεῖπον (ἀντιπροσαγορεύω) serving as aor2 to ἀντιπροσαγορεύω, Theophr.: aor1 pass. ἀντιπροσερρήθην, Xen.

αντιπροσκαλεομαι.def: ἀντιπροσκαλέομαι to summon in turn, Dem.

αντιπροσφερω.def: ἀντιπροσφέρω to bring near in turn, τί τινι Xen.

αντιπροσωποσ.def: ἀντιπρόσωπος (πρόσωπον) with the face towards, facing, τινι Xen.: face to face, id.

αντιπροτεινω.def: ἀντιπροτείνω to offer in turn, τὴν δεξιάν Xen.

αντιπρωροσ.def: ἀντίπρῳρος (πρώιρα) 1. with the prow towards, Hdt., Thuc.: prow to prow, Thuc. 2. like ἀντιπρόσωπος, face to face, Soph.

αντιπυλοσ.def: ἀντίπυλος (πύλη) with gates opposite, ἀλλήληισι Hdt.

αντιπυργοω.gloss: to build a tower over against
αντιπυργοω.def: ἀντιπυργόω to build a tower over against, πόλιν τήνδ’ ἀντεπύργωσαν reared up this rival city, Aesch.

αντιρροποσ.def: ἀντίρροπος (from ἀντιρρέπω) counterpoising, compensating for, τινός Dem.; λύπης ἀντ. ἄχθος the counterpoising weight of sorrow, Soph.:—adv., ἀντιρρόπως πράττειν τινί so as to balance his power, Xen.

αντισεμνυνομαι.def: ἀντισεμνύνομαι Mid. to meet pride with pride, Arist.

αντισηκοω.def: ἀντισηκόω to counterbalance, compensate for, c. dat., Aesch.; c. gen., Eur.

αντισκευαζομαι.gloss: to furnish for oneself in turn
αντισκευαζομαι.def: ἀντισκευάζομαι Mid. to furnish for oneself in turn, Xen.

αντισκωπτω.def: ἀντισκώπτω to mock in return, Plut.

αντισοομαι.def: ἀντισόομαι (ἰσόω) Pass to oppose on equal terms, Thuc.

αντισπαστοσ.gloss: drawn in the contrary direction: spasmodic, convulsive
αντισπαστοσ.def: ἀντίσπαστος (from ἀντισπάω) drawn in the contrary direction: spasmodic, convulsive, Soph.

αντισπαω.gloss: to draw the contrary way, hold back
αντισπαω.def: ἀντισπάω 1. to draw the contrary way, hold back, Aesch., Ar.: Pass. to suffer a check, Arist. 2. to draw to itself, Xen.

αντισταθμοσ.def: ἀντίσταθμος (στάθμη) counterpoising: in compensation for, c. gen., Soph.

αντιστασιαζω.def: ἀντιστασιάζω to form a party against, τινί Xen.; οἱ ἀντιστασιάζοντες οἱ ἀντιστασιῶται, id.

αντιστασισ.def: ἀντίστασις I. an opposite party, Plat. II. a standing against, resistance, Plut.

αντιστασιωτησ.def: ἀντιστασιώτης one of the opposite faction or party, Hdt., Xen.

αντιστατεω.def: ἀντιστατέω (from ἀντιστάτης) to resist, oppose, τινί Plat.; absol., Hdt.

αντιστοιχεω.def: ἀντιστοιχέω (from ἀντίστοιχος) to stand opposite in rows or pairs, ἀλλήλοις Xen.: to stand vis-a-vis in a dance, id.

αντιστοιχοσ.def: ἀντίστοιχος ranged opposite in rows or pairs, Arist.: standing over against, Eur.

αντιστρατευομαι.def: ἀντιστρατεύομαι Dep. to make war against, τινι Xen.

αντιστρατηγεω.def: ἀντιστρατηγέω (from ἀντιστράτηγος) to be Propraetor, Plut.

αντιστρατηγοσ.def: ἀντιστράτηγος I. the enemy's general, Thuc. II. the Propraetor or Pro-consul, Polyb.

αντιστρατοπεδεια.def: ἀντιστρατοπεδεία (from ἀντιστρατοπεδεύω) an encamping opposite, Polyb.

αντιστρατοπεδευω.def: ἀντιστρατοπεδεύω to encamp over against, τινί Isocr., Polyb.; mostly in Mid. with perf. pass., Hdt., attic

αντιστρεφω.gloss: to turn to the opposite side
αντιστρεφω.def: ἀντιστρέφω to turn to the opposite side: intr. to wheel about, face about, Xen.

αντιστροφη.def: ἀντιστροφή (from ἀντιστρέφω) a turning about: the antistrophe or returning of the chorus, answering to a previous στροφή, except that they now moved from left to right instead of from right to left.

αντιστροφοσ.gloss: turned so as to face one another: correlative, coordinate, counterpart
αντιστροφοσ.def: ἀντίστροφος (ἀντιστρέφω) turned so as to face one another: correlative, coordinate, counterpart, τινι to a thing, Plat.: also ἀντίστροφός τινος, as if ἀντ. were a Subst., the correlative or counterpart of, id.; adv. -φως, coordinately, τινί id.

αντισυλλογιζομαι.def: ἀντισυλλογίζομαι to answer by syllogism, Arist.

αντισυνανταω.def: ἀντισυναντάω to meet face to face, Anth.

αντισφαιριζω.def: ἀντισφαιρίζω to play at ball against, οἱ ἀντισφαιρίζοντες the parties in a game at ball, Xen.

αντιταλαντευω.def: ἀντιταλαντεύω = ἀντισηκόω, to counterbalance, compensate for, Anth.

αντιτασσω.gloss: to set opposite to, range in battle against
αντιτασσω.def: ἀντιτάσσω I. to set opposite to, range in battle against, τινά τινι Hdt., Aesch., etc.; τι πρός τι Aeschin.:—so in Mid., Thuc. II. Mid. also to set oneself against, meet face to face, meet in battle, Eur., etc.; τινι Dem.:—Pass. to be drawn out against, τινι Hdt., Xen.; πρός τινα Hdt., Xen.; κατά τινα Xen.

αντιτεινω.gloss: to stretch out in return, to offer in return, to repay
αντιτεινω.def: ἀντιτείνω I. to stretch out in return, to offer in return, to repay, τι ἀντί τινος Eur. II. intr. to strive against, counteract, resist, τινί, or absol., Hdt., attic 2. of places, to lie over against, τινί Plut.

αντιτεμνω.def: ἀντιτέμνω to cut against, i. e. to provide a remedy or antidote, Eur.

αντιτεχναομαι.def: ἀντιτεχνάομαι Dep to contrive in opposition, counterplan, c. acc., Hdt.

αντιτεχνοσ.def: ἀντίτεχνος (τέχνη) rivalling in an art or craft, Ar., Plat.; c. dat., Plat.

αντιτιθημι.def: ἀντιτίθημι I. to set against, oppose, c. dat., Simon.: to contrast, compare, τί τινι Hdt., Eur.; also τί τινος, Thuc.; τι πρός τι Dem. 2. ἀντ. τινά τινι to match one against the other in battle, Lat. committere, ἴσους ἴσοισι ἀντιθείς Eur.:—Pass. to be matched one against another, Hdt. 3. to retort, rejoin, Eur., Thuc. II. to deposit in return, Eur., Xen.:— to give in return or as a recompense, τί τινος one thing for another, Eur.

αντιτιμαω.def: ἀντιτιμάω I. to honour in return, τινά, Xen.:—f. mid. in pass. sense, id. II. Mid as law-term, to fix a counter-estimate of damages, c. gen. pretii, Plat.

αντιτιμωρεομαι.def: ἀντιτιμωρέομαι Dep. to avenge oneself on, τινα Eur., Thuc.; absol. to take vengeance, Ar.

αντιτινω.def: ἀντιτίνω I. to pay or suffer punishment for a thing, τι Theogn.; absol., Soph. II. Mid. to exact or inflict in turn, τί τινος one thing for another, Aesch., Eur. 2. to avenge, punish, σὸν φόνον Eur.

αντιτολμαω.def: ἀντιτολμάω to dare to stand against another, πρός τινα Thuc.

αντιτομοσ.def: ἀντίτομος (ἀντιτέμνω) cut as a remedy for an evil: —ἀντίτομον, ου, τό, a remedy, antidote, Hom.; τινος for a thing, Pind.

αντιτονοσ.def: ἀντίτονος (ἀντιτείνω) strained against, resisting: as Subst., ἀντίτονα, τά, cords for a ballista, Plut.

αντιτοξευω.def: ἀντιτοξεύω to shoot arrows in turn, Xen.

αντιτορεω.def: ἀντιτορέω to bore right through, c. gen., Il.; c. acc. to break open, id.

αντιτοσ.def: ἄντιτος paid back, requited, avenged: ἄντιτα ἔργα the work of revenge or retribution, Od.; παιδός for her son, Il.

αντιτρεφω.def: ἀντιτρέφω to maintain in turn, Xen.

αντιτυγχανω.def: ἀντιτυγχάνω to meet with in return, τινός Theogn., Thuc.

αντιτυποσ.def: ἀντίτυπος (τύπτω) I. repelled by a hard body, τύπος ἀντ. blow and counter-blow, of hammer and anvil, Orac. ap. Hdt.:—of sound, echoed, echoing, στόνος Soph.; κατὰ τὸ ἀντ. by repercussion, of an echo, Luc. 2. corresponding, as the stamp to the die, ἀντ. τῶν ἀληθινῶν figuring or representing the true, NTest. II. act., of a hard body, repellent, rigid, Xen.; of hard ground, ἀντιτύπᾳ ἐπὶ γᾶι πέσε Soph. 2. metaph. of men, stubborn, obstinate, Xen. 3. opposed to, τινός Aesch.: adverse, of events, Xen.

αντιτυποω.gloss: to express as by a figure
αντιτυποω.def: ἀντιτυπόω to express as by a figure, Anth.

αντιτυπτω.def: ἀντιτύπτω to beat in turn, Ar., Plat.

αντιφεριζω.gloss: to set oneself against, measure oneself with
αντιφεριζω.def: ἀντιφερίζω (ἀντιφέρω) to set oneself against, measure oneself with, τινί Il., Ar.; παρά τινα Pind.

αντιφερνοσ.def: ἀντίφερνος (φερνή) instead of a dower, Aesch.

αντιφερω.def: ἀντιφέρω to set against, τι ἐπί τινι Anth.:—Dep or Pass. to set oneself against, fight against, Hom.

αντιφευγω.gloss: to go into exile in turn
αντιφευγω.def: ἀντιφεύγω to go into exile in turn, Eur.

αντιφημι.def: ἀντίφημι to speak against, to contradict, Plat.

αντιφθεγγομαι.def: ἀντιφθέγγομαι I. to return a sound, echo, Pind., Eur. II. to speak against, Luc.

αντιφθογγοσ.def: ἀντίφθογγος (from ἀντιφθέγγομαι) of answering sound, imitative, Anth.

αντιφιλεω.def: ἀντιφιλέω to love in return, Plat., Xen.

αντιφιλησισ.def: ἀντιφίλησις (from ἀντιφιλέω) return of affection, Arist.

αντιφιλοσοφεω.def: ἀντιφιλοσοφέω to hold contrary tenets, Luc.

αντιφιλοτιμεομαι.gloss: to be moved by jealousy against
αντιφιλοτιμεομαι.def: ἀντιφιλοτιμέομαι Pass. to be moved by jealousy against, πρός τι Plut.

αντιφιλοφρονεομαι.def: ἀντιφιλοφρονέομαι Dep to receive kindly in turn, Plut.

αντιφονοσ.gloss: in return for slaughter, in revenge for blood
αντιφονοσ.def: ἀντίφονος I. in return for slaughter, in revenge for blood, Aesch., Soph. II. θάνατοι ἀντ. deaths by mutual slaughter, Aesch.

αντιφορτιζομαι.gloss: to take in a return cargo
αντιφορτιζομαι.def: ἀντιφορτίζομαι I. Mid. to take in a return cargo, Dem. II. to import in exchange for exports, Xen.: also as Pass., to be received in exchange for the cargo, id.

αντιφρασσω.def: ἀντιφράσσω to barricade, block up, Xen.

αντιφυλακη.def: ἀντιφυλακή a watching one against another, Thuc.

αντιφυλαξ.def: ἀντιφύλαξ one posted to watch another, Luc.

αντιφυλασσω.def: ἀντιφυλάσσω to watch in turn, Plat.:—Mid. to be on one's guard against, τινά Xen.

αντιφωνεω.def: ἀντιφωνέω 1. to sound in answer, reply, Trag. 2. c. acc. rei, to utter in reply, Soph.:—c. acc. pers. to reply to, answer, id.

αντιφωνοσ.def: ἀντίφωνος (φωνή) sounding in answer, responsive to, c. gen., Eur.

αντιχαιρω.def: ἀντιχαίρω (in aor.2 pass. part. ἀντιχαρείς.) to rejoice in answer to, τινί Soph.

αντιχαριζομαι.def: ἀντιχαρίζομαι to shew kindness in turn, τινί Hdt., Xen.

αντιχειροτονεω.def: ἀντιχειροτονέω to vote against doing a thing, ἀντ. μὴ παρέχειν Ar.; absol., Thuc.

αντιχορηγεω.def: ἀντιχορηγέω (from ἀντιχόρηγος) to be a rival choragus, τινί to another, Dem.

αντιχορηγοσ.def: ἀντιχόρηγος a rival choragus, Dem., etc.

αντιχραω.def: ἀντιχράω (χράω B) (only in aor1, ἀντέχρησε) to be sufficient, like ἀποχράω, Hdt.

αντιψαλλω.gloss: to play a lyre in accompaniment to
αντιψαλλω.def: ἀντιψάλλω to play a lyre in accompaniment to, τινί Ar.

αντιψηφιζομαι.def: ἀντιψηφίζομαι Dep to vote against, πρός τι Plut.

αντλεω.gloss: to bale out bilge-water, bale the ship
αντλεω.def: ἀντλέω (ἄντλος) I. to bale out bilge-water, bale the ship, Theogn., Eur. 2. generally, to draw water, Hdt. II. metaph. of toil or suffering, to exhaust, come to the end of, like Lat. exantlare or exhaurire labores, Aesch., Eur. 2. to squander, Soph.

αντλημα.def: ἄντλημα (from ἀντλέω) a bucket for drawing water, NTest.

αντλια.def: ἀντλία 1. the hold of a ship, Soph., Ar. 2. bilge-water, filth, Ar.

αντλοσ.def: ἄντλος (perhaps for ἀνά-τλος, the Root of -τλος being ΤΛΕ, τλάω) 1. the hold of a ship, where the bilgewater settles, Lat. sentina, Od. 2. the bilge-water in the hold, Eur.; ἄντλον οὐκ ἐδέξατο let in no bilgewater, metaph. for "let no enemy come in, " Aesch.; εἰς ἄντλον ἐμβαίνειν πόδα, metaph. for getting into a difficulty, Eur.

αντοικτειρω.def: ἀντοικτείρω to pity in return, τινά Eur.

αντομαι.def: ἄντομαι (ἀντί) (Dep. only in pres. and impf.) I. =ἀντάω to meet, in battle, c. dat., Il.:—absol., διπλόος ἤντετο θώρηξ the breastplate doubled (by the belt) met or stopped (the dart), id. II. = ἀντιάζω 1. 2, c. acc. pers. to approach with prayers, entreat, Soph., Eur.

αντομνυμι.def: ἀντόμνυμι to swear in turn, c. fut. inf., Xen.

αντονομαζω.gloss: to name instead, call by a new name
αντονομαζω.def: ἀντονομάζω to name instead, call by a new name, Thuc.

αντοφειλω.def: ἀντοφείλω to owe one a good turn, Thuc.

αντοφθαλμεω.gloss: to meet face to face, to face
αντοφθαλμεω.def: ἀντοφθαλμέω (ὀφθαλμός) to meet face to face, to face, τινί Polyb., NTest.

αντοχεομαι.def: ἀντοχέομαι Pass. to drive or ride against, Mosch.

αντριασ.def: ἀντριάς ⁎Fem. adj. of a grotto, Anth.

αντρον.def: ἄντρον Lat. antrum, a cave, grot, cavern, Od., Trag.

αντυξ.def: ἄντυξ I. like ἴτυς, the edge or rim of anything round or curved: 1. the rim of the round shield, Il. 2. the rail round the front of the chariot, the chariot-rail, id.; sometimes double, and therefore ἄντυγες in pl., id., Soph. II. post-Hom., 1. in pl. the chariot itself, Soph., Eur. 2. the frame of the lyre, Eur. 3. the orbit of a planet, Hhymn.; the disk of the moon, Mosch.

αντωδοσ.def: ἀντῳδός (ἄιδω) singing in answer, responsive, Ar., Anth.

αντωμοσια.def: ἀντωμοσία (ἀντόμνυμι) an oath or affidavit made one against the other, i. e. by plaintiff and defendant, Plat., etc.

αντωνεομαι.def: ἀντωνέομαι 1. Dep to buy instead, Xen. 2. to bid against, ἀλλήλοις Lys.; ὁ ἀντωνούμενος a rival bidder, Dem.

αντωποσ.gloss: with the eyes opposite, facing, fronting
αντωποσ.def: ἀντωπός (ὤψ) with the eyes opposite, facing, fronting, Luc., Anth.

αντωφελεω.def: ἀντωφελέω to assist or benefit in turn, τινά Xen.:—Pass. to derive profit in turn, id.

ανυβριστοσ.def: ἀνύβριστος (ὑβρίζω) I. not insulted, Plut. II. act. not insolent, decorous, id.

ανυδροσ.def: ἄνυδρος (ὕδωρ) wanting water, waterless, of arid countries, Hdt.:—of a corpse, deprived of funeral lustrations, Eur.

ανυμεναιοσ.def: ἀνυμέναιος without the nuptial song, unwedded, Soph., Eur.: neut. pl. as adv., Soph., Eur.

ανυμνεω.def: ἀνυμνέω to praise in song, c. acc., Eur.

ανυμφευτοσ.def: ἀνύμφευτος (νυμφεύω) unwedded, Soph.; ἀν. γονή birth from an ill-starred marriage, id.

ανυμφοσ.def: ἄνυμφος (νύμφη) I. not bridal, unwedded, Soph.; νύμφη ἄνυμφος a bride that is no bride, unhappy bride, Eur. II. without bride or mistress, μέλαθρα id.

ανυπερβλητοσ.def: ἀνυπέρβλητος (ὑπερβάλλω) not to be surpassed or outdone, Xen., etc.:—adv. -τως, Arist.

ανυπευθυνοσ.gloss: not liable to give account, irresponsible
ανυπευθυνοσ.def: ἀνυπεύθυνος (εὐθῦναι) not liable to give account, irresponsible, Ar., Plat.

ανυποδησια.def: ἀνυποδησία (from ἀνυπόδητος) a going barefoot, Plat., Xen.

ανυποδητεω.def: ἀνυποδητέω (from ἀνυπόδητος) to go barefoot, Luc.

ανυποδικοσ.def: ἀνυπόδικος not liable to action, Plut.

ανυποπτοσ.def: ἀνύποπτος without suspicion, unsuspected, Thuc., Xen.:—adv. -τως, unsuspectedly, Thuc.

ανυποστατοσ.def: ἀνυπόστατος (ὑφίστημι) not to be withstood, irresistible, Xen., etc.

ανυποτακτοσ.def: ἀνυπότακτος (ὑποτάσσω) I. not made subject, τινι NTest. II. unruly, refractory, of persons, id.

ανυσιεργοσ.def: ἀνυσιεργός (ἔργον) (ᾱ metri grat.) finishing work, industrious, Theocr.

ανυσιμοσ.def: ἀνύσιμος (ἀνύω) efficacious, effectual, εἴς τι Xen.: adv. -μως, Sup. -ώτατα, Plat.

ανυστοσ.def: ἀνυστός (ἀνύω) to be accomplished, practicable, Eur.; ὡς ἀνυστόν, like ὡς δυνατόν, σιγῆι ὡς ἀν. as silently as possible, Xen.

ανυτικοσ.def: ἀνυτικός to be accomplished, practicable, Xen.

ανυφαινω.def: ἀνυφαίνω to weave anew, renew, Plat.

ανυψοω.def: ἀνυψόω to raise up, exalt, Anth., in Mid.

ανυω.def: ἀνύω (the Verb ἄνω) I. to effect, achieve, accomplish, complete, Lat. conficere, c. acc. rei, Hom., etc.; absol., οὐδὲν ἤνυε he did no good, Hdt.; c. acc. et inf. to bring to pass that.., Soph.:—Mid. to accomplish for one's own advantage, Od., Plat., etc. 2. to make an end of, destroy, Hom., etc. 3. to finish a journey, ὅσσον νηῦς ἤνυσεν much as a ship can do, Od.; so, ἀν. θαλάσσης ὕδωρ to make its way over the sea water, id. 4. in attic absol. to make one's way, πρὸς πόλιν Soph.; ἐπὶ ἀκτάν Eur.; also, θάλαμον ἀνύτειν to reach the bridal chamber, Soph.; with inf., ἤνυσε περᾶν succeeded in crossing, Aesch.; and with an adj., εἶναι being omitted, εὐδαίμων ἀνύσει will come to be happy, Soph. 5. Pass. of Time, to come to an end, Theocr. 6. in Pass. also of persons, to grow up, Aesch. 7. to get, procure, φορβάν Soph., etc. II. with a partic., οὐκ ἀνύω φθονέουσα I gain nothing by gruding, Il. III. to do quickly, make haste, Ar.; then, like φθάνω, ἄνυε πράττων make haste about it, id.; ἄνυσον ὑποδησάμενος make haste and get your shoes on, id.; also ἀνύσας with an imperat., ἄνοιγ’, ἄνοιγ’ ἀνύσας make haste and open the door, id.; ἀνύσας τρέχε, λέγ’ ἀνύσας id., etc.

ανω.def: ἄνω (radic. form of ἀνύω,) I. to accomplish, achieve, finish, ὁδόν Od.; οὐδὲν ἦνον Eur. II. Pass., of the close ofa period of time, νὺξ ἄνεται night is drawing to a close, Il.; ἔτος ἀνόμενον the waning year, Hdt.:—generally to be finished, Il.; ἤνετο τὸ ἔργον Hdt.

ἄνω (ἀνά) I. implying Motion, I. up, upwards, Hom., etc.; ἄνω ἰόντι going up the country, (i.e. inland), Hdt. II. implying Rest, up, aloft, on high, Soph., Plat., etc. 2. on earth, as opp. to the world below, Soph.; οἱ ἄνω the living, opp. to οἱ κάτω the dead, id. 3. in heaven, as opp. to earth, οἱ ἄνω θεοί the gods above, Lat. superi, id. 4. generally of position, ἄνω καθῆσθαι to sit in the upper quarter of the city, i. e. the Pnyx, Dem.; ἡ ἄνω βουλή, i. e. the Areopagus, Plut. 5. geographically, on the north, northward, Hdt. 6. inward from the coast, id., Xen.; ὁ ἄνω βασιλεύς the king of Persia, Hdt. 7. of Time, formerly, of old, Plat., etc. 8. above, like Lat. supra, in referring to a passage, id. 9. of tones in the voice, Plut. III. ἄνω καὶ κάτω, up and down, to and fro, Eur., Ar., etc. 2. upside down, topsy-turvy, Lat. susque deque, τὰ μὲν ἄνω κάτω θήσω, τὰ δὲ κάτω ἄνω Hdt.; ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω στρέφων Aesch., etc. B. as prep. with gen. above, Hdt. C. comp. ἀνωτέρω, absol. higher, Aesch.; further, Hdt. 2. c. gen. above, beyond, id. II. Sup. ἀνωτάτω highest, id., etc.

ανωγα.def: ἄνωγα (Deriv. uncertain.) (The verb ἄνωγα is a perfect form with present sense. The pluperfect is used with imperfect sense.) to command, order, also to advise, desire, urge:— c. acc. pers. et inf., σιωπᾶν λαὸν ἀνώγει bade the people keep silence, Il.; also c. dat. pers., Od.; c. acc. pers., without inf., θυμὸς ἄνωγέ με my spirit bids me, Hom.

ανωγαιον.gloss: anything raised from the ground; the upper floor of a house
ανωγαιον.def: ἀνώγαιον (ἄνω, γαῖα) anything raised from the ground; the upper floor of a house, used as a granary, Xen.; as a dining-room, Lat. coenaculum, NTest.

ανωδυνοσ.def: ἀνώδυνος (ὀδύνη) I. free from pain, Soph. II. act. allaying pain, Anth.

ανωθεν.def: ἄνωθεν (ἄνω) I. adv. of place from above, from on high, Hdt., Trag., etc.; ὕδατος ἄνωθεν γενομένου, i. e. rain, Thuc.: from the upper country, from inland, id. 2. = ἄνω, above, on high, Trag.; οἱ ἄν. the living, opp. to οἱ κάτω, Aesch.:—c. gen., Hdt. II. of Time, from the beginning, Plat., Dem.:— by descent, Theocr.; τὰ ἄν. first principles, Plat. 2. over again, anew, NTest.

ανωθεω.gloss: to push up, push off from shore
ανωθεω.def: ἀνωθέω 1. to push up, push off from shore, Od. 2. Mid. to push back from oneself, to repel, repulse, Hdt.

ανωιστοσ.def: ἀνώιστος (οἴομαι) unlooked for, unexpected, Il., Mosch.

ανωλεθροσ.def: ἀνώλεθρος (ὄλεθρος) indestructible, Plat.; epic ἀν-όλεθρος having escaped ruin, Il.

ανωμαλια.def: ἀνωμαλία (from ἀνώμαλος) 1. unevenness, Plat., etc. 2. of persons, irregularity, Aeschin.

ανωμαλοσ.def: ἀνώμαλος (ὁμαλός) 1. uneven, irregular, Plat.: τὸ ἀν. unevenness of ground, Thuc. 2. of fortune, id.

ανωμοτοσ.def: ἀνώμοτος (ὄμνυμι) I. unsworn, not bound by oath, Eur.; θεῶν ἀνώμοτος without swearing by the gods, id. II. not sworn to, εἰρήνη Dem.

ανωνομαστοσ.def: ἀνωνόμαστος (ὀνομάζω) nameless, indescribable, ineffable, Eur., Ar.

ανωνυμοσ.def: ἀνώνυμος (ὄνυμα, aeolic for ὄνομα) I. without name, nameless, Od., Hdt., etc. II. nameless, inglorious, Pind., Eur., Plat.

ανωρια.def: ἀνωρία (from ἄνωρος) untimeliness, ἀν. τοῦ ἔτεος the bad season of the year, Hdt.

ανωρυομαι.def: ἀνωρύομαι Dep to howl aloud, Anth.

ανωτατοσ.def: ἀνώτατος Sup. adj. formed from ἄνω, topmost, Hdt.

ανωφελησ.def: ἀνωφελής (ὠφελέω) 1. unprofitable, useless, Aesch., Soph., etc. 2. hurtful, prejudicial, Thuc.; τινι to one, Plat.: adv. -λῶς, Arist.

ανωφελητοσ.def: ἀνωφέλητος (ὠφελέω) unprofitable, useless, Soph.; τινι to one, Aesch.

αξεινοσ.def: Ἄξεινος sc. πόντος, the Axine, afterwards called the Euxine (Euxeinus qui nunc Axenus ille fuit Ov.), Pind., Eur.

αξενοσ.def: ἄξενος inhospitable, of persons, Hes., Plat.; of places, Soph., Eur.:—comp. and Sup. -ώτερος, -ώτατος, Eur.

αξια.def: ἀξία (ἄξιος) 1. the worth or value of a thing, c. gen., Hdt., Eur.; money-value, price, amount, Hdt.; τῆς ἀξίας τιμᾶσθαι to estimate the penalty at the real amount, Plat.; κατ’ ἀξίαν τῆς οὐσίας Xen. 2. of persons, worth, reputation, rank, Thuc., etc. 3. generally, a man's due, his deserts, τὴν ἀξίαν λαμβάνειν, τῆς ἀξίας τυγχάνειν to get one's deserts, Hdt., Ar.; κατ’ ἀξίαν according to desert, duly, Eur., Plat.; παρὰ τὴν ἀξίαν, οὐ κατ’ ἀξίαν Thuc., Dem.

αξινη.def: ἀξίνη (Deriv. unknown.) an axe-head, Il.: battle-axe. id.: generally, an axe, Xen., NTest.

αξιοθεατοσ.def: ἀξιοθέατος well worth seeing, Hdt., Xen.

αξιοκοινωνητοσ.def: ἀξιοκοινώνητος (κοινωνέω) worthy of one's society, Plat.

αξιολογοσ.def: ἀξιόλογος (λέγω) 1. worthy of mention, noteworthy, Hdt., Plat., etc.; πόλεμος ἀξιολογώτατος Thuc.:— adv. -γως, Xen. 2. of persons, of note, important, Thuc.

αξιομακαριστοσ.def: ἀξιομακάριστος worthy to be deemed happy, Xen.

αξιομαχοσ.def: ἀξιόμαχος (μάχομαι) 1. a match for another in battle or war, τινι Hdt., Thuc.; πρός τινα Plut.: absol., Hdt., etc. 2. c. inf. sufficient in strength or number to do a thing, id. adv. -χως, Plut.

αξιομνημονευτοσ.def: ἀξιομνημόνευτος (μνημονεύω) worthy of mention, Plat., Xen.; shapely, beautiful, Manetho.

αξιονικοσ.def: ἀξιόνικος (νίκη) worthy of victory, Xen.; c. inf., ἀξιονικότερος ἔχειν τοῦτο τὸ κράτος more worthy to hold this power, Hdt.

αξιοπιστοσ.def: ἀξιόπιστος trustworthy, Plat., Dem.; εἴς τι in a thing, Xen.

αξιοσ.gloss: weighing as much, of like value, worth as much as
αξιοσ.def: ἄξιος (ἄγω IV, and so properly weighing as much.) I. weighing as much, of like value, worth as much as, c. gen., Il., Hdt.; οὐδ’ ἑνὸς ἄξιοί εἰμεν Ἕκτορος we are not worth one Hector, Il.; πάντων ἄξιον ἦμαρ, Lat. instar omnium, id.; πολλοῦ ἄξιος worth much, Xen.; πλείστου ἄξιον, quantivis pretii, Thuc.; so, παντός, τοῦ παντὸς ἄξιον Plat.; λόγου ἄξιος, ἀξιόλογος, Hdt., etc.:—opp. to these are οὐδενὸς ἄξ. Theogn.; ὀλίγου, σμικροῦ ἄξ. Plat., etc. 2. c. dat. pers., σοὶ δ’ ἄξιόν ἐστιν ἀμοιβῆς ’tis worth a return to thee, i. e. will bring thee a return, Od.; πολλοῦ or πλείστου ἄξιον εἶναί τινι Xen., etc. 3. absol. worthy, goodly, of persons and things, Od., etc.; in attic it sometimes has an opposite sense, of a proper value, cheap, Ar. b. of things, deserved, meet, due, δίκη Soph.; χάρις Xen. 4. sufficient for, c. gen., Dem. II. worthy of, deserving, meet for, c. gen. rei, φυγῆς, γέλωτος Eur.; c. gen. pers., ποιεῖν ἄξια οὔτε ὑμῶν οὔτε πατέρων Thuc.:—c. gen. rei et dat. pers., ἡμῖν δ’ Ἀχιλλεὺς ἄξιος τιμῆς is worthy of honour at our hands, Eur.; πολλῶν ἀγαθῶν ἄξιος ὑμῖν Ar. 2. c. inf., πεφάσθαι ἄξιος worthy to be killed, Il.; ἄξιός εἰμι πληγὰς λαβεῖν I deserve a flogging, Ar. 3. ἄξιόν [ἐστι] ’tis meet, fit, due, Il., Hdt.; c. dat. pers. et inf., τῆι πόλει ἄξιον ξυλλαβεῖν τὸν ἄνδρα ’tis meet for the city, is her duty, to arrest the man, Ar.:—the inf. is sometimes omitted, ἄξιον γὰρ Ἑλλάδι ’tis meet in the eyes of Hellas [so to do], id. III. adv. ἀξίως, c. gen., worthily of, Hdt.:—absol., Soph.

αξιοσπουδαστοσ.def: ἀξιοσπούδαστος (σπουδάζομαι) worthy of zealous endeavours, Xen.

αξιοστρατηγοσ.def: ἀξιοστράτηγος worthy of being general, Xen.

αξιοτεκμαρτοσ.gloss: worthy of being brought in evidence, credible
αξιοτεκμαρτοσ.def: ἀξιοτέκμαρτος (τεκμαίρομαι) worthy of being brought in evidence, credible, Xen.

αξιοχρεωσ.def: ἀξιόχρεως (χρέος) worthy of a thing, and so, I. absol., like ἀξιόλογος, note-worthy, considerable, notable, Hdt., Thuc. 2. serviceable, sufficient, αἰτίη Hdt.; ἀξ. ἐγγυηταί trustworthy, substantial, Plat. II. c. inf. able, sufficient to do, Hdt., Eur., etc. III. c. gen. rei, worthy, deserving of, Hdt., Dem.

αξιοω.def: ἀξιόω (ἄξιος) I. to think or deem worthy of a thing, whether of reward, Eur., Xen.; or of punishment, Hdt., Plat.:— Pass. to be thought worthy, τινός Hdt., Eur., etc. 2. c. acc. pers. to esteem, honour, Trag. II. c. acc. pers. et inf. to think one worthy to do or be, Eur., etc.:—Pass., Aesch., etc. 2. to think fit, expect, require, demand that, Lat. postulare, ἀξ. τινα ἐλθεῖν Hdt., etc. III. c. inf. only, ἀξ. κομίζεσθαι, τυγχάνειν to think one has a right to receive, expect to receive, Thuc.:—Pass. to be required to do, Dem. 2. to think fit, expect, consent, resolve, ἀξιῶ θανεῖν Soph.; εἴ τις ἀξιοῖ μαθεῖν if he deigns to learn, Aesch.:—so in Mid., ἀξιοῦσθαι μέλειν to deign to care for, id., etc.; also as a real Mid., οὐκ ἀξιούμενος not deeming himself worthy, Hdt. IV. to claim, νικᾶν ἠξίουν claimed the victory, Thuc.: absol. to make a claim, id. V. to hold an opinion, Dem.; ἐν τῶι τοιῶιδε ἀξιοῦντι in such a state of opinion, Thuc.

αξιωμα.gloss: that of which one is thought worthy, an honour
αξιωμα.def: ἀξίωμα (ἀξιόω) I. that of which one is thought worthy, an honour, Eur.; γάμων ἀξ. honour of marriage, id. 2. honour, reputation, Lat. dignitas, Eur., Thuc. 3. rank, position, Thuc.:—of things, worth, quality, id. II. that which is thought fit, a decision, purpose, Soph., Dem. 2. in Mathematics, a self evident theorem, an axiom, Arist.

αξιωσισ.def: ἀξίωσις (ἀξιόω) I. a thinking worthy, Hdt. 2. a being thought worthy, reputation, Thuc. II. a demand or claim, id. III. a thinking fit, an opinion, principle, maxim, id. IV. ἀξ. τῶν ὀνομάτων the meaning of words, id.

αξονιοσ.def: ἀξόνιος (ἄξων) belonging to the axle, Anth.

αξυγκροτητοσ.gloss: not welded together by the hammer
αξυγκροτητοσ.def: ἀξυγκρότητος (συγκροτέω) not welded together by the hammer:— metaph. of rowers, not trained to keep time, Thuc.

αξυλοσ.def: ἄξυλος (ξύλον) I. with no timber, timberless, ἄξυλος ὕλη a coppice, brushwood, Il.:—others take it to be a wood from which no timber has been cut, a thick wood. II. without wood, Hdt.

αξων.def: ἄξων (ἄγω) I. an axle, Lat. axis, Il., etc. II. οἱ ἄξονες, the wooden tablets of Solon's laws, made to turn upon an axis, Plut.

αοζοσ.def: ἄοζος (Perh. from α copul., ὁδός; cf. ἀκόλουθος.) a servant, attendant, Aesch.

αοιδη.def: ἀοιδή (ἀείδω) 1. song, a singing, whether the art of song, Hom.; or the act of singing, song, Il. 2. the thing sung, a song, Hom., etc. 3. the subject of song, Od.

αοιδιμοσ.def: ἀοίδιμος (ἀοιδή) sung of, famous in song, Hdt.: in bad sense, notorious, infamous, Il.

αοιδοπολοσ.gloss: one busied with song, a poet
αοιδοπολοσ.def: ἀοιδοπόλος (πολέω) one busied with song, a poet, Anth.

αοιδοσ.def: ἀοιδός (ἀείδω) I. a singer, minstrel, bard, Lat. vates, Hom., Hdt.; c. gen., χρησμῶν ἀοιδός Eur.; of the cock, Theocr. 2. as fem. songstress, of the nightingale, Hes.; of the Sphinx, Soph. 3. an enchanter, Lat. incantator, id. II. as adj. tuneful, musical, ὄρνις ἀοιδοτάτα Eur.

αοικητοσ.def: ἀοίκητος (οἰκέω) I. uninhabited, Hdt. II. houseless, Dem.

αοικοσ.def: ἄοικος I. houseless, homeless, Hes., Soph., etc. II. ἄοικος εἰσοίκησις a homeless, i. e. miserable, home, Soph.

αοινοσ.def: ἄοινος 1. without wine, ἄοινοι χοαί, such as were offered to the Erinyes, Aesch.; hence Soph. calls the Erinyes ἄοινοι;—ἀοίνοις ἐμμανεῖς θυμώμασιν frantic with sober, deliberate rage, Soph. 2. of men, drinking no wine, sober, Xen.; of a place, having none, id.

αοκνοσ.def: ἄοκνος without hesitation, untiring, Hes., Soph., Thuc.

αολλησ.def: ἀολλής (α copul., εἴλω, cf. ἀλής) all together, in throngs, shoals or crowds, Hom., Soph., etc.

αολλιζω.def: ἀολλίζω (ἀολλής) I. to gather together, Il.:—Pass. to come together, assemble, id. II. of things, to gather together, heap up, Anth.

αοπλοσ.def: ἄοπλος without shields (ὅπλα), without heavy armour, Thuc., etc.: generally, unarmed, Plat.; ἅρμα ἄοπλ. a chariot without scythes, Xen.

αορ.def: ἄορ (ἀείρω) (ᾰ in ἄορ; but in trisyll. cases also ᾱ.) a hanger, sword, Hom.: he also uses a masc. acc. pl., ἄορας.

αορατοσ.gloss: unseen, not to be seen, invisible
αορατοσ.def: ἀόρατος I. unseen, not to be seen, invisible, Plat., etc. II. act. without sight, Luc.

αοργησια.gloss: a defect in the passion of anger, "lack of gall"
αοργησια.def: ἀοργησία (from ἀόργητος) a defect in the passion of anger, "lack of gall", Arist.

αοριστοσ.def: ἀόριστος (ὁρίζω) I. without boundaries, Thuc. II. undefined, indefinite, Dem., etc.

αορνοσ.def: ἄορνος (ὄρνις) I. without birds, Soph. II. Ἄορνος, ὁ, lake Avernus, Strab.

αορτεω.def: ἀορτέω (lengthened form of ἀείρω, only in aor.1 pass. part. ἀορτηθείς) suspended, Anth.

αορτηρ.def: ἀορτήρ (ἀείρω) a strap to hang anything to, a sword-belt, Hom.: a knapsack-strap, Od.

αοσσητηρ.def: ἀοσσητήρ (from ἀοσσέω) an assistant, helper, aider, Hom.

απαγγελια.def: ἀπαγγελία (from ἀπαγγέλλω) 1. a report, as of an ambassador, Dem. 2. a narrative, recital, Thuc., Plat.

απαγγελλω.def: ἀπαγγέλλω 1. of a messenger, to bring tidings, report, announce, τί τινι Il., Hdt., etc.; τι πρός τινα Aesch., etc.; ἀπ. τι οἴκαδε to carry a report home, Plat.:—absol., πάλιν ἀπ. to bring back tidings, report in answer, Od.:—Pass., ἐξ ὧν ἀπηγγέλλετο as he was reported, Dem.; c. part., ἀπηγγέλθη ἐκκεκλεμμένος was reported to have been stolen away, Hdt. 2. of a speaker or writer, to relate, narrate, id., attic

απαγε.def: ἄπαγε (properly the imperat of ἀπάγω, in intr. sense.) away! begone! hands off! Lat. apage! Eur., Ar.

απαγησ.def: ἀπαγής (πήγνυμι) not firm or stiff, of Persian caps, Hdt.

απαγινεω.def: ἀπαγινέω (ionic for ἀπάγω) (only in pres. and impf.) esp of paying tribute, Hdt.

απαγορευσισ.def: ἀπαγόρευσις (from ἀπαγορεύω) failure of strength, exhaustion, Plut., Luc.

απαγορευτεοσ.def: ἀπαγορευτέος (verb. adj. from ἀπαγορεύω) one must give up, Luc.

απαγορευω.def: ἀπαγορεύω (mostly in pres. and impf.) I. to forbid, ἀπ. τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν τι Hdt., attic; τινά Xen. 2. to dissuade, Hdt. II. intr. to bid farewell to, c. dat., ἀπαγ. τῶι πολέμωι to give up, renounce war, Plat.; c. part. to give up doing, Xen.:—absol. to give up, fail, sink, id.; of things, τὰ ἀπαγορεύοντα worn out and useless, id.

απαγριοομαι.def: ἀπαγριόομαι to become wild or savage, Soph.

απαγχω.def: ἀπάγχω to strangle, throttle, Od., Ar.; to choke with anger, Ar.:—Mid. and Pass. to hang oneself, to be hanged, Hdt., attic: to be ready to choke, Ar.

απαγω.def: ἀπάγω I. to lead away, carry off, Od., Trag.:— Mid. to take away for or with oneself, Hdt., Trag.:— Pass., ἐς ὀξὺ ἀπηγμένος brought to a point, tapering off, Hdt. 2. intr. (sub. ἑαυτόν) to retire, withdraw, march away, id., Xen.; cf. ἄπαγε. II. to bring back, bring home, Hom., attic III. to return what one owes, render, pay, τὸν φόρον Ar., Thuc. IV. to arrest and carry off, παρά τινα Hdt.:—esp. as attic lawterm, to bring before a magistrate and accuse, Dem.:— then, to carry off to prison, Plat., etc. V. to lead away from the subject, id., etc.

απαγωγη.def: ἀπαγωγή (from ἀπάγω) I. a leading away, Xen. II. payment of tribute, Hdt. III. as attic law-term, a process by which a person caught in the act (ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι) might be arrested and brought before the Magistrates, Oratt.: — the written complaint laid before the Court, Lys.

απαδω.gloss: to sing out of tune, be out of tune
απαδω.def: ἀπᾴδω I. to sing out of tune, be out of tune, Plat. II. metaph. to dissent, ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων id. 2. to wander away, ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐρωτήματος id.

απαειρω.def: ἀπαείρω poet. for ἀπαίρω, to depart, Eur.:—Mid. to depart from, c. gen., Il.

απαθανατιζω.def: ἀπαθανατίζω to aim at immortality, Plat., Arist.

απαθεια.def: ἀπάθεια (from ἀπαθής) want of sensation, insensibility, Arist.

απαθησ.def: ἀπαθής (πάθος) I. not suffering or having suffered, without experience of a thing, c. gen., Theogn., Hdt., attic:—absol., id.attic II. without passion or feeling: — adv., ἀπαθῶς ἔχειν to be without feeling, Plut.

απαιγειροομαι.gloss: to be changed into a poplar
απαιγειροομαι.def: ἀπαιγειρόομαι Pass. to be changed into a poplar, Strab.

απαιδαγωγητοσ.def: ἀπαιδαγώγητος without teacher or guide, Arist.: uneducated, untaught, τινος in a thing, id.

απαιδευσια.def: ἀπαιδευσία (from ἀπαίδευτος) I. want of education, Thuc., Plat. 2. ignorance, boorishness, coarseness, Plat., etc. II. c. gen., ἀπαιδευσίαι ὀργῆς from want of control over passion, Thuc.

απαιδευτοσ.def: ἀπαίδευτος (παιδεύω) I. uneducated, Eur., Plat.:— c. gen. uninstructed in a thing, Xen. 2. ignorant, boorish, coarse, Eur., Plat. II. adv., ἀπαιδεύτως ἔχειν to be without education, Eur.

απαιθριαζω.def: ἀπαιθριάζω (αἰθρία) to clear away clouds from the sky, Ar.

απαινυμαι.def: ἀπαίνυμαι to take away, withdraw, τί τινος Od.: to pluck off, Mosch.

απαιολαω.def: ἀπαιολάω (from ἀπαιόλη) to perplex, confound, Eur.

απαιολη.def: ἀπαιόλη (αἰόλος) cheating, fraud, personified in Ar.

απαιρω.gloss: to lift off, carry off, take away, to remove from
απαιρω.def: ἀπαίρω I. to lift off, carry off, take away, to remove from, τί τινος Eur.: absol., Hdt. II. to lead away a sea or land force, id.:—intr. (sub. ναῦς, στρατόν, etc.), to sail or march away, depart, id., attic; c. gen., ἀπαίρειν χθονός to depart from the land, Eur.: c. acc. cogn., ἀπ. πρεσβείαν to set out on an embassy, Dem.

απαισ.def: ἄπαις I. childless, Hdt.; τὰς ἄπαιδας οὐσίας her childless estate, Soph.:—c. gen., ἄπ. ἔρσενος γόνου without male heirs, Hdt.; τέκνων ἄπαιδα Eur.; etc. II. Νυκτὸς παῖδες ἄπαιδες children of Night, yet children none, Aesch.

απαισσω.def: ἀπαΐσσω ([ἀπᾱ- Hom.]) I. to spring from aheight, c. gen., Il. II. to dart away, Soph.

απαισχυνομαι.def: ἀπαισχύνομαι to refuse through shame, Plat.

απαιτεω.def: ἀπαιτέω I. to demand back, demand, Hdt.:— ἀπ. τί τινα to demand something of one, id., attic; ἀπ. ὅπλα τοῦ πατρός Soph.; also, χάριν ἀπ. τινα Plat. II. Pass., of things, to be demanded in payment, Hdt. 2. of persons, to have demanded of one, ἀπαιτεῖσθαι εὐεργεσίαν Xen.

απαιτησισ.def: ἀπαίτησις (from ἀπαιτέω) a demanding back, Hdt.; ἀπ. ποιεῖσθαι to make a formal demand, Dem.

απαιτιζω.def: ἀπαιτίζω only in pres. part., = ἀπαιτέω, to demand back, χρήματα Od.

απαιωρεομαι.gloss: to hang down from above, hang suspended, hover about
απαιωρεομαι.def: ἀπαιωρέομαι Pass. to hang down from above, hang suspended, hover about, Hes.

απακριβοομαι.gloss: to be finished off, highly finished
απακριβοομαι.def: ἀπακριβόομαι I. Pass. to be finished off, highly finished, Plat., Isocr. II. as Mid. to finish off, Anth., Luc.

απαλαιστροσ.gloss: not trained in the palaestra, unskilled in wrestling
απαλαιστροσ.def: ἀπάλαιστρος (παλαίστρα) not trained in the palaestra, unskilled in wrestling, Anth.: awkward, Cic.

απαλαλκε.def: ἀπάλαλκε (aor2 with no pres. in use, v. ἄλαλκε) to ward off something from one, τί τινος Hom.; epic inf. ἀπαλαλκέμεν, Theocr.

απαλαμνοσ.gloss: without hands, helpless, good for naught
απαλαμνοσ.def: ἀπάλαμνος I. without hands, helpless, good for naught, Il. II. impracticable, reckless, lawless, ἔρδειν ἔργ’ ἀπάλαμνα Solon.; ἀπάλαμνόν τι πάσχειν Eur.

απαλαμοσ.def: ἀπάλαμος (παλάμη) like ἀπάλαμνος, helpless, Hes., Pind. [ᾱπ - metri grat.]

απαλαομαι.def: ἀπαλάομαι Pass. to go astray, wander, Hes.

απαλγεω.gloss: to feel no more pain at
απαλγεω.def: ἀπαλγέω to feel no more pain at a thing, τι Thuc.; ἀπ. τὸ πένθος to put away sorrow, Plut.

απαλειφω.def: ἀπαλείφω to wipe off, expunge from a register, Dem.; ἀπ. τι to cancel it, Aeschin.

απαλεξω.def: ἀπαλέξω I. to ward something off from a person, τί τινος Il. 2. reversely to keep a person from suffering something, τινά τινος Od. II. Mid. to defend oneself, ἀπαλέξασθαί [τι] Soph.

απαληθευω.def: ἀπαληθεύω to speak the whole truth, Xen., in Mid.

απαλθαινομαι.def: ἀπαλθαίνομαι Dep to heal thoroughly, Il.

απαλλαγη.def: ἀπαλλαγή (ἀπαλλάσσω) I. deliverance, release, relief from a thing, riddance of it, πόνων, ξυμφορᾶς Aesch., Soph., etc. 2. absol. a divorce, Eur. II. (from Pass.) a going away, a means of getting away, an escape, departure, Hdt.; ἡ ἀπ. ἀλλήλων separation from one another, of combatants, Thuc. 2. ἀπ. τοῦ βίου departure from life, Xen.; ψυχῆς ἀπὸ σώματος Plat.

απαλλακτεοσ.def: ἀπαλλακτέος (ἀπαλλάσσω) I. one must release from, τινά τινος Plut. II. (from Pass.) one must withdraw from, get rid of, τινός Plat.

απαλλαξειω.gloss: to wish to be delivered from
απαλλαξειω.def: ἀπαλλαξείω (Desiderat. of ἀπαλλάσσομαι.) to wish to be delivered from or get rid of, τινός Thuc.

απαλλασσω.def: ἀπαλλάσσω (The middle future ἀπαλλάξομαι has a passive sense.) A. Act. I. to set free, release, deliver a person from a thing, τινά τινος Hdt., attic 2. to put away or remove a thing from a person, τί τινος Eur., etc. 3. c. acc. only, to put away, remove, dismiss, τι or τινα id., Thuc., etc.: to destroy, ἑαυτόν Plut. II. intr. to get off, come off, end so and so, οὐκ ὡς ἤθελε Hdt.; κακῶς ἀπ. Plat.; χαίρων Hdt.:—c. gen. to depart from, βίου Eur. B. Pass. and Mid. to be set free or released from a thing, get rid of it, c. gen., Hdt., attic 2. to get off, καλῶς Eur.; ἀζήμιος Ar. 3. absol. to be acquitted, Dem. II. to remove, depart from, ἐκ χώρης Hdt., etc.; γῆς Eur. 2. ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι τοῦ βίου to depart from life, id.; and without τοῦ βίου, to depart, die, id., Thuc., etc. 3. ἀπ. λέχους to be divorced, Eur. 4. ἀπ. τοῦ διδασκάλου to leave school, Plat. 5. ἀπ. ἐκ παίδων to become a man, Aeschin. 6. πολλὸν ἀπηλλαγμένος τινός far inferior to him, Hdt. III. to leave off or cease from τῶν μακρῶν λόγων Soph.; σκωμμάτων Ar.:—absol. to have done, give over, cease, Soph., Plat.:—c. part., εἰπὼν ἀπαλλάγηθι speak and be done with it, Plat.; also in part. with a Verb, οὐκοῦν ἀπαλλαχθεὶς ἄπει; have done and begone, Soph. 2. to depart from enmity, i. e. to be reconciled, Plat.

απαλλοτριοω.def: ἀπαλλοτριόω to estrange, alienate, Aeschin., Arist.

απαλοαω.def: ἀπαλοάω to thresh out, σῖτος ἀπηλοημένος (perf. pass. part.) Dem.:—metaph. to bruise, crush, Il.

απαλοσ.def: ἁπαλός (Deriv. uncertain.) I. soft to the touch, tender, of the body, Hom., Soph.; of fresh fruit, Hdt.; of tender meat, Xen. II. metaph. soft, gentle, ἁπαλὸν γελάσαι to laugh gently, Od.; ἁπ. δίαιτα soft, delicate, Plat.

απαλοτησ.def: ἁπαλότης (from ἁπαλός) softness, tenderness, Xen., etc.

απαλυνω.def: ἁπαλύνω (ἁπαλός) 1. to soften, Xen. 2. to make tender, τοὺς πόδας id.

απαμαλδυνω.def: ἀπαμαλδύνω to bring to naught, Anth.

απαμαω.def: ἀπαμάω (ἀπᾱ- Hom., ἀπᾰ- Soph.) to cut off, Od., Soph.

απαμβλισκω.def: ἀπαμβλίσκω I. to make abortive, Plut. II. intr. to miscarry, id.

απαμβλυνω.def: ἀπαμβλύνω to blunt the edge of a sword: metaph., τεθηγμένον τοί μ’ οὐκ ἀπαμβλύνεις λόγωι Aesch.:—Pass. to be blunted, lose its edge, id., Plat.

απαμειρω.gloss: to deprive one of share in
απαμειρω.def: ἀπαμείρω to deprive one of share in a thing:—Pass. to be bereft, τινός of a thing, Hes.

απαμελεομαι.def: ἀπαμελέομαι (ἀμελέω) Pass. to be neglected utterly, perf. part. ἀπημελημένος Hdt., Soph.

απαμπλακειν.def: ἀπαμπλακεῖν (= ἀφαμαρτεῖν (aor2 of ἁμαρτάνω）) (aor2 with no pres. in use) to fail utterly, Soph.

απαμυνω.def: ἀπαμύνω I. to keep off, ward off, τί τινι something for (i. e. from) another, Il.; τί τινος Luc.: c. acc. to ward off, κακά Hdt.; ἀπ. τὸν βάρβαρον to repulse him, id. II. Mid. to keep off from oneself, to drive back, repel, τινά Od., Hdt. 2. absol. to defend or protect oneself, Hom.

απαναινομαι.def: ἀπαναίνομαι to disown, reject, Hom., Aesch.

απαναισχυντεω.gloss: to have the effrontery to do
απαναισχυντεω.def: ἀπαναισχυντέω (ἀναίσχυντος) I. to have the effrontery to do or say a thing, Plat. II. to deny shamelessly, Dem.

απαναλισκω.gloss: to use quite up, utterly consume
απαναλισκω.def: ἀπαναλίσκω to use quite up, utterly consume, Thuc.

απανδροομαι.gloss: to become manly, come to maturity
απανδροομαι.def: ἀπανδρόομαι Pass. to become manly, come to maturity, Eur., Luc.

απανευθε.def: ἀπάνευθε I. afar off, far away, Il. II. prep. c. gen. far away from, aloof from, τῶν ἄλλων θεῶν id.; ἀπ. θεῶν without their knowledge, id. 2. out from, issuing from, id.

απανθεω.gloss: to leave off blooming, fade, wither
απανθεω.def: ἀπανθέω to leave off blooming, fade, wither, Plat., Luc.

απανθιζω.def: ἀπανθίζω to pluck off flowers, Lat. decerpere: metaph., ματαίαν γλῶσσαν ἀπανθίσαι to cull the flowers of idle talk, i. e. talk at random, Aesch.:—Mid. to gather honey from flowers, to cull the best of, Luc.

απανθρακιζω.def: ἀπανθρακίζω to broil on the coals, Ar.

απανθρακοω.def: ἀπανθρακόω to burn to a cinder, Luc.

απανθρωποσ.def: ἀπάνθρωπος far from man: I. of places, desert, desolate, Aesch. II. of men, inhuman, Plut.

απανιστημι.gloss: to make rise up and depart, send away
απανιστημι.def: ἀπανίστημι I. to make rise up and depart, send away, τὴν στρατιήν Hdt., Thuc. II. Pass., with aor2 and perf. act., and fut. mid., to arise and go away, depart, leave one's country, emigrate, Hdt., Thuc.

απανταω.def: ἀπαντάω I. to move from a place to meet a person; then, generally, to meet, encounter, τινί Hdt., Thuc., etc.:—absol., ὁ ἀεὶ ἀπαντῶν anyone that meets you, any chance person, Plat.:—often with a prep., ἀπ. τινι εἰς τόπον to come or go to a place to meet him, meet him at a place, Hdt.: —without a dat. pers., to present oneself at a place, Xen. 2. often in hostile sense, to meet in battle, Eur.; ἀπ. Ἀθηναίοις ἐς Τάραντα Thuc.: to oppose in any way, Plat.:—absol. to present oneself in arms, Eur. 3. as a law term, to meet in open court, Plat., Dem.:— absol. to appear in court, Dem. 4. ἀπ. εἰς or πρός τι to enter upon a thing, attempt or approach it, Plat., Aeschin.; to have recourse to.., Dem. II. of things, to come upon one, happen to one, Eur., Plat., etc.

απαντικρυ.def: ἀπαντικρύ right opposite, Xen.; c. gen., Dem.

απαντιον.def: ἀπαντίον right opposite, ἐς τὴν ἀπ. ἀκτήν Hdt.

απαντλεω.gloss: to draw off water from a ship's hold
απαντλεω.def: ἀπαντλέω to draw off water from a ship's hold: metaph., ἀπ. ὕβρισμα χθονός Eur.:—c. acc. only, to draw off, Aesch.: to lighten, lessen, πόνους id.; βάρος ψυχῆς Eur.

απανυω.def: ἀπανύω to finish entirely, νῆες ἀπήνυσαν (sc. ὁδόν) the ships performed the voyage, Od.

απαξ.gloss: once, once only, once for all
απαξ.def: ἅπαξ (α copul. and root παγ, πήγνυμι, cf. lat. simplex.) I. once, once only, once for all, like Lat. semel, Od., Hdt., attic 2. c. gen., ἅπ. τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ once in the year, Hdt. II. without any notion of number, after εἴπερ, ἤν, ἐπεί, ὡς, ὅταν, like Lat. ut semel, εἴπερ ἐσπείσω γ’ ἅπαξ if once you have made a treaty, Ar.; ὡς ἅπαξ ἤρξατο once he had begun, Xen.

απαξαπασ.def: ἁπαξάπας all at once, mostly in pl., Ar.

απαξιοω.def: ἀπαξιόω I. to disclaim as unworthy, disown, τι or τινα Thuc. II. ἀπ. τί τινος to deem a thing unworthy of one, Luc.:—Mid. to banish from one's house, Aesch.

απαπποσ.def: ἄπαππος with no grandfather: metaph. unfathered by a thing, Aesch.

απαραβατοσ.def: ἀπαράβατος (παραβαίνω) not passing over to another, not passing away, unchangeable, NTest.

απαραιτητοσ.gloss: not to be moved by prayer, inexorable
απαραιτητοσ.def: ἀπαραίτητος (παραιτέω) I. of persons, not to be moved by prayer, inexorable, Plat., etc.:—adv. -τως, Thuc. II. of punishments, not to be averted by prayers, inevitable, unmerciful, Dinarch.

απαραμυθητοσ.def: ἀπαραμύθητος (παραμυθέομαι) not to be persuaded, inconsolable, ἀθυμία Plut.

απαρασκευοσ.def: ἀπαράσκευος (παρασκευή) without preparation, unprepared, Thuc., Xen.

απαρασσω.def: ἀπαράσσω to strike off, cut off, Il., Hdt.: to sweep off from the deck of a ship, ἀπὸ τῆς νηός Hdt.; ἀπὸ τοῦ καταστρώματος Thuc.

απαργμα.def: ἄπαργμα (= ἀπαρχή, mostly in pl., Ar.)

απαρεσκω.def: ἀπαρέσκω I. to be disagreeable to, τινί Thuc. II. Mid. to shew displeasure, Il.

απαρηγορητοσ.def: ἀπαρηγόρητος (παρηγορέω) I. inconsolable, Plut. II. not to be advised or controlled, id.

απαρθενευτοσ.def: ἀπαρθένευτος (παρθενεύω) unmaidenly, unfitting a maiden, Eur., in neut. pl. as adv.

απαρθενοσ.def: ἀπάρθενος no more a maid, Theocr.; νύμφην ἄνυμφον παρθένον τ’ ἀπάρθενον "virgin wife and widow'd maid, " Eur.

απαριθμεω.def: ἀπαριθμέω I. to count over, reckon up, Xen. II. to reckon or pay back, repay, id.

απαριθμησισ.def: ἀπαρίθμησις (from ἀπαριθμέω) a counting over, recounting, Thuc.

απαρκεω.def: ἀπαρκέω I. to suffice, be sufficient, Trag. II. to be contented, acquiesce, Aesch.

απαρνεομαι.def: ἀπαρνέομαι I. to deny utterly, deny, Hdt.; followed by μή and inf., Eur., etc.: ἀπαρνηθῆναί τι to refuse, reject, Thuc. II. fut. ἀπαρνηθήσεται in pass. sense, shall be denied or refused, Soph., NTest.

απαρνοσ.def: ἄπαρνος (ἀρνέομαι) denying utterly, ἄπαρνός ἐστι μὴ νοσέειν he denies that he is ill, Hdt.: c. gen., ἄπαρνος οὐδενός denying nothing, Soph.

απαρταω.def: ἀπαρτάω I. to hang up from, ἀπ. δέρην to strangle, Eur.:—Pass. to hang loose, Xen. 2. metaph. to make dependent upon, ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ Luc. II. to detach, separate, τί τινος Dem.:—Pass., ἀπηρτημένοι detached, disunited, id. III. intr. in Act. to remove oneself, go away, Thuc.

απαρτι.def: ἀπαρτί I. completely, of numbers, exactly, just, Hdt. II. of Time, from now, from this time, henceforth, Ar., NTest. 2. just now, even now, NTest.

απαρτιζω.def: ἀπαρτίζω I. to make even, move regularly, Aesch. II. to get ready, complete, Arist. 2. intr. to be even or exact, id.

απαρτιλογια.def: ἀπαρτιλογία (λόγος) an even number or sum, Hdt.

απαρτιον.gloss: a sale of goods by auction
απαρτιον.def: ἀπάρτιον a sale of goods by auction, Plut.

απαρυω.def: ἀπαρύω to draw off, skim off cream, Hdt.: metaph. to draw off the force of a thing, in verb. adj. ἀπαρυστέον, Ar.

απαρχη.gloss: the beginning of a sacrifice, the primal offering
απαρχη.def: ἀπαρχή (from ἀπάρχομαι) 1. mostly in pl. ἀπαρχαί, the beginning of a sacrifice, the primal offering (of hairs cut from the forehead), Eur. 2. the firstlings for sacrifice, first-fruits, Hdt., attic:—metaph., ἀπαρχὴ τῆς σοφίας Plat.

απαρχομαι.def: ἀπάρχομαι Dep. I. to make a beginning, esp. in sacrifice, τρίχας ἀπάρχεσθαι to begin the sacrifice with the hair, i. e. by cutting off the hair from the forehead and throwing it into the fire, Il.: to begin the sacrificial rites, Od. II. c. gen. to cut off part of a thing, to offer it, to offer part of a thing, Hdt., Eur. III. to offer the firstlings or first-fruits, Hdt., Ar. 2. metaph. to take as the first-fruits, as the choice or best, Theocr. IV. ἀπάρχω Act., to be the first, be leader, dance, Anth.

απασ.def: ἅπας (α copul., πᾶς) 1. quite all, the whole, and in pl. all together, Hom., etc. 2. with an Adj., ἀργύρεος ἅπας all silver, i.e. of massive silver, Od.; ἅπαν κακόν altogether evil, Ar. 3. in sing., like πᾶς, everyone, Lat. unusquisque, πᾶν everything, unumquodque, Hdt., Attic

απασπαιρω.def: ἀπασπαίρω to gasp away life, Eur.

απαστια.gloss: an abstaining from food, a fast
απαστια.def: ἀπαστία (from ἄπαστος) an abstaining from food, a fast, Ar.

απαστοσ.def: ἄπαστος (πατέομαι) not having eaten, fasting, Il.: c. gen., ἄπαστος ἐδητύος ἠδὲ ποτῆτος without having tasted meat or drink, Od.

απασχολεω.def: ἀπασχολέω (ἄσχολος) to leave one no leisure, Luc.:—Pass. to be wholly occupied, id.

απασχολια.def: ἀπασχολία (from ἀπασχολέω) detention by business, Strab.

απαταω.def: ἀπατάω (ἀπάτη) to cheat, trick, outwit, beguile, Hom., etc.: Pass. to be deceived, Soph.; ἀπατᾶσθαι, ὡς.., to be deceived into thinking that.., Plat.

απατερθε.def: ἀπάτερθε I. apart, aloof, Il. II. prep. c. gen. far away from, ὁμίλου id.

απατεων.def: ἀπατεών (ἀπάτη) a cheat, rogue, quack, Plat., Xen.

απατη.def: ἀπάτη (prob. from ἅπτομαι, cf. ἀπαφίσκω) 1. a trick, fraud, deceit, Il.: a stratagem, Thuc.: in pl. wiles, Hom. 2. guile, fraud, deceit, treachery, Hdt., attic

απατηλιοσ.def: ἀπατήλιος (from ἀπάτη) guileful, wily, ἀπατήλια εἰδώς skilled in wiles, Od.; ἀπ. βάζειν id.

απατουρια.def: Ἀπατούρια the Apatouria, a festival at Athens in the month Pyanepsion, at which the grown-up youths (κοῦροι) were enrolled in the φρατρίαι, Oratt. (Prob. from πατρία, φρατρία, with α euphon.)

απατωρ.def: ἀπάτωρ (πατήρ) without father, fatherless, Soph., Eur.: c. gen., ἀπ. ἐμοῦ not having me for a father, Soph.

απαυγαζω.def: ἀπαυγάζω to beam forth, Call. (in Mid.)

απαυγασμα.def: ἀπαύγασμα (from ἀπαυγάζω) efflux of light, effulgence, NTest.

απαυδαω.def: ἀπαυδάω I. to forbid, Soph.; ἀπ. μή c. inf. to prohibit from doing a thing, id., Eur. II. to decline, shun, πόνους Eur.: to deny, renounce, νεῖκος Theocr. III. to be wanting towards, fail, φίλοισι Eur.; ἀπ. ὑπὸ λιμοῦ Luc.

απαυθαδιζομαι.def: ἀπαυθαδίζομαι Mid. to speak or act boldly, speak out, Plat.

απαυθημεριζω.def: ἀπαυθημερίζω (αὐθήμερος) to return the same day, Xen.

απαυραω.def: ἀπαυράω (ἀπούρας as if from ἀπούρημι) I. to take away or wrest from, rob of, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ἄμφω θυμὸν ἀπηύρα Il.; τοὺς μὲν τεύχε’ ἀπηύρα id. 2. c. gen. pers., κούρην Ἀχιλῆος ἀπούρας id. 3. c. dat. pers., πολέσσιν θυμὸν ἀπηύρα id. 4. Mid., ἀπουράμενοι ψυχάς having lost their lives, Hes. II. to receive good or ill, to enjoy or suffer, id., Eur. Cf. ἐπαυρίσκομαι.

απαυστοσ.def: ἄπαυστος (παύομαι) I. unceasing, never-ending, Aesch., Soph. 2. not to be stopped or assuaged, insatiable, δίψα Thuc. II. c. gen. never ceasing from, γόων Eur.

απαυτομολεω.gloss: to go of one's own accord, desert
απαυτομολεω.def: ἀπαυτομολέω to go of one's own accord, desert, Thuc.

απαφισκω.def: ἀπαφίσκω (ἅπτομαι palpare, ἁφή) like ἀπατάω, to cheat, beguile, Od.

απαχθομαι.def: ἀπάχθομαι Mid. to be grievous, τινι Sapph.

απεδοσ.def: ἄπεδος (α copul., πέδον) even, level, flat, Hdt., Thuc., etc.: —ἄπεδον, ου, τό, a plain, flat surface, Hdt.

απεθιζω.def: ἀπεθίζω to disaccustom, ἀπ. τινὰ μὴ ποιεῖν Aeschin.; part. perf. ἀπειθικώς, Plut.

απειδον.gloss: to look away from other things at
απειδον.def: ἀπεῖδον to look away from other things at a thing, and so simply to look at, ἔς or πρός τι Thuc.

απειθεω.def: ἀπειθέω to be disobedient, refuse compliance, Aesch.; c. dat. to disobey, Eur., Plat.

απειθησ.def: ἀπειθής (πείθομαι) I. disobedient, τοῖς νόμοις Plat.; of ships, τοῖς κυβερνήταις ἀπειθεστέραι less obedient to them, Thuc. II. act. not persuasive, incredible, Theogn.

απεικαζω.gloss: to form from a model, to express, copy
απεικαζω.def: ἀπεικάζω I. to form from a model, to express, copy, of painters, Xen., etc.:—Pass. to become like, resemble, ἀπεικασθεὶς θεῶι in a god's likeness, Eur. 2. to express by a comparison, Plat.:— Pass. to be copied or expressed by likeness, id. 3. to liken, compare with, τί τινι Eur., Plat. II. ὡς ἀπεικάσαι as one may guess, to conjecture, Soph.

απεικαστεοσ.def: ἀπεικαστέος (verb. adj. of ἀπεικάζω) one must represent, Xen.

απεικονιζω.def: ἀπεικονίζω (εἰκών) to represent in a statue, Anth.

απειλεω.def: ἀπειλέω to force back; mostly in Pass., ἐς ἀπορίην ἀπειλημένος forced into great difficulties, Hdt.

ἀπειλέω (ἀπειλή) to hold out either in the way of promise or threat: I. in good sense, to promise, ἠπείλησεν ἄνακτι ῥέξειν ἑκατόμβην Il.; ἠπείλησας εἶναι ἀρίστους didst profess that they were best, Od. II. commonly in bad sense, to threaten, Lat. minari, absol. or c. dat. pers., Hom., etc.; c. acc. cogn., ἠπείλησεν μῦθον spake a threatening speech, Il.:—also in Mid., NTest. 2. c. acc. of the thing threatened, θάνατον ἀπ. τινι Hdt. 3. dependent clauses added in inf. fut., γέρας ἀφαιρήσεσθαι ἀπειλεῖς Il., etc.; attic also in inf. aor.:—also ἀπ. ὅτι.., ὡς.., attic III. Pass. ἀπειλοῦμαι, of persons, to be terrified by threats, Xen.

απειλη.def: ἀπειλή (Deriv. uncertain) I. mostly in pl., boastful promises, boasts, Il. II. in bad sense, threats, Hom., etc.:—in sg. a threat of punishment, Soph., Thuc.

απειλητηριοσ.def: ἀπειλητήριος (ἀπειλέω) of or for threatening, λόγοι Hdt.

απειμι.def: ἄπειμι (εἰμί sum) 1. to be away or far from, τινος Od., etc.; ἀπό τινος Thuc.: c. dat. to be wanting, φίλοισιν Eur., etc. 2. absol. to be away or absent, and of things, to be wanting, Soph., etc.; of the dead, Eur.
