αρπαζω.def: ἁρπάζω I. to snatch away, carry off, Hom., Hdt., etc.:—absol. to steal, be a thief, Ar. 2. to seize hastily, snatch up, λᾶαν Il.; δόρυ Aesch.; ἁρπ. τινὰ μέσον to seize him by the waist, Hdt.; c. gen. part., ἁρπ. τινὰ ποδός by the foot, Eur. 3. to seize, overpower, Aesch.: also to seize a post, Xen. II. to plunder, πόλεις Thuc., etc. (From Root ΑΡΠ, come also ἅρπη, Ἅρπυιαι, cf. Lat. rapio.)

αρπακτοσ.def: ἁρπακτός (ἁρπάζω) 1. gotten by rapine, stolen, Hes. 2. to be caught, i. e. to be got by chance, hazardous, id.

αρπαλεοσ.def: ἁρπαλέος (ἁρπάζω) I. greedy: adv. ἁρπαλέως, greedily, eagerly, Od., Theogn. II. attractive, alluring, Od., Pind.

αρπαλιζω.gloss: to catch up, be eager to receive
αρπαλιζω.def: ἁρπαλίζω (ἁρπάζω) 1. to catch up, be eager to receive, τινὰ κωκυτοῖς Aesch. 2. to exact greedily, id.

αρπαξ.def: ἅρπαξ (ἁρπάζω) I. rapacious, Lat. rapax, Ar., Xen. II. as Subst., 1. ἅρπαξ, rapine, Hes. 2. ἅρπαξ, a robber, plunderer, Ar.

αρπεδονη.def: ἁρπεδόνη a cord, for binding or for snaring game, Xen.: a bowstring, Anth. (Deriv. unknown.)

αρπη.def: ἅρπη (v. ἁρπάζω) I. a bird of prey, a kite, Il. II. a sickle, = δρέπανον, Hes.

αρπυιαι.def: Ἅρπυιαι (ἁρπάζω) the snatchers, a personification of whirlwinds or hurricanes, Od. The Harpies, as described by Virgil, belong to later mythology.

αρραβων.def: ἀρραβών earnest-money, caution-money, deposited by the purchaser and forfeited if the purchase is not completed, Lat. arrhabo, arrha, Isae., NTest. (A Hebr. word.)

αρρενωπια.def: ἀρρενωπία (From ἀρρενωπός) a manly look manliness, Plat.

αρρενωποσ.def: ἀρρενωπός (ὤψ) masculine-looking, masculine, manly, Plat., Luc.

αρρηκτοσ.def: ἄρρηκτος (ῥήγνυμι) unbroken, not to be broken, Hom., Hdt., Aesch., etc.: unwearied, Il.

αρρητοσ.def: ἄρρητος I. unspoken, unsaid, Lat. indictus, Od., etc.; οὐκ ἐπ’ ἀρρήτοις λόγοις not without warning spoken, Soph. II. not to be spoken, not to be divulged, of sacred mysteries, Hdt., Eur., etc.; διδακτά τε ἄρρητά τ’, i. e. things profane and sacred, Soph. 2. unutterable, inexpressible, horrible, Lat. nefandus, id., Eur.; ἄρρητ’ ἀρρήτων "deeds without a name, " Soph. 3. shameful to be spoken, id. ῥητὰ καὶ ἄρρητα, "dicenda tacenda, " Dem. III. in Mathem., ἄρρητα, irrational quantities, surds, Plat.

αρρηφορεω.def: ἀρρηφορέω (from Ἀρρηφόροι) (The meaning of Ἀρρη - is uncertain.) to serve as Ἀρρηφόρος, Ar.

αρρηφορια.def: ἀρρηφορία the procession of ἀρρηφόροι Lys.
ἀρρηφόρια the festival arrephoria. Ἀρρηφόρια, τά.

αρρηφοροι.def: Ἀρρηφόροι (φέρω) at Athens two maidens of noble birth, chosen in their seventh year, who carried the peplos and other holy things of Athena Polias.

αρρισ.def: ἄρρις without power of scenting, Xen.

αρριχοσ.def: ἄρριχος a wicker basket, Ar., Anth.

αρρυθμεω.gloss: not to be in rhythm with
αρρυθμεω.def: ἀρρυθμέω (from ἄρρυθμος) not to be in rhythm with, Plat.

αρρυθμια.def: ἀρρυθμία (from ἄρρυθμος) want of rhythm or proportion, Plat.

αρρυθμοσ.def: ἄρρυθμος of sounds, not in rhythm or time, unrhythmical, opp. to εὔρυθμος, Plat.:—metaph. in undue measure, Eur.: ill-proportioned, Xen.

αρρωξ.def: ἀρρώξ (ῥήγνυμι, ἔρρωγα) without cleft or breach, unbroken, γῆ Soph.

αρρωστεω.def: ἀρρωστέω (ἄρρωστος) to be weak and sickly, Xen., Dem.

αρρωστημα.def: ἀρρώστημα (from ἀρρωστέω) 1. an illness, a sickness, Dem. 2. a moral infirmity, Plut.

αρρωστια.def: ἀρρωστία (from ἄρρωστος) weakness, sickness, Thuc., etc.; ἀρρ.τοῦ στρατεύειν inability to serve, id.

αρρωστοσ.def: ἄρρωστος (ῥώννυμι) weak, sickly:— adv., ἀρρώστως ἔχειν to be ill, Aeschin. 2. in moral sense, weak, feeble, τὴν ψυχήν Xen.:— remiss, εἴς τι in a thing, Thuc. II. also, v. ἄρδω.

αρσην.def: ἄρσην 1. male, Lat. mas, Il., etc.; ἄρρην, ὁ, or ἄρρεν, the male, Aesch.; οἱ ἄρσενες the male sex, Thuc. 2. masculine, strong, Eur.: metaph. mighty, κτύπος ἄρσην πόντου Soph. 3. of the gender of nouns, masculine, ὀνόματα Ar.

αρσιπουσ.def: ἀρσίπους (ἀερσίπους) contr. for ἀερσίπους, raising the foot, active, Hhymn., Anth.

αρσισ.def: ἄρσις (αἴρω) I. a raising of the foot in walking, Arist. II. in Prosody, arsis, opp. to thesis.

αρταβη.def: ἀρτάβη a Persian measure, artaba, = 1 medimnus + 3 choenices, Hdt.

αρταμεω.gloss: to cut in pieces, rend asunder
αρταμεω.def: ἀρταμέω (from ἄρταμος) to cut in pieces, rend asunder, Eur.

αρταμοσ.def: ἄρταμος (Deriv. uncertain.) a butcher, cook, Xen.

αρτανη.gloss: that by which something is hung up, a rope, noose, halter
αρτανη.def: ἀρτάνη (ἀρτάω) that by which something is hung up, a rope, noose, halter, Aesch., Soph.

αρταω.def: ἀρτάω (⁎ἄρω) I. to fasten to or hang one thing upon another, τι ἀπό τινος Thuc.: to fasten in a noose, τὴν δέρην Eur.:—Mid., βρόχους ἀρτωμένη fastening halters to one's neck, id. II. Pass. to be hung upon, hang upon, ἠρτῆσθαι ἔκ τινος id.: hence to depend upon, Lat. pendere ab aliquo, Hdt. Cf. ἀρτέομαι.

αρτεμισ.def: Ἄρτεμις (Deriv. uncertain.) Artemis, the Roman Diana, goddess of the chase, daughter of Zeus and Latona, sister of Apollo: in Hom., women who die suddenly are said to be slain by her ἀγανὰ βέλεα: cf. Ἀπόλλων.

αρτεμισιον.def: Ἀρτεμίσιον (from Ἄρτεμις) a temple of Artemis, Hdt.

αρτεομαι.gloss: to be prepared, get ready, make ready
αρτεομαι.def: ἀρτέομαι I. as Pass. to be prepared, get ready, make ready, c. inf., πολεμεῖν ἀρτέοντο, ἀρτέετο ἐς πόλεμον Hdt.; also, II. as Mid., c. acc., ναυμαχίην ἀρτέεσθαι to prepare a sea-fight, id. (Akin to ἀρτύω, not to ἀρτάω.)

αρτημα.def: ἄρτημα (ἀρτάω) I. a hanging ornament, earring, Hdt.; cf. λίθινος. II. any hanging weight, Plut.

αρτηρια.def: ἀρτηρία (Deriv. uncertain.) I. the wind-pipe or trachea, Plat., etc.; πνεύμονος ἀρτηρίαι the vessels of the lungs, Soph. II. an artery, only in late writers.

αρτι.def: ἄρτι (⁎ἄρω) adv. just, exactly, 1. of the present, just now, even now, with pres. and perf., Theogn., Aesch., etc. 2. of the past, just now, just, with imperf. and aor., Eur., etc. 3. in late writers of the future, just now, presently, Luc., etc.

αρτιαζω.gloss: to play at odd and even
αρτιαζω.def: ἀρτιάζω (ἄρτιος) I. to play at odd and even, Lat. par impar ludere, Ar. II. to count, Anth.

αρτιασμοσ.gloss: the game of odd and even
αρτιασμοσ.def: ἀρτιασμός (from ἀρτιάζω) the game of odd and even, Arist.

αρτιγενειοσ.def: ἀρτιγένειος (γένειον) with beard just sprouting, Anth.

αρτιδακρυσ.def: ἀρτίδακρυς (δάκρυ) just weeping, ready to weep, Eur.

αρτιδοροσ.def: ἀρτίδορος (δείρω) just stript off or peeled, Anth.

αρτιδροποσ.gloss: ready for plucking, of tender age
αρτιδροποσ.def: ἀρτίδροπος (ἄρτιος, δρέπω) ready for plucking, of tender age, Aesch.

αρτιεπησ.def: ἀρτιεπής (ἄρτιος, ἔπος) ready of speech, glib or ready of tongue, Il., Pind.

αρτιζυγια.def: ἀρτιζυγία (ζυγός) a recent union, ἀνδρῶν ἀρτ., i. e. newly-married husbands, Aesch.

αρτιζω.def: ἀρτίζω (⁎ἄρω) to get ready, prepare, Anth.: so in Mid., Theocr.

αρτιθαλησ.def: ἀρτιθαλής (θάλλω) just budding or blooming, Anth.

αρτικολλοσ.def: ἀρτίκολλος (κόλλα) I. close-glued, clinging close to, ἀρτίκολλος ὥστε τέκτονος χιτών ἀρτίως κολληθεὶς ὡς ὑπὸ τέκτονος, Soph. II. metaph. fitting well together, ἀρτ. συμβαίνει turns out exactly right, Aesch.; ἀρτίκολλόν τι μαθεῖν to hear it in the nick of time, opportunely, id.

αρτιμαθησ.def: ἀρτιμαθής (μαθεῖν) having just learnt a thing, c. gen., Eur.

αρτιοσ.gloss: complete, perfect of its kind, suitable, exactly fitted
αρτιοσ.def: ἄρτιος (ἄρτι) I. complete, perfect of its kind, suitable, exactly fitted; ἄρτια βάζειν to speak to the purpose (cf. ἀρτιεπής), Hom.; ἄρτια ᾔδη thought things agreeable, was of the same mind, id.:— meet, right, proper, Solon, Theogn. 2. c. inf. prepared, ready, to do a thing, Hdt. II. of numbers, perfect, i. e. even, opp. to περισσός (odd), Plat., etc. III. adv. ἀρτίως, just, now first, like ἄρτι, used by Soph. both of present time with pres. and perf.; and of past with imperf. and aor.

αρτιπαγησ.def: ἀρτιπαγής (πήγνυμι) I. just put together or made, Theocr., Anth. II. freshly coagulated, id.

αρτιπουσ.def: ἀρτίπους (ἄρτιος, πούς) I. sound of foot, Od., Hdt.:—generally, strong or swift of foot, Il. II. （ἄρτι, πούς) coming just in time, Soph.

αρτιστομοσ.def: ἀρτίστομος (στόμα) speaking in good idiom, or with precision, Plut.

αρτιτοκοσ.def: ἀρτίτοκος (τίκτω) I. new-born, Anth., Luc. II. paroxyt. ἀρτιτόκος, ον, having just given birth, Anth.

αρτιτρεφησ.def: ἀρτιτρεφής (τρέφω) just nursed, ἀρτιτρεφεῖς βλαχαί the wailings of young children, Aesch.

αρτιτροποσ.def: ἀρτίτροπος (ἄρτι, τρόπος) just of age, marriageable.

αρτιφρων.def: ἀρτίφρων (ἄρτιος, φρήν) sound of mind, sensible, Od., Eur.: c. gen., γάμων fully conscious of a thing, Aesch.

αρτιχνουσ.def: ἀρτίχνους with the first bloom on, Anth.

αρτοκοποσ.def: ἀρτοκόπος a baker, Hdt., Xen. (Prob. for ἀρτοπόπος, from πέπτω, cf. Lat. coquus.)

αρτολαγυνοσ.gloss: with bread and bottle in it
αρτολαγυνοσ.def: ἀρτολάγυνος with bread and bottle in it, πήρα Anth.

αρτοπωλιον.def: ἀρτοπώλιον (from ἀρτόπωλις) a baker's shop, bakery, Ar.

αρτοσ.def: ἄρτος (Deriv. uncertain.) a cake or loaf of wheat-bread (barley-bread is μᾶζα), mostly in pl., Od.; ἄρτος οὖλος soft bread, id.

αρτοσιτεω.def: ἀρτοσιτέω (σιτέομαι) to eat wheaten bread, Xen.

αρτοφαγεω.def: ἀρτοφαγέω (from ἀρτοφάγος) to eat bread, Hdt.

αρτυνασ.def: ἀρτύνας (cf. ἁρμοστής.) (from ἀρτῡ́νω) a magistrate at Argos and Epidaurus, Thuc.

αρτυνω.def: ἀρτύνω (⁎ἄρω) Ep. form of ἀρτύω to arrange, prepare, devise, λόχον ἀρτύνειν, Lat. insidias struere, Od.; μνηστῆρσιν θάνατον ἀρτ. id.:—Mid. to prepare for oneself, id.

αρτυω.def: ἀρτύω (⁎ἄρω) like ἀρτύνω to arrange, devise, prepare, δόλον, ὄλεθρον, γάμον Hom.; so Hdt., attic

αρυβαλλοσ.def: ἀρύβαλλος I. a bag or purse, Stesich. II. a bucket shaped like a purse, i. e. narrow at top, Ar. (Deriv. unknown.)

αρυσσομαι.def: ἀρύσσομαι (ἀρύω) Mid. to draw for oneself, Hdt

αρυστηρ.def: ἀρυστήρ (ἀρύω) a cup or ladle, Hdt.

αρυω.def: ἀρύω to draw water or any liquor for others, Hes., Xen.:—Mid. to draw water for oneself, ἀρυσσάμενος ποταμῶν ἄπο having drawn water from the rivers, Hes.; ἀρύσασθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ ποταμοῦ Xen.; c. acc., ἀρύσασθαι πῶμα Eur.; c. gen. partit., ἀρύτεσθαι Νείλου ὑδάτων to draw of the waters of the Nile, Ar.; ἐς τὸν κόλπον τρὶς ἀρυσάμενος τοῦ ἡλίου having (as it were) drawn the rays of the sun into his bosom, Hdt.

αρχαικοσ.def: ἀρχαϊκός (ἀρχαῖος) old-fashioned, antiquated, primitive, ἀρχαϊκὰ φρονεῖν Ar.

αρχαιογονοσ.gloss: of ancient race, of old descent
αρχαιογονοσ.def: ἀρχαιόγονος of ancient race, of old descent, Soph.

αρχαιολογεω.def: ἀρχαιολογέω (from ἀρχαιολόγος) to discuss antiquities or things out of date, Thuc.

αρχαιομελισιδωνοφρυνιχηρατοσ.def: ἀρχαιομελισιδωνοφρυνιχήρατος (μέλι, Σιδών, Φρύνιχος, ἐρατός) dear honey-sweet old songs from Phrynichus' Phoenissae, Ar.

αρχαιοπλουτοσ.gloss: rich from olden time, of old hereditary wealth
αρχαιοπλουτοσ.def: ἀρχαιόπλουτος rich from olden time, of old hereditary wealth, Aesch., Soph.

αρχαιοπρεπησ.def: ἀρχαιοπρεπής (πρέπω) distinguished from olden time, time-honoured, Aesch.

αρχαιοσ.def: ἀρχαῖος (ἀρχή 1) from the beginning: I. of things, ancient, primeval, olden, Hdt., attic 2. like ἀρχαϊκός, old-fashioned, antiquated, primitive, Aesch., Ar. 3. ancient, former, τὸ ἀρχ. ῥέεθρον Hdt., etc. II. of persons, ancient, old, Aesch., Thuc., etc.: οἱ ἀρχαῖοι the Ancients, the old Fathers, Prophets, NTest. III. adv. ἀρχαίως, anciently, Dem.; so, τὸ ἀρχαῖον, ionic contr. τὠρχαῖον Hdt., attic τἀρχαῖον Aesch. 2. in olden style, Plat., Aeschin. IV. as Subst., τὸ ἀρχαῖον, the original sum, the principal, Lat. sors, Ar., Oratt.

αρχαιοτροπια.def: ἀρχαιοτροπία (from ἀρχαιότροπος) old fashions or customs, Plut.

αρχαιρεσια.def: ἀρχαιρεσία (αἵρεσις) an election of magistrates, Hdt.; mostly in pl., Xen., etc.

αρχαιρεσιαζω.gloss: to hold the assembly for the election of magistrates
αρχαιρεσιαζω.def: ἀρχαιρεσιάζω (from ἀρχαιρεσία) 1. to hold the assembly for the election of magistrates, Plut.: to elect, id. 2. to canvass for election, id.

αρχειον.gloss: the senate-house, town-hall, residence of the chief magistrates
αρχειον.def: ἀρχεῖον (ἀρχή 11) I. the senate-house, town-hall, residence of the chief magistrates, Lat. curia, Hdt., Xen. II. the magistracy, Arist.

αρχελαοσ.def: ἀρχέλαος leading the people, a chief, Aesch.

αρχετησ.def: ἀρχέτης a leader, prince, Eur.: as adj., ἀρχ. θρόνος a princely throne, id.

αρχετυπον.def: ἀρχέτυπον an archetype, pattern, model, Anth.: the figure on a seal, Luc.

αρχευω.def: ἀρχεύω (ἄρχω) to command, c. dat., Il.

αρχεχοροσ.def: ἀρχέχορος leading the chorus or dance, Eur.

αρχη.def: ἀρχή (ἄρχω) I. a beginning, origin, first cause, Hom., etc.:—with Preps. ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀρχῆθεν, from the beginning, from of old, Od., attic; ἐξ ἀρχῆς πάλιν anew, afresh, Ar.:—so, ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς Hdt., Trag.:— κατ’ ἀρχάς in the beginning, at first, Hdt.:—absol. in acc. ἀρχήν, to begin with, first, id.; ἀρχὴν οὐ absolutely not, not at all, Lat. omnino non, id., attic; with numerals, ἀρχὴν ἑπτά in all, Hdt. 2. the end, corner, of a bandage, rope, sheet, id., Eur., NTest. II. the first place or power, sovereignty, dominion, command, Hdt., attic; c. gen. rei, ἀρχὴ τῶν νεῶν, τῆς θαλάσσης Thuc., etc. 2. a sovereignty, empire, realm, Hdt., Thuc. 3. in Prose, a magistracy, office, Hdt., attic:—also a term of office, τὴν ἐνιαυσίαν ἀρχήν Thuc.:—these offices were commonly obtained in two ways, χειροτονητή by election, κληρωτή by lot, Aeschin. 4. in pl., αἱ ἀρχαί (as we say) "the authorities, " i. e. the magistrates, Thuc., etc.

αρχηγενησ.def: ἀρχηγενής (γίγνομαι) causing the first beginning of a thing, c. gen., Aesch.

αρχηγετευω.def: ἀρχηγετεύω to be chief leader, τῶν κάτω Hdt.

αρχηγετεω.def: ἀρχηγετέω to make a beginning, Soph.

αρχηγετησ.def: ἀρχηγέτης (ἡγέομαι) 1. a first leader, the founder of a city or family, Hdt., etc. 2. generally, a leader, prince, chief, Aesch., Soph. 3. a first cause, author, τύχης, γένους Eur.

αρχηγοσ.def: ἀρχηγός (ἡγέομαι) I. beginning, originating a thing, c. gen., Eur. II. as Subst., like ἀρχηγέτης, founder, of a tutelary hero, Soph. 2. a prince, chief, Aesch., Simon., Thuc. 3. a first cause, originator, τοῦ πράγματος Xen.

αρχηθεν.gloss: from the beginning, from of old, from olden time
αρχηθεν.def: ἀρχῆθεν (ἀρχή) from the beginning, from of old, from olden time, Hdt.:—with a neg., ἀρχῆθεν μή not at all, id.

αρχιδιον.def: ἀρχίδιον (Dim. of ἀρχή II.3) a petty office, petty officer, Ar., Dem.

αρχιερατικοσ.def: ἀρχιερατικός (from ἀρχιερεύσις) of the high-priest, NTest.

αρχιερευσ.def: ἀρχιερεύς an arch-priest, chief-priest, Hdt.:— at Rome, the Pontifex Maximus, Plut.:—at Jerusalem, the high-priest, NTest.

αρχιθεωρεω.def: ἀρχιθεωρέω (from ἀρχιθέωρος) to be ἀρχιθέωρος, Dem.

αρχιθεωροσ.def: ἀρχιθέωρος (θεωρός) the chief of a θεωρία or sacred embassy, Andoc., Arist.

αρχικοσ.def: ἀρχικός (ἀρχή) 1. of or for rule, royal, Aesch., Thuc. 2. of persons, fit for rule, skilled in government or command, Xen., Plat.: c. gen. having command of, Arist.

αρχισυναγωγοσ.def: ἀρχισυνάγωγος (συναγωγή) the ruler of a synagogue, NTest.

αρχιτεκτονεω.def: ἀρχιτεκτονέω (ἀρχιτέκτων) 1. to be the architect, Plut. 2. generally, to construct, contrive, Ar.

αρχιτεκτων.gloss: a chief-artificer, master-builder, director of works, architect, engineer
αρχιτεκτων.def: ἀρχιτέκτων I. a chief-artificer, master-builder, director of works, architect, engineer, Hdt. 2. generally, a constructor, author, Eur., Dem. II. at Athens, the manager of the state theatre and of the Dionysia, id.

αρχιτελωνησ.def: ἀρχιτελώνης a chief toll-collector, chief-publican, NTest.

αρχιτρικλινοσ.def: ἀρχιτρίκλινος the president of a banquet (triclinium), NTest.

αρχιυπασπιστησ.gloss: chief of the men at arms
αρχιυπασπιστησ.def: ἀρχιυπασπιστής chief of the men at arms, Plut.

αρχοσ.def: ἀρχός a leader, chief, commander, Il.

αρχω.def: ἄρχω (pf. pass. ἦργμαι only in mid. sense) in pass. sense:— to be first, I. of Time, to begin, make a beginning, both in Act. and Mid.: 1. c. gen. to make a beginning of, πολέμοιο, μάχης, etc., Hom.; so Hdt. and attic:—Mid. also in a religious sense, like ἀπάρχεσθαι, ἀρχόμενος μελέων beginning the sacrifice with the limbs, Od.; ἄρχειν σπονδῶν Thuc. 2. c. gen. also to begin from or with, ἐν σοὶ μὲν λήξω σέο δ’ ἄρξομαι Il.; so, ἄρχεσθαι ἔκ τινος Od.; ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ παιδίων even from boyhood, Hdt. 3. c. gen. rei et dat. pers., ἄρχ. θεοῖς δαιτός to make preparations for a banquet to the gods, Il.; τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε id., etc. 4. c. acc., ἄρχειν ὁδόν τινι, like Lat. praeire viam alicui, to shew him the way, Od.; absol. (sub. ὁδόν), to lead the way, Hom.; then generally ἄρχειν τι Aesch., Soph. 5. c. inf. to begin to do a thing, Hom., etc.; c. part. of continued action or condition, ἦρχον χαλεπαίνων Il.; ἄρχ. διδάσκων Xen. 6. absol., ἄρχε begin! Hom.; ἄρχει ἡ ἐκεχειρία Thuc.; ἅμα ἦρι ἀρχομένωι, θέρους ἀρχομένου id. II. of Authority, to lead, rule, govern, only in Act.: 1. c. gen. to rule, be leader of.., τινός Hom., attic 2. c. dat. to rule over, Hom., Aesch. 3. absol. to rule, govern, id.: esp. to hold a subordinate office, ὁκοῖον εἴη ἄρχειν μετὰ τὸ βασιλεύειν Hdt.:—at Athens, to be archon, Dem.; cf. ἄρχων. 4. Pass. to be ruled, governed, Hdt., attic; οἱ ἀρχόμενοι subjects, Xen.

αρχων.def: ἄρχων (part. of ἄρχω) 1. a ruler, commander, chief, captain, Hdt., Aesch., etc. 2. Ἄρχοντες, οἱ, the chief magistrates at Athens, nine in number, the first being ὁ Ἄρχων or Ἄρχων ἐπώνυμος, the second ὁ Βασιλεύς, the third ὁ Πολέμαρχος, the remaining six οἱ Θεσμοθέται. 3. title of the chief magistrates in other places, as the Ephors at Sparta, Hdt.

αρω.def: ἄρω radical form of ἀραρίσκω, whence come ἄρθρον, ἁρμόζω, ἄρτι, ἄρτιος, ἀρτύω, etc.

αρωγη.def: ἀρωγή (ἀρήγω) I. help, aid, succour, protection, Ζηνὸς ἀρωγή aid given by Zeus, Il.; ἐπ’ ἀρωγῆι in anyone's favour, id.; ἀρ. νόσου, help against.., Plat. II. of persons, an aid, succour, Aesch., Soph.

αρωγοσ.def: ἀρωγός (ἀρήγω) I. aiding, succouring, propitious, serviceable, τινι Aesch.; absol., id., Soph. 2. c. gen. serviceable towards a thing, Aesch., Soph.; πρός τι Thuc. II. as Subst. a helper, aid, esp. in battle, Il.: a defender before a tribunal, advocate, id.

αρωμα.def: ἄρωμα any spice or sweet herb, Xen.
ἄρωμα (ἀρόω) arable land, corn-land, Lat. arvum, Ar.

ασ.def: ἇς Aeol. and Dor for ἕως.

ασαλαμινιοσ.def: ἀσαλαμίνιος not having been at Salamis, Ar.

ασαλευτοσ.def: ἀσάλευτος (σαλεύω) not agitated, tranquil, of the sea:—metaph. of the mind, Eur.

ασαντοσ.def: ἄσαντος (σαίνω) not to be soothed, ungentle, Aesch.

ασαομαι.def: ἀσάομαι (ἄση) to feel loathing or nausea, to be disgusted or vexed at a thing, c. dat., Theogn.; τὴν ψυχὴν ἀσηθῆναι Hdt.; ἀσώμενος ἐν φρεσί Theocr.

ασαρκησ.def: ἀσαρκής (σάρξ) not fleshly, i. e. spiritual, Anth.

ασαφησ.def: ἀσαφής indistinct to the senses, dim, faint, Thuc.; or to the mind, dim, obscure, Soph., Thuc.; νὺξ ἀσαφεστέρα ἐστίν by night one sees less distinctly, Xen.: —adv. -φῶς, obscurely, ἀσαφῶς ποτέρων ἀρξάντων without knowing which began, Thuc.

ασβεστοσ.def: ἄσβεστος I. unquenchable, inextinguishable, of fire, Il.; of laughter, etc., Hom.; ἄσβ. πόρος ὠκεανοῦ ocean's ceaseless flow, Aesch. II. as Subst., ἄσβεστος (sc. τίτανος), unslaked lime, Plut.

ασεβεια.def: ἀσέβεια (from ἀσεβής) ungodliness, impiety, profaneness, Eur., Xen., etc.

ασεβεω.gloss: to be impious, to act profanely, sin against the gods
ασεβεω.def: ἀσεβέω (from ἀσεβής) 1. to be impious, to act profanely, sin against the gods; εἴς τινα or τι Hdt., Eur.; περί τινα or τι Hdt., Xen. 2. c. acc. pers. to sin against him, Aesch.; hence in Pass., ἠσέβηται οὐδέν no sin has been committed, Andoc.

ασεβημα.def: ἀσέβημα (ἀσεβής) an impious or profane act, Thuc., Dem.

ασεβησ.def: ἀσεβής (σέβω) ungodly, godless, unholy, profane, Soph.: τὸ ἀσεβές ἀσέβεια, Xen.

ασειρωτοσ.def: ἀσείρωτος (σειρά) not drawn by traces (but by the yoke), Eur.

ασελγαινω.def: ἀσελγαίνω to behave licentiously, Plat.:—Pass., of acts, τὰ ἠσελγημένα, outrageous acts, Dem.

ασελγησ.def: ἀσελγής (The origin of -σελγής is uncertain.) licentious, wanton, brutal, Dem.:—adv., ἀσελγῶς πίονες extravagantly fat, Ar.; ἀς. ζῆν Dem.

αση.def: ἄση (ἄω to satiate) nausea, distress, vexation, Hdt., Eur.

ασημαντοσ.def: ἀσήμαντος (σημαίνω) I. without leader or shepherd, Il. II. unsealed, unmarked, Hdt.

ασημοσ.def: ἄσημος (σῆμα) I. without mark or sign, ἄς. χρυσός uncoined gold, Hdt.; ἄς. ἀργύριον Thuc.; ἄς. ὅπλα arms without device, Eur. II. of sacrifices or oracles, giving no sign, unintelligible, Hdt., Trag. III. leaving no mark, indistinct, Soph.; of sounds, inarticulate, unintelligible, Hdt.; ἄσημα βοῆς ἄσημος βοή, Soph.:—generally, unperceived, unnoticed, Aesch., Soph. IV. of persons, cities, etc., of no mark, unknown, obscure, Eur.

ασθενεια.gloss: want of strength, weakness, feebleness, sickliness
ασθενεια.def: ἀσθένεια (ἀσθενής) 1. want of strength, weakness, feebleness, sickliness, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἀσθένεια βίου poverty, Hdt. 2. sickness, a disease, Thuc.

ασθενεω.def: ἀσθενέω (ἀσθενής) to be weak, feeble, sickly, Eur., Thuc., etc.; ἠσθένησε he fell sick, Dem.

ασθενησ.def: ἀσθενής (σθένος) I. without strength, weak, feeble, weakly, Hdt., etc.; ἀσθενέστερος πόνον ἐνεγκεῖν too weak to bear labour, Dem.:— τὸ ἀσθενὲς ἀσθένεια, Thuc. 2. of property, weak, poor, Hdt., Eur.; οἱ ἀσθενέστεροι the weaker sort, i. e. the poor, Xen. 3. insignificant, οὐκ ἀσθενέστατος σοφιστής Hdt.; of streams, petty, small, id. II. adv. ἀσθενῶς, feebly, slightly, Plat.: comp. -έστερον or -έστερα id., Thuc.

ασθμα.def: ἆσθμα (ἄω, to blow) I. short breath, panting, from toil, Il., Aesch. II. generally, a breath, breathing, Mosch.: a blast, Anth.

ασθμαινω.gloss: to breathe hard, gasp for breath
ασθμαινω.def: ἀσθμαίνω (ἆσθμα) to breathe hard, gasp for breath, of one out of breath or dying, mostly in pres. part., Il.

ασιανοσ.def: Ἀσιανός Asiatic, Thuc., etc. also Ἀσιάτης, fem. Ἀσιᾶτις, Ionic Ἀσιήτης Ἀσιῆτις, Aesch., Eur.

ασιαρχησ.def: Ἀσιάρχης (ἄρχω) an Asiarch, the highest religious official under the Romans in the province of Asia, NTest.

ασιασ.def: Ἀσιάς 1. fem. adj. = Ἀσιανή, Asiatic 2. (sc. κιθάρα) the lyre as improved in Lesbos.

ασιδηροσ.def: ἀσίδηρος I. not of iron, Eur.: not made by iron, Anth. II. without sword, unarmed, Eur.

ασικχοσ.def: ἄσικχος (Deriv. uncertain.) not nice as to food, Plut.

ασινησ.def: ἀσινής (σίνομαι) I. unhurt, unharmed, of persons, Od., Hdt.: secure, happy of life and fortune, Aesch. 2. of things, undamaged, Hdt. II. act. not harming, id.: harmless, Xen. 2. protecting from harm, Aesch. III. adv. ἀσινῶς, innocently, Sup. -εστατα Xen.

ασισ.def: ἄσις slime, mud, such as a river brings down, Il.

ασιτεω.def: ἀσιτέω (ἄσῑτος) to abstain from food, fast, Eur., Plat.

ασιτια.def: ἀσιτία (ἄσῑτος) want of food, Hdt., Eur.

ασιτοσ.def: ἄσιτος without food, fasting, Od., attic

ασκαλαβωτησ.def: ἀσκαλαβώτης (Deriv. unknown.) the spotted lizard, Lat. stellio, Ar.

ασκαντησ.def: ἀσκάντης (Deriv. unknown.) I. a poor bed, pallet, Ar. II. a bier, Anth.

ασκαρδαμυκτι.def: ἀσκαρδαμυκτί (ἀσκαρδάμυκτος) without winking, with unchanged look, Xen.

ασκαρδαμυκτοσ.def: ἀσκαρδάμυκτος (σκαρδαμύσσω) not blinking or winking, Ar.

ασκελησ.def: ἀσκελής (α euphon., σκέλλω) 1. dried up, withered, Od. 2. neut. ἀσκελές as adv. toughly, obstinately, stubbornly, ἀσκελὲς αἰεί id.; so, ἀσκελέως αἰεί Il.

ασκεπαρνοσ.def: ἀσκέπαρνος (σκέπαρνον) without the axe, unhewn, Soph.

ασκεπτοσ.def: ἄσκεπτος (σκοπέω) I. inconsiderate, unreflecting, Plat.:—adv. -τως, inconsiderately, Thuc., etc. II. unconsidered, unobserved, Xen.

ασκευησ.gloss: without the implements of his art
ασκευησ.def: ἀσκευής (σκευή) without the implements of his art, Hdt.

ασκευοσ.def: ἄσκευος (σκευή) unfurnished, unprepared, Soph.: c. gen. unfurnished with a thing, id.

ασκεω.gloss: to work curiously, form by art, fashion
ασκεω.def: ἀσκέω I. to work curiously, form by art, fashion, Hom.; ἀσκήσας with skilful art, id. 2. of adornment, to dress out, trick out, decorate, adorn, deck, Hdt.: Pass., πέπλοισι Περσικοῖς ἠσκημένη Aesch.:—Mid., σῶμ’ ἠσκήσατο adorned his own person, Eur. II. in Prose, to practise, exercise, train, Lat. exercere, properly of athletic exercise: 1. of the person trained, Ar.; ἀσκεῖν τὸ σῶμα εἴς or πρός τι for an object or purpose, Xen., etc. 2. of the thing practised, ἀσκ. τέχνην Hdt.; metaph., ἀσκ. τὴν ἀλήθειαν id.; κακότητα Aesch.; ἀσέβειαν Eur. 3. c. inf., ἄσκει τοιαύτη μένειν endeavour to remain such, Soph.; ἀσκ. ἀγαθὰ ποιεῖν to make a practice of doing good, Xen. 4. absol. to practise, go into training, οἱ ἀσκοῦντες those who practise gymnastics, id.

ασκηθησ.def: ἀσκηθής (Deriv. uncertain.) unhurt, unharmed, unscathed, Hom.

ασκησισ.def: ἄσκησις (ἀσκέω) I. exercise, practice, training, Thuc., Xen., etc.; in pl. exercises, Plat.:—c. gen., ἄσκ. τινος practice of or in a thing, id. II. generally, a mode of life, profession, art, Luc.

ασκητεοσ.def: ἀσκητέος (ἀσκέω) I. to be practised, Xen. II. ἀσκητέον, one must practise, σοφίαν Plat.

ασκητησ.def: ἀσκητής (ἀσκέω) one who practises any art or trade, ἀσκ. τῶν πολεμικῶν Xen.: esp. an athlete, one trained for the arena, Ar., Plat.

ασκητοσ.def: ἀσκητός (ἀσκέω) I. curiously wrought, Od.: adorned, πέπλωι with a robe, Theocr. 2. to be acquired by practice, Plat., Xen. II. of persons, practised in a thing, c. dat., Plut.

ασκληπιαδαι.def: Ἀσκληπιάδαι a name for physicians, Theogn., Soph.

ασκληπιειον.def: Ἀσκληπιεῖον the temple of Asclepius, Luc.

ασκληπιειοσ.def: Ἀσκληπίειος of, belonging to Asclepius, Ἀσκληπίεια (sc. ἱερά) his festival, Plat.

ασκληπιοσ.def: Ἀσκληπιός Asclepius, Lat. Aesculapius, a Thessalian prince, famous as a physician, Il.:—later, son of Apollo, tutelary god of medicine.

ασκοποσ.def: ἄσκοπος (σκοπέω) I. inconsiderate, heedless, Il.: unregardful of a thing, c. gen., Aesch. II. pass. unseen, invisible, Soph. 2. not to be seen, unintelligible, obscure, Aesch., Soph.: inconceivable, incalculable, id.

ασκοσ.def: ἀσκός 1. a leathern-bag, a wine-skin, Hom.; ἀσκὸς βοός the bag of ox-skin in which Aeolus bottled up the winds, Od.; ἀσκὸς Μαρσυέω a bag made of the skin of Marsyas, Hdt.:— a bladder, Eur. 2. proverb. usage, ἀσκὸν δείρειν τινά to flay one alive, maltreat wantonly, Ar.; ἀσκὸς δεδάρθαι Solon.

ασκωλια.gloss: the 2nd day of the rural Dionysia, when they danced upon greased wine-skins
ασκωλια.def: ἀσκώλια (ἀσκός) the 2nd day of the rural Dionysia, when they danced upon greased wine-skins, "unctos saluere per utres."

ασκωλιαζω.def: ἀσκωλιάζω (ασκώλια) to dance as at the Ἀσκώλια, Ar.

ασκωμα.def: ἄσκωμα (ἀσκός) the leather padding of the hole which served for the row-lock, put there to make the oar move easily, Ar.

ασμα.def: ᾆσμα (ἄιδω) a song, a lyric ode, or lay, Plat.

ασμενοσ.def: ἄσμενος (ἥδομαι, the perf. part. of which would be ἡσμένος) well-pleased, glad, always with a Verb, φύγεν ἄσμενος he escaped gladly or he was glad to have escaped, Hom., etc.; ἐμοὶ δέ κεν ἀσμένωι εἴη glad would it make me! Il.; ἀσμένωι δέ σοι νὺξ ἀποκρύψει φάος glad wilt thou be when night shuts out the light, Aesch.: —adv. ἀσμένως, gladly, readily, id., Eur.: Sup. ἀσμεναίτατα, -έστατα, Plat.

ασπαζομαι.gloss: to welcome kindly, bid welcome, greet
ασπαζομαι.def: ἀσπάζομαι 1. to welcome kindly, bid welcome, greet, Lat. salutare, τινα Hom., etc.; as the common form on meeting, ἀσπάζομαί σε or ἀσπάζομαι alone, Ar.; πρόσωθεν αὐτὴν ἀσπ. I salute her at a respectful distance, i. e. keep away from her, Eur.:— also to take leave of, id., Xen. 2. to embrace, kiss, caress, Ar.; of dogs, Lat. blandiri, Xen. 3. of things, to follow eagerly, cleave to, Lat. amplector, ἀσπ. τὸν οἶνον Plat. 4. ἀσπ. ὅτι to be glad that, Ar.

ασπαιρω.def: ἀσπαίρω (α euphon., σπαίρω) to pant, gasp, struggle convulsively, of the dying, Hom., Hdt.; but, μοῦνος ἤσπαιρε he was the only one who still made a struggle, Hdt.

ασπαλαθοσ.def: ἀσπάλαθος (Deriv. unknown.) aspalathus, a prickly shrub, yielding a fragrant oil, Theogn.; used as an instrument of torture, Plat.

ασπαρτοσ.def: ἄσπαρτος (σπείρω) 1. of land, unsown, untilled, Od. 2. of plants, not sown, growing wild, id.

ασπασιοσ.def: ἀσπάσιος (ἀσπάζομαι) I. welcome, gladly welcomed, Hom. II. well-pleased, glad, id.:— adv. -ίως, gladly, id., Hdt.

ασπασμα.def: ἄσπασμα (ἀσπάζομαι) a greeting, esp. in pl. embraces, Eur.

ασπασμοσ.def: ἀσπασμός (ἀσπάζομαι) a greeting, embrace, salutation, Theogn., NTest.

ασπαστοσ.def: ἀσπαστός = ἀσπάσιος, welcome, Od., Hdt. adv. -τῶς, id.

ασπειστοσ.gloss: to be appeased by no libations, implacable
ασπειστοσ.def: ἄσπειστος (σπένδω) to be appeased by no libations, implacable, Dem.

ασπερμοσ.def: ἄσπερμος (σπέρμα) without seed or posterity, Il.

ασπερχεσ.def: ἀσπερχές (α euphon., σπέρχω) (a neut. form used as adv.) hastily, hotly, vehemently, Hom.

ασπετοσ.def: ἄσπετος (εἰπεῖν) unspeakable, unutterable, unspeakably great, Hom.:—neut. as adv. unspeakably, Il.

ασπιδαποβλησ.gloss: one that throws away his shield, a runaway
ασπιδαποβλησ.def: ἀσπιδαποβλής (ἀποβάλλω) one that throws away his shield, a runaway, Ar.

ασπιδοπηγειον.def: ἀσπιδοπηγεῖον (πήγνυμι) the workshop of a shieldmaker, Dem.

ασπιδοφερμων.def: ἀσπιδοφέρμων (φέρβω) living by the shield, i. e. by war, Eur.

ασπιλοσ.def: ἄσπιλος (σπίλος) without spot, spotless, Anth., NTest.

ασπισ.def: ἀσπίς I. a round shield, Lat. clipeus, of bull's hide, overlaid with metal plates, with a boss (ὀμφαλός) in the middle, and fringed with tassels (θύσανοι): different from the oblong shield (ὅπλον, Lat. scutum) used by the ὁπλῖται. 2. in Prose, used for a body of soldiers, ὀκτακισχιλίη ἀσπίς 8, 000 men-at-arms, Hdt. 3. military phrases: ἐπ’ ἀσπίδας πέντε καὶ εἴκοσι τάξασθαι to be drawn up 25 deep, Thuc.; so, ἐπ’ ἀσπίδων ὀλίγων τετάχθαι id.; ἐπ’ ἀσπίδα, παρ’ ἀσπίδα (opp. to ἐπὶ δόρυ) on the left, towards or to the left, because the shield was on the left arm, Xen.; παρ’ ἀσπ. στῆναι to stand in battle-array, Eur. II. an asp, an Egyptian snake, Hdt.

ασπιστησ.gloss: one armed with a shield, a warrior
ασπιστησ.def: ἀσπιστής (ἀσπίς) one armed with a shield, a warrior, gen. pl. ἀσπιστάων, Il.:—as adj., ἀσπισταὶ μόχθοι τευχέων, i. e. the shield of Achilles, Eur.

ασπιστωρ.def: ἀσπίστωρ (ἀσπίς) (= ἀσπιστής) κλόνοι ἀσπίστορες turmoil of shielded warriors, Aesch.

ασπλαγχνοσ.def: ἄσπλαγχνος (σπλάγχνον) without bowels: metaph. heartless, spiritless, Soph.

ασπονδοσ.def: ἄσπονδος (σπονδή) I. without drink-offering, of a god, to whom no drink-offering is poured, ἄσπ. θεός i. e. death, Eur. II. without a regular truce (which was ratified by σπονδαί), Thuc.; ἀσπόνδους τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀνελέσθαι to take up their dead without leave asked, id.; τὸ ἄσπονδον a keeping out of treaty or covenant with others, neutrality, id. 2. admitting of no truce, implacable, deadly, Lat. internecinus, of war, Aesch., Dem.

ασπουδαστοσ.gloss: not to be zealously pursued, not worth pursuing
ασπουδαστοσ.def: ἀσπούδαστος (σπουδάζω) not to be zealously pursued, not worth pursuing, Eur.

ασπουδι.gloss: without zeal, without a struggle, ignobly
ασπουδι.def: ἀσπουδί (σπουδή) without zeal, without a struggle, ignobly, Il.

ασσαριον.def: ἀσσάριον Dim. of Lat. as, a farthing, NTest., Plut.

ασσον.def: ἆσσον (ἄγχι) nearer, very near, Hom.: c. gen., ἆσσον ἐμεῖο nearer to me, Il.; with a double comp., μᾶλλον ἆσσον Soph.:—hence, as a new comp., ἀσσοτέρω, with or without gen., Od.; Sup. ἀσσοτάτω, Anth.; whence adj. ἀσσότατος id.

ασσυρια.gloss: Assyria, the country of the Assyrians
ασσυρια.def: Ἀσσυρία (sc. γῆ), ἡ Assyria, the country of the Assyrians, id.

ασταθμητοσ.def: ἀστάθμητος (σταθμάομαι) unsteady, unstable, ἀστέρες Xen.; ὁ δῆμος ἀσταθμητότατον πρᾶγμα Dem.: uncertain of life, Eur.; τὸ ἀστάθμητον uncertainty, Thuc.

αστακτι.def: ἀστακτί (ἄστακτος) not in drops, i. e. in floods, Soph., Plat.

αστακτοσ.def: ἄστακτος (στάζω) not in drops, gushing, Eur.

αστανδησ.def: ἀστάνδης a courier, Persian word, Plut.

αστασιαστοσ.def: ἀστασίαστος (στασιάζω) not disturbed by faction, Thuc.: of persons, free from party-spirit, not factious, Plat.

ασταφισ.def: ἀσταφίς (α euphon., σταφίς) as collect. noun, dried grapes, raisins, Lat. uva passa, Hdt.

ασταχυσ.def: ἄσταχυς (α euphon., σταχύς) an ear of corn, Il., Hdt.

αστεγαστοσ.def: ἀστέγαστος (στεγάζω) uncovered: διὰ τὸ ἀστέγαστον from their having no shelter, Thuc.

αστειζομαι.def: ἀστεΐζομαι (ἀστεῖος) Dep. to talk cleverly, Plut.

αστειοσ.def: ἀστεῖος (ἄστυ) of the town: hence, like Lat. urbanus, town-bred, polite, courteous, opp. to ἄγροικος, Plat.:— refined, elegant, pretty, witty, clever Ar., Plat.:—ironically, ἀστ. κέρδος a pretty piece of luck, Ar.

αστεμφησ.def: ἀστεμφής (στέμβω) 1. unmoved, unshaken, Il.; ἀστεμφὲς ἔχεσκε [τὸ σκῆπτρον] he held it stiff, id.:— adv., ἀστεμφέως ἐχέμεν to hold fast, Od.: also neut. ἀστεμφές, as adv. stiff, stark, Mosch. 2. of persons, stiff, unflinching, Theocr.

αστενακτοσ.def: ἀστένακτος (στενάζω) without sigh or groan, Soph., Eur.

αστεοσ.def: ᾀστέος (ἄιδω) one must sing, Ar., Plat.

αστεργανωρ.gloss: without love of man, shunning wedlock
αστεργανωρ.def: ἀστεργάνωρ (στέργω, ἀνήρ) without love of man, shunning wedlock, Aesch.

αστεργησ.def: ἀστεργής (στέργω) without love, implacable, hateful, Soph.

αστεροεισ.def: ἀστερόεις (ἀστήρ) I. starred, starry, Il. II. like a star, glittering, id.

αστεροπητησ.def: ἀστεροπητής (ἀστεροπή) the lightener, of Zeus, Il.

αστερωποσ.def: ἀστερωπός (ἀστήρ, ὤψ) I. star-faced, bright-shining, Eur. II. starry, id.

αστεφανωτοσ.def: ἀστεφάνωτος (στεφανόω) uncrowned, not to be crowned, Plat., etc.

αστη.def: ἀστή (ἀστός) fem. of ἀστός, Hdt., etc.

αστηρ.def: ἀστήρ (The Root is ΣΤΕΡ, α being euphon., cf. Lat. stella, i. e. sterula.) (dat. pl. = ἄστρασι not ἀστράσι) 1. a star, Il., etc.; cf. ἄστρον. 2. a flame, light, fire, Eur.

αστηρικτοσ.def: ἀστήρικτος (στηρίζω) not steady, unstable, Anth., NTest.

αστιβησ.def: ἀστιβής (στείβω) 1. untrodden, Aesch.: desert, pathless, Soph. 2. not to be trodden, holy, id.

αστικοσ.def: ἀστικός (ἄστυ) I. of a city or town, opp. to country, Aesch.; τὰ ἀστικὰ Διονύσια (also called τὰ κατ’ ἄστυ), Thuc. II. like ἀστεῖος, polite, neat, nice, ἀστικά (as adv.) Theocr.

αστικτοσ.def: ἄστικτος (στίζω) not marked with στίγματα, not tattooed, Hdt.

αστολοσ.def: ἄστολος (στέλλω) unequipped, of Charon's boat, used in the same way as γάμος ἄγαμος, Aesch.

αστομοσ.def: ἄστομος (στόμα) I. without mouth: of horses, hardmouthed, restive, Soph. II. of dogs, soft-mouthed, unable to hold with the teeth, Xen. III. of metal, soft, incapable of a fine edge, Plut.

αστοργοσ.def: ἄστοργος (στοργή) without natural affection, Aeschin.; ὥστοργος (i. e. ὁ ἄστ.) the heartless one, Theocr.

αστοσ.def: ἀστός (ἄστυ) a townsman, citizen, Hom., attic

αστοχεω.gloss: to miss the mark, to miss, fail
αστοχεω.def: ἀστοχέω (from ἄστοχος) to miss the mark, to miss, fail, τινος or περί τινος Polyb.; περί τι NTest.

αστοχοσ.gloss: missing the mark, aiming badly at
αστοχοσ.def: ἄστοχος missing the mark, aiming badly at, τινος Plat., Anth.

αστραβη.gloss: a mule's saddle, an easy padded saddle
αστραβη.def: ἀστράβη (Deriv. uncertain.) a mule's saddle, an easy padded saddle, Dem.

αστραγαλιζω.def: ἀστραγαλίζω (ἀστράγαλος) to play with ἀστράγαλοι, Plat.

αστραγαλισισ.def: ἀστραγάλισις (ἀστραγαλίζω) a playing with ἀστράγαλοι, Arist.

αστραγαλοσ.def: ἀστράγαλος (Deriv. uncertain.) I. one of the neck-vertebrae, Hom. II. the ball of the ankle joint, Lat. talus, Hdt., Theocr. III. pl. ἀστράγαλοι, dice or agame played with dice, Il., Hdt.:—they were at first made of knuckle-bones, and never had more than four flat sides, whereas the κύβοι had six. They played with four: the best throw (βόλος), when each die came differently, was called Ἀφροδίτη, Lat. jactus Veneris; the worst, when all came alike, κύων, Lat. canis.

αστραπη.def: ἀστραπή (ἀστεροπή, στεροπή) 1. a flash of lightning, lightning, Hdt., attic; in pl. lightnings, Aesch., Soph. 2. any bright light, NTest.

αστραπτω.def: ἀστράπτω (α euphon., στράπτω, cf. ἀστεροπή) I. to lighten, hurl lightnings, of omens sent by Zeus, Il., Ar. 2. impers., ἀστράπτει it lightens, ἤστραψε it lightened, attic II. to flash like lightning, Soph., Eur., etc.:—c. acc. cogn., ἐξ ὀμμάτων δ’ ἤστραπτε σέλας (sc. Τυφών) he flashed flame from his eyes, Aesch.

αστρατεια.def: ἀστρατεία 1. exemption from service, Ar. 2. a shunning of service, which at Athens was a heavy offence, φεύγειν γραφὴν ἀστρατείας to be accused of it, id.; ἀστρατείας ἁλῶναι, ὀφλεῖν to be convicted of it, Oratt.

αστρατευτοσ.gloss: without service, never having seen service
αστρατευτοσ.def: ἀστράτευτος (στρατεύω) without service, never having seen service, Ar.

αστρεπτοσ.def: ἄστρεπτος (ἄστροφος) 1. = ἄστροφος Theocr.:—adv. -τεί, Anth. 2. unbending, inflexible, id.

αστρον.def: ἄστρον mostly in pl. the stars, Hom., attic; in sg., mostly of Sirius, Xen., etc.; cf. ἀστήρ.

αστρονομικοσ.gloss: skilled in astronomy, pertaining to astronomy
αστρονομικοσ.def: ἀστρονομικός (ἀστρονόμος) skilled in astronomy, pertaining to astronomy, Plat.

αστροφοσ.def: ἄστροφος (στρέφω) without turning away, unturning, Lat. irretortus, ὄμματα Aesch.; ἀφέρπειν ἄστρ. to go away without turning back, Soph.

αστρωοσ.def: ἀστρῷος (ἄστρον) starry, Anth.; ἀστρ. ἀνάγκη the law of the stars, id.

αστρωτοσ.def: ἄστρωτος without bed or bedding, Plat.: metaph. unsmoothed, rugged, Eur.

αστυ.def: ἄστυ I. a city, town, Hom., etc.; Σούσων ἄ. the town of Susa, Aesch.; ἄ. Θήβης Soph. II. the Athenians called Athens Ἄστυ, as the Romans called Rome Urbs, mostly without the Art. (as we speak of "being in town, " "going to town"), Ar.

αστυαναξ.def: ἀστυάναξ lord of the city, epith. of certain gods, Aesch.: in Hom. only as prop. n.

αστυβοωτησ.def: ἀστυβοώτης (βοάω) crying through the city, of a herald, Il.

αστυγειτων.def: ἀστυγείτων (gen. ονος) 1. near or bordering on a city, Hdt., Aesch. 2. as Subst. a neighbour to the city, a borderer, Hdt., Thuc.

αστυδε.def: ἄστυδε into, to, or towards the city, Hom.

αστυδρομεομαι.gloss: to have the streets filled with fugitives
αστυδρομεομαι.def: ἀστυδρομέομαι Pass. to have the streets filled with fugitives, Aesch.

αστυλοσ.def: ἄστυλος without pillar or prop, Anth.

αστυνικοσ.def: ἀστύνικος (νίκη) (sc. πόλις) Athens, the victorious city, Aesch.

αστυνομια.def: ἀστυνομία the office of ἀστυνόμος, Arist.

αστυνομικοσ.def: ἀστυνομικός of or for an ἀστυνόμος or his office, Plat.

αστυνομοσ.def: ἀστυνόμος (νέμω) I. protecting the city, θεοί Aesch.; ὀργαὶ ἀστ. the feelings of social life, Soph. II. as Subst. a magistrate at Athens, who had the care of the police, streets, and public buildings, five for the city and five for Peiraeeus, Plat., etc.

ασυγκριτοσ.def: ἀσύγκριτος (συγκρίνω) not to be compared, unlike, Plut.

ασυκοφαντητοσ.gloss: not plagued by informers, not calumniated
ασυκοφαντητοσ.def: ἀσυκοφάντητος (συκοφαντέω) not plagued by informers, not calumniated, Aeschin., Luc.

ασυλλογιστοσ.def: ἀσυλλόγιστος (συλλογίζομαι) not reasoning justly:— adv., -τως, ἀσυλλογίστως ἔχειν τινός to be unable to reason about a thing, Plut.

ασυλοσ.def: ἄσυλος (σύλη) I. safe from violence, inviolate, of persons seeking protection, Eur.:—c. gen., γάμων ἄσυλος safe from marriage, id. II. of places, γῆν ἄσυλον παρασχεῖν to make the land a refuge, id.

ασυμβατοσ.def: ἀσύμβατος (συμβαίνω) not coming to terms, Thuc.:—adv., -τως ἔχειν to be irreconcilable, Plut.

ασυμβλητοσ.def: ἀσύμβλητος (συμβάλλω) not to be guessed, unintelligible, Soph.

ασυμβολοσ.def: ἀσύμβολος not paying one's scot or share (συμβολαί), Lat. immunis, δειπνεῖν ἀσύμβολον Aeschin.

ασυμμετρια.def: ἀσυμμετρία (ἀσύμμετρος) want of proportion or harmony, Plat.

ασυμμετροσ.def: ἀσύμμετρος I. having no common measure, τινι with a thing, Plat.; πρός τι Plut. II. unsymmetrical, disproportionate, Xen.

ασυμπαθησ.def: ἀσυμπαθής without sympathy with, τινι Plut.

ασυμφοροσ.def: ἀσύμφορος inconvenient, inexpedient, useless, Hes.: c. dat. inexpedient for, prejudicial to, Eur., Thuc.; also ἔς or πρός τι id.:— adv. -ρως, Xen.

ασυμφωνοσ.def: ἀσύμφωνος not agreeing in sound, Plat.:—metaph. discordant, at variance, τινι with another, id.; πρός τινα NTest.

ασυμψηφοσ.def: ἀσύμψηφος not agreeing with, τινος Plut.

ασυνεσια.def: ἀσυνεσία (ἀσύνετος) want of understanding, stupidity, Eur., Thuc.

ασυνετοσ.def: ἀσύνετος void of understanding, stupid, Hdt., attic; not to be understood, unintelligible, Eur.

ασυνηθεια.def: ἀσυνήθεια (ἀσυνήθης) want of experience in a thing, c. gen., Arist.

ασυνηθησ.def: ἀσυνήθης unaccustomed, inexperienced, unacquainted, with others, Arist.

ασυνθετοσ.def: ἀσύνθετος (συντίθημι) I. uncompounded, Plat. II. （συντίθεμαι) bound by no covenant, faithless, Dem., NTest.

ασυντακτοσ.def: ἀσύντακτος 1. not ranged together; of soldiers, not in battle-order, Xen. 2. undisciplined, disorderly, Thuc., Xen. 3. not combined in society, id. 4. not put on the tax-roll, free from public burdens, Dem.

ασυντονοσ.def: ἀσύντονος not strained, slack:— adv. -νως, lazily, Sup. -ώτατα, Xen.

ασυσκευαστοσ.def: ἀσυσκεύαστος not arranged, not ready, Xen.

ασυστατοσ.def: ἀσύστατος (συνίσταμαι) 1. having no cohesion or consistency, Plat. 2. metaph. incoherent, irregular, Lat. dispar sibi, Ar.; ἀξ. ἄλγος fitful, ever-recurring pain, Aesch.

ασφαδαστοσ.def: ἀσφάδαστος (σφαδάζω) without convulsion or struggle, of one dying, Aesch., Soph.

ασφαλαξ.def: ἀσφάλαξ (α euphon., σπάλαξ) a mole, Babr.

ασφαλεια.def: ἀσφάλεια (ἀσφαλής) 1. security against stumbling or falling, ἀσφ. πρὸς τὸν πηλόν Thuc.: stability, Soph. 2. assurance from danger, personal safety, security, Hdt., Thuc., etc.; ἀσφ. διδόναι, παρέχειν Xen. 3. assurance, certainty, ἀσφ. μὴ ἂν ἐλθεῖν αὐτούς certainty that they would not come, Thuc.; ἀσφάλεια λόγου the certainty of an argument, Xen., NTest.

ασφαλειοσ.def: Ἀσφάλειος (ἀσφαλής) of Poseidon, the securer, Ar.

ασφαλησ.gloss: not liable to fall, immoveable, steadfast, firm
ασφαλησ.def: ἀσφαλής (σφάλλομαι) I. not liable to fall, immoveable, steadfast, firm, θεῶν ἕδος Od., etc. 2. of friends and the like, unfailing, trusty, Soph., etc.: c. inf., φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς the hasty in council are not safe, id.: so of things, sure, certain, Thuc., etc. 3. assured from danger, safe, secure, Soph., etc.; ἐν ἀσφαλεῖ in safety, Thuc.; τὸ ἀσφαλές ἀσφάλεια, id.; ἀσφαλές [ἐστι], c. inf., it is safe to.., Ar. 4. ἀσφ. ῥήτωρ a convincing speaker, id. II. epic adv. ἀσφαλέως ἔχειν or μένειν to be, remain fast, firm, steady, Hom.; so neut. ἀσφαλές as adv., id.; ἀσφ. ἀγορεύει without faltering, Od.; ἔμπεδον ἀσφαλέως without fail for ever, Hom.; still further strengthd., ἔμπεδον ἀσφαλὲς ἀεί Il. III. attic adv. ἀσφαλῶς in all senses of the adj., in safety, with certainty, Soph.:—comp. -έστερον, Hdt., Plat.; Sup. -έστατα, id.

ασφαλιζομαι.def: ἀσφαλίζομαι Mid. to make safe, secure, NTest.

ασφαλτοσ.def: ἄσφαλτος asphalt, bitumen, forming in lumps, (θρόμβοι) on the surface of the river Is near Babylon and at Ardericca near Susa, Hdt. (Seems to be a foreign word.)

ασφαραγεω.def: ἀσφαραγέω (α euphon., σφαραγέω) to resound, clang, of armed men, Theocr.

ασφοδελοσ.def: ἀσφόδελος (Deriv. unknown) I. ἀσφόδελος as noun, asphodel, king's-spear, a plant of the lily kind, Hes., Theocr. II. oxyt., as adj., ἀσφοδελὸς λειμών the asphodel mead, which the shades of heroes haunted, Od.

ασχαλαω.def: ἀσχαλάω (Deriv. uncertain.) to be distressed, grieved, Hom.: to be vexed at a thing, c. gen., Od.

ασχαλλω.def: ἀσχάλλω (= ἀσχαλάω) to be vexed at a thing, Aesch., Eur.; τι id.

ασχετοσ.def: ἄσχετος (σχεῖν) not to beheld in or checked, irrepressible, ungovernable, Hom.

ασχηματιστοσ.def: ἀσχημάτιστος (σχηματίζω) without form or figure, Plat.

ασχημονεω.gloss: to behave unseemly, disgrace oneself, to be put to shame
ασχημονεω.def: ἀσχημονέω (ἀσχήμων) to behave unseemly, disgrace oneself, to be put to shame, Eur., Plat.

ασχημοσυνη.def: ἀσχημοσύνη (ἀσχήμων) want of form, ungracefulness, Plat.: in moral sense, indecorum, id.

ασχημων.def: ἀσχήμων (σχῆμα) 1. misshapen, unseemly, shameful, Lat. turpis, Eur. 2. of persons, ἀσχ. γενέσθαι to be indecorous, Hdt.

ασχολεω.def: ἀσχολέω to engage, occupy, τινά Luc.

ασχολια.gloss: an occupation, business, want of leisure
ασχολια.def: ἀσχολία an occupation, business, want of leisure, Thuc.; ἀσχ. ἔχειν φιλοσοφίας πέρι to have no leisure for pursuing it, Plat.; ἀσχ. ἄγειν to be engaged or occupied, id.; ἀσχ. παρέχειν τινί to cause one trouble, id.

ασχολοσ.def: ἄσχολος (σχολή) I. of persons, without leisure, engaged, occupied, busy, Plat., Dem.; ἄσχ. ἔς τι with no leisure for a thing, Hdt.; ἄσχ. περί τι busy about.., Plut.:—adv., ἀσχόλως ἔχειν to be busy, Eur. II. of actions, allowing no leisure, id.

ασχυ.gloss: the inspissated juice of a Scythian tree
ασχυ.def: ἄσχυ the inspissated juice of a Scythian tree, Hdt.

ασωτευομαι.gloss: to lead a profligate, wasteful life
ασωτευομαι.def: ἀσωτεύομαι (ἄσωτος) Dep. to lead a profligate, wasteful life, Arist.

ασωτοσ.gloss: having no hope of safety, abandoned, profligate
ασωτοσ.def: ἄσωτος (σώζω) I. having no hope of safety, abandoned, profligate, Lat. perditus, Soph., Arist. II. act., ἄσωτος γένει bringing ruin on the race, fatal to it, Aesch.

ατακτεω.def: ἀτακτέω (ἄτακτος) 1. of a soldier, to be undisciplined, disorderly, Xen., Dem. 2. generally, to lead a disorderly life, Xen.

ατακτοσ.def: ἄτακτος I. not in battle-order, of troops, Hdt., Thuc., etc. 2. undisciplined, disorderly, irregular, lawless, id., etc. II. adv. -τως, in an irregular, disorderly manner, of troops, id.: comp. ἀτακτότερον, id.

αταλαιπωροσ.def: ἀταλαίπωρος without pains or patience, indifferent, careless, Thuc.

αταλαντοσ.def: ἀτάλαντος (α copul., τάλαντον) equal in weight, equivalent, or equal to, τινι Hom.

αταλαφρων.def: ἀταλάφρων (φρήν) tender-minded, of a child, Il.

αταλλω.gloss: to skip in childish glee, gambol
αταλλω.def: ἀτάλλω (ἀταλός) (only in pres. and imperf.) I. to skip in childish glee, gambol, Il. II.. Act. to bring up a child, rear, foster, like ἀτιτάλλω, Soph.:—Pass. to grow up, wax, Hhymn.; the Act. is so used by Hes.

αταλοσ.def: ἀταλός (akin to ἁπαλός) tender, delicate, of young creatures, Hom.; ἀταλὰ φρονέοντες of young, gay spirit, Il.

αταξια.def: ἀταξία (ἄτακτος) 1. want of discipline, disorderliness, properly among soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., etc. 2. generally disorder, irregularity, Plat., etc.

αταομαι.gloss: to suffer greatly, be in dire distress
αταομαι.def: ἀτάομαι (ἄτη) to suffer greatly, be in dire distress, ἀτώμενος Soph., Eur.

αταρ.def: ἀτάρ 1. but, yet, Lat. at, to introduce an objection or correction, Il., attic; it always begins a sentence or clause, but is placed after the voc., Ἕκτορ, ἀτάρ που ἔφης still thou didst say, Il.:— ἀτάρ sometimes answers to μέν, more emphatic than δέ, Hom., attic 2. in attic to mark a rapid transition to another thought, Aesch., etc.; so ἀτὰρ δή Eur.

αταρακτοσ.def: ἀτάρακτος (ταράσσω) not disturbed, without confusion, steady, of soldiers, Xen.

αταρβησ.def: ἀταρβής (τάρβος) 1. unfearing, fearless, Il.; ἀτ. τῆς θέας having no fear about the sight, Soph. 2. causing no fear, Aesch.

ατασθαλια.def: ἀτασθαλία (ἀτάσθαλος) presumptuous sin, recklessness, arrogance, Hom. always in pl.; in sg., Hes., Hdt.

ατασθαλλω.def: ἀτασθάλλω (from ἀτασθαλος) (only in pres. part.) acting presumptuously, in arrogance, Od.

ατασθαλοσ.def: ἀτάσθαλος (ἄτη, though α does not agree in quantity) presumptuous, reckless, arrogant, Hom., Hdt.

αταφια.def: ἀταφία (From ἄταφος) want of burial, Luc.

ατε.def: ἅτε I. properly acc. pl. neut. of ὅστε, used as Adv., just as, so as, Il., Hdt., Soph. II. in causal sense, inasmuch as, seeing that, Lat. quippe, with part., ἅτε ἔχων Hdt., Thuc., etc.; with gen. absol., ἅτε τῶν ὁδῶν φυλασσομένων quippe viae custodirentur, Hdt.; with the part. omitted, δίκτυα δοὺς [αὐτῶι], ἅτε θηρευτῆι [ὄντι] id.

ατεγκτοσ.def: ἄτεγκτος (τέγγω) not to be wetted: metaph. not to be softened, relentless, Soph., Eur.

ατειρησ.gloss: not to be worn away, indestructible
ατειρησ.def: ἀτειρής (τείρω) not to be worn away, indestructible, of iron, Hom.: metaph. stubborn, unyielding, Il.

ατειχιστοσ.def: ἀτείχιστος (τειχίζω) 1. unwalled, unfortified, Thuc. 2. not walled in, not blockaded, id.

ατεκμαρτοσ.gloss: not to be guessed, obscure, baffling
ατεκμαρτοσ.def: ἀτέκμαρτος (τεκμαίρομαι) 1. not to be guessed, obscure, baffling, Hdt., Thuc.:—adv., ἀτεκμάρτως ἔχειν to be in the dark about a thing, Xen. 2. of persons, uncertain, inconsistent, Ar.

ατεκνοσ.def: ἄτεκνος (τέκνον) I. without children, childless, Hes., Trag. II. in causal sense, destroying children, Aesch.

ατεκνοω.def: ἀτεκνόω to make childless:— Pass. to be deprived of children, Anth.

ατελεια.def: ἀτέλεια (ἀτελής) exemption from public burdens (τέλη), Lat. immunitas, granted to those who deserved well of the state, attic; c. gen., ἀτ. στρατηΐης exemption from service, Hdt.

ατελεστοσ.def: ἀτέλεστος (τελέω) I. without end or issue, to no purpose, without effect, unaccomplished, Hom. II. uninitiated in mysteries, c. gen., Eur.; absol., Plat.

ατελευτητοσ.def: ἀτελεύτητος (τελευτάω) I. not brought to an end or issue, unaccomplished, Il. II. of a person, impracticable, Soph.

ατελησ.def: ἀτελής (τέλος) I. without end, i. e., 1. not brought to an end or issue, unaccomplished, Od., Xen.:— incomplete, Soph., Thuc., Plat. 2. act. not bringing to an end, not accomplishing one's purpose, Pind., Plat., etc. II. （τέλος iv) at Athens, free from tax or tribute, scot-free, Lat. immunis, absol., or c. gen., ἀτ. τῶν ἄλλων free from all other taxes, Hdt., attic 2. of sums, without deduction, nett, clear, ὀβολὸς ἀτ. an obol clear gain, Xen., Dem. III. （τέλος v) uninitiated in mysteries, c. gen., Hhymn.

ατεμβω.def: ἀτέμβω (Deriv. unknown.) (only in pres.) to maltreat, to afflict, perplex, Od.: Pass., c. gen., to be bereft or cheated of a thing, Hom.

ατενησ.def: ἀτενής (α copul., τείνω) I. strained tight, clinging, of ivy, Soph.: metaph. II. of men's minds and speech, intent, earnest, Hes., Plat.; also stiff, stubborn, inexorable, Aesch., Ar.:—adv. ἀτενῶς earnestly, ἀτ. ἔχειν πρός τι Plut.

ατενιζω.def: ἀτενίζω (ἀτενής) to look intently, gaze earnestly, εἴς τι Arist.; τινί upon one, NTest.

ατερ.def: ἄτερ I. without, Hom.; ἄτερ Ζηνός without his will, Il. II. aloof or apart from, id., Trag.

ατεραμνοσ.def: ἀτέραμνος (τέρην) unsoftened: metaph. stubborn, unfeeling, merciless, Od., Aesch.

ατερμων.def: ἀτέρμων (τέρμα) without bounds; ἀτ. πέπλος having no end or issue, inextricable, Aesch.; ἀτέρμονες αὐγαί the countless rays of the mirror, Eur.

ατεροσ.def: ἅτερος 1. Dor for ἕτερος, Ar. 2. ἅτερος [ᾱ], attic crasis for ὁ ἕτερος, neut. θἄτερον [ᾱ], gen. θἀτέρου, etc.

ατερπησ.def: ἀτερπής (τέρπω) unpleasing, joyless, melancholy, Hom., Aesch.; ἀτερπέστερον εἰς ἀκρόασιν less attractive to the ear, Thuc.

ατευκτεω.def: ἀτευκτέω (From ἄτευκτος) to fail in gaining a thing, c. gen., Babr.

ατεχνια.def: ἀτεχνία (From ἄτεχνος) want of art or skill, unskilfulness, Plat.

ατεχνοσ.gloss: without art, ignorant of the rules of art, unskilled, empirical
ατεχνοσ.def: ἄτεχνος (τέχνη) without art, ignorant of the rules of art, unskilled, empirical, Plat.

ατεχνωσ.def: ἀτεχνῶς (with penult. short) adv. of ἀτεχνής, simply, i. e. really, absolutely, Lat. plane, omnino, Ar., Plat., etc.; καλὸν ἀτ. simply beautiful, Ar.:—in comparisons, ἀτεχνῶς ὥσπερ just as, Plat.:—with negat., just not, Ar.; ἀτεχνῶς οὐδείς simply no one, id.
ἀτέχνως (adverb of ἄτεχνος) without rules of art, empirically, Xen., Plat.

ατεω.def: ἀτέω in part. ἀτέων, fool-hardy, reckless, Il., Hdt.

ατη.def: ἄτη (ἀάω, φορ ἀάτη) I. bewilderment, infatuation, reckless impulse, caused by judicial blindness sent by the gods, Hom.:—hence Ἄτη is personified as the goddess of mischief or reckless conduct, Ἄτη, ἣ πάντας ἀᾶται Il.: the Λιταί come slowly after her, undoing the evil she has worked, id. II. as a consequence, 1. reckless guilt or sin, as that of Paris, id. 2. bane, ruin, Hom., Trag.:—of persons, a bane, pest, Aesch., Soph.

ατηκτοσ.def: ἄτηκτος not melted or to be melted, Plat.

ατημελησ.def: ἀτημελής I. neglected, Plut. II. careless:— adv., ἀτημελῶς ἔχειν id.

ατημελητοσ.def: ἀτημέλητος (τημελέω) I. unheeded, uncared for, Xen. 2. baffled, disappointed, Aesch. II. taking no heed, slovenly, Alciphro:—adv., ἀτημελήτως ἔχειν to take no heed of a thing, c. gen., Xen.

ατηροσ.def: ἀτηρός I. blinded by ἄτη, hurried to ruin, Theogn. II. baneful, ruinous, mischievous, Aesch., Soph.: τὸ ἀτηρόν bane, ruin, Aesch.; ἀτηρότατον κακόν Ar.

ατθισ.def: Ἀτθίς Attic:— as Subst. (sub. γῆ), Attica, Eur.

ατιετοσ.def: ἀτίετος (τίω) I. unhonoured, Aesch. II. act. not honouring or regarding, τινος Eur.

ατιζω.gloss: not to honour, to hold in no honour
ατιζω.def: ἀτίζω (τίω, α privat.) not to honour, to hold in no honour, θεούς Aesch.: absol. in part., ἀτίζων, unheeding, Il.

ατιμαγελεω.def: ἀτιμαγελέω (From ἀτιμαγέλης) to forsake the herd, Theocr.

ατιμαγελησ.def: ἀτιμαγέλης (ἀγέλη) despising the herd, i.e. straying, feeding alone, Theocr., Anth.

ατιμαζω.gloss: to hold in no honour, to esteem lightly, dishonour, slight
ατιμαζω.def: ἀτιμάζω (ἄτιμος) I. to hold in no honour, to esteem lightly, dishonour, slight, c. acc., Hom., attic: so in Mid., Soph.:—c. acc. cogn., ἔπη ἀτιμάζεις πόλιν thou speakest words in dishonour of the city, id.:—Pass. to suffer dishonour, Hdt., attic 2. c. gen. rei, ἀτ. λόγου to treat as unworthy of speech, Aesch.; ἀτ. ὧν ἀτ. τούτων ἅ, Soph.:—also, μή μ’ ἀτιμάσηις τὸ μὴ οὐ θανεῖν deem me not unworthy to die, id.; οὐκ ἀτιμάσω προσειπεῖν will not disdain to.., Eur. II. = ἀτιμόω in legal sense, to deprive of civil rights, Xen.

ατιμαστεοσ.def: ἀτιμαστέος (From ἀτιμάζω) to be despised, Plat.

ατιμαω.def: ἀτιμάω (ἄτιμος) to dishonour, treat lightly, Hom.

ατιμητοσ.def: ἀτίμητος (τιμάω) I. unhonoured, despised, Il. II. （τῑμή II) not valued or estimated, δίκη ἀτ. a cause in which the penalty is not assessed in court, but fixed by law beforehand, Dem.

ατιμια.def: ἀτιμία I. dishonour, disgrace, Od., Soph., etc.; ἐν ἀτιμίηι τινὰ ἔχειν, ἀτιμίην προστιθέναι τινί Hdt.; ἀτ. τινός dishonour done to one, Eur. 2. at Athens, the loss of civil rights, Lat. deminutio capitis, Aesch., Oratt. II. ἐσθημάτων ἀτ., i. e. ragged garments, Aesch.

ατιμοπενθησ.def: ἀτιμοπενθής (πένθος) sorrowing for dishonour incurred, Aesch.

ατιμοσ.def: ἄτιμος (τιμή I) I. unhonoured, dishonoured, Il., Trag.; comp. ἀτιμότερος less honourable, Xen.; c. gen. without the honour of.., not deemed worthy of.., Aesch.; also, χάρις οὐκ ἄτιμος πόνων no unworthy return for.., id. 2. at Athens, deprived of privileges, Lat. capite deminutus, opp. to ἐπίτιμος, Ar., etc.; also c. gen., ἄτ. γερῶν deprived of privileges, Thuc.; ἄτ. τοῦ συμβουλεύειν deprived of the right of advising, Dem. II. （τιμή II) without price or value, οἶκον ἄτιμον ἔδεις thou devourest his substance without payment made, Od. 2. unrevenged, Aesch. III. adv. -μως, dishonourably, ignominiously, id., Soph.

ατιμοω.def: ἀτιμόω I. to dishonour, Aesch.:— Pass. to suffer dishonour or indignity, Hdt., Aesch., Eur. II. at Athens, to punish with ἀτιμία (2), Lat. aerarium facere, Ar., Oratt.

ατιμωρητοσ.def: ἀτιμώρητος unavenged, i. e., I. unpunished, ἀτ. γίγνεσθαι to escape punishment, Hdt., Thuc.:— adv. -τως, with impunity, Plat. II. for which no revenge has been taken, ἀτιμώρητον ἐᾶν θάνατον Aeschin. III. undefended, unprotected, Thuc.

ατιμωσισ.def: ἀτίμωσις a dishonouring, dishonour done to, c. gen., τραπέζας, πατρός Aesch.

ατιταλλω.def: ἀτιτάλλω redupl. form of ἀτάλλω, to rear up a child, foster, cherish, tend, Hom.; of horses, Pass., χῆν’ ἀτιταλλομένην ἐνὶ οἴκωι Od.

ατιτησ.def: ἀτίτης (τίομαι) I. unpunished, Aesch. II. （τίω) unhonoured, id.

ατιτοσ.def: ἄτιτος (τίω) I. unhonoured, unavenged, Il. II. unpaid, id. [where ῑ].

ατλαγενησ.def: Ἀτλαγενής (γίγνομαι) sprung from Atlas, of the Pleiads, Hes.

ατλαντικοσ.def: Ἀτλαντικός (Ἀτλαντικός) of Atlas, Atlantic, τέρμονες Ἀτλ. the pillars of Hercules, Eur.

ατλαντισ.def: Ἀτλαντίς θάλασσα ἡ Ἀ. καλουμένη, the Atlantic ocean, Hdt.

ατλασ.def: Ἄτλας (α euphon., τλάς, v. Ταλαω) I. Atlas, one of the elder gods, who bore up the pillars of heaven, Od.:—later, one of the Titans, Hes., Aesch. II. in hist. writers, Mount Atlas in Africa, regarded as the pillar of heaven, Hdt.

ατλητεω.def: ἀτλητέω (From ἄτλητος) to be unable to bear a thing, to be impatient, Soph.

ατλητοσ.def: ἄτλητος I. not to be borne, insufferable, Il., Orac. ap. Hdt., Soph. 2. not to be dared, ἄτλητα τλᾶσα Aesch. II. act. incapable of bearing a thing, c. gen., Anth.

ατμητοσ.def: ἄτμητος I. not cut up, unravaged, Thuc., Plut.: of mines, not yet opened, Xen. II. undivided, indivisible, Plat.

ατμιζω.def: ἀτμίζω (ἀτμός) to smoke, Soph.: of water, to steam, Xen.

ατμοσ.def: ἀτμός (ἄω to blow) steam, vapour, Aesch.

ατοκοσ.gloss: having never yet brought forth, never having had a child
ατοκοσ.def: ἄτοκος I. having never yet brought forth, never having had a child, Hdt., Eur. II. not bearing interest, Plat.

ατολμητοσ.def: ἀτόλμητος not to be endured, insufferable, Pind.: of wicked men, Aesch.

ατολμια.def: ἀτολμία (From ἄτολμος) want of daring, cowardice, backwardness, Thuc., Dem.

ατολμοσ.gloss: daring nothing, wanting courage, spiritless, cowardly
ατολμοσ.def: ἄτολμος (τόλμα) daring nothing, wanting courage, spiritless, cowardly, Ar., Thuc.:—of women, unenterprising, retiring, Aesch.:—c. inf. not having the heart to do a thing, id.

ατομοσ.def: ἄτομος (τέμνω) I. uncut, unmown, Soph. II. that cannot be cut, indivisible, Plat.; ἐν ἀτόμωι in a moment, NTest.

ατονεω.def: ἀτονέω (From ἄτονος) to be relaxed, exhausted, Plut.

ατοξοσ.def: ἄτοξος (τόξον) without bow or arrow, Luc.

ατοπια.gloss: a being out of the way
ατοπια.def: ἀτοπία a being out of the way, and so: 1. extraordinary nature of a thing, Thuc. 2. strangeness, oddness, eccentricity, Ar., Plat.

ατοποσ.def: ἄτοπος I. out of place, and so, 1. strange, unwonted, extraordinary, Eur., etc. 2. strange, odd, eccentric, δοῦλοι τῶν ἀεὶ ἀτόπων slaves to every new paradox, Thuc.; τῶν ἀτοπωτάτων ἂν εἴη Dem. 3. unnatural, disgusting, foul, πνεῦμα Thuc. II. adv. —πως, marvellously or absurdly, id., Plat.

ατρακτοσ.def: ἄτρακτος (Deriv. uncertain.) I. a spindle, Hdt., Ar., etc. II. an arrow, Soph.; cf. ἠλακάτη.

ατρακτυλισ.def: ἀτρακτυλίς (derivation unknown.) a thistle-like plant, used for making spindles, Theocr.

ατραποσ.def: ἀτραπός (τρέπω) properly a path with no turnings, generally a path-way, road, Hom., Hdt., Thuc., etc.

ατρεκεια.def: ἀτρέκεια (From ἀτρεκής) I. reality, strict truth, certainty, Hdt. II. personified Ἀτρέκεια, severity, Pind.

ατρεκησ.def: ἀτρεκής (Deriv. uncertain.) I. real, genuine, Il. 2. strict, precise, exact, ἀριθμός Hdt.:— τὸ ἀτρεκές ἀτρέκεια, id.; τὸ ἀτρεκέστερον greater exactness, id.; τὸ ἀτρεκέστατον id. 3. sure, certain, Eur. II. used by Hom. mostly in adv. ἀτρεκέως, with ἀγορεύειν, καταλέξαι, to tell truly, exactly; so also Hdt. 2. also neut. as adv., δεκὰς ἀτρεκές just ten of them, Od.; so, τὸ ἀτρεκές Theogn.

ατρεμασ.def: ἀτρέμας (τρέμω) (ἀτρέμα used by Poets for ἀτρέμας before a conson., Il.) without trembling, without motion, Hom.; ἀτρέμας εὕδειν id.; ἀτρέμας ἧσο sit still, Il.; ἀτρέμας ἔχειν to keep quiet, Hdt.; ἀτρ. ἅπτεσθαί τινος gently, softly, Eur.; ἀτρ. πορεύεσθαι to go softly, Xen.

ατρεμεω.gloss: not to tremble, to keep still
ατρεμεω.def: ἀτρεμέω (From ἀτρεμής) not to tremble, to keep still or quiet, Hes.; οὐδαμᾶ κω ἠτρεμήσαμεν, of a restless people, Hdt. From

ατρεμησ.def: ἀτρεμής (τρέμω) not trembling, unmoved, Plat., Xen. adv. ἀτρεμέως Theogn.

ατρεμια.def: ἀτρεμία (ἀτρεμής) a keeping still, ἀτρεμίαν ἔχειν or ἄγειν Xen.

ατρεμιζω.def: ἀτρεμίζω to keep quiet, Theogn., Hdt.; οὐκ ἀτρ. to be restless, id.

ατρεστοσ.def: ἄτρεστος (τρέω) not trembling, unfearing, fearless, Lat. intrepidus, Trag.: c. gen., ἄτρ. μάχας fearless of fight, Aesch.; so, ἄτρ. ἐν μάχαις Soph.; ἄτρ. εὕδειν securely, id.:—also neut. pl. ἄτρεστα as adv., Eur.

ατριβησ.def: ἀτριβής (τρίβω) not rubbed: of places, not traversed, pathless, Thuc.: of roads, not worn or used, Xen.: generally, fresh, new, Lat. integer, id.

ατριπτοσ.def: ἄτριπτος (τρίβω) of hands, not worn by work, Od.; of corn, not threshed, Xen.; ἄτρ. ἄκανθαι thorns on which one cannot tread, or untraversed thorns, Theocr.

ατροποσ.def: ἄτροπος (τρέπω) 1. unchangeable, eternal, Theocr. 2. inflexible, unbending, Anth.:—hence Ἄτροπος, ἡ, name of one of the Μοῖραι or Parcae, Hes.; v. Κλωθώ.

ατροφεω.gloss: to pine away, suffer from atrophy
ατροφεω.def: ἀτροφέω (from ἄτροφος) to pine away, suffer from atrophy, Plut.

ατρυγετοσ.def: ἀτρύγετος (τρυγάω) yielding no harvest, unfruitful, of the sea, Hom.; of the air, id.

ατρυμων.def: ἀτρύμων (= ἄτρυτος) c. gen., ἀτρ. κακῶν not worn out by ills, Aesch.

ατρυτοσ.def: ἄτρυτος (τρύω) 1. not worn away, untiring, unwearied, Aesch.: indefatigable, Plut. 2. of things, unabating, Soph., Mosch.; of a road, wearisome, Theocr.

ατρυτωνη.def: Ἀτρυτώνη the unwearied, a name of Pallas, Hom. (Lengthd. form of ἀτρύτη, as Ἀϊδωνεύς of Ἅιδης.)

ατρωτοσ.def: ἄτρωτος I. unwounded, Aesch., Soph. II. invulnerable, Eur.

αττα.def: ἄττα a salutation used to elders, father, Hom.

ατταγασ.def: ἀτταγᾶς (Deriv. unknown.) a bird, prob. a kind of partridge; or, as others think, the godwit or redshank, Ar.

ατταγην.def: ἀτταγήν a bird, prob. a kind of grouse, attagen Ionicus, Hor.

ατταται.def: ἀτταταῖ a cry of pain or grief, Trag., Ar.

αττελαβοσ.def: ἀττέλαβος (deriv. unkown) a kind of locust without wings, Hdt.

αττησ.def: ἄττης Ἀττης Ὕης, a form of exorcism, used by the priests of Cybele, Dem.

αττικιζω.def: Ἀττικίζω (αττικός) to side with the Athenians, Thuc., Xen.

αττικισμοσ.gloss: a siding with Athens, attachment to her
αττικισμοσ.def: Ἀττικισμός (from Ἀττικίζω) a siding with Athens, attachment to her, Thuc.

αττικιστι.def: Ἀττικιστί (αττικός) in the Attic dialect, Dem.

αττικιων.def: Ἀττικίων (From Ἀττικός) my little Athenian, Ar.

αττικοσ.def: Ἀττικός (ἀκτή) I. Attic, Athenian, Solon, etc.; ἡ Ἀττική (sc. γῆ), Attica, Hdt., etc.; cf. Ἀτθίς. II. Adv. -κῶς in Attic style, Dem.

αττικωνικοσ.def: Ἀττικωνικός a comic alteration of Ἀττικός, after the form of Λακονικός, Ar.

ατυζω.gloss: to be distraught from fear, mazed, bewildered
ατυζω.def: ἀτύζω I. Pass.: to be distraught from fear, mazed, bewildered, Hom.; ἀτυζόμενοι πεδίοιο fleeing bewildered o'er the plain, Il.: also to be distraught with grief, ἀτυζόμενος Soph., Eur.: c. acc., ὄψιν ἀτυχθείς amazed at the sight, Il. II. in late Ep. we find the Act. ἀτύζω, with 3 sing. aor. 1 opt. ἀτύξαι, to strike with terror, Theocr.

ατυραννευτοσ.def: ἀτυράννευτος (τυραννεύω) not ruled by tyrants, Thuc.

ατυφοσ.def: ἄτυφος without pride or arrogance, modest, Plat.

ατυχεω.def: ἀτυχέω (ἀτυχής) 1. to be unlucky or unfortunate, fail, miscarry, Hdt., Thuc., etc. 2. c. gen., to fail of a thing, fail in getting or gaining it, τῆς ἀληθείας Xen.; so, c. part., Thuc. 3. ἀτ. πρός τινα to fail with another, i. e. to fail in one's request, Xen.:—Pass., τὰ ἀτυχηθέντα mischances, failures, Dem.

ατυχια.def: ἀτυχία ill-luck:—a misfortune, miscarriage, mishap, Xen.

αυ.def: αὖ I. again, anew, afresh, once more, Hom., etc.; after numerals, δεύτερον αὖ, τρίτον αὖ, etc., id. II. generally, again, i. e. further, moreover, besides, Lat. porro, Od., attic 2. in turn, on the other hand, following δέ, Il., attic. III. the pleon. phrases, πάλιν αὖ, αὖ πάλιν, ἔμπαλιν αὖ, αὖθις αὖ, αὖθις αὖ πάλιν, are only attic, mostly Trag.
αὖ αὖ αὖ, bow wow, of a dog, Ar.

αυαινω.def: αὐαίνω (αὔω to dry) 1. to dry Od., Hdt., Xen. 2. to dry or parch up, αὐανῶ βίον I shall waste life away, Soph.: Pass., αὐανθείς withered, Aesch.; so in fut. mid., αὐανοῦμαι I shall wither away, Soph.

αυαλεοσ.def: αὐαλέος (αὖος) dry, parched, Hes.; of eyes, dry, sleepless, Anth.

αυγαζω.gloss: to view in the clearest light, see distinctly, discern
αυγαζω.def: αὐγάζω (αὐγή) I. to view in the clearest light, see distinctly, discern, Soph.; so in Mid., Il., Hes. II. of the sun, to beam upon, illumine, τινά Eur.

αυγη.gloss: the light of the sun, sunlight
αυγη.def: αὐγή 1. the light of the sun, sunlight, and in pl. his rays or beams, Hom.; ὑπ’ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο, i.e. still alive, Od.; so, αὐγὰς ἐσιδεῖν, λεύσσειν, βλέπειν Theogn., Aesch., Eur.; but, ὑπ’ αὐγὰς λεύσσειν or ἰδεῖν τι to hold up to the light and look at, id.; κλύζειν πρὸς αὐγάς to rise surging towards the sun, Aesch.:—metaph., βίου δύντος αὐγαί "life's setting sun, " id.:— αὐγή the dawn, day-break, NTest. 2. generally, any bright light, as of fire, Hom.; of lightning, Il.; of the eyes, Soph.; hence αὐγαί, like Lat. lumina, the eyes, Eur. 3. any gleam on the surface of bright objects, sheen, αὐγὴ χαλκείη Il.; αὐγὰ πέπλου Eur.

αυδαζομαι.def: αὐδάζομαι (αὐδή) to cry out, speak, Hdt.: an aor1 act. αὔδαξα occurs in Anth.

αυδαω.def: αὐδάω (αὐδή) I. c. acc. rei, 1. to utter sounds, speak, Il., Eur. 2. c. acc. rei, to speak or say something, Il., Soph.: so as Dep., id.:—Pass., ηὐδᾶτο γὰρ ταῦτα so 'twas said, id. 3. of oracles, to utter, proclaim, tell of, id.; to speak out concerning a thing, Aesch. II. c. acc. pers., 1. to speak to, address, accost, Hom.: to invoke a god, Eur. 2. c. acc. et inf. to tell, bid, order one to do, Soph.; αὐδ. τινα μὴ ποιεῖν to forbid one to do, Aesch.; αὐδῶ σιωπᾶν Soph.: so as Dep., id. 3. to call by name, call so and so, Eur.: Pass., αὐδῶμαι παῖς Ἀχιλλέως Soph.; κάκιστ’ αὐδώμενος most ill reported of, Aesch. 4. like λέγειν, to mean such an one, Eur.

αυδη.def: αὐδή I. the human voice, speech, opp. to ὀμφή (a divine voice), Il. 2. the sound or twang of the bowstring, Od.; of a trumpet, Eur.; of the τέττιξ, Hes. II. = φήμη, a report, account, Soph., Eur. 2. an oracle, id.

αυδηεισ.def: αὐδήεις (αὐδή) speaking with human voice, Od.; when θεὸς αὐδήεσσα is applied to Calypso and Circe, it means a goddess who used the speech of mortals, id.

αυερυω.def: αὐερύω to draw back or backwards, Il.; to draw the bow, id.: absol., in a sacrifice, to draw the victim's head back, so as to cut its throat, id. (It can hardly be a compd. of αὖ ἐρύω, for αὖ is never elsewh. used in the local sense of back: perh. for ἀνερύω, i. e. ἀνϝερύω.)

αυθαδεια.def: αὐθάδεια (From αὐθάδης) self-will, wilfulness, stubbornness, contumacy, presumption, Aesch., etc.

αυθαδησ.gloss: self-willed, wilful, dogged, stubborn, contumacious, presumptuous
αυθαδησ.def: αὐθάδης (ἥδομαι) self-willed, wilful, dogged, stubborn, contumacious, presumptuous, Hdt., etc.:— metaph. of things, remorseless, unfeeling, Aesch.:— adv. -δως, Ar.; comp. -έστερον, Plat.

αυθαδιζομαι.def: αὐθαδίζομαι (From αὐθάδης) Dep. to be self-willed, Plat.

αυθαδισμα.def: αὐθάδισμα (From αὐθαδίζομαι) an act of self-will, wilfulness, Aesch.

αυθαιμων.gloss: of the same blood, a brother, sister, kinsman
αυθαιμων.def: αὐθαίμων (αἷμα) of the same blood, a brother, sister, kinsman, Soph.; so αὔθαιμος, ον, id.

αυθαιρετοσ.def: αὐθαίρετος I. self-chosen, self-elected, Xen. II. by free choice, of oneself, Eur.: independent, Thuc. III. of things taken upon oneself, self-incurred, voluntary, Soph., Thuc., etc.

αυθεκαστοσ.gloss: one who calls each thing by its name
αυθεκαστοσ.def: αὐθέκαστος one who calls each thing by its name, Arist.

αυθεντεω.def: αὐθεντέω to have full power over, τινός NTest.

αυθεντησ.def: αὐθέντης (The part -έντης is of uncertain deriv.) (contr. for αὐθοέντης) I. one who does anything with his own hand, an actual murderer, Hdt., Eur., etc.:—more loosely, one of a murderer's family, id. 2. an absolute master, autocrat, id. II. as adj., αὐθέντης φόνος, αὐθένται θάνατοι murder by one of the same family, Aesch.

αυθημεροσ.def: αὐθήμερος (ἡμέρα) I. made or done on the very day, Aeschin. II. adv. αὐθημερόν (oxyt.), on the very day, on the same day, immediately, Aesch., etc.; ionic αὐτημερόν, Hdt.

αυθι.def: αὖθι 1. on the spot, here, there, Hom.; αὖθι ἔχειν to keep him there, as he is, Od. 2. of Time, forthwith, straightway, Il.

αυθιγενησ.gloss: born on the spot, born in the country, native
αυθιγενησ.def: αὐθιγενής (γίγνομαι) born on the spot, born in the country, native, Lat. indigena, Hdt.; αὐτ. ποταμοί rivers that rise in the country, id.; ὕδωρ αὐτ. a natural spring, id.:— genuine, sincere, Eur.

αυθισ.def: αὖθις a lengthd. form of αὖ: I. of place back, back again, Il.; ἂψ αὖτις id.; this sense rare in attic II. of Time, again, afresh, anew, Hom., attic; strengthd., ὕστερον αὖτις, ἔτ’ αὖτις, πάλιν αὖτις Il., etc.; βοᾶν αὖθις to cry encore! Xen. 2. of future Time, again, hereafter, Il., Aesch. III. of Sequence, moreover, in turn, on the other hand, id., Soph.

αυιαχοσ.def: αὐίαχος (i. e. ἀϝίαχος) epith. of the Trojans in Il., either 1. （α copul., ἰαχή) loud-shouting, noisy, or, 2. (from α privat.) noiseless, silent.

αυλαξ.def: αὖλαξ 1. a furrow made in ploughing, Lat. sulcus, Hom., etc.; αὔλακ’ ἐλαύνειν to draw a furrow, Hes. 2. metaph. of a wife as the bearer of children, Soph., Eur. 3. metaph. also, a furrow in the skin, a gash, wound, Aesch., Eur. 4. = ὄγμος, a swathe, Theocr. (Prob. from same Root as ὁλκός, Lat. sulcus, from ἕλκω.）

αυλειοσ.def: αὔλειος of or belonging to the αὐλή or court, ἐπ’ αὐλείηισι θύρηισι at the door of the court, i. e. the outer door, house- door, Od.; so in Hdt. and attic

αυλεω.def: αὐλέω (αὐλός) I. to play on the flute, Hdt., Plat., etc.; αὐλ. ἔξοδον to play a finale, Ar. II. Pass., of tunes, to be played on the flute, Xen.; but, αὐλεῖται μέλαθρον is filled with music, Eur. 2. in Pass. also of persons, to be played to, hear music, Xen.

αυλη.def: αὐλή (prob. from ἄημι (ἄϝημι) to blow, for the αὐλή was open to the air) I. in Hom. the court-yard, surrounded with out-buildings, and having the altar of Ζεὺς Ἑρκεῖος in the middle, so that it was at once the meeting-place of the family, and the cattle-yard, Il.: it had two doors, viz. the house-door (cf. αὔλειος), and another leading through the αἴθουσα into the πρόδομος, Od. 2. the wall of the court-yard, Il. II. after Hom., the αὐλή was the court or quadrangle, round which the house itself was built, having a corridor (περιστύλιον), from which were doors leading into the men's apartments; opposite the house-door (cf. αὔλειος) was the μέσαυλος or μέταυλος (q.v.), leading into the women's part of the house, Hdt., attic III. generally, any court or hall, Hom., Trag.

αυλημα.gloss: a piece of music for the flute
αυλημα.def: αὔλημα (αὐλέω) a piece of music for the flute, Ar., Plat.

αυλητησ.def: αὐλητής (αὐλέω) a flute-player, Lat. tibicen, Theogn., Hdt., etc.

αυλητικοσ.def: αὐλητικός (αὐλέω) (From αὐλητής) of or for the flute, Plat.; ἡ -κή (sc. τέχνη) flute-playing, id.

αυλητρισ.def: αὐλητρίς (αὐλέω) a flute-girl, Lat. tibicina, Ar., Xen., etc.

αυλιαδεσ.def: Αὐλιάδες (αὐλή) Αὐλιάδες Νύμφαι Nymphs protecting cattlefolds, Anth.

αυλιζομαι.def: αὐλίζομαι (αὐλή) to lie in the court-yard, of cattle, Od.; to pass the night, lodge, Eur.; of soldiers, to bivouac, Hdt.

αυλιον.def: αὔλιον (αὐλή) I. a country house, cottage, Hhymn.: a fold, stable, Eur., Xen. II. a chamber, cave, grotto, Soph.

αυλιοσ.def: αὔλιος (αὐλή) of or for farm-yards, rustic, Eur.

αυλισ.gloss: a place for passing the night in, a tent, roosting-place
αυλισ.def: αὖλις (αὐλή) a place for passing the night in, a tent, roosting-place, Hom., Eur.

αυλισκοσ.def: αὐλίσκος Dim. of αὐλός, a small reed, pipe, Theogn.

αυλοθετεω.def: αὐλοθετέω (τίθημι) to make flutes or pipes, Anth.

αυλοποιικη.def: αὐλοποιική (From αὐλοποιός) sc. τέχνη, flute-making, Plat.

αυλοσ.def: αὐλός (ἄημι to blow) 1. a flute or rather clarionet (for it was played by a mouthpiece, γλωσσίς, Aeschin.), Il., etc.; αὐλοὶ ἀνδρήϊοι and γυναικήϊοι, Lat. tibiae dextrae and sinistrae, bass and treble, Hdt.; sometimes one person played two αὐλοί at once, Theocr.; αὐλὸς Ἐνυαλίου, i. e. a trumpet, Anth.:— ὑπ’ αὐλοῦ to the sound of the flute, Hdt.; so, πρὸς αὐλόν, ὑπὸ τὸν αὐλόν Xen. 2. any tube or pipe, as the socket of a spear-head, the groove into which the tongue of a buckle fitted, Hom.; the pipe of bellows, Thuc.:— αὐλὸς παχύς, in Od., seems to mean a jet of blood through the tube of the nostril.

αυλων.def: αὐλών (αὐλός) 1. a hollow way, defile, glen, Hhymn., Hdt., Ar. 2. a canal, aqueduct, trench, Hdt. 3. a channel, strait, Aesch.; αὐλῶνες πόντιοι the sea straits, i. e. the Archipelago, Soph.

αυλωπισ.def: αὐλῶπις (ὤψ) of a helmet, with a tube in front, to hold the λόφος, Il.

αυξανω.def: αὐξάνω (poet. ἀέξω q. v.) I. to make large, increase, augment, Hdt., etc. (Hom. only uses ἀέξω). 2. to increase in power, strengthen, exalt, aggrandise, Hdt., attic: also to promote to honour, glorify, magnify, Trag., Plat. II. Pass. to grow, wax, increase, Hes., Hdt., etc.; αὐξ. ἐς πλῆθος, ἐς ὕψος id.; of a child, to grow up, id.; ηὐξανόμην I grew taller, Ar.; so with an adj., αὐξάνεσθαι μέγας to wax great, Eur. Hence

αυξησια.def: Αὐξησία (αὔξω) the Goddess of growth, Hdt.

αυξησισ.def: αὔξησις (αὔξω) growth, increase, Thuc.; of crops, Hdt.

αυοσ.def: αὖος (αὔω) 1. dry, of timber, Od.: dried, of fruit, Hdt.: withered, of leaves, Ar.:—neut. as adv., αὖον ἀϋτεῖν or αὔειν to ring dry and harsh, of metal, Il. 2. dried up, exhausted, Theocr.

αυπνοσ.def: ἄυπνος 1. sleepless, wakeful, of persons, Od., attic: metaph. sleepless, never-resting, πηδάλια Aesch.; κρῆναι Soph. 2. of sleepless nights, Hom. 3. ὕπνος ἄϋπνος a sleep that is no sleep, from which one easily awakes, Soph.

αυρα.def: αὔρα (ἄημι) 1. air in motion, a breeze, esp. a cool breeze, the fresh air of morning, Lat. aura, Od., Hdt., attic Poets; rare in Prose:—metaph. steam, Ar. 2. metaph. also, of changeful events, Eur., Ar.; of anything thrilling, Eur.

αυριον.def: αὔριον (akin to ἠώς) I. to-morrow, Lat. cras, Hom., etc.; ἐς αὔριον on the morrow or till morning, id. II. as Subst., the morrow, Il.; in attic, ἡ αὔριον (sc. ἡμέρα) the morrow, Eur.; ἡ αὔρ. ἡμέρα Xen.; ἡ ἐς αὔρ. ἡμέρα Soph.; ὁ αὔριον χρόνος Eur.

αυσταλεοσ.def: αὐσταλέος (αὔω to dry) sunburnt, squalid, Lat. siccus, Od., Hes.

αυστηροσ.gloss: making the tongue dry and rough, harsh, rough, bitter
αυστηροσ.def: αὐστηρός (αὔω to dry) making the tongue dry and rough, harsh, rough, bitter, Plat.:—metaph. austere, harsh, id., NTest.

αυστηροτησ.def: αὐστηρότης (From αὐστηρός) harshness, roughness, οἴνου Xen.: metaph. austerity, harshness, Plat.

αυταγγελοσ.gloss: carrying one's own message, bringing news of what oneself has seen
αυταγγελοσ.def: αὐτάγγελος carrying one's own message, bringing news of what oneself has seen, Soph., Thuc.; c. gen. rei, λόγων αὐτ. Soph.

αυταγρετοσ.def: αὐτάγρετος (ἀγρέω) self-chosen, left to one's choice, Od., Hhymn.

αυταδελφοσ.def: αὐτάδελφος I. related as brother or sister, Aesch., Soph. II. as Subst. one's own brother or sister, id.

αυτανδροσ.gloss: together with the men, men and all
αυτανδροσ.def: αὔτανδρος (ἀνήρ) together with the men, men and all, Polyb.

αυτανεψιοσ.def: αὐτανέψιος an own cousin, cousin-german, Aesch., Eur.

αυταρκεια.def: αὐτάρκεια (From αὐτάρκης) sufficiency in oneself, independence, Plat.

αυταρκησ.gloss: sufficient in oneself, having enough, independent
αυταρκησ.def: αὐτάρκης (ἀρκέω) sufficient in oneself, having enough, independent of others, Hdt., Plat.; νηδὺς αὐτάρκης acting of itself, Aesch.; χώρα αὐτ. a country that supplies itself, independent of imports, Thuc.; αὐτ. πρός τι strong enough for a thing, id., Xen.; c. inf. able of oneself to do a thing, Dem.; αὐτ. βοή a sufficient, vigorous shout, Soph.

αυτε.def: αὖτε (αὖ, τε, — ωηερε τε is otiose, as in ὅστε) I. again, Il. II. to mark Sequence, again, furthermore, next, id., Soph. 2. on the other hand, on the contrary, following μέν like δέ, Hom., attic Poets.

αυτεξουσιοσ.def: αὐτεξούσιος (ἐξουσία) in one's own power; τὸ αὐτεξούσιον free power, Babr.

αυτεπαγγελτοσ.gloss: offering of oneself, of free will
αυτεπαγγελτοσ.def: αὐτεπάγγελτος (ἐπαγγέλλω) offering of oneself, of free will, Hdt., Eur., Thuc., etc.

αυτεπωνυμοσ.def: αὐτεπώνυμος of the same surname with, τινος Eur.

αυτερετησ.def: αὐτερέτης one who rows himself, i. e. rower and soldier at once, Thuc.

αυτεω.def: ἀυτέω (αὔω to cry) (From ἀύτη) 1. to cry, shout, Il., Aesch.:—c. acc. cogn., βοὰν ἀϋτῶ Eur.; ἀϋτεῖ δ’ ὀξύ Aesch. 2. c. acc. pers. to call to, Il., Eur.:—c. acc. pers. et inf., Eur.

αυτη.def: ἀυτή (αὔω to cry) a cry, shout, esp. battle-shout, war-cry, Hom.: generally a sound, Aesch.

αυτηκοοσ.gloss: one who has himself heard, an ear-witness
αυτηκοοσ.def: αὐτήκοος (ἀκούω) one who has himself heard, an ear-witness, Thuc., Plat.

αυτημαρ.def: αὐτῆμαρ = αὐθημερόν, on the self-same day, Il.

αυτικα.def: αὐτίκα (αὐτός) I. forthwith, straightway, at once, Hom., etc.; which notion is strengthened in αὐτίκα νῦν, μάλ’ αὐτίκα Od.; c. partic., αὐτίκ’ ἰόντι immediately on his going, id.; so, αὐτίκα γενόμενος as soon as born, Hdt.; αὐτίκα καὶ μετέπειτα now and hereafter, Od.; so, τὸ αὐτίκα and τὸ μέλλον, Thuc.:—with a Subst., τὴν αὐτίχ’ ἡμέραν Soph.; ὁ αὐτίκα φόβος momentary fear, Thuc. 2. also in a slightly future sense, presently, Lat. mox, Soph., etc. II. for example, to begin with, Ar., Plat., etc.; αὐτίκα δὴ μάλα Dem.

αυτμη.def: ἀυτμή (ἄημι) 1. breath, Il.; ἀϋτμὴ Ἡφαίστοιο the fiery breath of Hephaestus, id.; πυρὸς ἀϋτμή Od.; of bellows, Il.; of wind, Od. 2. odour, scent, fragrance, Hom.

αυτοανθρωποσ.gloss: the ideal man, the form of man
αυτοανθρωποσ.def: αὐτοάνθρωπος the ideal man, the form of man, Arist.

αυτοβοει.gloss: by a mere shout, at the first shout
αυτοβοει.def: αὐτοβοεί (βοή) by a mere shout, at the first shout, αὐτ. ἑλεῖν to take without a blow, Thuc.

αυτογεννητοσ.def: αὐτογέννητος self-produced: αὐτογέννητα κοιμήματα μητρός a mother's intercourse with her own child, Soph.

αυτογνωμονεω.gloss: to act of one's own judgment
αυτογνωμονεω.def: αὐτογνωμονέω (From αὐτογνώμων) to act of one's own judgment, Xen. From

αυτογνωμων.gloss: on one's own judgment, at one's own discretion
αυτογνωμων.def: αὐτογνώμων on one's own judgment, at one's own discretion, Arist.: adv. -όνως, Plut.

αυτογυοσ.gloss: having the share-beam of one piece with the pole
αυτογυοσ.def: αὐτόγυος (γύης) of a plough, having the share-beam of one piece with the pole, Hes.

αυτοδαικτοσ.def: αὐτοδάικτος (δαίζω) self-slain or mutually slain, Aesch.

αυτοδαξ.def: αὐτοδάξ with the very teeth, ὁ αὐτοδὰξ τρόπος your ferocious temper, Ar.

αυτοδικοσ.gloss: with independent jurisdiction, with one's own law-courts
αυτοδικοσ.def: αὐτόδικος (δίκη) with independent jurisdiction, with one's own law-courts, Thuc.

αυτοδιον.def: αὐτόδιον (It seems to be lengthd. from αὐτός, as μαψίδιος from μάψ, μινυνθάδιος from μίνυνθα.) straightway, Od.

αυτοεκαστοσ.def: αὐτοέκαστος το αὐτ. the ideal or form of each object, Arist.

αυτοετει.def: αὐτοετεί (From αὐτοετής) in the same year, Theocr.

αυτοετησ.def: αὐτοετής (ἔτος) in or of the same year: adv. αὐτόετες, in the same year, within the year, Od.

αυτοθελησ.def: αὐτοθελής (θέλω) of one's own will, Anth.

αυτοθεν.def: αὐτόθεν (αὐτοῦ) I. of Place, from the very spot, Lat. illinc, Hom., attic; αὐτ. ἐξ ἕδρης straight from his seat, without rising, Il.; αὐτ. ἐκ Σαλαμῖνος Hdt., etc.; αὐτόθεν from where thou standest, Soph.; αὐτ. βιοτεύειν to find a living from the place, Thuc.:— οἱ αὐτ. the natives, id. II. of Time, on the spot, at once, Lat. illico, Il., Hdt., attic

αυτοθι.def: αὐτόθι Adv. for αὐτοῦ, on the spot, Il., Hdt., attic

αυτοκαβδαλοσ.def: αὐτοκάβδαλος (Deriv. unknown.) wrought or done carelessly, slovenly, random, Arist.:—adv. -λως, id.

αυτοκασιγνητη.def: αὐτοκασιγνήτη an own sister, Od., Eur.

αυτοκασιγνητοσ.def: αὐτοκασίγνητος an own brother, Il., etc.

αυτοκελευθοσ.def: αὐτοκέλευθος going one's own road, Anth.

αυτοκελευστοσ.def: αὐτοκέλευστος self-bidden, i. e. unbidden, of one's own accord, Xen., Anth.

αυτοκλητοσ.def: αὐτόκλητος self-called, i. e. uncalled, unbidden, Aesch., Soph.

αυτοκομοσ.def: αὐτόκομος (κόμη) I. with natural hair, shaggy, Ar. II. hair or leaves and all, Luc.

αυτοκρατησ.def: αὐτοκρατής (κρατέω) ruling by oneself, absolute, autocratic, Eur., Plat.
