αυτοκρατορικοσ.def: αὐτοκρατορικός (From αὐτοκράτωρ) of or for an autocrat: adv. -κῶς, despotically, Plut.

αυτοκρατωρ.def: αὐτοκράτωρ (κρατέω) I. one's own master: 1. of persons or states, free and independent, Lat. sui juris, Thuc., Xen. 2. of ambassadors, possessing full powers, plenipotentiary, Ar., Thuc., etc. 3. of rulers, absolute, arbitrary, despotic, id., etc. 4. of reasoning, peremptory, id. II. c. gen. complete master of, ἑαυτοῦ id.; τῆς ἐπιορκίας αὐτ. at liberty to swear falsely, Dem.

αυτοκτιτοσ.def: αὐτόκτιτος (κτίζω) self-produced, i. e. natural, ἄντρα Aesch.

αυτοκτονεω.def: αὐτοκτονέω (From αὐτοκτόνος) to slay one another, Soph.

αυτοκτονοσ.def: αὐτοκτόνος (κτείνω) 1. self-slaying; Adv. -νως, with one's own hand, Aesch.:—so χεὶρ αὐτ., of Medea, who slew her own children, Eur. 2. slaying one another, Aesch.; θάνατος αὐτ. death by each other's hand, id.

αυτοκυβερνητησ.def: αὐτοκυβερνήτης one who steers himself, Anth.

αυτοκωποσ.gloss: together with the hilt, up to the hilt
αυτοκωποσ.def: αὐτόκωπος (κώπη) together with the hilt, up to the hilt, Aesch.

αυτοληκυθοσ.gloss: one who carries his own oil-flask, a shabby fellow
αυτοληκυθοσ.def: αὐτολήκυθος one who carries his own oil-flask, a shabby fellow, Dem.

αυτομαθησ.gloss: having learnt of oneself, self- taught
αυτομαθησ.def: αὐτομαθής (μαθεῖν) having learnt of oneself, self- taught, Anth.

αυτομαρτυσ.def: αὐτόμαρτυς oneself the witness, an eyewitness, Aesch.

αυτοματιζω.gloss: to act of oneself, act unadvisedly
αυτοματιζω.def: αὐτοματίζω (From αὐτόματος) to act of oneself, act unadvisedly, Xen.

αυτοματοσ.gloss: acting of one's own will, of oneself
αυτοματοσ.def: αὐτόματος 1. of persons, acting of one's own will, of oneself, Il., etc. 2. of things, self-moving, self-acting, spontaneous, of the gates of Olympus, the tripods of Hephaestus, Il.:—of plants, growing of themselves, Hdt. 3. without apparent cause, accidental, id.; αὐτ. θάνατος a natural death, Dem. II. αὐτόματον, ου, τό, mere chance, ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐτομάτου or ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, Lat. sponte, by chance, naturally, Hdt., Thuc. III. adv. -τως ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, Hdt.

αυτομεδων.def: Αὐτομέδων self-ruler, name of Achilles' charioteer, Il.

αυτομολεω.def: αὐτομολέω (From αὐτόμολος) to desert, Hdt., attic; αὐτ. πρὸς τοὺς Πέρσας Hdt.; ἐς Ἀθήνας ἐκ Περσέων id.

αυτομολοσ.def: αὐτόμολος (μολεῖν) going of oneself, without bidding: as Subst. a deserter, Hdt., attic

αυτονομεομαι.gloss: to live by one's own laws, be independent
αυτονομεομαι.def: αὐτονομέομαι Dep. to live by one's own laws, be independent, Thuc., Dem.

αυτονομια.gloss: freedom to use one's own laws, independence
αυτονομια.def: αὐτονομία freedom to use one's own laws, independence, Thuc., etc.

αυτονομοσ.gloss: living under one's own laws, independent
αυτονομοσ.def: αὐτόνομος (νέμομαι) 1. living under one's own laws, independent, Hdt., attic 2. generally, of one's own free will, Soph. 3. of animals, feeding and ranging at will, Anth.

αυτοπαθεια.def: αὐτοπάθεια (From αὐτοπαθής) one's own feeling or experience, Polyb.

αυτοπαθησ.def: αὐτοπαθής speaking from one's own feeling or experience:— adv. -θως, Polyb.

αυτοπημων.def: αὐτοπήμων (πῆμα) for one's own woes, Aesch.

αυτοποιοσ.def: αὐτόποιος (ποιέω) self-produced, as the Athenian olive, Soph.

αυτοπολισ.def: αὐτόπολις free as a state, independent, Thuc.

αυτοπολιτησ.def: αὐτοπολίτης citizen of a free state, Xen.

αυτοπουσ.def: αὐτόπους on one's own feet, Luc.

αυτοπρεμνοσ.gloss: together with the root, root and branch
αυτοπρεμνοσ.def: αὐτόπρεμνος (πρέμνον) together with the root, root and branch, Soph., Ar.; αὐτ. τι διδόναι to give in absolute possession, Aesch.

αυτοπροσωποσ.gloss: in one's own person, without a mask
αυτοπροσωποσ.def: αὐτοπρόσωπος (πρόσωπον) in one's own person, without a mask, Luc.

αυτοπτησ.def: αὐτόπτης (ὄψομαι, fut. of ὁράω) seeing oneself, an eyewitness, Hdt.

αυτοπωλησ.def: αὐτοπώλης (πωλέω) selling one's own goods or products, Plat.

αυτοπωλικοσ.def: αὐτοπωλικός (From αὐτοπώλης) = αὐτοπώλης: ἡ -κη (sc. τέχνη), the trade of an αὐτοπώλης, Plat.

αυτορριζοσ.def: αὐτόρριζος (ῥίζα) I. roots and all; poet. αὐτόριζος, Babr. II. self-rooted, self-founded, Eur.

αυτοσ.def: αὐτός self, Lat. ipse:— in the oblique cases simply for the personal Pron., him, her, it:— with the Artic. ὁ αὐτός, ἡ αὐτή, τὸ αὐτό (or ταὐτόν), etc., the very one, the same. I. self, myself, thyself, etc., acc. to the person of the Verb., Hom., etc.: 1. oneself, one's true self, the soul, not the body, Od.; or opp. to others, as king to subjects, parent to children, man to wife, etc., Hom.; hence absol. for the master, τίς οὗτος;—Αὐτός, i. e. Socrates, Ar.; similarly in neut. αὐτὸ δείξει the result will shew, Eur. 2. of oneself, of one's own accord, Lat. sponte, Hom., Soph. 3. by oneself, alone, αὐτός περ ἐών although alone, Il.; αὐτοί ἐσμεν we are by ourselves, i. e. among friends, Ar. 4. in Plat., τὸ δίκαιον αὐτό right in itself, the idea of right, etc.; cf. αὐτοάνθρωπος. 5. in dat. with Subst., together with, ἀνόρουσεν αὐτῆι σὺν φόρμιγγι he sprang up lyre in hand, Il.; αὐτῆι σὺν πήληκι helmet and all, id.; and without σύν, αὐτοῖς ἀνδράσι men and all, Hdt., etc. 6. added to ordinal Numbers, e. g. πέμπτος αὐτός himself the fifth, i.e. himself with four others, Thuc. 7. in connexion with the person. Pron., ἐγὼ αὐτός, ἐμέθεν αὐτῆς, σὲ αὐτόν, etc., Hom.; in Hdt. and attic it coalesces with oblique cases of Pron., ἐμαυτοῦ, σε-αυτοῦ, ἑ-αυτοῦ:— it is joined with these reflexive Pronouns to add force, αὐτὸς καθ’ αὑτοῦ, αὐτοὶ ὑφ’ αὑτῶν Aesch., etc. 8. gen. αὐτοῦ is used with the possessive Pron., πατρὸς κλέος ἠδ’ ἐμὸν αὐτοῦ Il. 9. αὐτὸς ἑαυτοῦ is also used with comp. and Sup. adj. to express something unusual, αὐτὸς ἑωυτοῦ πολλῶι ὑποδεέστερος Hdt. II. he, she, it, for the simple Pron. of 3 person, only in oblique cases, and never at the beginning of a sentence, Hom., attic: cf. ἑαυτοῦ. III. with Article ὁ αὐτός, ἡ αὐτή, τὸ αὐτό, and attic contr. αὑτός, αὑτή, ταὐτό and ταὐτόν, gen. ταὐτοῦ, dat. ταὐτῶι, pl. neut. ταὐτά: ionic ὡὐτός, τὠυτό:— the very one, the same, Lat. idem, Hom., Hdt., attic:—it freq. takes a dat., like ὅμοιος, to denote sameness, τὠυτὸ ἂν ὑμῖν ἐπρήσσομεν we should fare the same as you, Hdt.; also, ὁ αὐτὸς καί, cf. Lat. simul ac, id. IV. αὐτο- in Compos.: 1. of itself, i. e. natural, native, not made, as in αὐτόκτιτος. 2. of mere.., of nothing but.., as in αὐτόξυλος. 3. of oneself, self-, as in αὐτοδίδακτος, αὐτόματος: and so independently, as in αὐτόνομος. 4. just, exactly, as in αὐτόδεκα. 5. with reflex. sense of αὑτοῦ and ἀλλήλων, as αὐθέντης, αὐτοκτονέω. 6. together with, as in αὐτόπρεμνος, αὐτόρριζος.

αυτοσε.def: αὐτόσε (αὐτοῦ) thither, to the very place, Lat. illuc, Hdt., Thuc.

αυτοσιδηροσ.gloss: of sheer iron, with stroke of sword
αυτοσιδηροσ.def: αὐτοσίδηρος of sheer iron, with stroke of sword, Eur.

αυτοσταδιη.def: αὐτοσταδίη (ἵσταμαι) a stand-up fight, close fight, ἔν γ’ αὐτοσταδίηι Il.

αυτοστολοσ.def: αὐτόστολος (στέλλω) self-sent, going or acting of oneself, Soph., Anth.

αυτοστονοσ.def: αὐτόστονος (στένω) lamenting by or for oneself, Aesch.

αυτοσφαγησ.def: αὐτοσφαγής (σφάζω) slain by oneself or by kinsmen, Soph., Eur.

αυτοσχεδιαζω.def: αὐτοσχεδιάζω (From αὐτοσχέδιος) I. to act or speak off-hand, Xen. 2. c. acc. to devise off-hand, extemporise, Thuc., Xen. II. in bad sense, to act, speak, or think unadvisedly, try rash experiments, Plat.

αυτοσχεδιαστησ.def: αὐτοσχεδιαστής (From αὐτοσχέδιος) one who acts or speaks offhand: a raw hand, bungler, Lat. tiro, Xen.

αυτοσχεδιοσ.def: αὐτοσχέδιος I. hand to hand, αὐτοσχεδίηι (sc. μάχηι) in close fight, in the fray, Il.: αὐτοσχεδίην as adv., = αὐτοσχεδόν, Hom. II. off-hand, of an improvisatore, Hhymn.

αυτοσχεδον.gloss: near at hand, hand to hand
αυτοσχεδον.def: αὐτοσχεδόν near at hand, hand to hand, Lat. cominus, of close fight, Hom.

αυτοτελησ.gloss: ending in itself, complete in itself, supporting oneself
αυτοτελησ.def: αὐτοτελής (τέλος) I. ending in itself, complete in itself, supporting oneself, ἱππεῖς Luc. II. （τέλος IV) taxing oneself, self-taxed, Thuc.

αυτοτροπησασ.def: αὐτοτροπήσας (as if from αὐτοτροπάω) to turn straightway, Hhymn.

αυτου.gloss: at the very place, just here, just there
αυτου.def: αὐτοῦ properly gen. of αὐτός, at the very place, just here, just there, Lat. illico, Hom., Hdt., attic; with the place added, αὐτοῦ ἐνὶ Τροίηι Il.; αὐτοῦ τῶιδ’ ἐνὶ χώρωι Od.; αὐτοῦ ταύτηι exactly here, Hdt., etc.

αυτουργεω.gloss: to work with one's own hand
αυτουργεω.def: αὐτουργέω (αὐτουργός) to work with one's own hand, Luc.

αυτουργητοσ.def: αὐτούργητος (From αὐτούργέω) self-wrought, rudely wrought, Anth.

αυτουργια.def: αὐτουργία (From αὐτουργός) I. a working on oneself, i. e. self-murder or the murder of one's own kin, Aesch. II. personal labour, opp. to slave-labour, Plut.

αυτουργοσ.def: αὐτουργός (⁎ἔργω) I. self-working, Soph. 2. as Subst., one who works his land himself (not by slaves), a husbandman, poor farmer, Eur.; of the Peloponnesians, Thuc.:—metaph., αὐτουργὸς τῆς φιλοσοφίας one that has worked at philosophy by himself, without a teacher, Xen. II. pass. self-wrought, simple, native, Anth.

αυτοφι.def: αὐτόφι epic gen. and dat. sg. and pl. of αὐτός Hom.; ἀπ. αὐτόφιν, παρ’ αὐτόφιν or -φι, from the very spot, Il.; ἐπ’ αὐτόφιν on the spot, id.

αυτοφλοιοσ.def: αὐτόφλοιος with the bark on, Theocr.

αυτοφονοσ.gloss: self-murdering, murdering those of one's own family
αυτοφονοσ.def: αὐτοφόνος (⁎φένω) self-murdering, murdering those of one's own family, Aesch.

αυτοφορτοσ.def: αὐτόφορτος I. bearing one's own baggage, Aesch. II. cargo and all, ναῦς Plut.

αυτοφυησ.def: αὐτοφυής (φύομαι) 1. self-grown, Plat.:— of home growth, Xen. 2. natural, opp. to artificial, Hes., Thuc.; κορύνα αὐτοφυής rough as it came from the tree, Theocr. 3. τὸ αὐτοφυές, one's own nature, Plat.

αυτοφυτοσ.def: αὐτόφυτος 1. self-caused, ἕλκεα Pind. 2. natural, αὐτ. ἐργασία, αὐτουργία, i. e. agriculture, Arist.

αυτοφωνοσ.def: αὐτόφωνος (φωνή) self-sounding, χρησμὸς αὐτ. an oracle delivered by the god himself, Luc.

αυτοφωροσ.gloss: self-detected, caught in the act of theft
αυτοφωροσ.def: αὐτόφωρος (φώρ) self-detected, caught in the act of theft, Soph.; ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι λαμβάνειν to catch in the act, Eur., Dem.; ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι ἁλῶναι Hdt.: in a more general sense, ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι καταλαμβάνειν τινα ἀμαθέστερον ὄντα to detect him point blank of ignorance, Plat.; ἐπ’ αὐτ. εἴλημμαι πλουσιώτατος ὤν Xen.

αυτοχειρ.def: αὐτόχειρ I. with one's own hand, Aesch., Soph., etc.: c. gen. the very doer or author of a thing, id., Dem. II. absol., like αὐθέντης, one who kills himself or one of his kin, Soph.: then, simply, a murderer, homicide, id., Dem.; in full, τὸν αὐτ. τοῦ φόνου the perpetrator of.., Soph. III. as adj. murderous, Eur.; πληγέντες αὐτόχειρι μιάσματι of brothers smitten by mutual slaughter, Soph.

αυτοχειρια.gloss: murder perpetrated by one's own hand
αυτοχειρια.def: αὐτοχειρία (From αὐτόχειρ) murder perpetrated by one's own hand, Plat.: dat. αὐτοχειρίαι, ionic -ίηι, with one's own hand, αὐτ. κτείνειν Hdt., etc.

αυτοχθων.def: αὐτόχθων I. sprung from the land itself, Lat. terrigena: αὐτόχθονες, οἱ, like Lat. Indigenae, aborigines, natives, Hdt., Thuc.; of the Athenians, Eur., Ar., etc. II. as adj. indigenous, Hdt.

αυτοχοωνοσ.def: αὐτοχόωνος (χόανος) (epic for αὐτοχόανος, αὐτόχωνος) rudely cast, massive, of a lump of iron used as a quoit, Il.

αυτοχρημα.gloss: in very deed, really and truly
αυτοχρημα.def: αὐτόχρημα I. in very deed, really and truly, Ar. II. just, exactly, Luc.

αυτοψια.gloss: a seeing with one's own eyes
αυτοψια.def: αὐτοψία (ὄψομαι, fut. of ὁράω) a seeing with one's own eyes, Luc.

αυτωσ.gloss: in this very manner, even so, just so, as it is
αυτωσ.def: αὔτως (Adv. of αὐτός) I. in this very manner, even so, just so, as it is, γυμνὸν ἐόντα, αὔτως—ὥστε γυναῖκα, unarmed just as I am— like a woman, Il. 2. in a contemptuous sense, just so, no better, τί σὺ κήδεαι αὔτως ἀνδρῶν; why take you no better care? id.; νήπιος αὔτως a mere child, id.; αὔτως ἄχθος ἀρούρης Od. II. in reference to the past, still so, just as before, as it was, Hom.; λευκὸν ἔτ’ αὔτως still white as when new, Il. III. in vain, without effect, οὐκ αὔτως μυθήσομαι Od.

αυχενιζω.def: αὐχενίζω (αὐχήν) to cut the throat of a person, behead, c. acc., Soph.

αυχεω.def: αὐχέω (αὔχη) I. like καυχάομαι, to boast, plume oneself, Hdt., Eur.; τινι or ἐπί τινι on a thing, id., Anth. II. c. acc. et inf. to boast or declare loudly that, protest that, Hdt., Thuc., Eur.:—c. inf. only, Aesch.; οὐ γάρ ποτ’ ηὔχουν μεθέξειν I never thought that.., id.

αυχημα.gloss: a thing boasted of, a pride, boast
αυχημα.def: αὔχημα (From αὐχέω) I. a thing boasted of, a pride, boast, Soph.: cause for boasting, glory, id., Thuc. II. boasting, self-confidence, id.

αυχην.def: αὐχήν (Deriv. uncertain.) I. the neck, throat, of men and beasts, Hom., etc. II. metaph. any narrow passage, a neck of land, isthmus, Hdt., Xen. 2. a narrow sea, strait, Hdt., Aesch.; of the point at which the Danube spreads into several branches, Hdt. 3. a narrow mountain-pass, defile, id.

αυχμεω.def: αὐχμέω (αὐχμός) to be squalid or unwashed, Lat. squaleo, Od., Ar., Plat.

αυχμηροσ.def: αὐχμηρός (αὐχμέω) dry, dusty, rough, squalid, Eur., Plat.; esp. of hair, Eur.

αυχμοσ.def: αὐχμός (αὔω to burn) 1. drought, Hdt., Thuc. 2. the effects of drought, squalor, Plat.

αυχμωδησ.def: αὐχμώδης (εἶδος) looking dry, squalid, κόμη Eur.: τὸ αὐχμῶδες drought, Hdt.

αυω.gloss: to burn, light a fire, get a light
αυω.def: αὔω (Akin to εὕω: hence αὐαίνω, αὐχμός.) to burn, light a fire, get a light, Od.

αυω.gloss: to shout out, shout, call aloud
αυω.def: αὔω (The Root is ΑϜ, akin to ἄημι: hence ἀϋτή.) 1. to shout out, shout, call aloud, Hom.; αὖε δ’ Ἀθήνη, μακρὸν ἄϋσε, etc., id.: —also in Trag.; c. acc. cogn. to utter, στεναγμόν, αὐδάν Eur. 2. c. acc. pers. to call upon, Hom. 3. rarely of things, to ring, ἀσπὶς ἄϋσεν Il.; cf. αὖος.

αφαγνιζω.def: ἀφαγνίζω to purify:— Mid. to purify oneself by offerings, τοῖς θεοῖς to the gods, Eur.

αφαιρεσισ.def: ἀφαίρεσις (From ἀφαιρέω) a taking away, carrying off, Plat.

αφαιρετεοσ.def: ἀφαιρετέος (verb. adj. of ἀφαιρέω) I. one must take away, Plat. II. ἀφαιρετέος, έα, έον, to be taken away, id.

αφαιρετοσ.def: ἀφαιρετός (From ἀφαιρέω) to be taken away, separable, Plat.

αφαιρεω.gloss: to take from, take away from
αφαιρεω.def: ἀφαιρέω I. to take from, take away from a person, τί τινι Od., etc.; also τί τινος, Ar., Xen.; and τί τινα Aesch., Soph.:—c. acc. solo, ἀπελὼν τὰ ἄχθεα having taken them off, Hdt.; ὀργὴν ἀφ. to remove it, Eur.; ἀφ. χωρίς separate, set aside, Plat. II. Mid., fut. ἀφαιρήσομαι, and later ἀφελοῦμαι: aor2 ἀφειλόμην:— to take away for oneself, take away, in sense and construction much like Act., Hom., etc. 2. followed by μή c. inf. to prevent, hinder from doing, Soph., Eur. 3. ἀφαιρεῖσθαί τινα εἰς ἐλευθερίαν, Lat. vindicare in libertatem, to set a man free, Plat., Dem. III. Pass., fut. -αιρεθήσομαι: aor1 ἀφηιρέθην: perf. ἀφῄρημαι, ionic ἀπαραίρημαι:— to be robbed or deprived of a thing, to have it taken from one, τι Hdt., attic

αφαλλομαι.def: ἀφάλλομαι I. to spring off or from, ἐκ νεώς Aesch.; ἀφήλατο jumped off, Ar. II. to rebound, glance off, Anth.

αφαλοσ.def: ἄφαλος without the φάλος or boss, in which the plume was fixed, Il.

αφαμαρτανω.def: ἀφαμαρτάνω I. to miss one's mark, c. gen., Il., Xen. II. to be deprived of what one has, Il.

αφανδανω.def: ἀφανδάνω to displease, not to please, Od., Hdt., Soph.

αφανεια.def: ἀφάνεια (From ἀφανής) I. obscurity, ἀξιώματος ἀφ. want of illustrious birth, Thuc. II. disappearance, utter destruction, Aesch.

αφανησ.def: ἀφανής (φαίνομαι) 1. unseen, invisible, viewless, of the nether world, Aesch.: χάσμα ἀφ. a blind pit, Hdt.; ἡ ἀφ. θεός, of Proserpine, Soph. 2. ἀφ. γίγνεσθαι ἀφανίζεσθαι, to disappear, be missing, Hdt., Eur.:— of soldiers missing after a battle, Thuc.: cf. ἀφανίζω. 3. unseen, unnoticed, secret, Solon, Thuc.: —c. part., ἀφ. εἰμι ποιῶν τι I do it without being noticed, Xen. 4. unknown, uncertain, obscure, Hdt., attic: of future events, τὸ ἀφανές uncertainty, Hdt.:—adv. ἀφανῶς, Thuc.; so ἐκ τοῦ ἀφανοῦς as adv., id.; and neut. pl. ἀφανῆ, Eur. 5. of persons, unnoticed, obscure, id., Thuc. 6. ἀφανὴς οὐσία personal property, as money, which can be made away with, opp. to φανερά (real), as land, Oratt.

αφανιζω.gloss: to make unseen, hide from sight
αφανιζω.def: ἀφανίζω (ἀφανής) I. to make unseen, hide from sight, Xen., Thuc., etc. 2. to do away with, remove, ἄχος Soph.; ἀφ. τινὰ πόλεος to carry off one from the city, Eur.; ἀφ. αὑτὸν εἰς τὸν νεών to disappear into the temple, Ar.:—of state criminals, to remove from sight, make away with, Hdt., Xen.: Pass. to be concealed or suppressed, Thuc. 3. to destroy utterly, rase to the ground, erase writing, id., Dem.: to obliterate traces, Xen. 4. to obliterate, tarnish one's good name, Thuc., Plat.:—but in good sense, ἀφ. ἀγαθῶι κακόν to wipe out ill deeds by good, Thuc.; δύσκλειαν id. 5. to disfigure, ἀφ. τὰ πρόσωπα, of hypocritical sadness, NTest. 6. to make away with property, Aeschin., Dem. II. Pass. to become unseen, to disappear, Hdt., Soph.; of persons buried by a sand-storm, Hdt.; or, lost at sea, Thuc., Xen.

αφανισισ.def: ἀφάνισις (From ἀφανίζω) I. a getting rid of, τῆς δίκης Ar. II. (from Pass.) disappearance, Hdt.

αφανιστεοσ.def: ἀφανιστέος (verb. adj. of ἀφανίζω) to be suppressed, Isocr.

αφαντοσ.def: ἄφαντος (φαίνομαι) 1. made invisible, blotted out, forgotten, Il.: hidden, Aesch., Soph.; ἀφ. βῆναι, οἴχεσθαι, ἔρρειν, ἀφανισθῆναι, to disappear, Trag. 2. in secret, Pind. 3. obscure, id.

αφαπτω.def: ἀφάπτω to fasten from or upon, ἅμματα ἀφ. to tie knots on a string, Hdt.:—Pass. to be hung on, hang on, perf. part. ἀπαμμένος (ionic for ἀφημμένος), Hdt.; ἀφημμένος ἔκ τινος Theocr.

αφαρ.gloss: straightway, forthwith, at once, quickly, presently
αφαρ.def: ἄφαρ I. straightway, forthwith, at once, quickly, presently, Hom., Trag. 2. thereupon, after that, Hom. II. in Theogn. as adj. swift, fleet (cf. ἀφάρτερος).

αφαρπαζω.def: ἀφαρπάζω to tear off or from, c. gen., Il.; to snatch away, steal from, τί τινος Ar.: c. acc. only, to snatch eagerly, Soph., Eur.

αφαρτεροσ.def: ἀφάρτερος (v. ἄφαρ II) more fleet, Il.

αφασσω.def: ἀφάσσω (ἁφή, ἅπτομαι) to handle, feel, c. acc., Hdt.

αφατοσ.def: ἄφατος 1. not uttered, nameless, Hes. 2. untold, unutterable, ineffable, extraordinary, Hdt., Soph.; ἄφατον ὡς there's no saying how, i. e. marvellously, immensely, Ar.

αφαυροσ.def: ἀφαυρός (Deriv. uncertain.) feeble, powerless, παιδὸς ἀφαυροῦ Il.; mostly in comp. and Sup., Hom., Hes.:—adv. -ρῶς, Anth.

αφαυω.def: ἀφαύω (αὔω, attic αὕω) to dry up, parch, Ar.

αφαω.def: ἁφάω (ἁφή, ἅπτομαι) to handle, rub, polish, Il.

αφεγγησ.def: ἀφεγγής (φέγγος) 1. without light, φῶς ἀφ. a light that is no light (i. e. to the blind), Soph.; νυκτὸς ἀφεγγὲς βλέφαρον, of the moon, as opp. to the sun, Eur. 2. obscure, dim, faint, Aesch. 3. metaph., ill-starred, unlucky, Soph.

αφειδεω.def: ἀφειδέω (From ἀφειδής) 1. to be unsparing or lavish of, ψυχῆς Soph.; ἑαυτοῦ Thuc.:—absol. ἀφειδήσας (sub. ἑαυτοῦ) recklessly, Eur.; but 2. ἀφειδεῖν πόνου to be careless of it, i. e. neglect, avoid, labour, Soph.

αφειδησ.def: ἀφειδής (φείδομαι) I. unsparing or lavish of a thing, c. gen., Aesch. 2. of actions, done without regard to cost or risk, Thuc. II. adv. -δῶς, ionic -δέως, freely, lavishly Hdt., Dem.:—also sparing no pains, with all zeal, id. 2. unsparingly, without mercy, Hdt.; comp. -έστερον, Sup. -έστατα, Xen.

αφειδια.def: ἀφειδία (From ἀφειδής) 1. profuseness, Plat. 2. harsh treatment, neglect, NTest.

αφεκτεοσ.def: ἀφεκτέος (verb. adj. of ἀπέχομαι) one must abstain from, τινός Xen.

αφελησ.def: ἀφελής (φελλεύς?) without a stone, even, smooth, Ar.: metaph. of persons, simple, plain, blunt, Dem., Luc.:—adv. ἀφελῶς, simply, roughly, Theogn.

αφελκω.def: ἀφέλκω I. to drag away suppliants, ἐκ τοῦ ἱροῦ Hdt., etc.; to drag or tow ships away, Thuc.:— to draw aside, ἐπί τι Xen. II. to draw off liquor, drink up, Aesch. 2. Mid. to draw off for oneself, Ar.

αφενοσ.def: ἄφενος (From same Root as Lat. opes.) riches, wealth, plenty, Il., Theogn.

αφερκτοσ.def: ἄφερκτος (ἀπείργω) shut out from a place, Aesch.

αφερπω.gloss: to creep off, steal away, retire
αφερπω.def: ἀφέρπω to creep off, steal away, retire, Soph.

αφεσισ.def: ἄφεσις (ἀφίημι) 1. a letting go, dismissal, Philipp. ap. Dem.:— a quittance or discharge from a bond, id.: exemption from service, Plut.: a divorce, id. 2. a letting go (Lat. missio) of horses from the starting-post, and then the starting-post itself, ἰσώσας τἀφέσει τὰ τέρματα having made the winning-post one with the starting-post, i. e. having come back to the starting-post, Soph.

αφεστηξω.gloss: I shall be absent, away from
αφεστηξω.def: ἀφεστήξω (old Attic future formed from ἀφέστηκα fut pf. of ἀφίστημι) I shall be absent, away from, τινός Plat., Xen.

αφετεοσ.def: ἀφετέος (verb adj. of ἀφίημι) 1. one must dismiss, Plat. 2. to be let go, id.

αφετηριοσ.def: ἀφετήριος (ἀφίημι) for letting go or starting for a race: ἀφ. Διόσκουροι whose statues stood at the starting place, Anth.

αφετοσ.gloss: let loose, at large, ranging at will
αφετοσ.def: ἄφετος (ἀφίημι) let loose, at large, ranging at will, of sacred flocks that were free from work, Aesch., Plat.: metaph. of person, dedicated to a god, Eur.: τὸ ἄφετον, freedom from restraint, Luc.

αφευω.def: ἀφεύω 1. to singe off, Ar. 2. to fry, toast, id.

αφεψω.def: ἀφέψω to refine by boiling off the refuse, to boil down, Hdt.:—esp. to boil free of dirt and dross, to refine, χρυσίον id.: to boil young again, Ar.:—Pass., ὕδωρ ἀπεψημένον Hdt.

αφη.def: ἁφή (ἅπτω) I. a lighting, kindling, περὶ λύχνων ἁφάς about lamp- lighting time, Hdt. II. （ἅπτομαι) a touching, touch, Aesch.: the sense of touch, Plat., etc.

αφηγεομαι.def: ἀφηγέομαι Dep. I. to lead from a point, and so, generally, to lead the way, go first, οἱ ἀφηγούμενοι the van, Xen. II. to tell or relate in full, explain, Hdt.: perf. in pass. sense, τὸ ἀπηγημένον what has been told, id.

αφηγημα.def: ἀφήγημα (From ἀφηγέομαι) a tale, narrative, Hdt.

αφηγησισ.def: ἀφήγησις (From ἀφηγέομαι) a telling, narrating, ἄξιον ἀπηγήσιος worth telling, Hdt.

αφηλιξ.def: ἀφῆλιξ beyond youth, elderly, mostly in comp. ἀπηλικέστερος, Hdt.

αφητωρ.def: ἀφήτωρ (ἀφίημι) the archer, of Apollo, Il.

αφθεγκτοσ.def: ἄφθεγκτος (φθέγγομαι) I. voiceless, Aesch., Anth. II. of places, where none may speak, Soph. III. pass. unspeakable, Plat.

αφθιτοσ.def: ἄφθιτος (φθίνω) not liable to perish, imperishable, Hom., Trag.: of persons, immortal, Hhymn.

αφθογγοσ.def: ἄφθογγος voiceless, speechless, Hdt., Aesch., etc.

αφθονια.def: ἀφθονία (From φθονέω) I. freedom from envy or grudging, readiness, Plat. II. of things, plenty, abundance, Pind., Plat.

αφθονοσ.def: ἄφθονος without envy: I. act. free from envy, Hdt., Plat. 2. ungrudging, bounteous, Lat. benignus, Trag. II. pass. not grudged, bounteously given, plentiful, abundant, Hdt., attic; ἐν ἀφθόνοις βιοτεύειν to live in plenty, Xen. 2. unenvied, provoking no envy, ὄλβος Aesch. III. irreg. comp. -έστερος, Sup. -έστατος, Plat.; but -ώτερος, -ώτατος, Xen. IV. adv. in abundance, ἀφθ. ἔχειν τινός to have enough of it, Plat.

αφθοροσ.def: ἄφθορος uncorrupt, of young persons, Anth.

αφιδρυω.def: ἀφιδρύω to remove to another settlement: Mid. to cause to be transported, Eur.

αφιεροω.def: ἀφιερόω to purify, hallow: Pass., perf. ταῦτ’ ἀφιερώμεθα I have had these expiatory rites performed, Aesch.

αφιημι.def: ἀφίημι (ι short in epic, except in augm. tenses: ῑ attic) I. to send forth, discharge, Lat. emittere, of missiles, Hom., etc.:—hence to let loose, utter, give vent to words, Hdt., Trag. 2. to let fall, Il. 3. to send forth an expedition, dispatch it, Hdt.: Pass., of troops, id. 4. to give up or hand over to, τινι τί id., attic:—Pass., ἡ Ἀττικὴ ἀπεῖτο ἤδη Hdt. II. to send away, let go, loose, set free, Il., attic:—c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, to set free from a thing, let off from, Hdt.: in legal sense to release from an engagement, accusation, etc., ἀφ. τινὰ φόνου Dem. 2. to dissolve, disband, break up an army, Hdt.:— to dismiss the council or law-courts, Ar. 3. to put away, divorce, Hdt. 4. to let go as an ἄφετος, consecrate, Xen. 5. of things, to get rid of, δίψαν Il.; to shed its blossoms, of plants, Od.; to slacken its force, of a dart, Il. 6. ἀφ. πλοῖον ἐς.. to loose ship for a place, Hdt. 7. in legal sense, c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, ἀφ. τινὶ αἰτίην to remit him a charge or a fine, Hdt., Dem. III. to leave alone, give up, let pass, neglect, Hdt., attic; foll. by a predicate, ἀφύλακτον ἀφ. to leave unguarded. 2. c. acc. et inf., ἀφ. τι δημόσιον εἶναι to give up to be public property, Thuc.; ἀφ. τὸ πλοῖον φέρεσθαι to let the boat be carried away, Hdt. 3. c. acc. pers. et inf. to let, suffer, permit one to do a thing, id., Plat., etc. IV. seemingly intr. (sub. στρατόν, ναῦς, etc.), to break up, march, sail, etc., Hdt. B. Mid. to send forth from oneself, send forth, attic 2. δειρῆς ἀφίετο πήχεε she loosed her arms from off my neck. 3. c. gen. only, τέκνων ἀφοῦ let go hold of the children, Soph., Thuc.

αφικανω.gloss: to arrive at, to have come to
αφικανω.def: ἀφικάνω (only in present and imperfect) to arrive at, to have come to, c. acc., Hom.

αφικνεομαι.def: ἀφικνέομαι 1. to come to one place from another, to arrive at, reach: c. acc. loci, Hom.; or ἀφ. ἐς.., ἐπί.., κατά.., πρός.., id., attic (in Prose the prep. is seldom omitted); absol. to arrive, Od.:—Hom. also puts the person reached in acc., μνηστῆρας ἀφ. came up to them, Od.; so, to come up to a throw (of the quoit), id.:— ἀφ. ἐπὶ or εἰς πάντα to try every means, Soph., Eur. 2. to come into a certain condition, ἀπ. ἐς πᾶν κακόν or κακοῦ, ἐς ἀπορίην, etc., Hdt., attic 3. ἀπ. τινι ἐς λόγους to hold converse with one, Hdt.; so, ἐς ἔριν, ἐς ἔχθεα ἀφ. τινι id.; διὰ μάχης, δι’ ἔχθρας ἀπ. τινί to come to battle, or into enmity with one, id.; διὰ λόγων τινί Eur. 4. ἐς τόξευμα ἀφ. to come within shot, Xen.

αφιλαγαθοσ.def: ἀφιλάγαθος not loving the good, NTest.

αφιλοσ.def: ἄφιλος I. without friends, friendless, Trag. II. unfriendly, hateful, id.—adv. ἀφίλως in unfriendly manner, Aesch.

αφιλοσταχυοσ.def: ἀφιλοστάχυος without ears of corn, starving, Anth.

αφιλοτιμια.def: ἀφιλοτιμία (From ἀφιλότιμος) want of due ambition, Arist.

αφιλοτιμοσ.def: ἀφιλότιμος without due ambition, Isae., Arist.

αφιξισ.def: ἄφιξις (ἀφικνέομαι) I. an arrival, Hdt., Dem. II. departure, NTest.

αφιππαζομαι.def: ἀφιππάζομαι Dep. to ride off or away, Plut.

αφιππευω.def: ἀφιππεύω to ride off, away, or back, Xen.

αφιππια.def: ἀφιππία (From ἄφιππος) awkwardness in riding, Xen.

αφιπποσ.def: ἄφιππος I. unsuited for cavalry, χώρα Xen. II. of persons, unused to riding, Plat.

αφιστημι.def: ἀφίστημι A. Causal in pres. and imperf., in fut. ἀποστήσω, aor1 ἀπέστησα, as also in aor1 mid.:— to put away, remove, c. acc., Aesch., etc.; ἀφ. τινὰ λόγου to hinder from speech, Eur.; ἀφ. τὴν ἐπιβουλήν to frustrate it, Thuc.; ἀφ. τὸν ἄρχοντα to depose him, Xen.; so in aor1 mid., δόρυ πυλῶν ἀπεστήσασθε removed war from your own gates, Eur. 2. to make to revolt, move to revolt, Hdt., Thuc. II. to weigh out, Xen.:—aor1 mid., ἀποστήσασθαι χρεῖος to weigh out or pay the debt in full, Il.; ἀποστήσασθαι τὸν χαλκόν to have the money weighed out to one, Dem. B. intr., in Pass., as also in aor2 act. ἀπέστην, imperat. ἀπόστηθι, ἀπόστα, perf. ἀφέστηκα in pres. sense, syncop. pl. ἀφέσταμεν, -στατε, -στᾶσι, inf. ἀφεστάναι, part. ἀφεστώς, -ῶσα, -ός or -ώς: fut. mid. ἀποστήσομαι: aor1 ἀπεστάθην [α]:— to stand away or aloof from, keep far from, c. gen., Hom., attic; μακρὰν τόποις καὶ χρόνοις ἀφ. Diod.; ἀφεστάναι φρενῶν to lose one's wits, Soph.; ἀφ. πραγμάτων to withdraw from business, Dem., etc. 2. in Prose, to revolt from, τινος or ἀπό τινος, Hdt., attic: absol. to revolt, Hdt. 3. ἀφ. τινός τινι to give up a thing to another, Dem.; hence, ἀφ. τινι to make way for him, give way to him, Eur.; c. inf. to shrink from doing, id. 4. absol. to stand aloof, Il., attic

αφλαστον.def: ἄφλαστον Lat. aplustre, the curved stern of a ship with its ornaments, Il., Hdt.

αφλεκτοσ.def: ἄφλεκτος (φλέγω) unburnt, unconsumed by fire, πέλανοι Eur.

αφλοιοσ.def: ἄφλοιος without bark, Epigr. ap. Plut.

αφλοισμοσ.def: ἀφλοισμός of an angry man, spluttering or perh. foaming, Il.

αφνειοσ.def: ἀφνειός (ἄφενος) rich, wealthy, Il.; c. gen., ἀφνειὸς βιότοιο rich in substance, Hom.; c. acc., Hes.; c. dat., Theocr.

αφνιδιοσ.def: ἀφνίδιος (ἄφνω) unforeseen, sudden, Aesch., Thuc.:—adv. -ίως, id.; also -ιον, Plut.

αφνω.def: ἄφνω unawares, of a sudden, Eur., Thuc.; cf. ἐξ-αίφνης.

αφοβητοσ.def: ἀφόβητος (φοβέομαι) without fear of, δίκης Soph.: absol. fearless, Anth.

αφοβοσ.def: ἄφοβος without fear: 1. fearless, intrepid, dauntless, Pind., Soph.:—adv. -βως, Xen. 2. causing no fear, free from fear, Aesch. 3. ἄφοβοι θῆρες beasts which no one fears, i. e. cattle, Soph.

αφοδοσ.def: ἄφοδος 1. a going away, departure, Hdt., Xen. 2. a going or coming back, return, id.

αφομοιοω.def: ἀφομοιόω I. to make like, τί τινί Plat.: to compare, τι id.:—Pass. to be or become like, τινι id. II. c. acc. rei only, to pourtray, copy, id., Xen.

αφομοιωμα.def: ἀφομοίωμα (From ἀφομοιόω) a resemblance, copy, Plat.

αφοπλιζω.def: ἀφοπλίζω to strip of arms, τινά τινος Luc.: to disarm, τινά Anth.:—Mid., ἀφοπλίζεσθαι ἔντεα to put off one's armour, Il.

αφοραω.def: ἀφοράω I. to look away from all others at one, to have in full view, to look at, τι or πρός τι Thuc.; also in Mid., Ar. 2. to view from a place, ἀπὸ δενδρέου Hdt. II. to look away, have the back turned, Xen.

αφορια.def: ἀφορία (ἄφορος) a not bearing: 1. non-production, dearth, καρπῶν Xen. 2. barrenness, sterility of land: metaph., ἀφ. φρενῶν id.

αφοριζω.def: ἀφορίζω I. to mark off by boundaries, Dem.: —Mid. to mark off for oneself, appropriate, Eur. 2. to distinguish, determine, define, Plat. II. c. acc. pers., 1. to banish, Eur. 2. to set apart, separate, NTest.: then, 3. to cast out, excommunicate, id. b. to set apart for some office, to appoint, ordain, id.

αφοριστεοσ.def: ἀφοριστέος (verb. adj. of ἀφορίζω) one must put aside, Arist.

αφορμαω.def: ἀφορμάω I. to make to start from a place:— Pass. to go forth, start, depart from a place, c. gen., Hom., attic II. intr. in same sense as Pass., Eur., Thuc.: of lightning, to break forth, Soph.; c. acc. cogn., ἀφορμᾶν πεῖραν to begin an enterprise. id.

αφορμη.def: ἀφορμή 1. a starting-point, esp. in war, a base of operations, Thuc.:—also a place of safety, Eur. 2. generally, a starting-point, the origin, occasion or pretext of a thing, id.; ἀφορμὴν παρέχειν, διδόναι to give occasion, Dem. 3. the means with which one begins a thing, resources, Xen., Dem.; ἀφ. ἔργων means for undertaking works, Xen. 4. the capital of a banker, id., Dem.

αφορμοσ.def: ἄφορμος (ὀρμή) departing from a place, c. gen., Soph.

αφοροσ.def: ἄφορος (φέρω) 1. not bearing, barren, Hdt., Xen. 2. causing barrenness, blighting, Aesch.

αφοσιοω.def: ἀφοσιόω I. to purify from guilt or pollution, τὴν πόλιν Plat. II. Mid. to purify oneself from sins of negligence, id.; ἀφοσιοῦσθαι τῆι θεῶι to make expiatory offerings to the goddess, Hdt. 2. c. acc. rei, to acquit oneself of an obligation, ἀποσιοῦσθαι τὴν ἐξόρκωσιν to quit oneself of one's oath, id.; ἀπ. λόγιον quitting oneself of the orders of an oracle, id.

αφοσιωσισ.def: ἀφοσίωσις (From ἀφοσιόω) expiation: ἀφοσιώσεως ἕνεκα for form's sake, Plut.

αφραδεω.def: ἀφραδέω (From ἀφραδής) (only in present) to be senseless, act thoughtlessly, Hom.

αφραδησ.def: ἀφραδής (φράζομαι) insensate, reckless, Od.; of the dead, senseless, lifeless, id. adv. ἀφραδέως, senselessly, recklessly, Il.

αφραδια.def: ἀφραδία (From ἀφραδής) folly, thoughtlessness, mostly in epic dat. pl., ἀφραδίηισι Hom.; δι’ ἀφραδίας Od.

αφραινω.def: ἀφραίνω (ἄφρων) to be silly, senseless, Hom.

αφρακτοσ.def: ἄφρακτος (φράσσω) I. unfenced, unfortified, unguarded, Thuc.; c. gen., ἄφρ. φίλων by friends, Soph.; c. dat., ἄφρ. ὅρκοις Eur. 2. not to be kept in, irrepressible, Aesch. II. unguarded, off one's guard, Thuc.

αφραστοσ.def: ἄφραστος (φράζω) I. unutterable, inexpressible, Hhymn., Aesch., Soph. II. （φράζομαι) not perceived or thought of, Aesch.; τὸ ἀφραστότατον χωρίον the place least likely to be thought of, Hdt.:—adv. -τως, beyond thought, Soph.

αφρεω.def: ἀφρέω (ἀφρός) to befoam, cover with foam, ἵπποι ἄφρεον στήθεα Il.

αφρηλογοσ.def: ἀφρηλόγος (ἀφρός, λέγω) gathering froth, skimming, τινός Anth.

αφρηστησ.def: ἀφρηστής (ἀφρός) the foamer, of a dolphin, Anth.

αφρητωρ.def: ἀφρήτωρ (ionic for ἀφράτωρ) without brotherhood (φράτρα), i. e. bound by no social tie, Il.

αφρογενησ.def: ἀφρογενής (γίγνομαι) foam-born, of Aphrodite, Hes.: fem. Ἀφρο-γένεια, Mosch.

αφροδισιαζω.def: ἀφροδισιάζω to indulge lust, Plat., Xen.

αφροδισιασ.def: Ἀφροδισίας sacred to Aphrodite, name of an island, Hdt.

αφροδισιοσ.def: Ἀφροδίσιος (From Ἀφροδίτη) I. belonging to Aphrodite, Plat. II. Ἀφροδίσια, τά, sexual pleasures, Xen. 2. a festival of Aphrodite, id. III. Ἀφροδίσιον, ου, τό, the temple of Aphrodite, id.

αφροδιτη.def: Ἀφροδίτη (ἀφρός) I. Aphrodite, Lat. Venus, goddess of love, said to be born from the sea-foam, Hhymn., Hes. II. as appellat. love, pleasure, Od.: —Ἀφρ. κακῶν enjoyment, Eur. 2. attractive beauty, grace, Lat. venustas, Aesch., Luc;. cf. Lat. venus.

αφρονεω.def: ἀφρονέω (ἄφρων) to be silly, act foolishly, only in part., Il., Anth.

αφροντιστεω.gloss: to have no care of, pay no heed to
αφροντιστεω.def: ἀφροντιστέω (From ἀφρόντιστος) to have no care of, pay no heed to a thing, c. gen., Xen.

αφροντιστοσ.def: ἀφρόντιστος (φροντίζω) I. thoughtless, heedless, taking no care, Lat. securus, Xen., Theocr.:—adv. -τως, inconsiderately, Soph.; ἀφρ. ἔχειν to be heedless, Xen.; also to be senseless, demented, Soph. II. pass. unthought of, unexpected, Aesch.

αφροσ.def: ἀφρός foam, of the sea, Il.: of an angry lion, foam, froth, id.; ἀπ’ ἀνθρώπων ἀφρόν frothy blood, Aesch.

αφροσυνη.def: ἀφροσύνη (ἄφρων) folly, thoughtlessness, senselessness, in sg. and pl., Hom., Soph., Thuc.

αφρων.def: ἄφρων (φρήν) without sense, of statues, Xen.:— crazed, frantic, or silly, foolish, Hom., attic: τὸ ἄφρον ἀφροσύνη, Thuc. adv. ἀφρόνως, senselessly, Soph.

αφυβριζω.def: ἀφυβρίζω to give loose to passion, Plut.

αφυδραινω.def: ἀφυδραίνω to wash clean from dirt:—Mid., aor1 -υδρηνάμην, to wash oneself clean, bathe, Eur.

αφυη.def: ἀφύη (in gen. pl. ἀφύων (not ἀφυῶν）) a sort of anchovy or sardine, Ar.

αφυησ.def: ἀφυής (φυή) 1. without natural talent, witless, dull, Plat.; ἀφυὴς πρός τι naturally unsuited to a thing, id., Xen. 2. simple, unschooled, Soph.

αφυκτοσ.gloss: not to be shunned, from which none escape
αφυκτοσ.def: ἄφυκτος (φεύγω) I. not to be shunned, from which none escape, Aesch., Soph.; of an arrow, unerring, id., Eur.; of a question, admitting no escape, inevitable, Plat. II. act. unable to escape, Ar.

αφυλακτεω.def: ἀφυλακτέω (From ἀφ-ὑλακτέω) to bark out luc.
ἀφυλακτέω (From ἀφύλακτος) to be off one's guard, Xen.: c. gen. to be careless about, id.

αφυλακτοσ.def: ἀφύλακτος (φυλάσσω) I. unguarded, unwatched, Hdt., Thuc. II. （φυλάσσομαι) unguarded, off one's guard, id.; ἀφύλακτον εὕδειν to sleep securely, Aesch.; ἀφ. τινα λαμβάνειν to catch one off his guard, Xen.; τὸ ἀφ. want of precaution, Thuc.:—adv. -τως, Xen. III. not to be guarded against, inevitable, Arist.

αφυλλοσ.def: ἄφυλλος (φύλλον) I. leafless, of dry wood, Il.; ἄφ. στόμα words not seconded by the suppliant's olivebranch, Eur. II. act. stripping off the leaves, blighting, Aesch.

αφυπνιζω.def: ἀφυπνίζω to wake one from sleep, Eur., Plut.

αφυπνοω.def: ἀφυπνόω I. to wake from sleep, Anth. II. to fall asleep, NTest.

αφυσγετοσ.def: ἀφυσγετός (Deriv. unknown.) the mud and filth which a stream carries with it, rubbish, Il.

αφυσσω.def: ἀφύσσω I. to draw liquids, esp. from a larger vessel with a smaller, οἶνον ἐν ἀμφιφορεῦσιν ἠφύσαμεν Od.:—Pass., πίθων ἠφύσσετο οἶνος was drawn from the wine-jars, id.:—metaph., πλοῦτον ἀφύξειν to draw full draughts of wealth, i. e. heap it up, τινί for another, Il. II. Mid. to draw for oneself, οἶνον id.; ῥοάς Eur.:—metaph., φύλλα ἠφυσάμην I heaped me up a bed of leaves, Od.

αφωνοσ.def: ἄφωνος (φωνή) 1. voiceless, speechless, dumb, silent, Theogn., Hdt., Dem.: c. gen., ἄφωνος ἀρᾶς unable to utter a curse, Soph.:—adv. -νως, without speaking, id.; neut. pl. as adv., Aesch. 2. ἄφωνα (sc. γράμματα), consonants, opp. to φωνοῦντα or φωνήεντα (vowels), Eur., Plat.

αχαια.def: Ἀχαία (Deriv. unknown.) name of Demeter in Attica, Hdt.

αχαιικοσ.def: Ἀχαιικός (αχαιός) of or for the Achaians, Achaian, Aesch., Eur.

αχαιισ.def: Ἀχαιίς 1. the Achaian land, with or without γαῖα, Il. 2. (sub. γυνή) an Achaian woman, id.

αχαινησ.gloss: with single points to his horns, a young deer
αχαινησ.def: ἀχαίνης (ἀκίς) with single points to his horns, a young deer, Babr.

αχαιοσ.def: Ἀχαιός Achaian, Lat. Achivus, Hom.:— Ἀχαιοί, οἱ, the Achaians or Greeks generally, id.

αχαλκευτοσ.def: ἀχάλκευτος (χαλκεύω) not forged of metal, Aesch.

αχαλκεω.def: ἀχαλκέω (From ἄχαλκος) to be penniless, Anth.

αχαλκοσ.def: ἄχαλκος without brass, ἄχαλκος ἀσπίδων, i. e. ἄνευ ἀσπίδων χαλκείων, Soph.

αχαλκωτοσ.def: ἀχάλκωτος (χαλκόω) not brasened; without money, Anth.

αχανη.def: ἀχάνη a Persian measure, = 45 μέδιμνοι, Ar.

αχανησ.def: ἀχανής (χανεῖν, aor2 inf. of χάσκω) I. not opening the mouth, Luc. II. （α euphon.) yawning, wide, Plut., Anth.

αχαρισ.def: ἄχαρις I. without grace or charms, graceless, Theogn. 2. unpleasant, disagreeable, οὐδὲν ἄχαρι παθέειν Hdt.; as euphem. for grievous, ἄχ. συμφορή id. II. ungracious, thankless, id.; χάρις ἄχαρις a graceless grace, thankless favour, Aesch., Eur.

αχαριστεω.def: ἀχαριστέω (From ἀχάριστος) 1. to be thankless, shew ingratitude, Xen. 2. = οὐ χαρίζομαι, to discourage, τινί Plat.;

αχαριστια.def: ἀχαριστία (From ἀχάριστος) 1. thanklessness, ingratitude, Xen., Dem. 2. ungraciousness, Plat.

αχαριστοσ.def: ἀχάριστος (χαρίζομαι) I. ungracious, unpleasant, unpleasing, Od.; irreg. comp., δόρπου ἀχαρίστερον (for -ιστότερον) id.: without grace or charms, Xen. II. of persons, ungracious, unfavourable, Theogn. 2. ungrateful, thankless, Hdt., attic; τινι Eur.; πρός τινα Xen. III. adv. -τως, with an ill-will, id.; ἀχαρίστως ἔχει μοι thanks are wanting to me, id.

αχαριτοσ.def: ἀχάριτος 1. = ἀχάριστος or ἄχαρις, Hdt. 2. ungrateful, thankless, id.; χάρις ἀχ., like χάρις ἄχαρις, Eur.

αχαρναι.def: Ἀχαρναί Acharnae, a demos of Attica, Thuc.

αχαρνευσ.def: Ἀχαρνεύς an inhabitant of Acharnae, pl. Ἀχαρνεῖς, poet. Ἀχαρνηΐδαι Ar.

αχαρνικοσ.def: Ἀχαρνικός belonging to or of Acharnae, Ar.

αχειμαντοσ.def: ἀχείμαντος (χειμαίνω) not vexed by storms, Alcae.

αχειροποιητοσ.def: ἀχειροποίητος not wrought by hands, NTest.

αχειροσ.def: ἄχειρος (χείρ) without hands: τὰ ἄχειρα of the hinder parts of the body, Xen.

αχειρωτοσ.def: ἀχείρωτος (χειρόω) I. untamed, unconquered, Thuc. II. not planted by man's hand, Soph.

αχελωιδεσ.gloss: islands at the mouth of the Achelous
αχελωιδεσ.def: Ἀχελωίδες sc. νῆσοι, islands at the mouth of the Achelous, Aesch.

αχελωοσ.def: Ἀχελῷος I. Achelous, name of several rivers; the best known ran through Aetolia and Acarnania, Il., Hes. II. any stream, or, generally, water, Eur.

αχερδοσ.gloss: a wild prickly shrub, a wild pear
αχερδοσ.def: ἄχερδος (Deriv. unknown.) a wild prickly shrub, a wild pear, Od., Soph.; masc. in Theocr.

αχερωισ.def: ἀχερωίς the white poplar, said to have been brought by Hercules from the banks of Acheron, Il.

αχερων.def: Ἀχέρων (ἄχος) Acheron, river of woe (cf. Κωκυτός), one of the rivers of the world below, Od.

αχευω.def: ἀχεύω (ἄχος) I. in pres. part. grieving, sorrowing, mourning, Hom. II. from the same Root ΑΧ, came also 1. aor2 in Causal sense, to grieve, vex, annoy, distress, Hom.: so also, redupl. fut. ἀκαχήσω, epic aor1 ἀκάχησα, id.; and a pres. ἀκαχίζω 2. pass. to be grieved, distressed, Hom.; c. gen. causae, to grieve for a person, id.; rarely c. dat. to grieve at a person's death, Od.; the cause of grief also in partic., μή τι θανὼν ἀκαχίζεο id. 3. later c. acc. to lament, Soph.

αχεω.def: ἀχέω (old form for ἰαχέω, Hhymn., Eur.)

αχηνια.def: ἀχηνία need, want, χρημάτων Aesch.; ὀμμάτων ἀχηνίαις in the eyes blank gaze, id.

αχθεινοσ.def: ἀχθεινός (ἄχθος) burdensome, oppressive, wearisome, Lat. molestus, of persons, Eur., Xen.:—adv. -νῶς, unwillingly, id.

αχθηδων.def: ἀχθηδών 1. a weight, burden, Aesch. 2. metaph. grievance, distress, vexation, annoyance, Thuc., Plat.; δι’ ἀχθηδόνα for the sake of teasing, Thuc. (From ἄχθος, as ἀλγηδών from ἄλγος.）

αχθομαι.def: ἄχθομαι (fut mid in pass sense) I. to be loaded, νηῦς ἤχθετο Od. II. of mental oppression, to be weighed down, vexed, annoyed, grieved, Hom.; τινι at a thing, or with a person, Hdt., etc.; so, ἐπί τινι Xen.; περί τινος Hdt.; ὑπέρ τινος Plat.:—also c. acc., ἄχθομαι ἕλκος Il.;—also c. part., either of subject, as ἄχθομαι ἰδών Soph.; or of object, ἤχθετο δαμναμένους at their being conquered, Il.; but the object is also in gen., οὐδὲν ἤχθετο αὐτῶν πολεμούντων he had no objection to going to war, Xen.

αχθοσ.def: ἄχθος (ἄχθομαι) I. a weight, burden, load, Hom.; ἄχθος ἀρούρης a dead weight on earth, cumberers of the ground, id. II. a load of grief, grief, trouble, distress, sorrow, Trag.

αχθοφορεω.def: ἀχθοφορέω (From ἀχθοφόρος) 1. to bear burdens, Plut. 2. to bear as a burden, τι Anth.

αχιλλειοσ.def: Ἀχίλλειος I. of Achilles, Hdt., Eur. II. Ἀχιλλείη κριθή Achilles-barley, a fine kind: hence Ἀχίλλειαι (μᾶζαι) cakes of fine barley, Ar.

αχιλλευσ.def: Ἀχιλλεύς (From ἄχος, the grief of the hero being the subject of the Il., cf. Ὀδυσσεύς) Achilles, son of Peleus and Thetis, prince of the Myrmidons.

αχιτων.def: ἀχίτων without tunic, i. e. wearing the ἱμάτιον only, of Socrates, Xen.

αχλαινια.def: ἀχλαινία (From ἄχλαινος) want of a cloak or mantle, Eur.

αχλαινοσ.def: ἄχλαινος (χλαῖνα) without cloak or mantle, Simon.

αχλυοεισ.def: ἀχλυόεις (From ἀχλύς) gloomy, Simon. ap. Hdt.

αχλυσ.def: ἀχλύς a mist, Lat. caligo, Od.; a mist over the eyes of one dying, Il.; or of a person deprived of the power of knowing others, id.—metaph. gloom, trouble, Aesch.

αχλυω.def: ἀχλύω (From ἀχλύς) to be or grow dark, Od.

αχνη.gloss: anything that comes off the surface
αχνη.def: ἄχνη anything that comes off the surface: I. foam, froth, of the sea, Od.; of wine, Eur.; ἄχνη οὐρανία the dew of heaven, Soph.; δακρύων ἄχνη dewy tears, id. II. of solids, the chaff that flies off in winnowing, in pl., Il.; the down on fruits, Anth. III. ἄχνην in acc. as adv., a morsel, the least bit, Ar.

αχολοσ.def: ἄχολος allaying bile or anger, Od.

αχορευτοσ.gloss: not attended with the dance, joyless, melancholy
αχορευτοσ.def: ἀχόρευτος (χορεύω) not attended with the dance, joyless, melancholy, Soph., Eur.

αχοροσ.def: ἄχορος without the dance, of death, Soph.: melancholy, Eur.

αχοσ.def: ἄχος pain, distress, Hom., Pind., attic Poets.

αχρειοσ.def: ἀχρεῖος I. useless, unprofitable, good for nothing, Hes., Soph., etc. 2. esp. unserviceable, unfit for war, Hdt.; τὸ ἄχρ. τοῦ στρατοῦ the unserviceable part of an army, id., Thuc., etc. II. in Hom. neut. ἀχρεῖον as adv., ἀχρεῖον ἰδών giving a helpless look, looking foolish, of Thersites after being beaten, Il.; ἀχρεῖον ἐγέλασσε laughing without cause or meaning, laughed with a forced laugh, Od.; so, ἀχρεῖον κλάζειν to bark without cause, Theocr.

αχρηματια.def: ἀχρηματία (from ἀχρήματος) want of money, Thuc.

αχρηματοσ.def: ἀχρήματος (χρήματα) without money or means, Hdt., Aesch.

αχρημοσυνη.def: ἀχρημοσύνη (from ἀχρήμων) want of money, Od., Theogn.

αχρημων.def: ἀχρήμων (χρήματα) without money, poor, needy, Solon, Eur.

αχρηστια.def: ἀχρηστία (ἄχρηστος) I. uselessness, Plat. II. the non-usance of a thing, id.

αχρηστοσ.def: ἄχρηστος (χράομαι) I. useless, unprofitable, unserviceable, Hdt., Thuc.: of an oracle, without effect, Eur.:— ἄχρ. ἔς or πρός τι unfit for a thing, Hdt.; ἄχρ. τινι useless to a person, id., Eur. 2. like ἀχρεῖος, of useless, do-nothing persons, Oratt. 3. act. making no use of, c. dat., Eur. II. （χρηστός) unkind, cruel, Hdt.

αχρι.def: ἄχρι I. adv. to the uttermost, utterly, Il. 2. after Hom., before Preps., ἄχρι εἰς.. ἄχρι πρὸς.., Lat. usque ad.., Xen., Luc. II. prep. with gen. even to, as far as: 1. of Time, until, ἄχρι μάλα κνέφαος until deep in the night, Od.; ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας Dem. 2. of Space, as far as, even to, ἄχρι τῆς ἐσόδου Hdt. 3. of Degree, ἄχρι τούτου up to this point, Dem.; ἄχρι τοῦ μὴ πεινᾶν Xen. III. as Conj., ἄχρι οὗ or ἄχρι alone: 1. of Time, Lat donec, until, so long as, ἄχρι οὗ ὅδε ὁ λόγος ἐγράφετο id.; ἄχρι ἄν with Subj., ἄχρι ἂν σχολάσηι till he should be at leisure, id. 2. of Space, so far as, id., Luc.

αχρωστοσ.def: ἄχρωστος (χρώζω) untouched, χερῶν ἐμῶν by my hands, Eur.

αχυρμια.def: ἀχυρμιά (ἄχυρον) a heap of chaff, Il., Anth.

αχυρον.def: ἄχυρον mostly in pl. ἄχυρα, husks, chaff, bran, Hdt.; metaph., ἄχυρα τῶν ἀστῶν Ar.

αχυροσ.def: ἀχυρός a chaff-heap, Ar.; but ἀχυρμός is prob. the true form.

αχυροτριψ.def: ἀχυρότριψ (τρίβω) threshing out the husks, Anth.

αχωριστοσ.def: ἀχώριστος (χωρίζω) I. not parted, not divided, Plat. II. （χῶρος) with no place assigned one, Xen.

αψ.def: ἄψ (ἀπό) 1. of Place, backwards, back, back again, Hom. 2. of actions, again, in return, id.; so, ἂψ αὖτις, ἂψ πάλιν, yet again, Il.

αψαυστοσ.gloss: untouched, not to be touched, sacred
αψαυστοσ.def: ἄψαυστος (ψαύω) I. untouched, not to be touched, sacred, Thuc. II. act. not touching a thing, c. gen., Soph.

αψευδεω.gloss: not to lie, to speak truth
αψευδεω.def: ἀψευδέω (from ἀψευδής) not to lie, to speak truth, πρός τινα Soph., Plat.

αψευδησ.gloss: without lie and deceit, truthful, sincere, trusty
αψευδησ.def: ἀψευδής (ψεῦδος) without lie and deceit, truthful, sincere, trusty, Hes., Hdt., etc.:—adv. -δέως, attic -δῶς, really and truly, id.

αψιδοομαι.def: ἁψιδόομαι (ἀψίς) Pass. to be encircled, Anth.

αψικοροσ.def: ἁψίκορος (ἅπτομαι, κόρος) satisfied with touching, i. e. fastidious, dainty, Plat.:— τὸ ἁψ. fastidiousness, Plut., Luc.

αψιμαχεω.gloss: to skirmish with an enemy, lead on to fight
αψιμαχεω.def: ἁψιμαχέω (from ἁψίμαχος) to skirmish with an enemy, lead on to fight, Plut.

αψισ.def: ἁψίς (ἅπτω) 1. a juncture, loop, mesh, such as form a net, Il. 2. the felloe or felly of a wheel, the wheel itself, Hes., Hdt., Eur. 3. any circle or disk, of the sun, id. 4. an arch or vault, Plat., Luc.

αψορροοσ.def: ἀψόρροος (ἄψ, ῥέω) backflowing, refluent, of Ocean, regarded as a stream encircling the earth and flowing back into itself, Hom.

αψορροσ.def: ἄψορρος (poetic for ἀψόρρος) going back, backwards, Il., Soph.:—neut. ἄψορρον as adv., backward, back again, Il., Aesch., Soph.

αψοφητοσ.def: ἀψόφητος (ψοφέω) noiseless; c. gen., ἀψ. κωκυμάτων without sound of wailings, Soph.

αψυκτοσ.def: ἄψυκτος (ψύχω) not capable of being cooled, Plat.

αψυχια.gloss: want of life: want of spirit, faint-heartedness
αψυχια.def: ἀψυχία (from ἄψυχος) want of life: want of spirit, faint-heartedness, Aesch., Eur.

αψυχοσ.def: ἄψυχος (ψυχή) I. lifeless, inanimate, Simon., Eur., Plat. 2. ἄψ. βορά non-animal food, Eur. II. spiritless, faint-hearted, Aesch.

αω.def: ἄω I. = ἄημι, to blow. II. = ἰαύω, to sleep, used only in aor1 ἄεσα, epic ἄεσσα Od.; also 1st pl. contr. ἄσαμεν, id.
ἄω to hurt, contr. from ἀάω.

ἄω (ἄμεναι contr. for ἀέμεναι) I. trans. to satiate, αἵματος ἆσαι Ἀρῆα to give him his fill of blood, Il. II. intr. to take one's fill of a thing, c. gen., χροὸς ἄμεναι, χροὸς ἆσαι Ib; so in Mid., ἄσεσθε κλαυθμοῖο, ποτῆτος ἄσασθαι id.

αωρι.gloss: at an untimely hour, too early
αωρι.def: ἀωρί (ἄωρος) Adv. of ἄωρος, at an untimely hour, too early, Luc., Anth.; ἀωρὶ τῆς νυκτός at dead of night, Antipho, Theocr.

αωρια.def: ἀωρία (ἄωρος) a wrong time: acc. as adv., ἀωρίαν ἥκειν to have come too late, Ar.; ἀωρίαι at an unseasonable time, so late, Luc.

αωροσ.def: ἄωρος (ὥρα) I. untimely, unseasonable, Lat. intempestivus, Aesch., Eur.:—c. gen., γήρως ἀωρότερα things unbecoming old age, Plut. 2. unripe, ἄωρος πρὸς γάμον id. II. without youthful freshness, ugly, Xen., Plat.
ἄωρος (ἀείρω, cf. μετέωρος) pendulous, waving about, of the πλεκτάναι or polypus-like legs of Scylla, Od.

αωτεω.def: ἀωτέω (ἄω to sleep) (only in pres.) to sleep well, Hom.

αωτον.def: ἄωτον (Deriv. uncertain.) I. fine wool, flock, οἰὸς ἄωτον, or without οἰός, the sheep's finest wool, Hom.; λίνοιο λεπτὸν ἄωτον the delicate flock of flax, i. e. the finest linen, Il. II. metaph. the finest, best of its kind, the flower of a thing, ἄωτος ζωᾶς the flower of life, Pind.; Χαρίτων ἄωτος their choisest gift, id.
